translation.simple: What is not truly real can never truly be, and what is truly real can never cease to exist. Those who see the deeper truth have understood this difference between these two.
translation.deep: This profound verse gently reminds us that all that is temporary, like our physical experiences and the world around us, has no ultimate, lasting reality. Yet, the eternal Self within, the soul, is always real and can never be destroyed or cease to be. Spiritual seers who perceive the ultimate truth recognize this unchanging essence, seeing beyond the fleeting illusions of the material world.
translation.essence: The core wisdom is that the unreal cannot endure, and the real can never perish. The wise recognize this eternal truth, discerning the everlasting divine amidst all change.

2-17.sanskrit:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।

विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित् कर्तुमर्हति।।2.17।।
2-17.transliteration:
avināśhi tu tadviddhi yena sarvam idaṁ tatam
vināśham avyayasyāsya na kaśhchit kartum arhati

translation.simple: Know this profound truth: your innermost self can never truly be destroyed. It is the subtle essence that gently pervades all that you see and experience. No one has the power to bring an end to this eternal spirit within.
translation.deep: Contemplate the sacred reality of an imperishable essence that gracefully permeates and sustains the entire cosmos. This same eternal Spirit resides within you as your true identity, untouched by birth or death. No force in existence can diminish or destroy this changeless, ever-present reality, for it is timeless and boundless.
translation.essence: Rest in the serene knowledge that your true Self is eternal, all-pervading, and utterly indestructible. It is the changeless reality of your being.

2-18.sanskrit:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः।

अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत।।2.18।।
2-18.transliteration:
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śharīriṇaḥ
anāśhino ’prameyasya tasmād yudhyasva bhārata

translation.simple: Our physical bodies are destined to end, but the spirit, the soul within, is eternal. It is indestructible and beyond all measure. With this understanding, fulfill your righteous duty, O seeker.
translation.deep: Meditate on the profound truth that this earthly vessel is temporary. The real 'you' is the eternal soul, imperishable and boundless, beyond the limitations of birth and death. This realization dissolves fear and sorrow, guiding you to act with unwavering purpose and calm resolve, knowing your true essence is divine and everlasting.
translation.essence: The body is fleeting, but the soul is eternal and indestructible. Act with this profound wisdom.

2-19.sanskrit:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्।

उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते।।2.19।।
2-19.transliteration:
ya enaṁ vetti hantāraṁ yaśh chainaṁ manyate hatam
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṁ hanti na hanyate

translation.simple: To believe the soul can ever take a life, or that it can ever be taken, is to miss its deepest truth. Our true self, the soul, is untouched by such happenings; it neither kills nor is killed.
translation.deep: This profound verse gently guides us beyond the illusion of life and death as we perceive them for the true self. The divine soul within is eternal, pure, and unchanging. It is not an actor in the drama of physical creation and destruction, nor is it a passive victim. When we mistakenly see the soul as capable of killing or being killed, we are still caught in the identification with the temporary body. Realizing this truth frees us from fear and sorrow, reminding us that our essence is ever-blissful and indestructible, an eternal spark of the Divine.
translation.essence: Know this eternal truth: the soul is never the killer, nor is it ever slain. It remains forever untouched, a beacon of changeless peace.

2-20.sanskrit:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचि

न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।

अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो

न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे।।2.20।।
2-20.transliteration:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadāchin
nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
ajo nityaḥ śhāśhvato ’yaṁ purāṇo
na hanyate hanyamāne śharīre

translation.simple: The true self, the soul, is never born and never truly dies. It doesn't come into being or pass away. It is unborn, eternal, everlasting, and ancient. Even when the body is destroyed, the soul remains unharmed and unaffected.
translation.deep: This profound verse unveils the immortal essence of the self, affirming that the soul transcends the cycles of birth and demise, remaining untouched by temporal limitations. It is not something that begins to exist or ceases to be; rather, it is eternally present, ancient, and everlasting. Thus, the destruction of the physical form does not affect the indestructible spiritual essence within, offering deep comfort and spiritual understanding of our unchanging nature.
translation.essence: The timeless truth revealed here is that the soul is eternally unborn and undying. It is ever-present, ancient, and remains completely untouched by the dissolution of the physical body, reminding us of our true, imperishable nature.

2-21.sanskrit:
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम्।

कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम्।।2.21।।
2-21.transliteration:
vedāvināśhinaṁ nityaṁ ya enam ajam avyayam
kathaṁ sa puruṣhaḥ pārtha kaṁ ghātayati hanti kam

translation.simple: O Arjuna, if you truly know that the soul within is eternal, never born, and can never be destroyed, how could you ever think that you are killing anyone, or causing another to be killed?
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to a profound understanding of the Self, or Atman. When we deeply grasp that the soul is beyond birth and death, eternally unchanging, the illusion of being the doer, or the one who causes an end, begins to fade. It encourages us to look beyond the temporary form and recognize the imperishable spark within all beings. Such wisdom brings a serene detachment from the body's actions and fosters a deeper connection to the timeless, divine essence.
translation.essence: Recognizing the soul as unborn, eternal, and indestructible liberates us from the misconception of being the killer or causing death.

2-22.sanskrit:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय

नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।

तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा

न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही।।2.22।।
2-22.transliteration:
vāsānsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya
navāni gṛihṇāti naro ’parāṇi
tathā śharīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇānya
nyāni sanyāti navāni dehī

translation.simple: Just as we lovingly set aside worn-out garments to wear fresh, new ones, so too, the eternal soul within us gently leaves an old body behind and takes on a new one. It's a natural, peaceful transition.
translation.deep: This profound truth from the Gita reassures us that our true essence, the soul, is distinct from the temporary physical body. Like a traveler changing clothes, the soul gracefully sheds an old form to embrace a new one, continuing its sacred journey. It reminds us of our imperishable nature, bringing a deep sense of peace and freeing us from the illusion of an ultimate end, for the soul's path is one of eternal continuity and divine purpose.
translation.essence: The eternal soul, our true self, simply changes bodies like one changes clothes. A gentle journey of continuous renewal, free from fear.

2-23.sanskrit:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।

न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः।।2.23।।
2-23.transliteration:
nainaṁ chhindanti śhastrāṇi nainaṁ dahati pāvakaḥ
na chainaṁ kledayantyāpo na śhoṣhayati mārutaḥ

translation.simple: The precious soul within us can never be cut by any weapon, nor can it ever be burned by fire. Water cannot make it wet, and the wind cannot ever dry it out. It remains eternally untouched.
translation.deep: This profound verse assures us that our true spiritual essence, the soul, is beyond the reach of all material forces. It transcends birth and death, remaining untouched by the elements that affect the physical body. Understanding this brings a deep sense of peace, knowing that our eternal self is always safe, pure, and connected to the Divine, regardless of worldly changes.
translation.essence: The soul is intrinsically indestructible, eternally pure, and unaffected by any physical element or worldly transformation, dwelling in its true, unchanging nature.

2-24.sanskrit:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च।

नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः।।2.24।।
2-24.transliteration:
achchhedyo ’yam adāhyo ’yam akledyo ’śhoṣhya eva cha
nityaḥ sarva-gataḥ sthāṇur achalo ’yaṁ sanātanaḥ

translation.simple: This spirit within can never be cut by any weapon, nor consumed by fire. It cannot be drenched by water or withered by the wind. For it is eternal, present everywhere, steady, unmoving, and ever-ancient.
translation.deep: Contemplate the profound nature of your true self, the soul. It is beyond all forms of destruction – immune to blades, flames, water's touch, or drying winds. This eternal essence is all-pervading, ever-present, a constant and unmoving presence throughout all time. Realizing this truth offers deep serenity, as it confirms the indestructible and everlasting nature of our innermost being, connected to the Divine.
translation.essence: Your true self, the soul, is eternally whole and indestructible. It is ever-present, unchanging, and timeless, offering profound peace.

2-25.transliteration:
avyakto ’yam achintyo ’yam avikāryo ’yam uchyate
tasmādevaṁ viditvainaṁ nānuśhochitum arhasi

translation.simple: The true self, the soul, cannot be seen with our eyes, nor fully understood by our minds; it is always constant and never changes. Knowing this truth, you will find peace and there will be no reason for sorrow.
translation.deep: It is revealed that the spiritual essence within is unmanifest, a subtle presence beyond sensory perception, and inconceivable to the analytical mind. It remains eternally untouched by any modification or decay. When we truly grasp this immutable, divine nature of the soul, all causes for lamentation vanish, and a profound, tranquil acceptance takes their place.
translation.essence: Understand the soul as unmanifest, beyond thought, and ever-unchanging. This wisdom frees the heart from all grief.

2-26.sanskrit:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्।

तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि।।2.26।।
2-26.transliteration:
atha chainaṁ nitya-jātaṁ nityaṁ vā manyase mṛitam
tathāpi tvaṁ mahā-bāho naivaṁ śhochitum arhasi

translation.simple: Even if you consider the self to be continuously born and continuously passing away, O mighty-armed one, there is still no cause for you to grieve.
translation.deep: Should your understanding be that the individual self is perpetually undergoing cycles of birth and dissolution, Arjuna, even within this perception of constant change and impermanence, the divine wisdom indicates that sorrow is an inappropriate response. True peace comes from accepting the flow of existence.
translation.essence: Whether one perceives the self as ever-present or continually cycling through birth and death, the fundamental message remains: sorrow and lamentation are unwarranted. Embrace a tranquil spirit, for in the grand tapestry of life, there is no true loss for which to grieve.

2-27.sanskrit:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च।

तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि।।2.27।।
2-27.transliteration:
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛityur dhruvaṁ janma mṛitasya cha
tasmād aparihārye ’rthe na tvaṁ śhochitum arhasi

translation.simple: Every being that takes birth is certain to experience death, and every being that passes away is certain to be born again. Since this sacred cycle is an unchangeable truth, there is no reason for you to feel sorrow.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna gently reveals the profound truth of existence: the journey of the soul through physical forms is an eternal, continuous flow. Just as a spirit enters a body, it will eventually depart, only to take on another form in due course. This divine arrangement of birth and rebirth is a fundamental law of the universe, not a matter for lamentation. Understanding this helps us detach from the fleeting nature of the body and connect with the eternal, unchanging essence within.
translation.essence: Birth and death are integral parts of the soul's journey, an unavoidable and continuous cycle. Embrace this deep wisdom and find peace, letting go of sorrow for what is eternally destined.

2-28.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत।

अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना।।2.28।।
2-28.transliteration:
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyakta-madhyāni bhārata
avyakta-nidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā

translation.simple: O Arjuna, all beings emerge from an unseen state before birth, manifest and live for a time, and then return to an unseen state after passing. Knowing this eternal cycle, what cause is there for lamentation?
translation.deep: Reflect, O Arjuna, that every creature appears from an unmanifest reality, dwells for a while in a visible form, and then gracefully merges back into the unmanifest. This understanding liberates the heart from the attachment to transient forms. When we recognize that this journey from the unseen to the seen and back again is the natural order, our minds find solace, and the burden of sorrow dissolves.
translation.essence: All life originates from the unseen, manifests for a period, and returns to the unseen. Understanding this cyclical nature brings profound peace and frees us from all sorrow.

2-29.sanskrit:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन

माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः।

आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श्रृणोति

श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित्।।2.29।।
2-29.transliteration:
āśhcharya-vat paśhyati kaśhchid enan
āśhcharya-vad vadati tathaiva chānyaḥ
āśhcharya-vach chainam anyaḥ śhṛiṇoti
śhrutvāpyenaṁ veda na chaiva kaśhchit

translation.simple: Some look upon the eternal Self within as a great marvel, full of wonder. Others speak of it with deep awe, sharing its mysterious beauty. And still others listen, captivated by these accounts. Yet, even after hearing and knowing much, very few truly grasp its ultimate nature.
translation.deep: The divine essence, the Atman, is beheld by some with profound astonishment, its mere presence stirring a deep sense of wonder within them. Others are inspired to articulate its incomprehensible glory, sharing words that barely hint at its timeless majesty. Many more listen intently, drawn by the incredible tales of this ultimate reality. Yet, even after such profound engagement – seeing, speaking, and hearing – the direct, experiential knowing of this Self, in its absolute truth, remains a most rare and sacred achievement, a testament to its infinite depth and spiritual mystery.
translation.essence: The Self is a profound wonder, seen, spoken of, and heard with awe, yet its ultimate, true understanding remains elusive, highlighting its sacred and mysterious nature.

2-30.sanskrit:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत।

तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि।।2.30।।
2-30.transliteration:
dehī nityam avadhyo ’yaṁ dehe sarvasya bhārata
tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṁ śhochitum arhasi

translation.simple: O Arjuna, the spirit dwelling within every body is eternal and can never truly be destroyed. Knowing this, you should not grieve for any living being.
translation.deep: This verse reveals a profound truth: the essence of life, the soul, is an eternal spark within every body, untouched by any form of destruction. When we truly grasp this, O Arjuna, our hearts are freed from the burden of lamentation for the transient forms. It invites us to perceive all beings through the lens of their indestructible spiritual nature, fostering deep tranquility and understanding.
translation.essence: The soul in all beings is eternal and cannot be destroyed. Therefore, there is no cause for sorrow.

2-31.sanskrit:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि।

धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाछ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते।।2.31।।
2-31.transliteration:
swa-dharmam api chāvekṣhya na vikampitum arhasi
dharmyāddhi yuddhāch chhreyo ’nyat kṣhatriyasya na vidyate

translation.simple: Beloved soul, when you reflect on your sacred duty, there is no cause for hesitation. Indeed, for one born to protect and uphold truth, there's no greater path than to embrace righteous action, even through struggle.
translation.deep: Ponder deeply, dear one, on the nature of your inherent dharma, the divine blueprint for your existence. To shrink from this path, especially when it calls for the defense of truth and goodness, is to deny your very essence. For a soul dedicated to righteousness, fulfilling its appointed duty, however challenging, is the surest way to spiritual elevation and inner peace.
translation.essence: Trust in your divine calling and fulfill your sacred duty without wavering. For a soul committed to righteousness, facing challenges to uphold truth is the truest path to spiritual fulfillment and grace.

2-32.sanskrit:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्।

सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम्।।2.32।।
2-32.transliteration:
yadṛichchhayā chopapannaṁ swarga-dvāram apāvṛitam
sukhinaḥ kṣhatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛiśham

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, this sacred battle has come to you effortlessly, like a divine gateway to higher realms. Only truly blessed warriors are granted such a profound opportunity.
translation.deep: Consider, Arjuna, how this moment has arrived by divine arrangement, presenting itself as an unbarred door to heavenly bliss. For a warrior, engaging in a righteous duty, even through conflict, is a path of profound spiritual merit. It is a sign of immense good fortune when one is chosen to uphold dharma, for it purifies the soul and elevates one towards divine grace.
translation.essence: The core message is that when divine providence brings forth a challenging situation, especially one that fulfills our righteous duty, it is a rare blessing. It is an open invitation to spiritual elevation, granted to those pure of heart, allowing them to fulfill their sacred purpose and draw closer to the divine.

2-33.sanskrit:
अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि।

ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि।।2.33।।
2-33.transliteration:
atha chet tvam imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṅgrāmaṁ na kariṣhyasi
tataḥ sva-dharmaṁ kīrtiṁ cha hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi

translation.simple: If you choose not to engage in this righteous battle, you will abandon your sacred duty and your good name. This path would lead to spiritual difficulty.
translation.deep: To turn away from a struggle that is aligned with righteousness, dear soul, is to step away from your profound inner calling, your 'svadharma'. It's not only the loss of external reputation but an internal discord that emerges when one fails to uphold the path of truth, leading to an unfavorable spiritual state.
translation.essence: Upholding your righteous duty, even amidst challenge, is paramount for your spiritual harmony and true self.

2-34.sanskrit:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम्।

संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते।।2.34।।
2-34.transliteration:
akīrtiṁ chāpi bhūtāni
kathayiṣhyanti te ’vyayām
sambhāvitasya chākīrtir
maraṇād atirichyate

translation.simple: Oh beloved one, if you choose inaction, people will forever speak of your lasting dishonor. For a person of high esteem, such disgrace is indeed considered a greater sorrow than death itself.
translation.deep: This wisdom gently guides us to reflect on the importance of integrity and the lasting impact of our choices. For a soul blessed with honor and respect, a fall into disgrace can feel profoundly more agonizing than the departure from this body. It speaks to the deep connection between our outer actions and our inner peace, urging us to always act in alignment with our true self and righteous path, for the purity of our reputation is a precious spiritual offering.
translation.essence: For a respected being, disgrace is more grievous than death, teaching us to cherish our sacred honor.

2-35.sanskrit:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः।

येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्।।2.35।।
2-35.transliteration:
bhayād raṇād uparataṁ mansyante tvāṁ mahā-rathāḥ
yeṣhāṁ cha tvaṁ bahu-mato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam

translation.simple: The great warriors will simply think you turned away from this battle out of fear. They, who once held you in such high regard, will then see your worth diminish.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly reminds Arjuna that our actions leave a lasting impression, not just upon the world, but within our own hearts. To step away from one's righteous duty (dharma), even out of a mistaken sense of compassion, can lead to a perception of fear and a loss of the esteem we once commanded. This teaching gently guides us to understand the importance of inner integrity and standing firm in our spiritual path, knowing that true honor comes from unwavering resolve.
translation.essence: Choosing courage in our duty over fear preserves our honor and strengthens our spirit.

2-36.sanskrit:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः।

निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्।।2.36।।
2-36.transliteration:
avāchya-vādānśh cha bahūn vadiṣhyanti tavāhitāḥ
nindantastava sāmarthyaṁ tato duḥkhataraṁ nu kim

translation.simple: Your adversaries will utter many words unfit to hear, belittling your capabilities. What greater sorrow could there be than such disregard?
translation.deep: When unkind words are spoken by those who oppose you, questioning your very capacity and honor, it can stir a deep sadness within the heart. To witness one's true potential and dedication disregarded in such a manner feels like a profound pain.
translation.essence: To have one's integrity and strength unjustly questioned by others can bring a deep ache to the spirit. This verse gently reminds us of the profound sorrow that can arise from such disregard.

2-37.sanskrit:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्।

तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः।।2.37।।
2-37.transliteration:
hato vā prāpsyasi swargaṁ jitvā vā bhokṣhyase mahīm
tasmād uttiṣhṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛita-niśhchayaḥ

translation.simple: Whether you are called to a heavenly abode, or if you live on to enjoy this earth, simply rise, O son of Kunti, with a steadfast heart for your sacred duty.
translation.deep: This profound teaching gently reminds us that our true reward lies not in the outcome, be it worldly success or departure to a higher realm, but in the purity and conviction with which we embrace our sacred duty. With a heart surrendered, O seeker, simply rise and act, knowing that the divine will guides every step.
translation.essence: Rise with an unwavering heart, O seeker, embrace your sacred duty without attachment to the outcome, for grace awaits you in all of life's paths.

2-38.sanskrit:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ।

ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि।।2.38।।
2-38.transliteration:
sukha-duḥkhe same kṛitvā lābhālābhau jayājayau
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṁ pāpam avāpsyasi

translation.simple: See happiness and sorrow, gain and loss, victory and defeat as equal. Then, step forward into your duty. By doing this, you will not gather any negative karmic reactions.
translation.deep: The path of inner peace asks us to see beyond the fleeting dance of opposites – joy and sorrow, gain and loss, triumph and defeat. When we approach life's experiences with a steady heart, unswayed by these temporary waves, our actions become pure. Then, stepping into our sacred duty, knowing we are not attached to the results, frees us from the accumulation of karmic bonds. It's an invitation to act from a place of profound inner freedom.
translation.essence: With a serene heart that sees joy and sorrow, gain and loss, victory and defeat as one, embrace your sacred duty. This path ensures your actions remain pure and free from karmic ties.

2-39.sanskrit:
एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु।

बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि।।2.39।।
2-39.transliteration:
eṣhā te ’bhihitā sānkhye
buddhir yoge tvimāṁ śhṛiṇu
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha
karma-bandhaṁ prahāsyasi

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, I have explained wisdom to you through deep understanding. Now, hear how this very wisdom, when applied to your actions, will gently release you from all karmic ties.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly reveals that He first shared profound wisdom from the path of analytical understanding (Sankhya). Now, He graciously invites us to listen to how this same truth, when practiced with a yogic spirit in our daily duties, becomes a powerful yet gentle means. By aligning our intelligence with this divine understanding, we can gracefully transcend the cycles of karma and discover true, lasting inner freedom.
translation.essence: Embrace profound spiritual understanding, then apply it to your actions with devotion. This harmonious path lovingly frees you from all karmic bonds, bringing deep peace.

2-40.sanskrit:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते।

स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्।।2.40।।
2-40.transliteration:
nehābhikrama-nāśho ’sti pratyavāyo na vidyate
svalpam apyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt

translation.simple: On this path of selfless devotion and sincere effort, no act ever goes in vain; there's no adverse consequence. Even a little bit of this righteous way of living protects us from great fears.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna reassures us that unlike worldly actions which may lead to impermanent results or even regret, efforts made on the spiritual path are eternally preserved. Here, every sincere step, every loving offering, every pure thought contributes to our ultimate good, never diminishing. This divine endeavor, even in its smallest form, grants a profound sanctuary, guarding our hearts and minds from the deepest anxieties and the cycle of suffering.
translation.essence: Every sincere spiritual effort, however small, is eternally fruitful and offers unwavering protection from all fears.

2-41.sanskrit:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन।

बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम्।।2.41।।
2-41.transliteration:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana
bahu-śhākhā hyanantāśh cha buddhayo ’vyavasāyinām

translation.simple: O Arjuna, on this sacred path, a mind that is truly resolved has a single, clear aim. But for those who are not steadfast, their thoughts branch out endlessly, going in many directions.
translation.deep: O Arjuna, understand that a mind deeply committed to the spiritual journey finds a singular, unwavering purpose. This resolute focus brings profound clarity and inner peace, guiding one steadily towards the Divine. In contrast, those who lack such firm determination find their intellects scattered, branching out into countless desires and doubts, creating confusion and endless wandering without true spiritual progress.
translation.essence: True devotion makes the mind one-pointed and resolute. Without such resolve, thoughts become endlessly scattered.

2-42.sanskrit:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः।

वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः।।2.42।।
2-42.transliteration:
yāmimāṁ puṣhpitāṁ vāchaṁ pravadanty-avipaśhchitaḥ
veda-vāda-ratāḥ pārtha nānyad astīti vādinaḥ
 kāmātmānaḥ swarga-parā janma-karma-phala-pradām
kriyā-viśheṣha-bahulāṁ bhogaiśhwarya-gatiṁ prati

translation.simple: Some, Arjuna, speak captivating words, like beautiful flowers, promising earthly joys and heavenly rewards. They are devoted to rituals and believe there is nothing beyond these temporary gains, lacking deeper insight.
translation.deep: O Arjuna, there are those whose wisdom is yet undeveloped, who are greatly attached to the alluring, 'flowery' descriptions within scriptures that promise material benefits and heavenly abodes through various rites. They become so engrossed in these promises that they declare there is no ultimate truth or lasting happiness beyond such temporary rewards. This verse gently cautions against being swayed by these attractive yet transient offerings, encouraging a focus on higher, eternal spiritual understanding.
translation.essence: Be mindful of attractive promises that lead only to fleeting rewards. True wisdom guides us past superficial gains towards the lasting peace and profound truth of the spirit.

2-43.sanskrit:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्।

क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति।।2.43।।
2-43.transliteration:
kāmātmānaḥ svarga-parā 

 janma-karma-phala-pradām

 kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulāṁ

 bhogaiśvarya-gatiṁ prati

translation.simple: Hearts filled with earthly longings, they aspire only for heavenly pleasures. They engage in many rituals, hoping for good births, abundant joy, and worldly power.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully describes souls who, with hearts full of worldly aspirations, direct their efforts towards heavenly pleasures. They engage in numerous ceremonial acts, believing these will grant them favorable births, abundant joys, and worldly power. It highlights an approach where the focus remains on the temporary rewards of action, rather than the liberation beyond all outcomes.
translation.essence: The essence here is a gentle insight into how desires for temporary pleasures, whether earthly or heavenly, and for power or fortunate births, shape our actions. While these pursuits may seem appealing, they ultimately bind us to the cycle of repeated existence, diverting our gaze from the lasting peace and spiritual liberation that lies beyond all outcomes.

2-44.sanskrit:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्।

व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते।।2.44।।
2-44.transliteration:
bhogaiśwvarya-prasaktānāṁ tayāpahṛita-chetasām
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate

translation.simple: When our minds become too attached to worldly pleasures and riches, it's difficult to develop a steady and determined focus for spiritual understanding. Our inner vision tends to get clouded.
translation.deep: This verse tenderly reminds us that a heart deeply entangled in the pursuit of material enjoyments and opulence finds its intelligence easily carried away. Such a mind struggles to achieve a resolute and unwavering determination, the kind that firmly establishes itself in deep spiritual contemplation and devotion. True inner clarity and purpose blossom when we gently guide our focus beyond the fleeting allure of the world.
translation.essence: A mind captivated by worldly desires cannot find resolute spiritual wisdom or inner peace.

2-45.sanskrit:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन।

निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्।।2.45।।
2-45.transliteration:
trai-guṇya-viṣhayā vedā nistrai-guṇyo bhavārjuna
nirdvandvo nitya-sattva-stho niryoga-kṣhema ātmavān

translation.simple: O Arjuna, the scriptures often discuss the three qualities of nature (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas). But you, dear one, endeavor to go beyond these qualities. Be free from the opposing pairs of joy and sorrow, always dwell in inner purity, and release your worries about what you gain or keep. Instead, remain firmly rooted in your true Self.
translation.deep: This profound verse guides us to transcend the influences of the three Gunas—the fundamental energies that color our perceptions and experiences in the material realm. To be 'beyond the Gunas' signifies acting from a place of pure intention, unattached to outcomes, driven by spiritual clarity rather than worldly impulses. It encourages liberation from the pull of dualities—the fleeting experiences of pleasure and pain, heat and cold—by recognizing them as temporary states. By establishing ourselves in unwavering goodness and releasing the anxieties of acquiring and preserving, we cultivate true inner freedom and abide in the tranquil wisdom of the Self, untouched by life's fluctuations.
translation.essence: Rise above nature's qualities, transcend dualities, release material concerns, and find peace in your true Self.

2-46.sanskrit:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके।

तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः।।2.46।।
2-46.transliteration:
yāvān artha udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake
tāvānsarveṣhu vedeṣhu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ

translation.simple: Imagine a vast land overflowing with water, like an endless ocean. What need is there then for a small well? In a similar way, for a soul who truly knows the ultimate truth, the purpose of all scriptures is fulfilled, as they have found the boundless source within.
translation.deep: This profound verse guides us to understand the shift from intellectual pursuit to direct spiritual realization. When a seeker experiences the boundless ocean of divine consciousness, the individual wells of scriptural knowledge, while precious as guides, become encompassed within that all-pervading experience. It gently suggests that true wisdom is not merely accumulated information but an awakened state of being, where the Self is united with the Supreme, rendering all preliminary practices and limited understandings as stepping stones to that ultimate, blissful union.
translation.essence: When your heart is filled with the boundless realization of the Divine, all scriptural wisdom finds its culmination and purpose within that single, all-encompassing experience.

2-47.sanskrit:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।

मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि।।2.47।।
2-47.transliteration:
karmaṇy-evādhikāras te mā phaleṣhu kadāchana
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stvakarmaṇi

translation.simple: You have the right to perform your duties, to engage in action, but your authority does not extend to controlling or owning the results of those actions. Do not let the desire for outcomes be the sole reason for your efforts, nor should you ever be attached to choosing inaction.
translation.deep: Beloved soul, the path of spiritual wisdom teaches us that our truest power lies in the pure intention and dedicated execution of our actions, not in the anxious expectation of their fruits. Offer your efforts with a sincere heart, understanding that the ultimate results unfold according to divine will. This sacred instruction also gently guides us away from the temptation of idleness, urging us to fulfill our responsibilities with a spirit of surrender, free from the binding desires of reward or the avoidance of duty.
translation.essence: Act with your whole being, but surrender all attachment to the fruits of your labor. Never be driven by outcome, nor ever shy away from your rightful action.

2-48.sanskrit:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।

सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते।।2.48।।
2-48.transliteration:
yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga uchyate

translation.simple: O Arjuna, simply perform your duties, letting go of any attachment to the results. Remain steady and calm, seeing both success and failure with the same peaceful outlook. This tranquil balance of mind is what we call true Yoga.
translation.deep: My dear Arjuna, with your heart firmly established in spiritual consciousness, engage in all your prescribed actions. Release any clinging attachment to the fruits of your endeavors. Remain serene and balanced, accepting both triumph and setback with an unwavering, equal spirit. This profound equanimity, this peaceful steadiness of mind in all circumstances, is truly the essence of Yoga – the path of divine connection and inner freedom.
translation.essence: Perform your actions with a detached heart, letting go of worries about the outcomes. Embrace both success and setback with a calm and equal spirit, for this tranquil balance is the very essence of spiritual connection.

2-49.sanskrit:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय।

बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः।।2.49।।
2-49.transliteration:
dūreṇa hy-avaraṁ karma buddhi-yogād dhanañjaya
buddhau śharaṇam anvichchha kṛipaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ

translation.simple: Dear Arjuna, actions performed just for their outcomes are far less valuable than those guided by inner wisdom and devotion. Seek your refuge in this spiritual understanding, for those who are driven only by the desire for results often find themselves in a state of unease.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that true spiritual progress lies not in the mere act itself, but in the purity of our intention and the wisdom ('Buddhi Yoga') guiding it. When our deeds are offered with a serene heart, unattached to the fruits, they become a profound yoga, connecting us to the Divine. The Lord compassionately points out that those who cling to the results of their actions ('kṛpaṇāḥ') become bound by expectation, anxiety, and eventual disappointment, missing the deeper joy of selfless service and inner peace.
translation.essence: Let your actions be guided by wisdom, not by the desire for rewards. Cultivate a selfless understanding, finding true peace beyond the pursuit of outcomes.

2-50.sanskrit:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते।

तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्।।2.50।।
2-50.transliteration:
buddhi-yukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛita-duṣhkṛite
tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśhalam

translation.simple: When our understanding is guided by the Divine, we gently move beyond the effects of both good and difficult deeds in this world. Therefore, lovingly dedicate yourself to the path of Yoga. Truly, Yoga is the beautiful art of performing all our actions with serene skill.
translation.deep: A soul whose intellect is unwavering and connected to the Supreme consciousness transcends the binding chains of both virtuous and unvirtuous actions. Such a one is no longer entangled by their results. Therefore, with utmost sincerity, devote yourself to the spiritual practice of Yoga. For Yoga, in its essence, is the profound wisdom and perfect equanimity with which one performs all duties, transforming work into a selfless offering.
translation.essence: Align your wisdom with the Divine, and you will rise above all karmic outcomes. Embrace Yoga, for it is the sacred skill in every action.

2-51.sanskrit:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः।

जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम्।।2.51।।
2-51.transliteration:
karma-jaṁ buddhi-yuktā hi phalaṁ tyaktvā manīṣhiṇaḥ
janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ padaṁ gachchhanty-anāmayam

translation.simple: When our actions are guided by true understanding, we naturally let go of attachment to their outcomes. Such wise souls are then released from the cycle of repeated births and attain a peaceful, sorrow-free abode.
translation.deep: This teaching reveals the serene path of true wisdom. It's about performing our actions with a clear, discerning mind, understanding that the outcome is not ours to control, but an offering. When we gracefully release our grip on what our efforts might bring, we begin to unbind ourselves from the continuous cycle of birth and rebirth. This spiritual liberation leads us to an eternal dwelling, a place of ultimate peace, utterly free from all suffering and distress.
translation.essence: Perform actions with wisdom, release attachment to their fruits, and find freedom from the cycle of birth, attaining an eternal state of peace without sorrow.

2-52.sanskrit:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति।

तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च।।2.52।।
2-52.transliteration:
yadā te moha-kalilaṁ buddhir vyatitariṣhyati
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṁ śhrotavyasya śhrutasya cha

translation.simple: When your intellect fully passes beyond the confusion of illusion, you will find true peace, becoming steady in spirit, undisturbed by all that has been heard or is yet to be heard.
translation.deep: O seeker, the Lord reveals a profound truth: as your intellect purifies itself and rises above the dense forest of worldly attachments and misconceptions, you will arrive at a state of serene detachment. In this tranquil wisdom, the endless stream of information – both what you have already learned and what you might yet encounter – will no longer sway your inner peace. Your true understanding will emerge from within, not from external knowledge alone.
translation.essence: Once the veil of delusion lifts, your inner wisdom will bring profound peace, leaving you calm and content, beyond the sway of all external knowledge.

2-53.sanskrit:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला।

समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि।।2.53।।
2-53.transliteration:
śhruti-vipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niśhchalā
samādhāv-achalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasi

translation.simple: When your understanding, which might have been swayed by many different ideas, settles into a steady calm, and your mind rests firmly in the peace of inner contemplation, then you will truly attain union with the Divine.
translation.deep: The spiritual journey requires a profound settling of the intellect. When your inner wisdom is no longer bewildered by diverse teachings or conflicting thoughts, but stands firm and unmoving, and your consciousness becomes unwavering in deep meditative absorption, then the true essence of Yoga unfolds. This state is a quiet surrender, where all distractions dissolve, revealing an undisturbed connection with the Supreme.
translation.essence: With a steady mind, no longer distracted by various thoughts, and an unwavering intellect fixed in divine contemplation, true spiritual union is achieved.

2-54.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव।

स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्।।2.54।।
2-54.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣhā samādhi-sthasya keśhava
sthita-dhīḥ kiṁ prabhāṣheta kim āsīta vrajeta kim

translation.simple: Arjuna, with a humble heart, asks the Lord: "O Keshava, how can we recognize one whose mind is truly steady in wisdom, one who rests peacefully in deep contemplation? What are the gentle signs of how they speak, how they sit, and how they walk?"
translation.deep: Arjuna, seeking profound understanding, humbly asks Lord Krishna to illuminate the path for seekers. He yearns to know not just the outer actions, but the inner serenity that radiates from a soul truly stable in divine wisdom, one whose mind is deeply rooted in the Supreme. How does such a soul, touched by grace, speak with clarity, sit with inner calm, and move with purpose, O Keshava? This question touches upon the very heart of spiritual transformation and its visible grace.
translation.essence: Arjuna earnestly asks Lord Krishna to describe the gentle yet profound qualities and everyday actions of a soul whose wisdom is unwavering and whose heart is absorbed in divine peace.

2-55.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्।

आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते।।2.55।।
2-55.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha mano-gatān
ātmany-evātmanā tuṣhṭaḥ sthita-prajñas tadochyate

translation.simple: When one lets go of all desires that dwell in the mind, O Arjuna, and finds deep peace and joy purely within the Self, by the Self, that soul is truly called a person of steady wisdom.
translation.deep: This profound verse guides us towards the state of 'sthitaprajña' – a soul whose understanding is unwavering. It speaks of a liberation not from action, but from the attachment to the fruits of action, driven by mental desires. When the heart's yearning for external gratifications ceases, and one discovers an infinite source of contentment within their own spiritual being, then the mind becomes perfectly still, reflecting the serene wisdom of the divine within.
translation.essence: True wisdom blossoms when the heart finds complete fulfillment in its own spiritual nature, freeing itself from the pull of worldly desires.

2-56.transliteration:
duḥkheṣhv-anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣhu vigata-spṛihaḥ
vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ sthita-dhīr munir uchyate

translation.simple: When your heart isn't shaken by sorrow, and you don't long for worldly joys, when you've let go of attachment, fear, and anger—that's when a wise one, a true silent sage, is known.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully describes the awakened soul, a 'sthitaprajna' or one of steady wisdom. Such a blessed being finds profound peace within, undisturbed by life's trials and tribulations. Their spirit does not chase fleeting worldly happiness, for they understand its impermanence. Having truly surrendered all attachment, overcome the grip of fear, and released the fires of anger, their intelligence is firmly rooted in the eternal truth, revealing a tranquil and illuminated presence.
translation.essence: A heart that remains calm in sorrow, untouched by desire for joy, and free from attachment, fear, and anger—this truly marks a soul of steady divine wisdom.

2-57.sanskrit:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम्।

नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.57।।
2-57.transliteration:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śhubhāśhubham
nābhinandati na dveṣhṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā

translation.simple: One whose heart is not overly attached to anything, accepting life's ups and downs without strong elation or deep sorrow, possesses a wisdom that is truly firm.
translation.deep: This state of being speaks to a soul that has truly understood the fleeting nature of worldly events. When the heart is free from clinging to outcomes, whether they bring comfort or challenge, one discovers an inner peace that is unassailable. This wisdom is not just intellectual; it's a deep spiritual stability, a consciousness firmly anchored in the divine Self, unaffected by the waves of material existence.
translation.essence: Serene wisdom blossoms when an unattached heart neither clings to joy nor resists sorrow.

2-58.sanskrit:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.58।।
2-58.transliteration:
yadā sanharate chāyaṁ kūrmo ’ṅgānīva sarvaśhaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā

translation.simple: Just as a tortoise pulls its limbs fully into its shell, when a seeker lovingly withdraws their senses from worldly objects, their wisdom becomes steady and peaceful.
translation.deep: This verse invites us to contemplate true inner mastery. Just as a tortoise finds safety by withdrawing, we too can find inner peace by consciously guiding our senses away from external allurements. This isn't harsh suppression, but a gentle turning inward, allowing our awareness to rest. When the senses are thus calm and collected, our spiritual understanding becomes firmly rooted, granting us profound and lasting wisdom.
translation.essence: When our senses gently withdraw from worldly attractions, much like a tortoise drawing in its limbs, our inner wisdom becomes perfectly still and established.

2-59.sanskrit:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः।

रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते।।2.59।।
2-59.transliteration:
viṣhayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ
rasa-varjaṁ raso ’pyasya paraṁ dṛiṣhṭvā nivartate

translation.simple: Even if one holds back from worldly enjoyments, the longing for them can still remain in the heart. But when a person experiences the Supreme Truth, that deep-seated longing for material things completely fades away.
translation.deep: When the embodied soul refrains from engaging with external sense objects, these attractions may withdraw their hold. Yet, the intrinsic 'taste' or subtle inclination for them often persists within. However, upon experiencing the Supreme, the ultimate Reality, even this deeply rooted 'taste' for worldly pleasures entirely ceases, giving way to a profound and lasting inner peace.
translation.essence: True freedom from worldly desires isn't just about turning away from them outwardly; it comes when the heart finds its ultimate joy and fulfillment in the Divine, making all other attachments naturally dissolve.

2-60.sanskrit:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः।

इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः।।2.60।।
2-60.transliteration:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣhasya vipaśhchitaḥ
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṁ manaḥ

translation.simple: O Arjuna, even a wise and sincere seeker, striving diligently, can find their mind forcibly drawn away by the powerful and restless senses.
translation.deep: This profound verse tenderly reminds us that even when we are wise and striving with all our heart, dear Arjuna, the very nature of our senses is to be restless and to powerfully pull our mind towards worldly attractions. It gently reveals the constant inner vigilance and divine grace needed to steady our hearts amidst these powerful currents.
translation.essence: Even the most earnest spiritual seeker must be ever-aware, for the senses possess a subtle power to draw the mind away, reminding us of the need for inner steadfastness and divine guidance.

2-61.sanskrit:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः।

वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.61।।
2-61.transliteration:
tāni sarvāṇi sanyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ
vaśhe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā

translation.simple: Calmly bring all your senses under control and keep your heart devoted to the Divine. Truly, for one whose senses are in gentle harmony, their wisdom becomes firm and steady.
translation.deep: This sacred verse reveals the path to an unshakeable inner foundation. When we consciously gather our senses from their outward pursuits and lovingly surrender our very being to the Supreme, we enter a state of profound equipoise. Through such dedicated devotion and self-mastery, our spiritual understanding deepens, becoming eternally stable and free from the illusions of the fleeting world.
translation.essence: When senses are mastered and the heart is given to the Divine, wisdom takes root and shines with clarity.

2-62.sanskrit:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।

सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते।।2.62।।
2-62.transliteration:
dhyāyato viṣhayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣhūpajāyate
saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho ’bhijāyate

translation.simple: When our mind constantly thinks about worldly pleasures, an attachment to them begins to form. From this attachment, desires are born. And when these desires are not met, anger arises within us.
translation.deep: This verse reveals a profound truth about the mind's journey. When we allow our thoughts to linger on sense objects, a subtle bond of attachment is forged. This attachment then gives birth to strong desires, pulling our heart and mind towards worldly pursuits. When these cherished desires face obstacles or are unfulfilled, the peaceful state of our consciousness is disturbed, leading to the turbulent emotion of anger. It's a gentle reminder to guard our thoughts, for they are the seeds of our inner experiences.
translation.essence: This verse gently teaches us how our inner peace can be disturbed. It reminds us that when our mind repeatedly focuses on worldly things, attachment grows. This attachment then transforms into desires. If these desires are not fulfilled, anger appears, clouding our hearts. To protect our inner calm, we must be careful about where we allow our thoughts to dwell.

2-63.sanskrit:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।

स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति।।2.63।।
2-63.transliteration:
krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛiti-vibhramaḥ
smṛiti-bhranśhād buddhi-nāśho buddhi-nāśhāt praṇaśhyati

translation.simple: My dear self, when anger rises, it creates a fog in our minds, causing us to forget our true purpose and divine path. This forgetfulness then weakens our wisdom, and without wisdom, we drift away from our true self and the Lord's guidance.
translation.deep: This sacred teaching unveils how unchecked anger silently begins a perilous journey within us. It first clouds our judgment, making us forget our true spiritual essence and our loving connection with the Divine. When this precious spiritual memory fades, our inner discernment, which helps us choose good over evil and move towards the Lord, also diminishes. Ultimately, to 'perish' means to lose our way back to our divine source, becoming entangled in the world's fleeting sorrows, far from the eternal peace and joy that the Divine offers.
translation.essence: Dear one, this verse softly reminds us: anger clouds our mind, makes us forget our divine nature, destroys our inner wisdom, and gently leads us away from the path of eternal peace and connection with the Lord.

2-64.transliteration:
rāga-dveṣha-viyuktais tu viṣhayān indriyaiśh charan
ātma-vaśhyair-vidheyātmā prasādam adhigachchhati

translation.simple: When we live free from strong likes and dislikes, and our senses are gently guided by our inner wisdom, we experience a profound peace. Even as we interact with the world, a deep calmness blossoms within, making our journey serene.
translation.deep: The spiritual seeker, having carefully cultivated detachment from both strong desires and aversions, moves through the realm of sensory experiences with an unwavering mind. Their senses, though engaging with the world, remain under the benevolent control of the disciplined self. This inner mastery brings forth a sublime tranquility, a divine grace that calms the heart and grants a profound sense of spiritual well-being, irrespective of external circumstances.
translation.essence: Release attachment and aversion, guide your senses with self-control, and a beautiful inner peace will naturally unfold.

2-65.sanskrit:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते।

प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते।।2.65।।
2-65.transliteration:
prasāde sarva-duḥkhānāṁ hānir asyopajāyate
prasanna-chetaso hyāśhu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣhṭhate

translation.simple: When you find inner peace and a sense of grace, all your troubles and sorrows begin to fade away. For a mind that is truly calm and clear, understanding becomes steady and strong very quickly.
translation.deep: In the serene embrace of inner tranquility, all forms of suffering and distress naturally dissolve, revealing a profound sense of peace. For one whose heart and mind are thus clear and poised, the light of wisdom swiftly stabilizes, granting unwavering insight and steadfast resolve.
translation.essence: Cultivating inner peace dissolves all sorrows and swiftly establishes a firm and clear understanding.

2-66.sanskrit:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना।

न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम्।।2.66।।
2-66.transliteration:
nāsti buddhir-ayuktasya na chāyuktasya bhāvanā
na chābhāvayataḥ śhāntir aśhāntasya kutaḥ sukham

translation.simple: If our mind isn't steady and focused, true wisdom won't easily appear. Without this inner discipline, deep devotion or contemplation becomes difficult. And without cultivating this inner state, how can we find peace? If there is no peace, where can true and lasting happiness be found?
translation.deep: A soul unyoked from inner discipline cannot truly discern wisdom, nor can it cultivate genuine spiritual feeling and contemplation. For one who does not nurture this inner sanctity and focus, peace remains a distant dream. And indeed, without the serenity of peace in one's heart, how can one ever truly experience the lasting bliss of the Divine?
translation.essence: Without a disciplined mind, wisdom and devotion are elusive. Lacking inner peace, true happiness cannot blossom.

2-67.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते।

तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि।।2.67।।
2-67.transliteration:
indriyāṇāṁ hi charatāṁ yan mano ’nuvidhīyate
tadasya harati prajñāṁ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi

translation.simple: When our mind lets itself be led by the wandering senses, it carries away our wisdom, much like a powerful wind can sweep a boat off its course on the water.
translation.deep: This sacred verse gently reveals a profound truth: if our mind succumbs to the fleeting allure of the senses, it steals away our inner discernment, our spiritual intelligence. Imagine a vessel upon the vast ocean; if the winds of desire are too strong and the captain (our mind) yields, the ship (our spiritual journey) is swept away. We are gently reminded to keep our mind steadfast, so our wisdom remains undisturbed, guiding us ever closer to the Divine shore.
translation.essence: Just as a boat is tossed by strong winds, our spiritual wisdom is lost when the mind follows the senses without control.

2-68.sanskrit:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.68।।
2-68.transliteration:
tasmād yasya mahā-bāho nigṛihītāni sarvaśhaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, when someone learns to gently draw their senses away from worldly attractions, their understanding becomes truly steady and peaceful.
translation.deep: O mighty-armed one, consider the wisdom of one who has mastered their senses. When the eyes no longer chase fleeting sights, the ears cease to crave passing sounds, and all senses are gently restrained from their usual pursuits, then the inner light of spiritual discernment shines forth. Such a soul finds true stillness, where divine wisdom takes firm root, undisturbed by external clamor.
translation.essence: When the senses are lovingly guided away from worldly desires, true wisdom blossoms within the heart, bringing profound peace.

2-69.sanskrit:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी।

यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः।।2.69।।
2-69.transliteration:
yā niśhā sarva-bhūtānāṁ tasyāṁ jāgarti sanyamī
yasyāṁ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśhā paśhyato muneḥ

translation.simple: What seems like night to ordinary beings, a time of spiritual slumber, is when the self-controlled person truly awakens to inner wisdom. And what the world considers its bustling day, where all are awake in material pursuits, is like night for the insightful sage, who finds peace away from it.
translation.deep: This verse gently reveals a profound difference in perspective. For those lost in worldly desires and sensory pleasures, the eternal truths and spiritual realities often remain hidden, like a deep night. Yet, for the disciplined soul, who has mastered their senses and mind, these very truths shine brightly, becoming their awakened reality. Conversely, the bustling activities and fleeting joys that captivate the attention of most, for the enlightened sage, are perceived as a spiritual night, a period of obscurity and unimportance, as their awareness is fixed on the unchanging divine.
translation.essence: The wise one finds clarity and purpose in spiritual understanding while others are absorbed in worldly matters. Conversely, what engrosses the world appears as darkness to the sage, whose light comes from within.

2-70.sanskrit:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं

समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।

तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे

स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी।।2.70।।
2-70.transliteration:
āpūryamāṇam achala-pratiṣhṭhaṁ
samudram āpaḥ praviśhanti yadvat
tadvat kāmā yaṁ praviśhanti sarve
sa śhāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī

translation.simple: Just as rivers flow into the vast ocean, which remains ever full and calm, so too do desires enter the heart of a steady soul. Such a person finds true peace, not one who constantly chases after every desire.
translation.deep: Envision the boundless ocean, perpetually replenished by countless rivers, yet it maintains its unmoving, profound tranquility. Similarly, when desires arise in a mind that is steadfast and deeply rooted in its true nature, that mind remains undisturbed, much like the ocean unmoved by the waters entering it. Genuine serenity emerges not from the relentless pursuit of temporary wishes, but from cultivating an inner stillness that allows desires to pass without agitating the soul's deep calm.
translation.essence: May our hearts be like the tranquil ocean, receiving all of life's currents without losing our inner peace. True peace blossoms not from grasping desires, but from cultivating an unwavering calm within.

2-71.sanskrit:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः।

निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति।।2.71।।
2-71.transliteration:
vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumānśh charati niḥspṛihaḥ
nirmamo nirahankāraḥ sa śhāntim adhigachchhati

translation.simple: A soul who gently releases all worldly desires, lives without longing, and lets go of the feeling of 'I' and 'mine' – that soul finds true and lasting peace.
translation.deep: This sacred verse reveals the path to a profound inner stillness. It teaches that lasting peace emerges not from fulfilling every desire, but from gracefully letting go of them all. When we shed the burden of personal craving, release the grip of 'this is mine,' and dissolve the false 'I,' we uncover a boundless tranquility that resides eternally within the spirit.
translation.essence: True peace blossoms when we gently release all desires, shed the weight of possessiveness, and quiet the voice of ego, finding serene harmony within.

2-72.sanskrit:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।

स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति।।2.72।।
2-72.transliteration:
eṣhā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṁ prāpya vimuhyati
sthitvāsyām anta-kāle ’pi brahma-nirvāṇam ṛichchhati

translation.simple: This divine state, dear Arjuna, once attained, frees a soul from all confusion. Remaining firm in this wisdom, even as life's journey ends, one finds ultimate peace in the Divine.
translation.deep: This profound state, O Partha, is a dwelling in the Divine, a realization of the ultimate truth. When a soul attains this serene wisdom, the mists of delusion can no longer obscure its vision. To remain steadfast in this awareness, even through the final moments of earthly existence, is to merge into the boundless bliss of Brahman, finding complete liberation and eternal tranquility.
translation.essence: Attaining this divine consciousness liberates one from all illusion. Dwelling in it, even at life's end, leads to ultimate peace and union with the Divine.

3-1.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन।

तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव।।3.1।।
3-1.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
jyāyasī chet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana
tat kiṁ karmaṇi ghore māṁ niyojayasi keśhava

translation.simple: Arjuna asked, 'O Lord, if You truly believe that the path of wisdom is superior to the path of action, then why do You ask me to engage in such a terrible battle?'
translation.deep: Arjuna, filled with a sincere query, turns to Lord Krishna, his loving guide. He asks, 'O Janardana, if Your view is that spiritual understanding surpasses the performance of actions, why then do You direct me towards this intense and formidable undertaking of war, O Keshava?' His heart yearns for deeper insight into the divine plan.
translation.essence: Arjuna, in genuine confusion, asks Lord Krishna why he is being directed to a severe battle, given Krishna's earlier emphasis on the supremacy of wisdom over action. It's a heartfelt plea for spiritual clarity from the Divine.

3-2.sanskrit:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे।

तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम्।।3.2।।
3-2.transliteration:
vyāmiśhreṇeva vākyena buddhiṁ mohayasīva me
tad ekaṁ vada niśhchitya yena śhreyo ’ham āpnuyām

translation.simple: Your words, Lord, seem to mix things, and my mind feels a little confused. Please tell me one clear path, so I can truly achieve what is best for me.
translation.deep: O Krishna, Your divine instructions, though profound, at times appear to present different perspectives, creating a sense of bewilderment in my intellect. My earnest heart longs for You to reveal that one definitive way by which I may attain supreme and lasting spiritual welfare.
translation.essence: Feeling a gentle confusion from diverse teachings, Arjuna humbly asks Krishna to point out a single, clear path to his ultimate spiritual well-being.

3-3.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ।

ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम्।।3.3।।
3-3.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
loke’smin dvi-vidhā niṣhṭhā purā proktā mayānagha
jñāna-yogena sāṅkhyānāṁ karma-yogena yoginām

translation.simple: The Lord lovingly explains, 'My dear Arjuna, I have previously taught that in this world, souls journey along two main paths. For those who seek wisdom and understanding, the path is through sacred knowledge. For those inclined towards dedicated action, the path is through selfless service.' It's a gentle reminder that different natures find their way to the Divine.
translation.deep: In His divine discourse, the Blessed Lord clarifies the spiritual landscape for Arjuna, the pure-hearted one. He reveals that from time immemorial, two distinct yet equally potent spiritual disciplines have been set forth. For those blessed with a keen intellect and a thirst for ultimate truth, the path of discrimination and profound knowledge (Jnana Yoga) is the natural way. For those whose hearts resonate with service and dedicated effort in the world, the path of selfless action (Karma Yoga) is their sacred calling. Both are His gracious provisions for souls to evolve and attain Him.
translation.essence: The Lord's timeless teaching assures us that whether through deep contemplation and wisdom or through devoted, selfless action, there are sacred paths for every seeker. Both journeys, guided by His grace, lead to the same divine realization and inner peace.

3-4.sanskrit:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते।

न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति।।3.4।।
3-4.transliteration:
na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣhkarmyaṁ puruṣho ’śhnute
na cha sannyasanād eva siddhiṁ samadhigachchhati

translation.simple: My dear one, simply avoiding actions or outwardly giving things up won't bring true spiritual freedom. Real perfection isn't found just by renouncing the world without understanding.
translation.deep: True spiritual liberation, the state of profound inner peace beyond the sway of actions, is not attained merely by refraining from starting tasks. Nor is genuine perfection achieved simply by an external act of renunciation. The Lord teaches that it is the inner disposition, the spirit in which one acts or renounces, that truly matters for spiritual progress.
translation.essence: Genuine spiritual freedom and perfection come from an internal shift in consciousness, not simply from avoiding action or external renunciation. The path is subtle.

3-5.sanskrit:
न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्।

कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः।।3.5।।
3-5.transliteration:
na hi kaśhchit kṣhaṇam api jātu tiṣhṭhatyakarma-kṛit
kāryate hyavaśhaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛiti-jair guṇaiḥ

translation.simple: Dear one, know this truth: no one can ever stay truly inactive, not even for a moment. We are all gently guided to perform actions by the qualities that naturally arise from our very being.
translation.deep: Let us contemplate this profound wisdom: No soul can ever fully cease from activity, even for the briefest breath. For indeed, all beings are moved to act, as if by an unseen hand, by the inherent qualities (gunas) born of material nature. This constant impulsion reveals the divine dynamism within creation, showing that our very existence is a flow of engagement.
translation.essence: Action is an inherent part of our being, a constant dance guided by nature's qualities within us.

3-6.sanskrit:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्।

इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते।।3.6।।
3-6.transliteration:
karmendriyāṇi sanyamya ya āste manasā smaran
indriyārthān vimūḍhātmā mithyāchāraḥ sa uchyate

translation.simple: When we outwardly control our physical actions but our mind keeps dwelling on worldly desires, such a person is considered to be misguided. This path isn't genuine spiritual purity.
translation.deep: This sacred verse gently guides us, revealing that true spiritual discipline extends beyond mere external restraint. If our bodily actions are held back, yet our inner thoughts are constantly captivated by the objects of the senses, we remain entangled in delusion. Such an individual, though perhaps appearing disciplined, possesses a deluded heart because their inner state contradicts their outer conduct. True devotion blossoms when our mind, speech, and actions are harmoniously aligned.
translation.essence: The Lord's wisdom here reminds us that authentic self-control arises from a pure heart, not just outward suppression. It's crucial for our minds to turn away from sense attachments even as our bodies remain still, fostering true inner peace and spiritual growth.

3-7.sanskrit:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन।

कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते।।3.7।।
3-7.transliteration:
yas tvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate ’rjuna
karmendriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ sa viśhiṣhyate

translation.simple: O Arjuna, one who gently guides their senses with a peaceful mind, and then uses their physical body to perform duties without any desire for the results, is truly distinguished.
translation.deep: This profound verse teaches us that true spiritual progress isn't about mere outward restraint. Instead, it's about cultivating inner mastery by guiding our senses with a focused and serene mind. When we then engage our faculties in performing our work, dedicating our efforts without attachment to personal gain, we embody the essence of Karma Yoga. This path of selfless action, rooted in inner control, elevates us to a state of superior understanding and devotion.
translation.essence: True wisdom blossoms when we calm our senses with the mind and then act selflessly, unburdened by the fruits of our labor. This path of devoted action makes us truly excel.

3-8.sanskrit:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः।

शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः।।3.8।।
3-8.transliteration:
niyataṁ kuru karma tvaṁ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ
śharīra-yātrāpi cha te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ

translation.simple: My dear one, always engage in your natural duties. For acting is far better than not acting at all. Indeed, without any effort, even your very body cannot be maintained.
translation.deep: This verse lovingly reminds us that purposeful action is not just a worldly necessity, but a spiritual practice. To act in line with our dharma, with a serene heart, is superior to idleness. Even our physical being, a sacred vessel, relies on our engagement. Through such dedicated effort, we align ourselves with the divine will and progress on our spiritual journey.
translation.essence: Act with purpose and devotion; for righteous action surpasses inaction, even for sustaining life itself. It's the path of progress and spiritual alignment.

3-9.sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः।

तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर।।3.9।।
3-9.transliteration:
yajñārthāt karmaṇo ’nyatra loko ’yaṁ karma-bandhanaḥ
tad-arthaṁ karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgaḥ samāchara

translation.simple: When we act only for personal gain, our actions can create burdens. But if we offer our work to a higher purpose, without expecting specific results, our actions become a path to freedom. So, dear heart, do your part with a devotional spirit, letting go of attachment to what comes next.
translation.deep: The Bhagavad Gita gently reminds us that actions driven purely by personal desires or the longing for outcomes can deeply bind us to this earthly existence. Yet, there is a sacred way to act: to dedicate all our efforts as a 'Yajna,' a selfless offering to the Divine. By embracing this perspective, performing our duties without clinging to their fruits, we transcend the cycles of karma. It is a profound call, O Seeker, to engage in the world with a heart unattached, finding true joy in the pure act of service itself, rather than in its perceived rewards.
translation.essence: Actions for self-desire create bonds; actions offered to the Divine bring freedom. Perform your duties with detachment and a loving heart.

3-10.sanskrit:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः।

अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक्।।3.10।।
3-10.transliteration:
saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛiṣhṭvā purovācha prajāpatiḥ
anena prasaviṣhyadhvam eṣha vo ’stviṣhṭa-kāma-dhuk

translation.simple: When the Creator brought forth all beings long ago, He also established the sacred path of selfless offering, or yajña. He lovingly declared that through this divine practice, all beings would prosper and find their pure desires fulfilled.
translation.deep: This profound verse reveals that from the very beginning of creation, the Lord of all beings, Prajapati, endowed humanity with the sacred principle of 'yajña' – actions performed with a spirit of devotion and giving. He assured that by engaging in such selfless endeavors, one would not only experience flourishing prosperity in life but also attain the fulfillment of all noble aspirations, truly connecting with the divine flow.
translation.essence: The Creator gifted us the path of 'yajña' – selfless action and devotion – as the divine key to unlock prosperity, spiritual well-being, and the fulfillment of all pure desires.

3-11.sanskrit:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः।

परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ।।3.11।।
3-11.transliteration:
devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ
parasparaṁ bhāvayantaḥ śhreyaḥ param avāpsyatha

translation.simple: Honor the divine with your sincere efforts, and the divine will bless you in return. By nurturing this sacred bond of mutual support, you will surely attain the highest well-being.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully reveals the cosmic dance of mutual nourishment. When we, through our righteous deeds and heartfelt devotion, sustain the divine principle that governs the universe, we activate a sacred reciprocity. The divine, in turn, provides for our welfare and spiritual growth. It's a profound teaching about understanding our place in the grand tapestry of existence, where every selfless act contributes to universal harmony and leads us to supreme spiritual benefit.
translation.essence: Honor the divine with your actions, and the divine will honor you. This sacred cycle of mutual nourishment leads to the highest welfare for all.

3-12.sanskrit:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।

तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः।।3.12।।
3-12.transliteration:
iṣhṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ
tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ

translation.simple: The loving divine forces, nourished by our humble offerings and selfless deeds, bless us with all the good things we desire. If we simply take and enjoy these gifts without offering gratitude or sharing, it is truly like taking what isn't rightfully ours alone, akin to a spiritual oversight.
translation.deep: This sacred verse reveals the cosmic principle of reciprocity. The 'devas,' representing the various aspects of the divine and natural forces, are nourished by our 'yajnas' – not just rituals, but acts of selfless service, gratitude, and mindful offering. In turn, they grant us all the sustenance and joy we experience. To partake of these blessings purely for oneself, without acknowledging their source or sharing with others, creates an imbalance. This isn't merely a social failing; it's a spiritual oversight, a form of 'theft' from the universal treasury, for it disregards the interconnectedness and mutual dependence that sustains all creation.
translation.essence: All blessings flow from the divine. To enjoy them selfishly, without gratitude or giving back, is a spiritual misalignment, akin to taking without offering.

3-13.sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः।

भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्।।3.13।।
3-13.transliteration:
yajña-śhiṣhṭāśhinaḥ santo muchyante sarva-kilbiṣhaiḥ
bhuñjate te tvaghaṁ pāpā ye pachantyātma-kāraṇāt

translation.simple: Those pure souls who partake of what remains after offering their efforts and resources in selfless service are freed from all misdeeds. But those who act solely for their own benefit, they truly consume the fruits of their own mistakes.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully reminds us that every action, especially how we sustain ourselves, carries spiritual weight. When we consecrate our efforts and sustenance to a higher purpose, to the Divine or for the welfare of others, we transcend the bindings of karma. Our actions become pure offerings, and we are cleansed of all imperfections. Conversely, when life's activities, even the most basic act of eating, are driven purely by selfish desire and personal gain, they create spiritual burdens, leading one to partake in the very essence of sin.
translation.essence: When we offer our endeavors and sustenance with a heart of service, we are divinely cleansed. But if we act only for ourselves, we partake of our own impurities.

3-14.sanskrit:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।

यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः।।3.14।।
3-14.transliteration:
annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād anna-sambhavaḥ
yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ

translation.simple: From the food we eat, all living beings come forth. This precious food comes from the rain. The rain, in turn, manifests from sincere, sacred offerings and actions. And these sacred actions arise from our dedicated efforts.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully reveals the divine tapestry of existence, showing how all life is interconnected. Our very sustenance, coming from food and rain, is part of a sacred cycle. The 'yajna' mentioned here points beyond mere rituals to any sincere, selfless action or offering made for the greater good. Such devoted actions, born of pure intent, invoke the very forces that sustain life, emphasizing our role in upholding this sacred harmony through our karma, or selfless work.
translation.essence: Life's cycle is deeply intertwined with our actions. Selfless deeds (karma) lead to sacred offerings (yajna), which bring forth rain, providing food and sustaining all beings. It's a gentle reminder of our responsibility to act with a spirit of giving, recognizing the divine interdependence that nourishes all creation.

3-15.sanskrit:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्।

तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्।।3.15।।
3-15.transliteration:
karma brahmodbhavaṁ viddhi brahmākṣhara-samudbhavam
tasmāt sarva-gataṁ brahma nityaṁ yajñe pratiṣhṭhitam

translation.simple: Understand that all our actions flow from the Divine, and this Divine source itself springs from the Eternal, Imperishable Truth. Therefore, this all-pervading Divine presence is forever rooted in every act of selfless offering.
translation.deep: This profound verse unveils the sacred chain of existence: all activity (karma) is born from the Supreme Spirit (Brahman), and this Brahman itself arises from the Imperishable, changeless Reality (Akshara). It illuminates the cosmic order where the divine energy permeates all. Hence, this all-pervading divine presence, the very essence of Brahman, is eternally upheld and made manifest in every selfless deed, every act of 'yajna' performed with devotion.
translation.essence: Our every action is divinely rooted, connected to the Eternal. This omnipresent Divine power is lovingly established in all selfless service, waiting to be realized.

3-16.sanskrit:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः।

अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति।।3.16।।
3-16.transliteration:
evaṁ pravartitaṁ chakraṁ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ
aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṁ pārtha sa jīvati

translation.simple: Dear soul, if one does not participate in the sacred cycle of giving and receiving, which sustains all life, and instead lives only for the fleeting pleasures of the senses, their journey on earth becomes directionless and unfulfilled.
translation.deep: The Lord has set in motion a beautiful cosmic dance, a cycle of selfless giving and mutual sustenance. When a soul turns away from this divine flow, focusing solely on personal gratification through the senses, their life misses its deeper purpose.
