Such a life, though seemingly lived, fails to connect with the source of true joy and fulfillment, leading to a hollow existence, O Arjuna.
translation.essence: To ignore the divine rhythm of selfless contribution and live merely for sensory delights is to miss life's true spiritual aim, rendering one's precious human birth in vain.

3-17.sanskrit:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः।

आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते।।3.17।।
3-17.transliteration:
yas tvātma-ratir eva syād ātma-tṛiptaśh cha mānavaḥ
ātmanyeva cha santuṣhṭas tasya kāryaṁ na vidyate

translation.simple: When a person truly finds their delight and contentment within their own spiritual Self, always feeling satisfied by that inner connection, then for such a one, the need for worldly duties no longer truly binds them.
translation.deep: This profound verse speaks of a sacred state where the soul's deepest joy and satisfaction are found not in external pursuits or material gains, but solely within the divine essence of the Self (Ātman). When a devotee cultivates such an intimate relationship with their inner spirit, feeling completely nourished and content in that holy space, the ordinary demands and obligations of the world gradually lose their power. It signifies a profound spiritual liberation, where inner peace becomes the guiding principle, freeing one from the endless cycle of action driven by external desires.
translation.essence: Finding ultimate joy and contentment within your own spiritual Self brings true freedom from worldly obligations.

3-18.sanskrit:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन।

न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः।।3.18।।
3-18.transliteration:
naiva tasya kṛitenārtho nākṛiteneha kaśhchana
na chāsya sarva-bhūteṣhu kaśhchid artha-vyapāśhrayaḥ

translation.simple: For one whose heart is truly connected to the Divine, there's no personal gain in what they do, nor any loss in what they don't. Their peace and fulfillment are not dependent on actions or their outcomes in this world.
translation.deep: A soul deeply immersed in the joy of the Self transcends the push and pull of material motivations. Their actions are not driven by a desire for benefit, nor do their inactions cause them distress. Free from all dependency on other beings or worldly outcomes, their satisfaction springs solely from their profound connection to the Divine within.
translation.essence: The enlightened soul is utterly free and self-sufficient; their joy is from within, untouched by deeds or non-deeds, and they depend on no external factor or being for their peace.

3-19.sanskrit:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।

असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः।।3.19।।
3-19.transliteration:
tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samāchara
asakto hyācharan karma param āpnoti pūruṣhaḥ

translation.simple: Always perform your duties, dear one, without attachment to the outcome. When you act without being tied to the results, you will surely attain the highest good.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to understand that our true spiritual ascent comes from fulfilling our responsibilities with a heart free from personal desires for the results. It's an invitation to offer our efforts as a sacred dedication, liberating us from the anxieties of success or failure. In this state of unattached action, our consciousness naturally expands, allowing us to experience the presence of the Supreme within and all around us, leading to ultimate peace and unity.
translation.essence: Perform your duties without attachment, and you will surely attain the highest spiritual reality.

3-20.sanskrit:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः।

लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि।।3.20।।
3-20.transliteration:
karmaṇaiva hi sansiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ
loka-saṅgraham evāpi sampaśhyan kartum arhasi

translation.simple: Great souls like King Janaka found perfect peace through their dedicated actions. You too should perform your duties, always considering the welfare and harmony of the world around you.
translation.deep: This verse teaches us that true spiritual realization is not found in renouncing activity, but in performing it with pure intention. By engaging in our responsibilities with a heart full of care for the collective well-being, our actions become a path to inner freedom and divine connection, just as they did for enlightened rulers of the past.
translation.essence: Act with purpose and for the good of all, understanding that such selfless service is a direct path to spiritual perfection.

3-21.sanskrit:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः।

स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते।।3.21।।
3-21.transliteration:
yad yad ācharati śhreṣhṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate

translation.simple: When a respected soul performs an action, others tend to follow their lead. The example they set becomes a path for the world to walk.
translation.deep: This sacred teaching illuminates the profound influence a sincere soul holds. Every action, every decision by one who is revered, creates a ripple that shapes the collective path. It is a gentle reminder to live with purity and purpose, knowing that our choices become beacons, guiding others towards goodness and divine truth.
translation.essence: A revered soul's conduct sets the standard; their example becomes the world's path. Let our lives be a gentle guide.

3-22.sanskrit:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन।

नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि।।3.22।।
3-22.transliteration:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṁ triṣhu lokeṣhu kiñchana
nānavāptam avāptavyaṁ varta eva cha karmaṇi

translation.simple: Lord Krishna tenderly reminds Arjuna, 'My dear Partha, in all the creation, there is no duty I am compelled to perform. Nothing remains for Me to achieve or acquire. Yet, I am constantly engaged in My divine work.'
translation.deep: This verse reveals a profound truth about the Divine. Though Lord Krishna is the supreme controller, perfectly complete and wanting for nothing in all existence, He continuously engages in activity. This is not for His personal gain, but out of His infinite compassion and wisdom. His actions uphold the cosmic order, guide humanity, and demonstrate the path of selfless duty for the welfare of all beings, showing that true action springs from love, not from attachment to results.
translation.essence: The Lord's actions are a timeless lesson: though self-sufficient, He acts purely for the world's good, inspiring us to perform our duties with selfless love and devotion, free from personal expectation.

3-23.sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।

मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।3.23।।
3-23.transliteration:
yadi hyahaṁ na varteyaṁ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣhyāḥ pārtha sarvaśhaḥ

translation.simple: Lord Krishna tells Arjuna, "My dear Partha, if I, the Supreme Lord, were to ever stop performing My duties with diligence and focus, then all mankind would naturally follow My example and cease their own actions."
translation.deep: This verse beautifully reveals the profound principle of divine leadership. The Lord, though in no need of action, continuously performs His duties with utmost diligence to maintain the cosmic order and to set an impeccable standard for all. If the Supreme Being were to ever waver or cease action, it would create a ripple effect, causing all of humanity to lose their sense of duty and purpose, leading to imbalance and chaos. It underscores that true leadership is demonstrated through selfless, tireless action, guiding the world by personal conduct rather than by mere decree.
translation.essence: The Lord, by His own tireless work, sets the perfect example for all of creation. He lovingly reminds us that performing our duties with dedication and sincerity not only enriches our own spiritual path but also guides and inspires others, contributing to the divine harmony of the world.

3-24.sanskrit:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्।

सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः।।3.24।।
3-24.transliteration:
utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṁ karma ched aham
sankarasya cha kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ

translation.simple: My dear one, even I, the Lord of all, remain ever engaged in My divine duties. If I were to ever cease My actions, these very worlds would surely crumble into disorder. I would then become the source of confusion, and all beings would face ruin.
translation.deep: Here, the Lord lovingly reveals a profound truth about His own divine nature. He, the Supreme Sustainer, performs His cosmic duties without fail to maintain the perfect harmony of all worlds. He explains that if He were to ever withdraw from His actions, the very fabric of existence would unravel, leading to widespread chaos and the suffering of all souls. This teaches us the immense importance of purposeful, righteous action, not just for ourselves, but for the greater good of all creation, following the divine example.
translation.essence: The Lord's continuous, selfless action is the very foundation of cosmic order. This verse lovingly reminds us that our own actions, when performed with devotion and purpose, contribute to the harmony and well-being of all beings, mirroring the divine will.

3-25.transliteration:
saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvānso yathā kurvanti bhārata
kuryād vidvāns tathāsaktaśh chikīrṣhur loka-saṅgraham

translation.simple: O Arjuna, just as ordinary people act with attachment to their tasks, a wise person should also act. But they perform their duties without any attachment, always for the good and welfare of all people in the world.
translation.deep: O Arjuna, observe how those who are still learning often perform their actions with deep attachment to the outcomes. A truly wise soul, however, also engages in all necessary duties, yet remains perfectly unattached to the results. Their every effort is born of a desire for the harmony and spiritual upliftment of the world, setting a beautiful, selfless example for others to follow.
translation.essence: Act with diligence, not for personal gain, but purely for the welfare of all. Let your selfless deeds inspire and guide the world.

3-26.sanskrit:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्।

जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन्।।3.26।।
3-26.transliteration:
na buddhi-bhedaṁ janayed ajñānāṁ karma-saṅginām
joṣhayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācharan

translation.simple: A wise soul does not disturb the understanding of those who are devoted to their worldly duties. Instead, the wise one, deeply absorbed in spiritual insight, beautifully performs all actions, inspiring others through their own example.
translation.deep: This verse gently teaches the compassionate approach of a truly enlightened individual. Knowing that some hearts are still finding their way through the world of action, the wise person refrains from imposing complex spiritual truths that might cause distress or confusion. Instead, they become a living embodiment of dedicated action, free from attachment. By diligently fulfilling their own responsibilities with inner peace and devotion, they subtly demonstrate how every task can become a sacred offering, guiding others not through words, but through the silent, powerful language of their own serene conduct.
translation.essence: The heart of this teaching is about leading with wisdom and kindness. A spiritually advanced soul inspires others not by creating doubt or disruption, but by radiating devotion and peaceful dedication in their own life, showing how every action can be a path to the divine.

3-27.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः।

अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते।।3.27।।
3-27.transliteration:
prakṛiteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśhaḥ
ahankāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate

translation.simple: Friend, all deeds are naturally performed by the subtle forces of creation. Yet, a soul, covered by a veil of ego, often believes, 'I am the one who does this work.'
translation.deep: This verse offers a profound insight: all actions in the world are brought about by the subtle interplay of nature's qualities. When our inner self becomes clouded by the ego, we mistakenly assume 'I' am the sole actor. This deep wisdom invites us to look beyond our personal sense of doership and recognize the larger divine orchestration at play, fostering humility and surrender.
translation.essence: The true essence lies in understanding that we are instruments in a grand divine dance. By letting go of the ego's claim 'I am the doer,' we unlock a profound sense of inner peace and freedom, surrendering to the natural flow of life guided by a higher power.

3-28.sanskrit:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः।

गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते।।3.28।।
3-28.transliteration:
tattva-vit tu mahā-bāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ
guṇā guṇeṣhu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate

translation.simple: O Arjuna, the one who truly knows understands that all actions spring from the interplay of nature's qualities. Realizing that these qualities are simply moving among themselves, such a person does not become entangled.
translation.deep: O mighty Arjuna, a soul touched by divine insight deeply comprehends the unique nature of qualities and their actions. This understanding reveals that the qualities of material nature inherently operate within themselves. With this profound realization, one finds a serene release from attachment, resting in inner peace.
translation.essence: When one truly perceives that all actions are but the dance of nature's qualities, a natural detachment blossoms, leading to inner tranquility.

3-29.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु।

तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत्।।3.29।।
3-29.transliteration:
prakṛiter guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu
tān akṛitsna-vido mandān kṛitsna-vin na vichālayet

translation.simple: Hearts that are captivated by the world's natural qualities often become deeply attached to the actions that arise from them. A truly wise soul, one who sees the complete truth, gently chooses not to disturb those who are still learning and finding their spiritual path.
translation.deep: This verse reveals the compassionate understanding of the enlightened. Many souls, deeply immersed in the three qualities of material nature – sattva, rajas, and tamas – mistakenly identify with the actions performed under their influence, feeling attachment and ownership. A spiritually awakened being, however, comprehends the true nature of the self as distinct from these material workings. Recognizing the varying stages of spiritual progress, such a wise individual extends grace by not agitating or confusing those who are not yet ready to grasp the full, profound truth. They allow each soul to evolve gently, without unnecessary mental or emotional disturbance.
translation.essence: Understand the allure of material qualities, cultivate non-attachment, and show gentle compassion to all, respecting their unique journey of awakening.

3-30.sanskrit:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा।

निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः।।3.30।।
3-30.transliteration:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi sannyasyādhyātma-chetasā
nirāśhīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ

translation.simple: Offer all your actions to Me, fixing your mind on the Divine. Let go of desires for results and the feeling of 'mine.' Then, perform your duties peacefully, free from all worry.
translation.deep: Entrust all your endeavors to the Divine, aligning your consciousness with the Supreme Spirit within. Release the attachments to outcomes and the sense of personal ownership over your efforts. When you act from this profound space of surrender, you engage in your responsibilities with a calm heart, untouched by anxiety or agitation.
translation.essence: Act for the Divine, without attachment to results or ownership, and find peace in your duties.

3-31.sanskrit:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः।

श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः।।3.31।।
3-31.transliteration:
ye me matam idaṁ nityam anutiṣhṭhanti mānavāḥ
śhraddhāvanto ’nasūyanto muchyante te ’pi karmabhiḥ

translation.simple: Those who lovingly follow My path, with sincere faith and no ill-will in their hearts, find themselves freed from the burdens of their past actions.
translation.deep: This sacred verse lovingly assures us that liberation from the cycles of action and reaction is not reserved for a select few. It is granted to all who sincerely follow the divine wisdom, holding steadfast faith and a heart purified of fault-finding. Through such devotion, their actions, though performed, cease to bind them, gently leading them towards true spiritual release.
translation.essence: Embrace divine guidance with unwavering faith and a heart free from envy to transcend the bonds of karma.

3-32.sanskrit:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम्।

सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः।।3.32।।
3-32.transliteration:
ye tvetad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣhṭhanti me matam
sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhāns tān viddhi naṣhṭān achetasaḥ

translation.simple: Those who look upon these teachings with a critical eye and choose not to follow My path, understand that they are veiled by ignorance, their hearts missing the light of wisdom, and their journey truly adrift.
translation.deep: Consider those who, through a critical gaze or a closed heart, turn away from the path I offer. Though they may possess other forms of knowledge, their minds are bewildered by a deeper ignorance. They miss the true essence of spiritual wisdom, becoming lost within themselves, their discernment clouded, and their inner journey veering off course.
translation.essence: When one dismisses divine guidance due to skepticism or a closed heart, the mind becomes deeply bewildered, losing its way on the path to true wisdom and peace.

3-33.sanskrit:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि।

प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति।।3.33।।
3-33.transliteration:
sadṛiśhaṁ cheṣhṭate svasyāḥ prakṛiter jñānavān api
prakṛitiṁ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṁ kariṣhyati

translation.simple: Even a wise soul acts in harmony with their own nature. All beings are drawn by their inborn tendencies. What can simple forceful restraint truly accomplish?
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that our inherent nature, *prakriti*, is a powerful force that guides all beings, even those with wisdom. It suggests that simply trying to suppress our inclinations through sheer willpower might not lead to lasting transformation. True spiritual growth often involves a deeper understanding of our own nature, and then, with divine grace, gently guiding it towards higher virtues rather than fighting it directly. We are invited to observe our inner workings with compassion, seeking to transcend our lower nature by cultivating a higher, divine one.
translation.essence: Our inborn nature shapes our actions. True transformation comes not from forceful suppression, but from inner understanding and a gentle alignment with the divine.

3-34.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ।

तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ।।3.34।।
3-34.transliteration:
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāga-dveṣhau vyavasthitau
tayor na vaśham āgachchhet tau hyasya paripanthinau

translation.simple: When our senses engage with the world, feelings of liking and disliking naturally arise. It is important not to let these feelings control us, as they can become obstacles to our inner peace.
translation.deep: Every encounter of our senses with objects of perception gives birth to either attraction or repulsion. A deeper understanding reveals that yielding to these twin impulses can distract us from our spiritual journey, clouding our judgment and disturbing our inner calm. True wisdom lies in gently observing them without allowing them to dictate our actions or disturb our connection to the divine.
translation.essence: Be aware of the natural pull of liking and disliking, but never let them take over. They are potential hindrances to your spiritual progress and inner tranquility.

3-35.sanskrit:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।

स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः।।3.35।।
3-35.transliteration:
śhreyān swa-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣhṭhitāt
swa-dharme nidhanaṁ śhreyaḥ para-dharmo bhayāvahaḥ

translation.simple: It is always better to follow your own path, even if it feels imperfect, than to perfectly walk someone else's. Finding peace in your own true nature, even unto the very end, is far better, for another's path can bring only fear and unease.
translation.deep: This profound verse gently guides us to honor our unique journey. Your 'svadharma' is not just an external duty but the sacred path aligned with your deepest self, your inherent nature and divine purpose. Even if your efforts seem flawed in the eyes of the world, pursuing your authentic calling brings a profound peace that surpasses any worldly success found on another's path. To abandon your true self for an imitation, no matter how appealing, invites disquiet and spiritual confusion. Embrace your unique unfolding; it is where your soul truly belongs and finds ultimate solace.
translation.essence: Embrace your unique, God-given path. It brings inner peace, even with imperfections. Following another's path, however alluring, only leads to fear and spiritual disquiet.

3-36.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः।

अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः।।3.36।।
3-36.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
atha kena prayukto ’yaṁ pāpaṁ charati pūruṣhaḥ
anichchhann api vārṣhṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ

translation.simple: Arjuna asks Lord Krishna, 'My dear Lord, what is it that compels a person to act wrongly, even when their heart truly wishes not to? It feels as if some unseen force pushes them against their own will.'
translation.deep: Arjuna here voices a fundamental human dilemma, seeking to understand the mysterious inner drive that propels individuals towards actions they later regret, despite their conscious desire for virtue. He contemplates the nature of this hidden compulsion, that seems to override one's own good intentions, leading to sorrow. It’s a poignant question about the subtle influences within us that challenge our spiritual resolve.
translation.essence: This verse captures the human predicament of acting against one's better judgment, asking about the unseen force that compels us to stray from our true, pure nature. It's a humble quest for insight into our inner struggles.

3-37.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः।

महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम्।।3.37।।
3-37.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
kāma eṣha krodha eṣha rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ
mahāśhano mahā-pāpmā viddhyenam iha vairiṇam

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord gently reveals that intense desires and fierce anger arise from our active, passionate nature. These are like hungry flames that consume our peace and lead to regrettable actions. Understand them as the true inner enemies we face.
translation.deep: The Divine wisdom shines light upon the internal struggles we face. It tells us that what we perceive as mere desires and moments of anger are actually profound forces, born from the restless quality of passion within us. These forces are insatiable, constantly demanding more, and when unchecked, they lead us down paths of unrighteousness and deep regret. Knowing them as our primary inner adversaries is a crucial insight for anyone seeking a peaceful and devotional life, guiding us to guard our hearts.
translation.essence: Desire and anger, born of passion, are our most formidable inner foes. They consume our peace and drive us to unrighteousness. Recognize them as such to walk the path of spiritual tranquility.

3-38.sanskrit:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च।

यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम्।।3.38।।
3-38.transliteration:
dhūmenāvriyate vahnir yathādarśho malena cha
yatholbenāvṛito garbhas tathā tenedam āvṛitam

translation.simple: Just as gentle smoke can veil a bright flame, or a fine layer of dust can obscure a clear mirror, and a precious seed of life rests hidden within its covering, so too is our pure awareness veiled by the arising of desire.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that our true spiritual insight, though always present, can be obscured. Like the natural way smoke covers fire or dust dims a mirror's shine, strong desires have a similar power to cloud our perception, making it hard to see the divine truth within and around us. It's a call to recognize how subtly our inner light can be veiled by worldly longings.
translation.essence: Our pure, inner wisdom is naturally veiled by desire, much like a bright flame by smoke, a clear mirror by dust, or a tender embryo within its sacred covering. This verse gently reveals how our true perception can be obscured by worldly longings.

3-39.sanskrit:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा।

कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च।।3.39।।
3-39.transliteration:
āvṛitaṁ jñānam etena jñānino nitya-vairiṇā
kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣhpūreṇānalena cha

translation.simple: O Arjuna, our inner wisdom, the clear light of knowledge, often gets covered. This covering comes from our eternal adversary: desire. Like a fire that can never truly be quenched, desire is insatiable and always seeking more.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that our profound inner knowing, the very essence of spiritual wisdom, can be overshadowed. The culprit, O Arjuna, is desire, which acts as a constant opponent to those seeking genuine understanding. Imagine a fire, always consuming yet never satisfied; such is the nature of desire. It relentlessly seeks fulfillment in external things, and in this endless pursuit, it veils the clarity of our inner wisdom, keeping us from our true spiritual path.
translation.essence: Our sacred wisdom is veiled by relentless desire, an unquenchable fire within. May we recognize this truth and seek to uncover our inner light.

3-40.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते।

एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम्।।3.40।।
3-40.transliteration:
indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣhṭhānam uchyate
etair vimohayatyeṣha jñānam āvṛitya dehinam

translation.simple: Our desires often reside within our senses, mind, and intellect. From these internal spaces, they can subtly delude us, gently covering the true understanding of our inner self.
translation.deep: This sacred verse illuminates how desires intricately weave themselves into the very fabric of our being – our powers of perception, our thoughts, and our capacity for reason. From these deeply personal dwelling places, desire subtly casts a veil, dimming the inherent spiritual knowledge that resides within the embodied soul. This process, when unchecked, can lead to a profound sense of confusion regarding our true nature and purpose, gently guiding us away from inner clarity.
translation.essence: Desire takes root in our senses, mind, and intellect, and from there, it gently obscures our innate wisdom, causing the soul to feel perplexed.

3-41.sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ।

पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम्।।3.41।।
3-41.transliteration:
tasmāt tvam indriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣhabha
pāpmānaṁ prajahi hyenaṁ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśhanam

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, the path to inner peace begins with a gentle discipline. First, bring your senses under your calm control. With this steadiness, you can then lovingly overcome that which seeks to cloud your wisdom and clear spiritual sight.
translation.deep: Beloved soul, understand the profound wisdom shared here: to truly progress on your spiritual journey, you must first tenderly guide your senses. For within these senses often stirs a powerful desire that, left unchecked, acts as a veil, obscuring not only your intellectual understanding (jnana) but also your intuitive spiritual realization (vijnana). By patiently mastering your senses, you dismantle this inner obstacle, allowing your spiritual insight to blossom forth.
translation.essence: First, with loving care, bring your senses into gentle control. This empowers you to conquer desires that dim your spiritual wisdom and hinder your awakening.

3-42.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः।

मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः।।3.42।।
3-42.transliteration:
indriyāṇi parāṇyāhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṁ manaḥ
manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ

translation.simple: They say our senses are powerful, guiding our experience of the world. Yet, our mind holds a higher sway, influencing these senses. Superior to the mind is our intellect or wisdom, which offers discernment. And beyond all these—senses, mind, and intellect—resides the true Spirit within us, our innermost Self, which is supreme.
translation.deep: This verse tenderly illuminates the inner architecture of our being, guiding us on a path of self-discovery. We begin with the senses, ever-responsive to the outer world, but it is the mind that processes and often directs their flow. Deeper still is the faculty of our intellect, or Buddhi, which brings wisdom, clarity, and the capacity for right understanding and decision-making. However, the ultimate truth revealed is that beyond all these layers, beyond thought and perception, resides the transcendent Self, the eternal spirit, the divine essence within us. Understanding this gentle hierarchy helps us to lovingly turn our awareness inward, recognizing that true peace and sovereignty lie not in the external or even in our thoughts, but in the tranquil abode of the Self.
translation.essence: From the compelling allure of the senses, through the thoughts of the mind, and up to the wisdom of the intellect, there is a beautiful hierarchy within. But beyond them all, silent and eternal, dwells the supreme Spirit—our true Self. It's a gentle invitation to journey inward, transcending the temporary, to connect with that 'He' within, the ultimate source of peace and light.

3-43.sanskrit:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना।

जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम्।।3.43।।
3-43.transliteration:
evaṁ buddheḥ paraṁ buddhvā sanstabhyātmānam ātmanā
jahi śhatruṁ mahā-bāho kāma-rūpaṁ durāsadam

translation.simple: Realize the wisdom that is higher than your mind's thoughts. Steady your inner self through your own spirit. With this strength, dear one, conquer the formidable enemy of desire, which can be so hard to face.
translation.deep: When you truly know that profound wisdom which surpasses all intellectual understanding, and with your spirit, you steady your very being, then you gain the power. O mighty soul, this is how you conquer that deep-seated enemy: desire, which takes on many forms and is so challenging to overcome. It is a call to awaken your inner strength.
translation.essence: Awaken to the wisdom beyond thought, steady your inner being, and with your inherent strength, conquer desire's pull.

4-1.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम्।

विवस्वान् मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत्।।4.1।।
4-1.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
imaṁ vivasvate yogaṁ proktavān aham avyayam
vivasvān manave prāha manur ikṣhvākave ’bravīt

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord lovingly shared, 'This eternal wisdom of yoga, I first revealed to Vivasvan, the Sun-god. Vivasvan then imparted it to Manu, and Manu, in turn, taught it to King Ikshvaku.'
translation.deep: Lord Krishna tenderly reminds us that this divine path of yoga, which is eternal and unchanging, has a sacred history. He Himself, as the Supreme Being, first revealed this profound wisdom to Vivasvan, the Sun-god. From Vivasvan, it flowed to Manu, the father of mankind, and then to Ikshvaku, the revered ancestor of great kings. This lineage assures us that the spiritual truth is pure, sacred, and has been carefully preserved through time, always originating from the Divine source.
translation.essence: This timeless spiritual wisdom, the yoga, originated from the Lord Himself. It has been lovingly passed down through a sacred lineage, ensuring its purity and eternal relevance for all seekers.

4-2.sanskrit:
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः।

स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप।।4.2।।
4-2.transliteration:
evaṁ paramparā-prāptam imaṁ rājarṣhayo viduḥ
sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣhṭaḥ parantapa

translation.simple: This sacred wisdom, received through an unbroken chain of teachers, was known by saintly kings. But with the great passage of time, O Arjuna, that profound yoga was lost here in this world.
translation.deep: This profound spiritual path, which came down through a sacred lineage, was once understood by great saintly kings. Yet, as time stretched into ages, this divine knowledge, this yoga, slowly became obscured and seemingly lost to humanity. It highlights the fleeting nature of human memory and the need for divine intervention to rekindle such truth.
translation.essence: Even the most profound spiritual wisdom, when entrusted to human hands, can fade with the relentless march of time. This verse subtly hints at the Lord's compassion in re-establishing this lost truth, reminding us that divine knowledge is ever-present, though sometimes momentarily obscured.

4-3.sanskrit:
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः।

भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम्।।4.3।।
4-3.transliteration:
sa evāyaṁ mayā te ’dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ
bhakto ’si me sakhā cheti rahasyaṁ hyetad uttamam

translation.simple: Lord Krishna tells Arjuna, 'This ancient path of yoga, I am sharing with you today. I do this because you are My devoted one and My dear friend. This sacred truth is indeed most profound.'
translation.deep: In this verse, Lord Krishna lovingly reveals to Arjuna the very same eternal wisdom, the path of divine union, that has always existed. He bestows this profound knowledge specifically upon Arjuna, highlighting the special relationship of a devotee and a cherished friend, for such a sacred bond is the key to receiving this supreme spiritual secret.
translation.essence: This verse beautifully illustrates the intimate connection between the Divine and the earnest seeker. It teaches that the most profound spiritual wisdom, though ancient and eternal, is revealed personally and confidentially by the Lord to those who approach Him with devotion and genuine friendship, making the teaching a blessing rather than a mere instruction.

4-4.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः।

कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति।।4.4।।
4-4.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
aparaṁ bhavato janma paraṁ janma vivasvataḥ
katham etad vijānīyāṁ tvam ādau proktavān iti

translation.simple: Arjuna, in his heartfelt confusion, asked, "Your birth, dear Krishna, seems so recent. Yet, You speak of teaching this ancient wisdom to Vivasvān, the Sun-god, long before. How am I to understand this profound statement?"
translation.deep: Arjuna's loving inquiry highlights the natural human difficulty in comprehending the divine. He knew Krishna as his contemporary, born in recent memory, yet the Lord claimed to be the original teacher of timeless knowledge to the ancient Sun-god. This sincere bewilderment from Arjuna serves as a perfect prelude for Krishna to unveil His eternal, unborn nature, which transcends the conventional understanding of birth and time.
translation.essence: Arjuna, with humble perplexity, questioned how his friend, Krishna, whose birth was recent, could have been the ancient instructor of the Sun-god. This sincere doubt prepares the ground for understanding the Lord's transcendent and timeless divine existence.

4-5.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन।

तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप।।4.5।।
4-5.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava chārjuna
tānyahaṁ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṁ vettha parantapa

translation.simple: Lord Krishna gently revealed: 'Arjuna, both you and I have journeyed through many, many lives. I remember each one perfectly, but you, O valiant one, do not recall them.'
translation.deep: In these gentle words, the Lord reveals a profound truth about His divine nature. While we, as individual souls, pass through countless lives and forget our pasts, He remembers every single one of His appearances. This shows His supreme wisdom and timeless presence, a comforting reminder that He is eternally aware of all journeys, past, present, and future, always watching over us with perfect love and understanding.
translation.essence: This verse beautifully teaches us that while our memories of past lives fade, the Divine Lord's knowledge is eternal and complete. He is the supreme knower of all time, ever-present and fully aware of our entire spiritual journey.

4-6.sanskrit:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन्।

प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया।।4.6।।
4-6.transliteration:
ajo ’pi sannavyayātmā bhūtānām īśhvaro ’pi san
prakṛitiṁ svām adhiṣhṭhāya sambhavāmyātma-māyayā

translation.simple: Though I am eternally unborn and My Spirit never diminishes, and even though I am the Lord of all beings, I lovingly manifest Myself. I do this by taking hold of My own divine nature, appearing through My own wondrous power.
translation.deep: Understand this profound truth: Though I am forever unborn and possess an imperishable spirit, and though I am the supreme Controller of all creation, I choose to appear in this world. This manifestation is not a limitation, but an act of My boundless grace. I take command of My own divine nature, and by My own mystical energy, I come forth. This reveals My absolute sovereignty and My intimate connection to the world, always for the greater good and to uplift devoted hearts.
translation.essence: The eternal, unborn Lord, though supreme, lovingly descends into the world by His own divine will and power, embracing His own nature to manifest.

4-7.sanskrit:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।

अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम्।।4.7।।
4-7.transliteration:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata
abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛijāmyaham

translation.simple: O Arjuna, whenever the path of righteousness seems to falter, and unrighteousness begins to flourish, at that very time, I lovingly manifest Myself.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully expresses the Lord's unwavering commitment to the cosmic order. It assures us that when the light of dharma diminishes and the shadows of adharma lengthen, the Divine does not remain distant. Instead, the Supreme Being graciously descends, not just to appear, but to actively restore harmony, re-establish truth, and uplift all sincere seekers. It's a profound promise of divine vigilance and merciful intervention.
translation.essence: The Lord's divine assurance: When dharma diminishes and adharma grows, He lovingly manifests to restore harmony and guide all back to the path of truth.

4-8.sanskrit:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।

धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे।।4.8।।
4-8.transliteration:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśhāya cha duṣhkṛitām
dharma-sansthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge

translation.simple: The Divine One assures us that He comes forth in every age to protect the gentle-hearted, to soothe the troubles caused by wrongdoers, and to tenderly re-establish the path of righteousness.
translation.deep: This sacred promise illuminates the Lord's boundless compassion and unwavering resolve. He manifests in our world, not for His own gain, but driven by a profound love for all creation. His coming is a divine intervention to protect the sincere seekers, to gently correct the imbalance caused by misguided actions, and to lovingly re-establish the spiritual order (dharma) that guides all beings towards peace and truth. It assures us that the Divine Hand is always at work, ensuring balance and guiding the universe with wisdom and grace.
translation.essence: This verse is a comforting divine promise: The Lord lovingly appears through the ages to safeguard the virtuous and to gently restore the timeless path of righteousness whenever it falters.

4-9.sanskrit:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।

त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन।।4.9।।
4-9.transliteration:
janma karma cha me divyam evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ
tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so ’rjuna

translation.simple: Whoever truly understands the divine nature of My coming and My deeds, O Arjuna, does not take birth again after leaving this body. Instead, they come directly to Me.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us of a profound truth: the Lord's appearance in the world and His every act are not bound by material laws, but are purely divine. To truly know this isn't just an intellectual grasp, but a deep spiritual realization that transforms the heart. Such a blessed soul, having understood this sacred mystery, transcends the cycle of birth and death. After leaving the physical body, they attain union with the Divine, finding eternal solace in the Lord's presence.
translation.essence: To truly know the divine truth of My appearance and My actions is to break free from the cycle of rebirth and attain eternal closeness with Me.

4-10.sanskrit:
वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः।

बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः।।4.10।।
4-10.transliteration:
vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhā man-mayā mām upāśhritāḥ
bahavo jñāna-tapasā pūtā mad-bhāvam āgatāḥ

translation.simple: Many souls, letting go of worldly desires, fear, and anger, find their solace in Me. With their hearts set on Me and seeking My shelter, they are purified by wisdom and devotion, ultimately reaching My divine nature.
translation.deep: When hearts bravely release the chains of worldly attachments, overcome fears, and calm the fires of anger, they naturally turn towards the Divine. Such devoted souls, absorbed in contemplation of the Self and finding refuge in Me, undertake a profound journey. Through the intense spiritual practice of true knowledge, their inner being is cleansed, allowing them to truly experience and embody My transcendent presence.
translation.essence: Freedom from desire, fear, and anger, coupled with single-pointed devotion and wisdom, purifies the soul. This purification leads to becoming one with the Divine.

4-11.sanskrit:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम्।

मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।4.11।।
4-11.transliteration:
ye yathā māṁ prapadyante tāns tathaiva bhajāmyaham
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣhyāḥ pārtha sarvaśhaḥ

translation.simple: However you approach Me, that is how I respond to you. O Partha, all beings, in every manner, ultimately follow My divine path.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna tenderly assures us that the Divine responds to our earnest calling exactly as we offer it. If we seek Him with pure devotion, He reciprocates with boundless love. If we yearn for guidance, He lights our way. It's a profound truth that every soul, O Arjuna, no matter their outward path, is ultimately moving towards the one Supreme Reality. In countless ways, all of humanity walks upon His divine path, drawn by His universal presence.
translation.essence: The Lord lovingly reciprocates our devotion in the very way we offer it. Ultimately, all beings, in every walk of life, are gently guided by His divine presence.

4-12.sanskrit:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः।

क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा।।4.12।।
4-12.transliteration:
kāṅkṣhantaḥ karmaṇāṁ siddhiṁ yajanta iha devatāḥ
kṣhipraṁ hi mānuṣhe loke siddhir bhavati karmajā

translation.simple: Here in this world, many hearts yearn for success in their deeds and offer their devotion to different gods. Truly, within this human experience, the results of one's efforts, bringing forth desired outcomes, manifest without much delay.
translation.deep: This verse gently points to a common human tendency: to seek immediate gratification and worldly achievements. When our hearts are set on goals within this material plane, whether it's wealth, health, or recognition, we naturally turn to sources that can grant these swift results. It highlights how readily one can attain the fruits of action in this human life, encouraging us to reflect on the true nature of our desires and the ultimate goal of our devotion.
translation.essence: In this human world, the path to desired results through action and worship of deities for those ends is often quick. This reminds us that immediate gratification for material wishes is readily available, prompting a quiet reflection on what truly sustains the soul.

4-13.sanskrit:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः।

तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम्।।4.13।।
4-13.transliteration:
chātur-varṇyaṁ mayā sṛiṣhṭaṁ guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśhaḥ
tasya kartāram api māṁ viddhyakartāram avyayam

translation.simple: The Lord kindly explains that the diverse roles within human society are established by Him, according to each person's inner qualities and natural actions. Even though He is the creator of this entire arrangement, know that He remains forever untouched by it, ever peaceful and unchanging.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna reveals that He is the origin of the natural divisions within humanity, which are distinguished by the unique qualities (gunas) and inherent activities (karmas) of each individual. This is not a rigid caste system but a recognition of natural inclinations. And while He is the very source of all creation and order, He profoundly declares Himself to be the non-doer, utterly detached and unaffected by the unfolding world. This speaks to His supreme transcendence and His eternal, immutable nature, beyond all action and its consequences.
translation.essence: God creates the natural order of human society based on our qualities and actions. Yet, He remains the ultimate Creator who is completely untouched and eternally unchanging, never bound by His own divine work.

4-14.sanskrit:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा।

इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते।।4.14।।
4-14.transliteration:
na māṁ karmāṇi limpanti na me karma-phale spṛihā
iti māṁ yo ’bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badhyate

translation.simple: Lord Krishna says: Actions do not cling to Me, nor do I have any desire for their outcomes. Whoever understands Me in this way is also freed from the binding effects of their own actions.
translation.deep: The Supreme Being, though performing all acts of creation and sustenance, remains ever untainted by them, for there is no personal attachment or longing for the fruits of these deeds. When a devotee deeply realizes this divine principle – that the Source of all existence operates with perfect detachment – they are inspired to act in the world with a similar spirit of selfless devotion, thus finding true liberation from the karmic cycle.
translation.essence: God is untouched by actions and their results because He desires nothing. Realizing this truth frees a soul from its own actions.

4-15.sanskrit:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः।

कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम्।।4.15।।
4-15.transliteration:
evaṁ jñātvā kṛitaṁ karma pūrvair api mumukṣhubhiḥ
kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṁ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṁ kṛitam

translation.simple: The enlightened ones of the past, who longed for true freedom, performed their tasks with this very understanding. So, dear heart, you too should engage in your actions, just as those wise souls did long ago.
translation.deep: Recognizing the deep spiritual truth about action—that true liberation comes through selfless work—our revered ancestors and earnest seekers consistently fulfilled their duties. Therefore, O aspiring soul, embrace your responsibilities with the same serene wisdom and devotion, walking the very path of pure action that the enlightened ones have always trod.
translation.essence: Inspired by the wise ones who came before, perform your duties with enlightened understanding, for this is the path to true freedom.

4-16.sanskrit:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः।

तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्।।4.16।।
4-16.transliteration:
kiṁ karma kim akarmeti kavayo ’pyatra mohitāḥ
tat te karma pravakṣhyāmi yaj jñātvā mokṣhyase ’śhubhāt

translation.simple: Even the most thoughtful minds sometimes get confused about what true action is, and what isn't. But I will now share with you the deep secret of action, which, once understood, will gently set you free from all worries and troubles.
translation.deep: The subtle distinction between righteous action and mere inaction remains a profound riddle, often perplexing even the most enlightened seers. Yet, the Lord lovingly offers to illuminate this path, revealing the true essence of action. Embracing this divine insight will lead to your complete liberation from the binds of all unfavorable circumstances and karmic reactions.
translation.essence: Even the wise struggle with understanding true action. Krishna offers to reveal this liberating knowledge, setting us free from all sorrow.

4-17.sanskrit:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः।

अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः।।4.17।।
4-17.transliteration:
karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṁ boddhavyaṁ cha vikarmaṇaḥ
akarmaṇaśh cha boddhavyaṁ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ

translation.simple: We must truly know what action is, what harmful action is, and what it means to not act at all. For the ways of action are wonderfully mysterious and deep.
translation.deep: It is essential to truly comprehend what constitutes proper action, what falls into the category of inappropriate action, and even the subtle meaning of inaction. The path of action is intricate and profound. Understanding these distinctions is not just about doing or not doing, but about grasping the spiritual law that governs all our deeds, leading to deeper insight and calm wisdom.
translation.essence: Knowing action, wrong action, and inaction is vital. For the true nature of karma is a profound spiritual mystery to be understood.

4-18.sanskrit:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः।

स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत्।।4.18।।
4-18.transliteration:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśhyed akarmaṇi cha karma yaḥ
sa buddhimān manuṣhyeṣhu sa yuktaḥ kṛitsna-karma-kṛit

translation.simple: He who sees true stillness amidst busy action, and finds meaningful purpose even in quiet repose, is truly wise among all people. Such a soul remains always connected to the Divine, gently fulfilling all duties without being bound by their outcomes.
translation.deep: This verse invites us to a profound understanding: to discern the spirit of non-doership even while engaged in intense activity, and to perceive a powerful, divine action unfolding within moments of apparent inactivity. The individual who grasps this subtle truth, knowing that the real 'doer' is the Supreme Self, not the limited ego, is truly enlightened among humankind. Such a one, ever absorbed in the essence of yoga, effortlessly performs all their duties, yet remains perfectly free from entanglement, living a life of serene spiritual mastery.
translation.essence: To perceive inner stillness within all actions, and sacred purpose within all quietude, is the mark of true wisdom. Such a soul, ever connected to the Divine, performs all duties with an unbound and peaceful heart.

4-19.sanskrit:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः।

ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः।।4.19।।
4-19.transliteration:
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāma-saṅkalpa-varjitāḥ
jñānāgni-dagdha-karmāṇaṁ tam āhuḥ paṇḍitaṁ budhāḥ

translation.simple: A soul whose every endeavor is pure, free from personal longing or selfish intent, and whose actions are purified by the gentle flame of true wisdom—such a one, the enlightened hearts declare, is truly wise.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully paints the portrait of a liberated being. Such a soul undertakes all tasks not driven by personal desires or ego-bound aspirations, but from a deeper place of surrender and duty. Their every action is then offered into the sacred fire of spiritual knowledge, burning away any potential for karmic entanglement. The wise sages, observing this profound inner transformation, recognize them as truly enlightened, for their work becomes an act of pure devotion.
translation.essence: The truly wise are those whose every action is free from selfish desire and is consecrated by the purifying light of true spiritual knowledge.

4-20.sanskrit:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः।

कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः।।4.20।।
4-20.transliteration:
tyaktvā karma-phalāsaṅgaṁ nitya-tṛipto nirāśhrayaḥ
karmaṇyabhipravṛitto ’pi naiva kiñchit karoti saḥ

translation.simple: One who releases attachment to the fruits of their actions, always content within and needing no external support, even when diligently engaged in work, truly does nothing that binds them.
translation.deep: This verse lovingly describes a liberated soul whose inner state transcends the ordinary experience of action. By surrendering the desire for outcomes and finding deep satisfaction in the eternal Self, such a being performs all duties with unwavering focus, yet their spirit remains untouched. Their actions flow from a place of pure intention, free from the ego's grasp, ensuring that no new karmic bonds are formed. It is a profound state of inner freedom, where one is active in the world yet remains eternally peaceful and unbound.
translation.essence: Let go of attachment to results, find your joy within, and act from a place of inner contentment; then, even in the midst of all activity, your spirit remains completely free and peaceful.

4-21.sanskrit:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः।

शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्।।4.21।।
4-21.transliteration:
nirāśhīr yata-chittātmā tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ
śhārīraṁ kevalaṁ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣham

translation.simple: When your heart is peaceful, free from worldly desires, and your mind is calm and steady, letting go of attachment to possessions, then simply doing what's needed for your body brings no unwanted karmic reactions.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully guides us towards a profound state of inner freedom. By consciously detaching from the fruits of our labor and mastering our mind and senses, we learn to release the grip of possessiveness. When our actions are no longer driven by personal wants but solely by the needs for our physical existence, they transcend the cycle of karma. This isn't about inaction, but about acting with a pure heart, unburdened by ego or expectation, finding liberation in every simple deed.
translation.essence: When the heart is pure, the mind serene, and attachment to worldly things is released, then even simple actions needed for life become offerings that free us from karmic ties.

4-22.sanskrit:
यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः।

समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते।।4.22।।
4-22.transliteration:
yadṛichchhā-lābha-santuṣhṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ
samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau cha kṛitvāpi na nibadhyate

translation.simple: A soul content with what life brings by grace, untouched by highs and lows, free from jealousy, and seeing success and failure equally, remains unburdened, even as they act.
translation.deep: This verse speaks of a profound inner liberation. It describes one who, having surrendered to the divine flow, finds contentment in all that manifests, accepting it as grace. Such a soul transcends the worldly dualities of pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor, understanding their ephemeral nature. Free from the poison of envy, they radiate inner peace. For them, success and failure are merely different manifestations of the cosmic play, observed with perfect equanimity. Thus, even as they actively participate in the world, their actions, performed without attachment to results, do not bind them to the cycle of karma. Their spirit remains ever free.
translation.essence: This verse beautifully teaches that true freedom lies in an inner state of contentment, accepting all outcomes as grace. By rising above life's dualities and shedding envy, one can engage in action without being bound, living a life of spiritual liberation.

4-23.sanskrit:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः।

यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते।।4.23।।
4-23.transliteration:
gata-saṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthita-chetasaḥ
yajñāyācharataḥ karma samagraṁ pravilīyate

translation.simple: When your heart is free from worldly attachments, and your mind is steady in spiritual wisdom, then all your actions, performed with a spirit of offering to the Divine, gently dissolve, leaving no karmic burden.
translation.deep: This verse reveals the sublime state of a soul liberated from material ties, whose consciousness is firmly rooted in divine knowledge. Such a spiritually awakened being performs every act not for personal gain or earthly outcomes, but purely as a selfless offering, a sacred 'yajna.' In this profound dedication, all actions, instead of creating karmic bonds, are purified and absorbed, leading to ultimate freedom from the cycle of cause and effect. It beckons us to live with an elevated awareness, where every deed becomes an expression of devotion.
translation.essence: A heart free from attachment, illuminated by wisdom, performs actions as an offering to the Divine. In this pure state, all deeds dissolve their karmic impressions, bringing ultimate peace and liberation.

4-24.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्।

ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना।।4.24।।
4-24.transliteration:
brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṁ brahma-karma-samādhinā

translation.simple: When we offer anything, let us see the Divine in the offering, in the act of giving, and even in the sacred fire that receives it. The one who offers is also a manifestation of the Divine. For those whose hearts are absorbed in this vision of the Divine in all actions, they surely reach the Divine alone.
translation.deep: This verse illuminates the profound unity of all existence. It reveals that in any sacred act, the offering itself, the one who offers, the fire that receives it, and the very act of offering are all expressions of the Supreme Brahman. When our awareness is deeply immersed in this truth, seeing the Divine in every aspect of our actions, then these actions become a direct means to realize Brahman. Such a state of 'Brahman-consciousness' in action transforms all our deeds into a spiritual journey leading to ultimate union with the Divine.
translation.essence: Realizing the Divine in every part of an action – the offering, the doer, the recipient – leads one directly to the Divine.

4-25.sanskrit:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते।

ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति।।4.25।।
4-25.transliteration:
daivam evāpare yajñaṁ yoginaḥ paryupāsate
brahmāgnāvapare yajñaṁ yajñenaivopajuhvati

translation.simple: Some devoted seekers lovingly perform their rituals and offerings to the divine beings, honoring their sacred presence. Yet others, with a deeper understanding, offer the very act of sacrifice into the boundless fire of Brahman, seeing all action as a sacred offering to the Ultimate Reality.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse illuminates the diverse paths of spiritual devotion. It speaks of those who find profound connection by directing their heartfelt offerings and worship towards specific celestial deities, honoring the cosmic order and the divine forces that govern it. Then there are those, embracing a more expansive realization, who understand that the 'sacrifice' is not merely an external ritual but an internal act of self-giving. They perceive no distinction between the offering, the act of offering, and the ultimate recipient. For these souls, every action and every offering is merged into the all-pervading light of Brahman, the Absolute Truth, thus transforming their entire existence into a continuous act of divine surrender.
translation.essence: Ultimately, this verse reminds us that paths to the Divine are varied. Some hearts offer devotion to celestial beings, while others perceive the act of offering itself as a sacrifice into the Supreme Brahman. Both journeys reflect a sincere aspiration to connect with the divine truth and serve the One.

4-26.sanskrit:
श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति।

शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति।।4.26।।
4-26.transliteration:
śhrotrādīnīndriyāṇyanye sanyamāgniṣhu juhvati
śhabdādīn viṣhayānanya indriyāgniṣhu juhvati

translation.simple: Some devotees offer their senses, like hearing and sight, into the sacred fire of self-control, finding peace in discipline. Others offer the very objects of the senses—sounds, sights, and tastes—into their purified senses, transforming every experience into a prayerful offering.
translation.deep: This profound verse illuminates different forms of spiritual sacrifice, or Yajna. Some yogis, with deep devotion, dedicate their sensory faculties—eyes, ears, and others—into the blazing fire of self-restraint (samyama). Through this discipline, they purify their perception and withdrawal from worldly distractions. Another path reveals the offering of sense objects themselves—the diverse sounds, forms, and flavors of the world—into the 'fires' of their own senses. This implies a state of profound awareness where engagement with the external world is not a source of attachment, but rather an act of conscious perception, transmuted into a spiritual offering, free from desire and aversion, making every interaction a step towards liberation.
translation.essence: The core message speaks of purifying our interaction with the world: either by reining in the senses through discipline, or by transforming our experience of sense objects into a conscious, detached, and sacred offering.

4-27.sanskrit:
सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे।

आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते।।4.27।।
4-27.transliteration:
sarvāṇīndriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi chāpare
ātma-sanyama-yogāgnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite

translation.simple: Some dedicated souls offer all their sensory actions and even the movements of their vital life energies into the sacred fire of self-control. This spiritual fire is beautifully illumined by true wisdom.
translation.deep: This verse speaks of those who engage in a profound inner sacrifice. They consciously take every action performed by their senses – what they see, hear, touch, taste, and smell – and even the subtle processes of their breath and life force, and offer them into an internal, purifying 'fire'. This fire is not an external flame, but the spiritual discipline of self-mastery and inner control, brilliantly kindled and sustained by the light of spiritual knowledge. It's an act of profound surrender, where all personal actions are transformed into a devotional offering.
translation.essence: The core message is about an internal spiritual offering: dedicating all actions of the senses and the life-breath to the purifying flame of self-discipline, which is ignited and brightened by divine wisdom, leading to inner purity and devotion.

4-28.transliteration:
dravya-yajñās tapo-yajñā yoga-yajñās tathāpare
swādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāśh cha yatayaḥ sanśhita-vratāḥ

translation.simple: Some offer their material possessions with devotion. Others dedicate themselves to the path of austerity and penance. Still others offer their efforts in the practice of yoga. And there are those who offer the diligent study of sacred texts and the pursuit of true knowledge. All these devoted souls are firm in their spiritual vows.
translation.deep: This verse gently reveals the diverse ways sincere souls offer their lives to the Divine. It's not just about external ritual, but the profound spirit of offering within. Some find their devotion in sharing their resources, while others find it in self-discipline and austerity. Many dedicate themselves to the path of Yoga, uniting with the Supreme through focused practice. And then there are those who deeply immerse themselves in sacred wisdom, offering their intellect and understanding as a spiritual act. Each path, embraced with unwavering commitment, leads towards the same ultimate truth, marked by a deep inner resolve.
translation.essence: With unwavering vows, seekers offer their lives in many ways: through selfless giving, dedicated penance, diligent yoga practice, or the profound pursuit of sacred wisdom. Each act is a heartfelt offering, guiding them steadily towards the Divine.

4-29.sanskrit:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राण प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे।

प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः।।4.29।।
4-29.transliteration:
apāne juhvati prāṇaṁ prāṇe ’pānaṁ tathāpare
prāṇāpāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ
 apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣhu juhvati
sarve ’pyete yajña-vido yajña-kṣhapita-kalmaṣhāḥ

translation.simple: Some devoted souls offer their incoming breath into the outgoing, and others offer their outgoing breath into the incoming. Still others, dedicated to breath control, gently hold both breaths, finding a deep stillness. All are dedicated to inner peace through these sacred practices.
translation.deep: Here, the Lord speaks of those who, with deep reverence, make an inner offering of their life-energy. Some lovingly merge the incoming breath (prana) into the outgoing (apana), finding harmony in this flow. Others offer the outgoing breath into the incoming, seeking balance. Then there are those who, with single-minded devotion, gently still the movement of both these vital breaths, cultivating a profound inner quietude. These practices are not mere exercises but sacred acts of self-offering, known as Pranayama, drawing the seeker closer to their true spiritual essence and the Divine within.
translation.essence: Devotees engage in various forms of breath control, offering their life-force in dedicated practice (Pranayama) to find inner stillness, harmony, and a deeper connection with the Divine.

4-30.sanskrit:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति।

सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः।।4.30।।
4-30.transliteration:
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān  prāṇeṣu juhvati

sarve py 'ete yajña-vido yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ

translation.simple: Some devotees, regulating their food, offer their very breaths into other breaths. All these spiritual seekers truly know the heart of sacrifice, and through their offerings, all inner impurities are gently purified.
translation.deep: This sacred verse describes those aspirants who, having disciplined their physical needs, engage in the profound practice of breath control, or Pranayama. They subtly offer the incoming vital breath into the outgoing, or the gross breath into the subtle, recognizing this as a powerful internal sacrifice (Yajña). Such dedicated souls deeply comprehend the essence of spiritual offering. Through this continuous process of inner discipline and surrender, their minds and hearts are purified of all karmic residues and worldly attachments, guiding them toward a state of profound inner peace and clarity.
translation.essence: By regulating diet and practicing breath control as a sacred offering, devotees cleanse their inner being. This path of self-sacrifice purifies the heart and reveals true spiritual wisdom.

4-31.sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम्।

नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतो़ऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम।।4.31।।
4-31.transliteration:
yajña-śhiṣhṭāmṛita-bhujo yānti brahma sanātanam
nāyaṁ loko ’styayajñasya kuto ’nyaḥ kuru-sattama

translation.simple: When we humbly offer our actions and receive what remains as a sacred gift, we naturally draw closer to the eternal Divine. But for those who do not live with this spirit of selfless giving, even this earthly life may feel incomplete, let alone any spiritual realms beyond.
translation.deep: This sacred verse unfolds a profound truth: by performing our duties and actions as a devoted offering – a 'yajña' – and then humbly accepting what remains as divine 'amrita', we are directly guided to the everlasting Brahman. This act of selfless giving purifies our very being. Conversely, a life lived without this spirit of offering, solely focused on personal gratification, misses the true essence of even this present world, leaving no pathway to higher spiritual planes or ultimate liberation, O Arjuna.
translation.essence: Perform actions as a sacred offering, and accept their pure remnants; this leads to the eternal Divine. Without this spirit of selfless offering, neither present contentment nor ultimate spiritual attainment is possible.

4-32.sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे।

कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे।।4.32।।
4-32.transliteration:
evaṁ bahu-vidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe
karma-jān viddhi tān sarvān evaṁ jñātvā vimokṣhyase

translation.simple: All these many kinds of spiritual efforts and offerings are spread forth from the divine source of wisdom. Understand that each one of them is born of action. Knowing this truth will gently guide you to liberation.
translation.deep: Countless forms of spiritual devotion and self-offering are revealed through the sacred teachings. Recognize that every one of these, without exception, blossoms forth from various actions performed with intention. When you truly grasp this deep understanding—that all spiritual paths ultimately involve action—you will discover the way to lasting liberation and inner peace.
translation.essence: The many sacred paths of devotion are illuminated by divine knowledge, and each stems from our actions. Understanding this simple truth brings the soul to ultimate freedom and peace.

4-33.sanskrit:
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप।

सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते।।4.33।।
4-33.transliteration:
śhreyān dravya-mayād yajñāj jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa
sarvaṁ karmākhilaṁ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate

translation.simple: Dear one, offering the sacrifice of true knowledge is far more valuable than any material offering. All our actions, without exception, ultimately find their beautiful completion and purpose in this divine understanding.
translation.deep: O Arjuna, recognize that the offering of wisdom, the 'Jnana Yajna,' holds a profound superiority over any sacrifice made with material possessions. For it is in the gentle light of this spiritual understanding that every single action, every deed we undertake, eventually reaches its perfect culmination and ultimate peace.
translation.essence: The greatest offering is knowledge itself, as all our deeds eventually merge and find their complete and perfect fulfillment in its profound embrace.

4-34.sanskrit:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया।

उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः।।4.34।।
4-34.transliteration:
tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśhnena sevayā
upadekṣhyanti te jñānaṁ jñāninas tattva-darśhinaḥ

translation.simple: To discover spiritual truth, approach a true teacher with deep humility. Ask your questions sincerely, from a place of genuine seeking, and offer your service with devotion. In this way, those wise souls who have directly experienced the ultimate reality will lovingly guide you to knowledge.
translation.deep: Embrace the path to ultimate knowledge by cultivating profound humility before a spiritual guide, letting go of pride. Engage them with heartfelt questions that arise from an authentic longing to understand the Truth. Dedicate yourself through selfless service, making your heart receptive. Through this sacred relationship, those enlightened beings, who have truly seen and embody the Supreme Reality, will mercifully reveal divine wisdom within your soul.
translation.essence: Approach the wise with humility, sincere questions, and devoted service; they will reveal the knowledge of Truth.

4-35.sanskrit:
यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव।

येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि।।4.35।।
4-35.transliteration:
yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṁ yāsyasi pāṇḍava
yena bhūtānyaśheṣheṇa drakṣhyasyātmanyatho mayi

translation.simple: Dear Arjuna, once you truly grasp this sacred wisdom, you will never again fall into such confusion. With this pure understanding, you will begin to see all beings, every single one, first within your own spiritual Self, and then, completely, within Me.
translation.deep: This verse holds a beautiful promise of liberation. Lord Krishna assures us that when we truly absorb this sacred knowledge, the mists of delusion will lift from our hearts forever. It means that the confusion and sorrow that arise from seeing separation will vanish. Through this profound insight, we will begin to perceive every living being, without exception, as manifestations of the same divine Spirit, dwelling within our own deepest Self. And finally, with utmost clarity, we will see them all resting perfectly within Me, the Supreme Being, realizing the oneness of all existence in its divine source.
translation.essence: This profound knowledge dispels all illusion forever. It empowers you to see every living being as inseparable from your own spiritual self, and ultimately, as resting completely within the Divine Lord.

4-36.sanskrit:
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः।

सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि।।4.36।।
4-36.transliteration:
api ched asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛit-tamaḥ
sarvaṁ jñāna-plavenaiva vṛijinaṁ santariṣhyasi

translation.simple: Even if you feel like you've committed many wrongs, the sturdy boat of spiritual knowledge will surely carry you across all your difficulties.
translation.deep: This sacred verse offers profound comfort, reminding us that true spiritual knowledge isn't just information, but a deep, transformative understanding of our divine essence and the Supreme. This wisdom acts like an unbreakable vessel, capable of carrying us beyond the burdens of all past actions, leading to liberation and inner peace, no matter how great the perceived transgressions.
translation.essence: No matter how burdened you feel by your past, pure spiritual wisdom is the divine boat that carries you safely across all challenges to liberation and peace.

4-37.sanskrit:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन।

ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा।।4.37।।
4-37.transliteration:
yathaidhānsi samiddho ’gnir bhasma-sāt kurute ’rjuna
jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasma-sāt kurute tathā

translation.simple: Just as a blazing fire completely turns its fuel into ashes, O Arjuna, similarly, the fire of true wisdom burns away the effects of all our actions.
translation.deep: Observe, Arjuna, how a well-kindled fire utterly consumes and transforms its fuel into ash. In the same sacred manner, the luminous fire of profound spiritual knowledge purifies and dissolves the accumulated impressions and binding consequences of all our deeds, leading the soul to a state of profound inner liberation.
translation.essence: The ultimate liberating power lies in divine knowledge. It acts as a purifying flame, consuming the karmic residue of all actions and freeing the spirit to attain lasting peace and spiritual freedom.

4-38.sanskrit:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते।

तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति।।4.38।।
4-38.transliteration:
na hi jñānena sadṛiśhaṁ pavitramiha vidyate
tatsvayaṁ yogasansiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati

translation.simple: Truly, nothing in this world purifies us quite like spiritual wisdom. A devoted soul, steady in their practice, will surely find this sacred knowledge gently blooming within their own heart in due time.
translation.deep: Among all the purifiers in this existence, none can compare to the profound sanctity of divine knowledge. This isn't an external acquisition, but a radiant truth that gradually unveils itself. A seeker whose path is perfected through yoga and dedicated practice will, in the gentle unfolding of time, realize this pristine wisdom deep within the sanctuary of their own being, experiencing its transformative power.
translation.essence: Divine knowledge is the highest purity. Through devoted spiritual practice, this sacred wisdom awakens within, revealing itself to the heart that patiently seeks it.

4-39.sanskrit:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः।

ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति।।4.39।।
4-39.transliteration:
śhraddhāvān labhate jñānaṁ tat-paraḥ sanyatendriyaḥ
jñānaṁ labdhvā parāṁ śhāntim achireṇādhigachchhati

translation.simple: With sincere faith and a dedicated heart, one gains spiritual wisdom by gently guiding their senses. This wisdom quickly brings an ultimate, serene peace.
translation.deep: This sacred verse reveals the beautiful journey to true insight. It teaches that a heart brimming with sincere faith, dedicated with unwavering devotion, and practicing gentle control over the senses, is ripe to receive spiritual wisdom. This profound knowledge is a divine gift that, once attained, swiftly ushers in a supreme and everlasting peace within the soul, a tranquility that settles all unrest.
translation.essence: Cultivate unwavering faith, dedicate yourself with devotion, and gently rein in your senses. This path grants divine wisdom, which swiftly leads to a supreme, lasting peace.

4-40.sanskrit:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति।

नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः।।4.40।।
4-40.transliteration:
ajñaśh chāśhraddadhānaśh cha sanśhayātmā vinaśhyati
nāyaṁ loko ’sti na paro na sukhaṁ sanśhayātmanaḥ

translation.simple: Those who lack true understanding, are without firm faith, and constantly held by doubt, sadly lose their spiritual path. For a soul consumed by doubt, there is no peace in this world, no comfort in the next, and no true happiness.
translation.deep: The spiritual journey blossoms beautifully with sincere understanding, unwavering faith, and a heart free from crippling doubt. When we close ourselves to wisdom, fail to trust in the higher truth, and allow constant suspicion to cloud our inner vision, our very being suffers. For such a soul, trapped in endless questioning, the beauty and purpose of this earthly existence remain hidden, the promise of the spiritual realm feels distant, and the deep, abiding joy of connection to the Divine remains elusive.
translation.essence: Cultivate inner knowing and firm faith, for a heart entangled in doubt finds no lasting peace. True happiness and profound connection, in this world and the next, only arise when we gently release the chains of uncertainty.

4-41.sanskrit:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम्।

आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय।।4.41।।
4-41.transliteration:
yoga-sannyasta-karmāṇaṁ jñāna-sañchhinna-sanśhayam
ātmavantaṁ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya

translation.simple: Beloved Arjuna, when you dedicate your work to the Divine with a surrendered heart, and when your mind is freed from all doubts by true spiritual understanding, then actions no longer hold you captive. You remain ever free.
translation.deep: Oh Dhananjaya, for the one who performs all actions as an offering, letting go of attachment to results (Karma Yoga), and whose inner wisdom has completely cleared away every shadow of doubt, such a self-realized soul remains untainted. Actions, by their very nature, cannot bind this tranquil being who lives in the awareness of the true Self, eternally liberated and at peace.
translation.essence: Offer your deeds to the Divine, let wisdom clear all doubts, and you shall forever remain free, untouched by the world's bindings.

4-42.sanskrit:
तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः।

छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत।।4.42।।
4-42.transliteration:
tasmād ajñāna-sambhūtaṁ hṛit-sthaṁ jñānāsinātmanaḥ
chhittvainaṁ sanśhayaṁ yogam ātiṣhṭhottiṣhṭha bhārata

translation.simple: Therefore, dear soul, with the gentle sword of your own understanding, cut through the doubts that sit within your heart, doubts born from not fully knowing. Embrace the path of spiritual union, and rise with renewed spirit.
