translation.simple: In that new life, the sincere soul naturally finds its way back to the spiritual understanding cultivated in earlier births. O Arjuna, with this foundation, it peacefully strives once more towards its journey of ultimate realization.
translation.deep: The spiritual progress of a sincere heart is never wasted. In a new life, the soul naturally reclaims that deep inner connection with wisdom cultivated in previous journeys. This sacred memory gently propels them, O Arjuna, to resume their earnest striving towards ultimate spiritual perfection and union with the divine.
translation.essence: The wisdom gathered in past lives gently returns, guiding the soul to continue its earnest journey towards ultimate spiritual union.

6-44.sanskrit:
पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः।

जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते।।6.44।।
6-44.transliteration:
pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hyavaśho ’pi saḥ
jijñāsur api yogasya śhabda-brahmātivartate

translation.simple: Even if one might feel a little unwilling, the spiritual seeds sown in past lives gently pull them back to the divine path. Just a sincere curiosity for understanding true spiritual union is powerful enough to elevate a soul beyond mere rituals and towards deeper realization.
translation.deep: The accumulated momentum of sincere spiritual practices from previous existences inevitably draws a soul back towards the sacred journey, even if there's a moment of hesitation or perceived helplessness. This demonstrates the eternal imprint of devotional effort. Moreover, even a heartfelt inquiry into the nature of Yoga, the path of divine connection, possesses such potency that it allows one to transcend the limited scope of ritualistic observances and intellectual understanding of scriptures, guiding them towards a more profound, experiential communion with the Divine.
translation.essence: The loving memory of past spiritual efforts gently guides us, and even a sincere longing for divine connection elevates us beyond rituals and words, leading us naturally to deeper truth.

6-45.sanskrit:
प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः।

अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम्।।6.45।।
6-45.transliteration:
prayatnād yatamānas tu yogī sanśhuddha-kilbiṣhaḥ
aneka-janma-sansiddhas tato yāti parāṁ gatim

translation.simple: A spiritual seeker who endeavors with earnest effort, purifying themselves from all impurities, gradually perfects their journey over many lifetimes. Through this steady devotion, they ultimately attain the supreme destination.
translation.deep: With dedicated and persistent spiritual practice, a devotee purifies their heart and mind, washing away the accumulated influences of past actions and desires. This profound path of inner transformation unfolds patiently across numerous lifetimes. Each sincere effort refines the soul, guiding it towards a state of ultimate perfection and union with the highest Truth, a journey that culminates in the supreme spiritual abode.
translation.essence: Through unwavering spiritual effort and sincere purification, the soul steadily progresses, lifetime after lifetime, until it reaches the supreme, eternal destination. It's a journey of divine grace and persistent striving.

6-46.sanskrit:
तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः।

कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन।।6.46।।
6-46.transliteration:
tapasvibhyo ’dhiko yogī
jñānibhyo ’pi mato ’dhikaḥ
karmibhyaśh chādhiko yogī
tasmād yogī bhavārjuna

translation.simple: Lord Krishna lovingly teaches that a yogi, one whose mind is steady in devotion, shines brighter than those performing harsh austerities, those deeply immersed in mere knowledge, or those engaged in ritualistic actions. So, dear Arjuna, strive to become such a yogi.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna tenderly reveals the unique eminence of the yogi. While austerities purify and knowledge enlightens, and righteous actions bear fruit, the yogi's path gently integrates all these into a profound inner union. Their steady mind, fixed on the Divine with love and devotion, experiences a peace and clarity that naturally encompasses and transcends the benefits of other paths. It's about cultivating a deep, living connection, where one's entire being is harmonized with the Supreme, leading to ultimate spiritual fulfillment.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna lovingly encourages us to embrace the path of the yogi, where inner union with the Divine brings a gentle, steady peace that is considered supreme among all spiritual endeavors.

6-47.sanskrit:
योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना।

श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः।।6.47।।
6-47.transliteration:
yoginām api sarveṣhāṁ mad-gatenāntar-ātmanā
śhraddhāvān bhajate yo māṁ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ

translation.simple: Among all seekers, the one whose heart is filled with faith, who always remembers Me and offers devotion, is held by Me as the most perfectly united with the Divine.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully reveals that the pinnacle of spiritual practice lies in the heart's deep, loving connection with the Divine. When a soul, with profound faith, dedicates their entire inner being to the Lord and worships Him with single-minded devotion, that individual achieves the most perfect and sublime union, transcending all other forms of spiritual striving.
translation.essence: True spiritual perfection blossoms in a heart overflowing with faith and unwavering devotion, continuously fixed on the Divine.

7-1.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः।

असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु।।7.1।।
7-1.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
mayyāsakta-manāḥ pārtha yogaṁ yuñjan mad-āśhrayaḥ
asanśhayaṁ samagraṁ māṁ yathā jñāsyasi tach chhṛiṇu

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord said: 'O Partha, please listen. If your heart is lovingly fixed on Me, and you practice spiritual connection, making Me your sole refuge, then you will surely come to know Me fully, without any doubt.'
translation.deep: This sacred verse gently guides us towards knowing the Divine in its entirety. It speaks of a heart deeply drawn to the Lord, a mind steadily engaged in spiritual union, finding all shelter in Him. When we surrender our focus in this way, He assures us that we will truly comprehend His complete nature, without a shadow of doubt. It's an invitation to a profound and peaceful revelation of truth.
translation.essence: With a mind devoted to the Divine, practicing spiritual union and taking refuge in the Lord, one surely comes to know Him completely, beyond all doubt.

7-2.sanskrit:
ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः।

यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते।।7.2।।
7-2.transliteration:
jñānaṁ te ’haṁ sa-vijñānam idaṁ vakṣhyāmyaśheṣhataḥ
yaj jñātvā neha bhūyo ’nyaj jñātavyam-avaśhiṣhyate

translation.simple: My dear soul, I shall now share with you a sacred wisdom, along with its full understanding. Once you truly know this, there will be nothing else left for you to discover or learn in this world.
translation.deep: Here, the Divine promises to bestow upon us not just theoretical understanding, but a knowledge complete with spiritual realization. When this sacred truth is truly known and experienced within, all other quests for knowledge cease, for the heart finds its ultimate contentment and clarity, resting in the absolute.
translation.essence: The Lord offers a complete, divinely revealed knowledge that, once absorbed with understanding, fulfills all seeking and leaves nothing further to be known.

7-3.sanskrit:
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्िचद्यतति सिद्धये।

यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्िचन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।।7.3।।
7-3.transliteration:
manuṣhyāṇāṁ sahasreṣhu kaśhchid yatati siddhaye
yatatām api siddhānāṁ kaśhchin māṁ vetti tattvataḥ

translation.simple: Among countless souls, only a few sincerely strive for spiritual perfection. And even among those who have begun to realize their spiritual goal, only a very rare one truly comes to know Me, the Lord, in My deepest essence.
translation.deep: This verse reveals the extraordinary rarity of true divine knowledge. It suggests that while many may pursue spiritual paths or achieve various forms of perfection, a deep and intimate understanding of the Lord Himself is a profound and exceptional blessing. It speaks to the journey beyond external striving, towards an internal realization that truly connects one with the Supreme Being in His entirety, a knowing that transcends mere intellectual grasp or temporary attainments.
translation.essence: The path to truly knowing the Divine is exceptionally rare and profound. Even among those who earnestly seek and attain spiritual progress, only a blessed few come to intimately realize the Lord in His full truth.

7-4.sanskrit:
भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च।

अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा।।7.4।।
7-4.transliteration:
bhūmir-āpo ’nalo vāyuḥ khaṁ mano buddhir eva cha
ahankāra itīyaṁ me bhinnā prakṛitir aṣhṭadhā

translation.simple: The solid earth, the flowing water, the warming fire, the air we breathe, and the vast space above – these are all from Me. Also, your mind, your intellect, and your sense of 'I' – these eight are distinct expressions of My divine nature, showing My presence everywhere.
translation.deep: Here, the Lord reveals how His divine presence is intricately woven into the fabric of reality. The five great elements that constitute the physical world – earth, water, fire, air, and ether – along with our subtle inner faculties of mind, intellect, and the individual sense of ego, are all manifestations of His unique material energy. These eight distinct forms are entirely dependent on Him, signifying that His creative power is the fundamental essence from which both the visible universe and our inner consciousness arise.
translation.essence: Every part of creation, from the physical elements to our inner thoughts, is a distinct and loving emanation of the Divine, revealing God's all-encompassing presence.

7-5.sanskrit:
अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम्।

जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत्।।7.5।।
7-5.transliteration:
apareyam itas tvanyāṁ prakṛitiṁ viddhi me parām
jīva-bhūtāṁ mahā-bāho yayedaṁ dhāryate jagat

translation.simple: Lord Krishna gently reveals that beyond this visible, changing world, there is another, higher nature—His own divine energy. This spiritual energy is the very life-force that lovingly sustains and supports this entire universe.
translation.deep: Here, the Lord distinguishes between His lower, material nature and His supreme, spiritual nature. This supreme nature is the 'jīva-bhūtam'—the individual living entities, the conscious souls. It is through these fragments of His own divine self, enlivening the material form, that the entire cosmic manifestation is held together and functions. Our very consciousness is a spark of this superior divine power, without which the material world would be inert and unmanifest.
translation.essence: The universe is sustained not just by material elements, but by a supreme, conscious spiritual energy—the divine life-force of the Lord, present within every living being.

7-6.sanskrit:
एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय।

अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा।।7.6।।
7-6.transliteration:
etad-yonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇītyupadhāraya
ahaṁ kṛitsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā

translation.simple: Realize that all living beings come forth from My divine energies. I am the true origin of this entire universe, and I am also its gentle dissolution.
translation.deep: Deeply ponder that all beings arise from My two divine natures, manifesting life in myriad forms. I am the foundational source from which this entire universe springs forth, and into Me, it gracefully dissolves. This reveals My absolute sovereignty and constant presence, weaving through every creation and every end.
translation.essence: All existence originates from the Divine and ultimately returns to Him. He is the beginning and the end.

7-7.sanskrit:
मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय।

मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव।।7.7।।
7-7.transliteration:
mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyat kiñchid asti dhanañjaya
mayi sarvam idaṁ protaṁ sūtre maṇi-gaṇā iva

translation.simple: The Lord lovingly declares, 'O Arjuna, there is nothing higher than Me. Everything you see, this entire universe, is strung upon Me, just as a string holds together many beautiful pearls.'
translation.deep: This profound verse assures us that Lord Krishna is the ultimate reality, the supreme truth beyond which nothing else exists. He is not merely a part of creation, but its very foundation and essence. Just as a thread provides the invisible yet essential support for a necklace of diverse jewels, so too does the Divine quietly and perfectly sustain all beings and phenomena, uniting them within His own boundless self. It reminds us of His omnipresence, holding everything in a unified embrace.
translation.essence: The supreme Divine is the unwavering essence and sustainer of all existence; nothing lies beyond His all-encompassing grace.

7-8.sanskrit:
रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः।

प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु।।7.8।।
7-8.transliteration:
raso ’ham apsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śhaśhi-sūryayoḥ
praṇavaḥ sarva-vedeṣhu śhabdaḥ khe pauruṣhaṁ nṛiṣhu

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, I am the refreshing taste that makes water sweet. I am the radiant light of the moon and the powerful brilliance of the sun. In all the holy scriptures, I am the sacred sound 'Om'. I am the subtle sound that fills the vast sky, and I am the courage and inner strength within all people.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to perceive the Divine not as something separate, but as the intimate essence of all creation. Lord Krishna reveals Himself as the very core quality that defines everything – the life-giving taste of water, the illuminating light of celestial bodies, the foundational sound 'Om' of all spiritual knowledge, the subtle vibration of space, and the purposeful endeavor within humans. Understanding this helps us recognize God's constant, all-pervading presence, transforming our view of the world into a continuous spiritual experience.
translation.essence: The Lord is the pure essence animating everything. He is the taste in water, the light in sun and moon, the sacred Om, the sound in space, and the strength in humanity. Experience Him as the life-force in all.

7-9.sanskrit:
पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ।

जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु।।7.9।।
7-9.transliteration:
puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛithivyāṁ cha tejaśh chāsmi vibhāvasau
jīvanaṁ sarva-bhūteṣhu tapaśh chāsmi tapasviṣhu

translation.simple: The Lord says, 'I am the gentle, pure fragrance of the earth, and the bright, warm glow of fire. I am the life breath that sustains every living being, and the disciplined devotion found in those who seek spiritual truth.'
translation.deep: In this verse, the Divine presence is revealed in the very fabric of creation. The pure, grounding scent of the earth, the illuminating warmth of fire, the life-giving energy that courses through every being, and the dedicated discipline of those on a spiritual path – all these are expressions of the Supreme. It encourages us to perceive the Lord not only in grand, overt displays, but also in the subtle, beautiful details of existence and the unwavering resolve within devoted hearts. It’s a call to recognize the unifying spirit of the Divine in every aspect of life.
translation.essence: The Lord lovingly shares that He is the pure essence in the earth's fragrance, the light in fire, the life in every being, and the discipline in those who seek Him. He is the beautiful, sustaining force in all creation.

7-10.sanskrit:
बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम्।

बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम्।।7.10।।
7-10.transliteration:
bījaṁ māṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ viddhi pārtha sanātanam
buddhir buddhimatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham

translation.simple: Lord Krishna tells Arjuna, 'Know Me as the eternal seed from which all beings sprout, O Partha. I am the intelligence in those who are wise, and the radiant energy in all that shines brightly.' This verse gently reminds us that God is the very origin of everything and also the essence of our finest qualities.
translation.deep: This profound verse invites us to perceive the Divine in the fundamental aspect of existence. Every creature, every living form, traces its ultimate origin to the eternal essence of the Lord, like an unchanging seed. Beyond mere existence, He is also the pure intelligence that guides the wise and the luminous splendor that characterizes the truly brilliant. It encourages us to look deeper, recognizing that the very capacity for wisdom and any spark of inner glow within us, and in the world, is a manifestation of His divine presence.
translation.essence: The Lord is the eternal origin and sustaining essence of all creation, embodying the highest wisdom and divine brilliance.

7-11.sanskrit:
बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्जितम्।

धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ।।7.11।।
7-11.transliteration:
balaṁ balavatāṁ chāhaṁ kāma-rāga-vivarjitam
dharmāviruddho bhūteṣhu kāmo ’smi bharatarṣhabha

translation.simple: I am the pure strength within the strong, a power untainted by selfish desires or attachments. And in all beings, O best among Bharatas, I am that good and righteous desire which aligns with spiritual purpose.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna reveals Himself as the very foundation of true power—not a strength born of ego or craving, but a selfless energy that serves a higher good. He also embodies the gentle, innate desires within every heart, but only those that are in harmony with dharma, with integrity and universal righteousness. This understanding encourages us to align our aspirations with divine will, recognizing that our noblest longings are indeed a reflection of Him.
translation.essence: I am the pure, selfless strength and the righteous desire within all beings.

7-12.sanskrit:
ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये।

मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि।।7.12।।
7-12.transliteration:
ye chaiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāśh cha ye
matta eveti tān viddhi na tvahaṁ teṣhu te mayi

translation.simple: Every state of being, be it pure and peaceful, driven by passion, or clouded by ignorance, know that it originates from Me. Yet, I am not bound by them, though they all exist within Me.
translation.deep: Consider all the varied expressions of life – the clarity of goodness (sattva), the restless energy of passion (rajas), and the dullness of inertia (tamas). Lord Krishna reveals that while these qualities emerge from His divine essence, He Himself remains beyond their influence. They reside within His boundless being, but He is not entangled in their temporary nature. This profound truth reminds us of His supreme transcendence even amidst His immanent creation.
translation.essence: The Divine is the source of all qualities and states of existence, yet remains ever pure and transcendent, holding all within, but bound by none.

7-13.sanskrit:
त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत्।

मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम्।।7.13।।
7-13.transliteration:
tribhir guṇa-mayair bhāvair ebhiḥ sarvam idaṁ jagat
mohitaṁ nābhijānāti māmebhyaḥ param avyayam

translation.simple: This whole world, caught up in the three qualities of nature, is often enchanted. Because of this, it doesn't recognize Me, who is supreme and never changes, existing beyond all these qualities.
translation.deep: The three qualities of nature—goodness, passion, and ignorance—form a powerful illusion that captivates all beings in this world. Deeply entangled in these fluctuating states, the living entities become so absorbed that they miss the presence of the Supreme Lord. He stands eternally beyond these temporary modes, unchanging and imperishable, yet remains unseen due to this profound bewilderment.
translation.essence: Due to the enchanting influence of the three qualities, the world remains unaware of Me, who transcends them all and is eternal.

7-14.sanskrit:
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया।

मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते।।7.14।।
7-14.transliteration:
daivī hyeṣhā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā
mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te

translation.simple: My divine energy, which weaves the qualities of nature, is truly hard to overcome. But those who take refuge solely in Me, they certainly cross beyond this illusion.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna explains that His divine energy, known as Maya, is intricately woven from the three fundamental qualities of nature, and by its very essence, it is incredibly difficult for any soul to transcend through personal effort. This Maya creates the captivating yet binding illusions of the material world. However, the Lord lovingly assures that those who truly surrender to Him alone, placing all their faith and devotion at His feet, are blessed with His grace to cross beyond this powerful and enchanting illusion.
translation.essence: The Lord's divine illusion is formidable and difficult to overcome. Yet, complete and loving surrender to Him is the sure path to transcend its sway and find true spiritual freedom.

7-15.sanskrit:
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः।

माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः।।7.15।।
7-15.transliteration:
na māṁ duṣhkṛitino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ
māyayāpahṛita-jñānā āsuraṁ bhāvam āśhritāḥ

translation.simple: Lord Krishna explains that those who engage in misdeeds, are lost in worldly illusions, and whose wisdom is veiled, do not turn to Him. They often embrace a nature that keeps them far from divine love and light.
translation.deep: This verse compassionately describes how certain souls, blinded by illusion and drawn to unrighteous acts, remain distant from the Lord's embrace. Their spiritual insight is eclipsed by the powerful play of material existence, leading them to cultivate a disposition that prevents them from surrendering to His infinite love and wisdom. It's a gentle reflection on the choices one makes, and how these choices affect their journey toward divine connection.
translation.essence: The Lord reveals that hearts clouded by illusion and entangled in ungodly ways naturally struggle to find refuge in His divine, loving presence.

7-16.sanskrit:
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन।

आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ।।7.16।।
7-16.transliteration:
chatur-vidhā bhajante māṁ janāḥ sukṛitino ’rjuna
ārto jijñāsur arthārthī jñānī cha bharatarṣhabha

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, four kinds of pure-hearted souls turn to Me in devotion. They are those who suffer, those who long to know, those who seek prosperity, and the truly wise, O noble one.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly shares that four kinds of virtuous souls come to Him. Some turn to Him in their moments of distress, seeking solace. Others approach with a sincere desire to know the ultimate truth. There are also those who pray for blessings and well-being in their lives. And then there are the truly wise, who understand Him deeply. This verse gently affirms that any inclination of the heart towards the Divine, born of good actions, is cherished by the Lord, paving the way for spiritual growth and inner peace.
translation.essence: Krishna lovingly receives four kinds of virtuous devotees: the suffering, the curious, the seekers of well-being, and the wise.

7-17.sanskrit:
तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्ितर्विशिष्यते।

प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः।।7.17।।
7-17.transliteration:
teṣhāṁ jñānī nitya-yukta eka-bhaktir viśhiṣhyate
priyo hi jñānino ’tyartham ahaṁ sa cha mama priyaḥ

translation.simple: Among all who turn to Me, the wise one, ever-united and devoted solely to Me, holds a special place. I am incredibly beloved to such a discerning soul, and truly, that soul is equally beloved to Me.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse speaks of a profound spiritual connection. Among the various paths of devotion, the wise soul who is ever-united with Me, offering singular, unwavering love, is exceptionally dear. Their wisdom is a deep knowing of My divine essence, leading to an unbroken communion. For Me, such a knowing devotee is supremely beloved, and in the same way, I am supremely beloved to them—a beautiful exchange of divine love and understanding that nourishes both the seeker and the sought.
translation.essence: At its heart, this verse reveals a sacred, reciprocal love: the wise soul, ever-united and singularly devoted, finds Me supremely dear, and I, in turn, hold that pure soul supremely dear to My heart.

7-18.sanskrit:
उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम्।

आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम्।।7.18।।
7-18.transliteration:
udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tvātmaiva me matam
āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā mām evānuttamāṁ gatim

translation.simple: Indeed, all who approach Me are noble souls. But the wise one, who knows Me as their very own Self – that is My view. Such a steadfast soul truly abides in Me alone as the supreme destination.
translation.deep: While all sincere seekers are dear to the Divine, there's a special grace for the wise devotee (jñānī) who recognizes God not as an external entity, but as their own innermost Self. The Lord declares that such a jñānī is none other than His very being, His essence. This isn't just an intellectual understanding; it's a deep realization that unites their consciousness with the Supreme. Such a steadfast soul, with a mind perfectly aligned, perceives God as the ultimate goal and ultimate reality, finding complete solace and identity in that divine connection.
translation.essence: All devotees are cherished, but the truly wise soul, who perceives the Divine as their own deepest Self, is held by God as His very own. This soul, ever harmonized, finds its ultimate peace and eternal home in God alone.

7-19.sanskrit:
बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते।

वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः।।7.19।।
7-19.transliteration:
bahūnāṁ janmanām ante jñānavān māṁ prapadyate
vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti sa mahātmā su-durlabhaḥ

translation.simple: After many, many births, a wise soul finally takes refuge in Me. They realize that Vasudeva, the Divine, is indeed everything. To find such a great soul, who sees Me as the all-pervading essence, is truly a rare and beautiful blessing.
translation.deep: The spiritual journey can span countless lifetimes, filled with experiences that gradually refine the soul. When a soul's wisdom truly blossoms, they reach a profound understanding: that I, Vasudeva, am the ultimate reality, the all-pervading essence from which everything originates. This realization is not just knowledge, but a deep, loving surrender where one sees the Divine in every aspect of existence. To encounter such a magnificent soul, whose heart and mind are so deeply immersed in this universal truth, is a truly rare and sacred gift.
translation.essence: Through many lives, true wisdom ultimately guides a soul to Me, realizing that Vasudeva is everything. This profound realization and surrender make them a rare and great spirit.

7-20.sanskrit:
कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः।

तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया।।7.20।।
7-20.transliteration:
kāmais tais tair hṛita-jñānāḥ prapadyante ’nya-devatāḥ
taṁ taṁ niyamam āsthāya prakṛityā niyatāḥ svayā

translation.simple: When our minds are clouded by many worldly desires, our true understanding can become dim. Then, compelled by our own inherent nature, we often turn to other divine forms, observing various vows and rituals.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that when diverse desires capture our hearts and minds, our spiritual clarity can waver. Our innate tendencies, shaped by countless experiences, then guide us to seek solace and blessings from various divine forms, observing specific vows. It's a journey driven by the heart's yearning, though the ultimate source of peace might be overlooked in that pursuit.
translation.essence: Our own desires can gently obscure our spiritual wisdom, leading us to honor various divine forms and rituals, compelled by our inherent nature. It's a call to observe the heart's true longing.

7-21.sanskrit:
यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति।

तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम्।।7.21।।
7-21.transliteration:
yo yo yāṁ yāṁ tanuṁ bhaktaḥ śhraddhayārchitum ichchhati
tasya tasyāchalāṁ śhraddhāṁ tām eva vidadhāmyaham

translation.simple: Lord Krishna lovingly assures us: Whatever divine form a sincere devotee chooses to worship with faith, I strengthen and make their devotion firm in that very form.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully illustrates the Lord's all-encompassing nature and boundless compassion. It reveals that the Divine respects and honors the unique spiritual path of each devotee. Regardless of the specific manifestation of God one chooses to adore, the Lord Himself, as the indwelling Spirit, nurtures and solidifies that genuine faith, guiding the individual closer to the ultimate truth through their chosen form.
translation.essence: God personally empowers and stabilizes a devotee's sincere faith in their chosen divine manifestation.

7-22.sanskrit:
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते।

लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान् हि तान्।।7.22।।
7-22.transliteration:
sa tayā śhraddhayā yuktas tasyārādhanam īhate
labhate cha tataḥ kāmān mayaiva vihitān hi tān

translation.simple: When a devotee, filled with heartfelt faith, worships their chosen divine form, they truly attain what their heart desires. Understand that these very blessings are lovingly arranged and given by Me, the ultimate divine source.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully explains that genuine faith, wherever it is placed, is always recognized by the Divine. A seeker might pray to a particular deity for their aspirations, yet it is I, the One Supreme Being, who orchestrates and grants those very wishes. It underscores that all paths of devotion, when sincere, are ultimately guided and fulfilled by Me.
translation.essence: All sincere devotion, regardless of its specific focus, is acknowledged and ultimately rewarded by the Supreme Lord, for He is the sole origin of all blessings.

7-23.sanskrit:
अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम्।

देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि।।7.23।।
7-23.transliteration:
antavat tu phalaṁ teṣhāṁ tad bhavatyalpa-medhasām
devān deva-yajo yānti mad-bhaktā yānti mām api

translation.simple: Understand, dear one, that the fruits desired by those with limited vision are always temporary. Those who worship lesser deities reach those deities, but My beloved devotees, they ultimately come to Me.
translation.deep: Reflect on the profound truth that all worldly achievements, however grand, have an end. When our devotion is directed towards temporary forms, our destination too remains within the temporary. But when the heart's true longing is for the Supreme, when devotion flows unconditionally to Me, the journey leads to an eternal embrace, a perpetual dwelling in the divine presence, beyond all cycles of birth and passing.
translation.essence: Seek Me with pure devotion, for all other paths lead to temporary destinations. Only My love grants eternal shelter.

7-24.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तं व्यक्ितमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः।

परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम्।।7.24।।
7-24.transliteration:
avyaktaṁ vyaktim āpannaṁ manyante mām abuddhayaḥ
paraṁ bhāvam ajānanto mamāvyayam anuttamam

translation.simple: People who lack deeper understanding often believe that I, the unmanifest and eternal Lord, have merely taken on a temporary human form. They do not know My supreme, unchanging, and peerless nature.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that our limited minds often try to comprehend the Divine within the confines of our own experiences. We might perceive the Lord in a particular form and mistakenly think that form defines His entirety. Yet, He reveals that His true being is infinitely beyond all temporary appearances – ever-present, imperishable, and of a supreme nature that is not fully grasped by mere intellectual reasoning, but by devotion and spiritual insight.
translation.essence: The Supreme Lord's true nature is eternal, unmanifest, and unsurpassed; His appearances are but expressions for our understanding, not His fundamental state of being.

7-25.sanskrit:
नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः।

मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम्।।7.25।।
7-25.transliteration:
nāhaṁ prakāśhaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyā-samāvṛitaḥ
mūḍho ’yaṁ nābhijānāti loko mām ajam avyayam

translation.simple: The Lord gently explains that He is not always visible to everyone, as He is veiled by His own divine, enchanting energy. Therefore, many in the world, caught in illusion, do not truly know Him as the eternal, never-changing reality.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly shares that His true, transcendental nature isn't openly visible to every eye. He is shielded by His own 'Yoga Maya,' a divine energy that gracefully veils Him from common perception. Because of this sacred mystery, many people, lost in worldly attachments, simply don't recognize Him as the timeless source, unborn and imperishable, who gently upholds all existence. It calls for a deeper heart to perceive His truth.
translation.essence: The Lord's eternal and unchanging nature is veiled by His divine energy, not immediately apparent to all. It requires a heart turned towards Him to truly recognize His unborn, imperishable reality.

7-26.sanskrit:
वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन।

भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन।।7.26।।
7-26.transliteration:
vedāhaṁ samatītāni vartamānāni chārjuna
bhaviṣhyāṇi cha bhūtāni māṁ tu veda na kaśhchana

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, I know every being from the very beginning, in this moment, and what is yet to come. Yet, no one truly knows Me in My complete divine nature.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna gently reminds Arjuna of His absolute knowledge, encompassing all of time – past, present, and future – for all living entities. He sees every moment, every life, every destiny. Yet, He reveals a profound mystery: His true, boundless essence remains beyond the full comprehension of anyone. This speaks to His supreme, unknowable nature, a realm of divine mystery that transcends all worldly understanding, accessible only through His grace.
translation.essence: The Divine Lord is the eternal Knower of all beings, across all time. Yet, His infinite essence remains a beautiful mystery, truly known only by His grace.

7-27.sanskrit:
इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत।

सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप।।7.27।।
7-27.transliteration:
ichchhā-dveṣha-samutthena dvandva-mohena bhārata
sarva-bhūtāni sammohaṁ sarge yānti parantapa

translation.simple: O Arjuna, from the very moment living beings come into existence, they are touched by a profound bewilderment. This confusion springs from the arising of desires and dislikes.
translation.deep: My dear Arjuna, contemplate this truth: all beings, from the moment of their manifestation in this world, find themselves enveloped in a deep illusion. This bewilderment is born from the potent energies of desire and aversion, which create the experience of dualities. These fundamental attractions and repulsions color our perception, subtly drawing us away from our true spiritual nature and into the complexities of the material realm.
translation.essence: At the heart of the matter, all beings are born into a state of spiritual confusion. This universal delusion is rooted in the interplay of desire and aversion, which shape our perception of reality.

7-28.sanskrit:
येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम्।

ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः।।7.28।।
7-28.transliteration:
yeṣhāṁ tvanta-gataṁ pāpaṁ janānāṁ puṇya-karmaṇām
te dvandva-moha-nirmuktā bhajante māṁ dṛiḍha-vratāḥ

translation.simple: When people commit virtuous actions and their past impurities are dissolved, they become free from the confusion caused by life's opposites like joy and sorrow. With firm dedication, they then come to worship Me.
translation.deep: For those devoted souls who consistently engage in pure and righteous deeds, the darkness of past errors naturally dissipates. This purification liberates them from the bewildering spell of worldly dualities – the pulls of pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor. With their minds clear and hearts resolute, they then dedicate their entire being to Me, steadfast in their spiritual commitment.
translation.essence: Virtuous living purifies the heart, frees one from dualities, and leads to unwavering devotion to the Divine.

7-29.sanskrit:
जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये।

ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम्।।7.29।।
7-29.transliteration:
jarā-maraṇa-mokṣhāya mām āśhritya yatanti ye
te brahma tadviduḥ kṛitsnam adhyātmaṁ karma chākhilam

translation.simple: Those who sincerely take refuge in Me and strive for liberation from the cycles of old age and death, truly come to know the Supreme Spirit, the divine inner self, and the complete nature of all actions.
translation.deep: When devoted seekers lovingly place their faith in Me, aspiring to transcend the worldly suffering of aging and mortality, their dedication unlocks a profound understanding. They come to grasp the Absolute Truth entirely, perceive the eternal spiritual essence within themselves (adhyātma), and comprehend the full scope and meaning of all actions (karma) in creation.
translation.essence: Taking refuge in the Divine and seeking freedom from impermanence grants complete knowledge of the Supreme, the inner spirit, and the true essence of every action.

7-30.sanskrit:
साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः।

प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः।।7.30।।
7-30.transliteration:
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṁ māṁ sādhiyajñaṁ cha ye viduḥ
prayāṇa-kāle ’pi cha māṁ te vidur yukta-chetasaḥ

translation.simple: Those who perceive Me as the essence of all creation, the indwelling spirit of the divine, and the ultimate receiver of all offerings, their hearts are firmly united with Me. With such unwavering devotion, they truly know Me, even in the final moments of life.
translation.deep: This profound verse teaches that the Divine is not separate but permeates every aspect of existence. When we recognize You, O Lord, as the very foundation of the perishable material world (adhibhūta), the governing consciousness behind all celestial forces (adhidaiva), and the ultimate recipient and purpose of every sacred act or sacrifice (adhiyajña) – then our connection deepens. Souls who cultivate such an unwavering, unified consciousness (yukta-chetasah) are blessed with the ultimate remembrance: they recall You, their beloved Divine, precisely at the critical moment of their transition from this world.
translation.essence: Cultivating the understanding that the Divine is present in all existence, divine principles, and acts of devotion leads to unwavering remembrance of the Lord, even at the moment of passing.

8-1.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम।

अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते।।8.1।।
8-1.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
kiṁ tad brahma kim adhyātmaṁ kiṁ karma puruṣhottama
adhibhūtaṁ cha kiṁ proktam adhidaivaṁ kim uchyate

translation.simple: Arjuna, with a gentle and seeking heart, approached the Lord and humbly asked, 'O Supreme Being, please enlighten me. What is that ultimate Reality, Brahman? What is the spiritual essence within us? What is pure action? And what is known as the material world, and what is the divine governing force?'
translation.deep: Here, Arjuna, with a heart truly yearning for wisdom, lays before Lord Krishna a series of fundamental inquiries. He wishes to know about the vast, ultimate Truth (Brahman), the indwelling spiritual self (Adhyatma), the essence of all our deeds (Karma), the changing nature of all beings (Adhibhuta), and the divine presence that guides the cosmos (Adhidaiva). These are not mere intellectual queries, but a humble seeking to understand the very core of reality and our place within it, aspiring to live in harmony with the divine.
translation.essence: With a humble and seeking heart, Arjuna turns to Lord Krishna, posing essential questions about the ultimate Reality, the spiritual self, the nature of actions, the material world, and the divine guiding principle, yearning for clarity on these truths.

8-2.sanskrit:
अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन।

प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः।।8.2।।
8-2.transliteration:
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṁ ko ’tra dehe ’smin madhusūdana
prayāṇa-kāle cha kathaṁ jñeyo ’si niyatātmabhiḥ

translation.simple: O Krishna, how is the Lord of sacrifice present within this very body? And for those with disciplined hearts, how can You be known at the sacred moment of leaving this world?
translation.deep: This verse opens a profound inquiry into the indwelling divine. Arjuna seeks to understand the presence of the Lord of sacrifice, not merely as an external deity, but as an intimate truth within our own being. He then probes the ultimate spiritual challenge: how does a soul, through self-mastery, truly perceive and connect with You, O Lord, when it's time to transition from this earthly form? It speaks to the culmination of a life lived in devotion and discipline.
translation.essence: Arjuna lovingly asks how the divine essence of sacrifice resides within us, and how we can perceive You, O Lord, with a tranquil heart at life's final moment.

8-3.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते।

भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः।।8.3।।
8-3.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
akṣharaṁ brahma paramaṁ svabhāvo ’dhyātmam uchyate
bhūta-bhāvodbhava-karo visargaḥ karma-sanjñitaḥ

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord said: The eternal, supreme truth is known as Brahman. Our innermost nature, our very soul, is called Adhyatma. The creative power that brings all living beings into existence is understood as karma.
translation.deep: The Supreme Lord lovingly reveals: That which is changeless and ultimate, beyond all destruction, is the Supreme Brahman. The inherent nature within each of us, our true spiritual essence, is called Adhyatma, the Self. And the divine creative outpouring, the very process that brings all beings forth into existence, is known as Karma, the unfolding action of creation itself.
translation.essence: This verse gently guides us to understand the fundamental truths: the imperishable Brahman as the ultimate reality, our inner spiritual essence as the Self (Adhyatma), and the cosmic creative force that gives rise to all beings as sacred action (Karma).

8-4.sanskrit:
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम्।

अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर।।8.4।।
8-4.transliteration:
adhibhūtaṁ kṣharo bhāvaḥ puruṣhaśh chādhidaivatam
adhiyajño ’ham evātra dehe deha-bhṛitāṁ vara

translation.simple: Lord Krishna explains that all material forms and creations are temporary and subject to change. The divine spirit, which illuminates all, is called *adhidaivata*. And O best among embodied beings, He lovingly assures us that He Himself is *adhiyajña*, the Lord of all sacrifices, dwelling right within our bodies.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that everything we perceive in the material world is fleeting. While the universal spirit governs the divine realm, the most profound truth revealed here is the Lord's intimate presence within us. He says, 'I am *adhiyajña* within this body.' This means that every action we perform, when offered with devotion and a sense of duty, becomes a sacred act. He is the inner witness and recipient, the very essence that makes our spiritual endeavors meaningful and complete.
translation.essence: The Lord teaches that material existence is temporary, and the divine spirit governs the celestial. Most beautifully, He assures us that He Himself, as the supreme recipient of all offerings, resides within our own bodies, making every sincere action a direct and powerful connection to Him.

8-5.sanskrit:
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम्।

यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः।।8.5।।
8-5.transliteration:
anta-kāle cha mām eva smaran muktvā kalevaram
yaḥ prayāti sa mad-bhāvaṁ yāti nāstyatra sanśhayaḥ

translation.simple: When the time comes to leave this earthly body, if one remembers Me alone with a devoted heart, they will surely come to My divine abode. This is a truth beyond all doubt.
translation.deep: This verse reveals the profound power of our final thoughts. When a soul departs from its earthly vessel, having held My divine form and name in remembrance, it naturally transcends to My supreme state. This is not merely a momentary act but a culmination of a life steeped in devotion, where the mind has been trained to turn towards the Divine. Such a soul sheds all worldly attachments and merges with My eternal essence, a truth that offers ultimate solace and direction for all spiritual seekers.
translation.essence: At the final breath, remembering the Divine ensures a direct journey to God's own eternal nature. This is a profound and certain truth.

8-6.sanskrit:
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम्।

तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः।।8.6।।
8-6.transliteration:
yaṁ yaṁ vāpi smaran bhāvaṁ tyajatyante kalevaram
taṁ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ

translation.simple: My dear one, whatever thoughts and feelings fill our heart as we gently leave this body, that is the very realm our soul will enter. For our inner state is always shaped by what we have lovingly contemplated.
translation.deep: This sacred verse reveals a profound spiritual truth: our journey beyond this life is a direct reflection of our consciousness, deeply imbued by what we consistently cherish and remember. It gently teaches us the importance of cultivating divine thoughts and loving remembrance daily, preparing our soul for a blessed transition to that cherished ideal.
translation.essence: Cultivate loving thoughts and divine remembrance always, for they gently guide your soul's journey at life's tender close.

8-7.transliteration:
tasmāt sarveṣhu kāleṣhu mām anusmara yudhya cha
mayyarpita-mano-buddhir mām evaiṣhyasyasanśhayam

translation.simple: Therefore, always remember Me, and continue to perform your duties. With your mind and understanding fixed on Me, you will certainly attain Me.
translation.deep: This verse offers a gentle yet profound path: to continuously remember the Divine amidst all of life's engagements. It teaches that true devotion is not about withdrawing, but about infusing every action with awareness of the Supreme. By offering our thoughts and intellect to the Lord, we naturally align ourselves with His presence, ensuring our spiritual journey leads directly to Him, without any shadow of doubt.
translation.essence: Remember the Divine always, fulfill your duties, and with your entire being dedicated to Him, you will undoubtedly reach Him.

8-8.sanskrit:
अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना।

परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन्।।8.8।।
8-8.transliteration:
abhyāsa-yoga-yuktena chetasā nānya-gāminā
paramaṁ puruṣhaṁ divyaṁ yāti pārthānuchintayan

translation.simple: Keep your heart engaged in loving practice, not letting it wander. By constantly remembering the Supreme Divine Being, O Arjuna, you will reach Him.
translation.deep: This verse reveals the profound path to the Divine, O Arjuna. When your mind is carefully trained through consistent spiritual discipline, making it unwavering and focused, and you then gently meditate upon the Supreme, the effulgent Divine Being, you will certainly attain that ultimate union with Him.
translation.essence: Through loving practice and an unwavering heart, continuously remembering the Divine is the gentle path to reach the Supreme.

8-9.sanskrit:
कविं पुराणमनुशासितार

मणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः।

सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूप

मादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात्।।8.9।।
8-9.transliteration:
kaviṁ purāṇam anuśhāsitāram
aṇor aṇīyānsam anusmared yaḥ
sarvasya dhātāram achintya-rūpam
āditya-varṇaṁ tamasaḥ parastāt

translation.simple: Always remember the Ancient One, who knows all and lovingly guides us. He is smaller than the smallest particle, yet He sustains everything in existence. His divine form is beyond our comprehension, shining with the brilliance of the sun, far removed from all shadows and darkness.
translation.deep: One should continuously meditate upon the Divine, who is the timeless Seer, the supreme administrator of the universe. He is infinitely subtler than the atom, yet He is the very foundation and sustainer of all creation. His sacred form is truly beyond human conception, radiating a light like that of a thousand suns, completely transcending the realm of material darkness and ignorance. Dwell on this Supreme Being with devotion.
translation.essence: Meditate on the all-knowing, ancient Divine Guide, subtler than the smallest, the sustainer of all, whose inconceivable form shines like the sun, eternally beyond darkness.

8-10.sanskrit:
प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेन

भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव।

भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक्

स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम्।।8.10।।
8-10.transliteration:
prayāṇa-kāle manasāchalena
bhaktyā yukto yoga-balena chaiva
bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśhya samyak
sa taṁ paraṁ puruṣham upaiti divyam

translation.simple: When the time of leaving this body arrives, if your mind is unwavering and full of pure devotion, and you gently focus your life-breath between the eyebrows with spiritual strength, you will surely attain that supreme and divine Being.
translation.deep: This profound verse speaks to the sacred moment of transition, guiding a devotee to prepare consciously. It emphasizes that a mind unshakeable in its spiritual resolve, coupled with profound love (bhakti) for the Divine, and supported by the inner strength cultivated through yoga, is paramount. By delicately centering the life-force (Prana) at the spiritual point between the eyebrows, one can achieve a serene and conscious departure, leading to a glorious union with the Supreme Divine, the ultimate source of all light and bliss.
translation.essence: An unwavering mind, deep devotion, and focused life-breath at the time of passing lead the devotee to attain the Supreme Divine.

8-11.sanskrit:
यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति

विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः।

यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति

तत्ते पदं संग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये।।8.11।।
8-11.transliteration:
yad akṣharaṁ veda-vido vadanti
viśhanti yad yatayo vīta-rāgāḥ
yad ichchhanto brahmacharyaṁ charanti
tat te padaṁ saṅgraheṇa pravakṣhye

translation.simple: The wise, who understand the ancient scriptures, speak of an imperishable reality. Dedicated souls, freed from worldly attachments, find their way into this very truth. Spiritual seekers, longing for this supreme state, live lives of self-control and devotion. Lord Krishna promises, 'I shall now briefly tell you about this precious goal.'
translation.deep: This verse reveals the ultimate reality, referred to as the imperishable, which wise souls across ages have glorified in the Vedas. It is the sacred haven into which devout seekers, having gently released all worldly cravings, lovingly enter. It is the supreme aspiration that inspires a life of pure discipline and devotion, a journey towards divine oneness. Lord Krishna, with boundless compassion, promises to reveal this sublime goal, offering a brief yet profound glimpse into this highest spiritual abode.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna will lovingly reveal the imperishable, ultimate spiritual truth—the cherished goal of the wise, the detached, and the devoted.

8-12.sanskrit:
सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च।

मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम्।।8.12।।
8-12.transliteration:
sarva-dvārāṇi sanyamya mano hṛidi nirudhya cha
mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇam āsthito yoga-dhāraṇām

translation.simple: Drawing all the senses inward from their outward pursuits, one then steadies the mind within the sanctuary of the heart. Gently lifting the life-breath to the crown of the head, one becomes deeply centered in this yogic meditation.
translation.deep: This verse illuminates a profound path of inner discipline. It speaks of consciously drawing our senses away from external distractions, turning our focus inward. The restless mind, often swayed by worldly currents, is then gently brought to rest within the quiet sanctuary of the heart. As this inner stillness deepens, the vital life-energy is reverently guided upwards towards the crown, a journey of ascending consciousness. In such a deeply absorbed state of yogic concentration, the soul prepares itself for its ultimate union with the Divine.
translation.essence: This verse guides us to master our inner world: to withdraw our senses, quiet our mind in the heart, and elevate our life-force, finding deep spiritual focus and preparing for divine connection.

8-13.sanskrit:
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन्।

यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम्।।8.13।।
8-13.transliteration:
oṁ ityekākṣharaṁ brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran
yaḥ prayāti tyajan dehaṁ sa yāti paramāṁ gatim

translation.simple: When a soul leaves their body, uttering the sacred sound 'Om' – which represents the eternal Divine – and keeping Me (the Lord) in their memory, they surely attain the supreme spiritual dwelling.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse gently guides us on the profound significance of our final moments. By focusing our mind on the singular sound 'Om,' which embodies the very essence of the Absolute Truth, and by holding a loving remembrance of the Divine within our heart as we depart from this earthly form, we ensure a serene and blessed passage to the highest spiritual realm. It reminds us that a life lived in constant remembrance prepares us for this ultimate, peaceful journey.
translation.essence: Chanting 'Om' and remembering the Divine at life's end leads one to the supreme spiritual abode.

8-14.sanskrit:
अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः।

तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः।।8.14।।
8-14.transliteration:
ananya-chetāḥ satataṁ yo māṁ smarati nityaśhaḥ
tasyāhaṁ sulabhaḥ pārtha nitya-yuktasya yoginaḥ

translation.simple: Lord Krishna promises, "To the one whose mind is solely fixed on Me, remembering Me always with devotion, I am very easy to attain. For such a soul, constantly connected to Me, I am always near and accessible."
translation.deep: This beautiful verse unveils a profound path to spiritual intimacy. When a seeker's heart and mind are wholly dedicated to remembering the Divine, without distraction or wavering, then the Lord's presence becomes not a distant ideal but an ever-present reality. This constant, loving remembrance is the very essence of true yoga, making the Supreme Spirit effortlessly accessible to the devotee whose soul is perpetually united with Him in devotion. It's a sacred promise of divine closeness through unwavering love.
translation.essence: A heart solely devoted to the Divine, remembering Him always, will find Him effortlessly near. Such constant remembrance is the path to immediate divine presence.

8-15.sanskrit:
मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम्।

नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः।।8.15।।
8-15.transliteration:
mām upetya punar janma duḥkhālayam aśhāśhvatam
nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ sansiddhiṁ paramāṁ gatāḥ

translation.simple: Pure souls, having truly come to Me, no longer experience rebirth in this fleeting world, which is a temporary home of sorrows. They have found the highest spiritual perfection.
translation.deep: Those great and elevated souls who achieve true union with Me transcend the cycle of repeated birth and death. They are freed from returning to this impermanent realm, which is inherently an abode of transient suffering, having attained the ultimate spiritual realization and supreme liberation.
translation.essence: Reaching Me, pure souls escape the cycle of sorrowful rebirth, achieving lasting peace and the highest perfection.

8-16.sanskrit:
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन।

मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते।।8.16।।
8-16.transliteration:
ā-brahma-bhuvanāl lokāḥ punar āvartino ’rjuna
mām upetya tu kaunteya punar janma na vidyate

translation.simple: O Arjuna, all worlds, even the highest abodes, are places where souls experience repeated birth and return. But for those who truly come to Me, O son of Kunti, there is no more returning to this world.
translation.deep: My dear Arjuna, contemplate that all realms of existence, even the most sublime, are temporary. Beings dwelling there are still bound by the law of time, experiencing cycles of creation and dissolution, birth and passing. But when a soul, with sincere devotion, attains My presence, O Kaunteya, it transcends these endless cycles. Such a soul reaches an eternal state, liberated from the necessity of ever being born again in the material world.
translation.essence: All worldly realms are cyclical, O Arjuna. But by attaining Me, O Kaunteya, one transcends all returning and finds eternal freedom from rebirth.

8-17.sanskrit:
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः।

रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः।।8.17।।
8-17.transliteration:
sahasra-yuga-paryantam ahar yad brahmaṇo viduḥ
rātriṁ yuga-sahasrāntāṁ te ’ho-rātra-vido janāḥ

translation.simple: Imagine a day for the creator, Brahma, lasting a thousand human ages, and His night extending for a thousand ages too. Those who truly understand this profound measure of time are the ones who truly know what day and night mean.
translation.deep: This verse gently unveils the vastness of divine time. When we learn that Brahma's single day and night each encompass a thousand ages, our perception of time shifts dramatically. It's a call to reflect on the immense cycles of creation and dissolution, reminding us that all material forms appear and disappear within these grand rhythms. This profound insight helps us cultivate detachment from the temporary, guiding our hearts towards the eternal reality that transcends all temporal bounds.
translation.essence: Understanding that Brahma's day and night each span a thousand ages grants us a glimpse into the boundless expanse of cosmic time. It's a gentle reminder of the infinite cycles of the universe and the wisdom in recognizing what truly endures beyond all temporary phases.

8-18.sanskrit:
अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे।

रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके।।8.18।।
8-18.transliteration:
avyaktād vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavantyahar-āgame
rātryāgame pralīyante tatraivāvyakta-sanjñake

translation.simple: With the dawn of a new cosmic day, all that is manifest and seen comes forth from a subtle, unmanifest source. And as the cosmic night descends, everything quietly returns to that same unseen state.
translation.deep: The Lord reveals the magnificent, eternal rhythm of creation and dissolution. All manifest beings, all that we perceive, gracefully emerge from a subtle, unmanifest state with the arrival of a cosmic day. They manifest, live, and then, at the coming of the cosmic night, gently merge back into that very same unmanifest source. This profound cycle, orchestrated by the Supreme, underscores the transient nature of the material world, always rooted in the eternal.
translation.essence: All that is manifest emerges from the unmanifest and dissolves back into it, following the divine cosmic rhythm. This cycle beautifully reminds us that everything we perceive is a temporary expression of an eternal, hidden source.

8-19.sanskrit:
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते।

रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे।।8.19।।
8-19.transliteration:
bhūta-grāmaḥ sa evāyaṁ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate
rātryāgame ’vaśhaḥ pārtha prabhavatyahar-āgame

translation.simple: Beloved Arjuna, all beings come into existence and then peacefully return to the unmanifest. When a new day dawns, they emerge again, and with the arrival of night, they gently fade away. This happens by a higher will, not their own.
translation.deep: This sacred verse unveils the profound, ceaseless rhythm of the cosmos. All manifest beings, O Arjuna, emerge into existence and then dissolve back into an unmanifest state, repeatedly. It is not by their own desire but by the grand design of the Divine that they appear with the dawn of a cosmic day and gently withdraw when the cosmic night descends. This continuous cycle reminds us of the temporary nature of all forms and the eternal, unchanging consciousness that beautifully orchestrates this entire cosmic play.
translation.essence: The heart of this teaching is the eternal, compassionate cycle of manifestation and dissolution. All beings appear and withdraw, not by their own accord, but by the gentle, unwavering will of the Divine. It's a reminder of the fleeting nature of all forms within the grand, eternal rhythm of existence, guided by the Supreme.

8-20.sanskrit:
परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः।

यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति।।8.20।।
8-20.transliteration:
paras tasmāt tu bhāvo ’nyo ’vyakto ’vyaktāt sanātanaḥ
yaḥ sa sarveṣhu bhūteṣhu naśhyatsu na vinaśhyati

translation.simple: Beyond all that is manifest and even the subtle, unmanifest state that appears and disappears, there is another divine nature. This everlasting reality does not perish, even when all other beings and worlds fade away.
translation.deep: The scriptures speak of a cosmic unmanifest state, which itself is subject to the cycles of creation and dissolution. Yet, transcending even this, lies a supreme, eternal unmanifest reality—the very imperishable nature of the Divine. This ultimate existence remains untouched by the passing of all material forms and worlds, standing eternally radiant and unchanging, a timeless sanctuary for the soul.
translation.essence: There exists an eternal, divine nature, distinct from all changing forms and temporary unmanifest states of creation. It is the ever-present reality that never perishes, offering true and everlasting peace.

8-21.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम्।

यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम।।8.21।।
8-21.transliteration:
avyakto ’kṣhara ityuktas tam āhuḥ paramāṁ gatim
yaṁ prāpya na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama

translation.simple: The Lord is called the Unseen, the Everlasting One, and He is the ultimate destination. Once you reach Him, you never have to come back to this world. Truly, that is My highest dwelling place.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna reveals His eternal nature as Unmanifest and Imperishable, a reality beyond our senses, yet ever-present. This is the supreme destination, dear seeker, where the soul finds ultimate freedom. To attain this state means liberation from the cycle of rebirth, a permanent communion with the Divine. It is My most sacred abode, a sanctuary of perfect peace and unchanging joy, from which no one ever returns.
translation.essence: Seek the Unseen, the Imperishable, for that is the ultimate goal. Attain My supreme abode and find eternal freedom, never to return to this transient world, dwelling in everlasting peace.

8-22.sanskrit:
पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया।

यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।।8.22।।
8-22.transliteration:
puruṣhaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyas tvananyayā
yasyāntaḥ-sthāni bhūtāni yena sarvam idaṁ tatam

translation.simple: O Partha, that Supreme Being is attained through unwavering, exclusive devotion. All beings reside within Him, and He pervades this entire universe.
translation.deep: Here, Lord Krishna reveals the profound truth about the ultimate reality. The Supreme Person, though seemingly distant, is intimately accessible through a pure and undivided heart. This means turning our love and focus solely towards Him, free from other desires. He is the very ground of existence, the gentle embrace within which all of creation finds its place, and simultaneously, He expands and permeates every single atom and space within this vast universe. To seek Him with such devotion is to realize our deepest connection to all that is.
translation.essence: The Supreme Lord, the home of all beings and the very fabric of the universe, is reached only through single-pointed, loving devotion.

8-23.sanskrit:
यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः।

प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ।।8.23।।
8-23.transliteration:
yatra kāle tvanāvṛittim āvṛittiṁ chaiva yoginaḥ
prayātā yānti taṁ kālaṁ vakṣhyāmi bharatarṣhabha

translation.simple: Lord Krishna gently tells Arjuna that He will now reveal the secrets of the journey after life. He will speak of those special times when devoted souls depart, some to reach a state where they never return, and others to come back again.
translation.deep: In this verse, the Lord prepares to unveil profound truths about the soul's journey after leaving the body. He speaks of two distinct paths, determined by the time and state of departure. For the yogi, understanding these divine timings and states is key to realizing whether their journey leads to ultimate liberation, a complete union with the Divine, or to another cycle of earthly existence, guided by the loving hand of the cosmos.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna promises to reveal the sacred timings and paths that decide a departed soul's destiny – either eternal freedom or a gentle return to the world, all part of His divine plan.

8-24.sanskrit:
अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम्।

तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः।।8.24।।
8-24.transliteration:
agnir jyotir ahaḥ śhuklaḥ ṣhaṇ-māsā uttarāyaṇam
tatra prayātā gachchhanti brahma brahma-vido janāḥ

translation.simple: When a soul, truly knowing the Divine, departs during moments of light—like bright days or the sun's auspicious northern journey—they gently ascend to merge with the Supreme Truth, finding eternal peace.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse unfolds a profound truth about liberation. It gently suggests that true freedom isn't merely about the cosmic timings of departure, but rather the purified inner state of the soul. The mention of 'fire,' 'light,' 'day,' and the 'northern journey' beautifully symbolize a consciousness illuminated by deep spiritual understanding and devotion. For those who have truly realized Brahman, the Absolute, their final journey is gracefully guided by this internal radiance, leading them to a complete and everlasting union with the Divine, forever beyond the cycle of rebirth. It speaks to a path where inner light guides the soul home.
translation.essence: The essence is that souls truly devoted to and enlightened by the Supreme Reality embark on a path of divine light upon departure, achieving serene and ultimate union with the Absolute Truth, never to return.

8-25.sanskrit:
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम्।

तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते।।8.25।।
8-25.transliteration:
dhūmo rātris tathā kṛiṣhṇaḥ ṣhaṇ-māsā dakṣhiṇāyanam
tatra chāndramasaṁ jyotir yogī prāpya nivartate

translation.simple: When a soul departs during times associated with smoke, night, the dark lunar fortnight, or the sun's southern journey, it reaches a temporary luminous realm, like that of the moon. From there, it gently returns to this world of existence.
translation.deep: This verse tenderly speaks of a path followed by souls whose actions lead them to temporary celestial abodes. Should one depart when the influence of smoke, night, the dark lunar cycle, or the sun's southward journey is prominent, they ascend to realms illumined by the moon's gentle light. These are beautiful destinations earned through pious deeds, yet they are not the ultimate freedom. After experiencing those joys, the soul lovingly returns to the cycle of life and rebirth, continuing its journey toward eventual liberation.
translation.essence: The core teaching here is that all temporary paths, even those leading to celestial comfort, ultimately bring the soul back to the earthly journey. True peace and liberation come from transcending all temporary realms, seeking the eternal, unchanging Divine.

8-26.sanskrit:
शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते।

एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः।।8.26।।
8-26.transliteration:
śhukla-kṛiṣhṇe gatī hyete jagataḥ śhāśhvate mate
ekayā yātyanāvṛittim anyayāvartate punaḥ

translation.simple: My dear friend, there are two ancient paths souls can take in this world. One path, filled with light, leads to a blessed state from which you never return to earthly cycles. The other path, though it may seem dim, brings you back again to continue your journey. These paths are always here for us.
translation.deep: Beloved one, the sacred wisdom reveals two everlasting journeys for all beings in this cosmos. The radiant path, illuminated by divine understanding and loving devotion, guides a soul to ultimate liberation—a profound union with the Divine where the cycle of rebirth ceases. This is a journey into eternal peace and true freedom. Conversely, the other path, often characterized by worldly attachments and desires, leads one back to experience life again, to learn and grow further. Our inner alignment, our prayers, and our every action gently guide us towards one of these timeless ways.
translation.essence: Two eternal paths await the soul: one leads to liberation, never to return; the other brings one back to worldly existence. Our choices guide us.

8-27.sanskrit:
नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन।

तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन।।8.27।।
8-27.transliteration:
naite sṛitī pārtha jānan yogī muhyati kaśhchana
tasmāt sarveṣhu kāleṣhu yoga-yukto bhavārjuna

translation.simple: O Arjuna, one who truly comprehends these two paths is never bewildered. Therefore, always keep yourself firmly connected through yoga.
translation.deep: By understanding the nature of these two journeys—the path of light leading to freedom and the path of darkness leading back to worldly life—a spiritual seeker, O Partha, finds profound clarity and peace. Let your heart and mind, therefore, remain always united with the Divine, cultivating this sacred connection in every moment.
translation.essence: Knowing the spiritual paths brings unwavering clarity. Thus, always remain steadfastly united with the Divine.

8-28.sanskrit:
वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव

दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम्।

अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा

योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम्।।8.28।।
8-28.transliteration:
vedeṣhu yajñeṣhu tapaḥsu chaiva
dāneṣhu yat puṇya-phalaṁ pradiṣhṭam
atyeti tat sarvam idaṁ viditvā
yogī paraṁ sthānam upaiti chādyam

translation.simple: When a soul truly understands this sacred wisdom, they move beyond the rewards promised for studying holy scriptures, performing sacred rituals, practicing austerities, or giving generously. Such a devoted one attains the ultimate, eternal dwelling place.
translation.deep: One who grasps the profound spiritual truth revealed here—the understanding of the direct path to the Divine—rises above all the accumulated merits of Vedic studies, grand sacrifices, rigorous penances, and acts of charity. This dedicated seeker, a true yogi, journeys to that supreme, primordial abode, a state of perfect union and unending tranquility.
translation.essence: Embracing this spiritual knowledge allows a devotee to transcend the fruits of all good deeds, guiding them directly to the supreme, eternal home with the Lord.

9-1.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे।

ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्।।9.1।।
9-1.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
idaṁ tu te guhyatamaṁ pravakṣhyāmyanasūyave
jñānaṁ vijñāna-sahitaṁ yaj jñātvā mokṣhyase ’śhubhāt

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord said: To you, who bear no ill will, I will now share the most profound secret. This divine wisdom, both in understanding and in experience, will truly set you free from all troubles.
translation.deep: The Supreme Lord spoke: To you, who are free from any fault-finding spirit, I shall now declare the most confidential spiritual knowledge. This sacred truth, understood conceptually and realized through devoted practice, is truly liberating. By embracing it, you will certainly transcend all that is inauspicious and find lasting peace.
translation.essence: The Lord promises to reveal the deepest, most secret wisdom to a sincere heart. This divine knowledge, once truly comprehended and lived, brings liberation from all misfortune and suffering.

9-2.sanskrit:
राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम्।

प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम्।।9.2।।
9-2.transliteration:
rāja-vidyā rāja-guhyaṁ pavitram idam uttamam
pratyakṣhāvagamaṁ dharmyaṁ su-sukhaṁ kartum avyayam

translation.simple: This sacred wisdom is the highest knowledge, the most precious secret. It is wonderfully pure and supreme. You can directly feel its truth, it leads to righteousness, and it's joyful and easy to practice, bringing everlasting peace.
translation.deep: Behold this divine teaching, celebrated as the sovereign knowledge and the most profound secret. It holds the power to purify the heart entirely, guiding one to the highest spiritual truth. Its reality is not just a concept, but something you can directly perceive and experience within yourself. Rooted in eternal righteousness, its practice brings immense joy and an effortless sense of peace. The blessings it bestows are imperishable, offering an eternal connection to the Divine.
translation.essence: This supreme wisdom, the king of knowledge and secrets, deeply purifies the soul. It is directly experienced, righteous, joyful, and eternally beneficial.

9-3.sanskrit:
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप।

अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि।।9.3।।
9-3.transliteration:
aśhraddadhānāḥ puruṣhā dharmasyāsya parantapa
aprāpya māṁ nivartante mṛityu-samsāra-vartmani

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, those souls who lack sincere faith in this divine path do not truly find Me. Instead, they continue on the path of birth, death, and worldly cycles.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us, O Arjuna, that faith (shraddha) is a vital key. Without a deep and earnest belief in the spiritual principles and the divine teachings, a soul cannot truly connect with the Supreme Being. Without this connection, one remains bound to the recurring journey of material existence, experiencing its cycles of coming and going, birth and death, unable to break free into the eternal embrace of the Divine.
translation.essence: The Lord teaches that unwavering faith in the spiritual journey is the very heart of finding Him. Without this sacred trust, a soul continues its worldly wanderings, bound by the cycle of life and death, ever longing for that ultimate union.

9-4.sanskrit:
मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना।

मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः।।9.4।।
9-4.transliteration:
mayā tatam idaṁ sarvaṁ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā
mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na chāhaṁ teṣhvavasthitaḥ

translation.simple: My unseen presence gracefully fills this entire universe. All beings find their existence within Me, yet I am not confined by their forms.
translation.deep: My divine essence, though unmanifest, lovingly pervades every corner of this creation. All beings draw their very life and rest within My being. Yet, My true nature is boundless; I am never limited or held by the individual forms they assume, remaining eternally transcendent.
translation.essence: I am the subtle, all-pervading spirit, the support of all existence, yet I remain ever-free and beyond all manifestation.

9-5.sanskrit:
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्।

भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः।।9.5।।
9-5.transliteration:
na cha mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśhya me yogam aiśhwaram
bhūta-bhṛin na cha bhūta-stho mamātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ

translation.simple: The Lord reveals a beautiful mystery: 'Though all beings come from Me, they do not truly rest *within* Me in a limiting way, nor am I contained by them. Behold My unique divine power! I am the one who sustains all creation, yet My spirit remains ever free and distinct, the loving source of all that exists.'
translation.deep: Here, the Lord lovingly reveals a profound truth about His own nature. He explains that while all of existence emanates from Him and finds its support in Him, He is never confined or limited by it. This is His divine and wondrous power, a mystery beyond human grasp. He is the ultimate sustainer, holding all beings within His cosmic vision, yet His own spiritual essence remains ever free, untouched, and distinct from all He creates. He is the gentle source of all life, yet forever transcendental.
translation.essence: The essence of this verse reveals the Lord's awe-inspiring nature: He is the loving origin and eternal sustainer of all creation. He holds everything in existence, yet His divine Self remains ever free, distinct, and untouched by it, a beautiful paradox of His infinite power.

9-6.sanskrit:
यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान्।

तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय।।9.6।।
9-6.transliteration:
yathākāśha-sthito nityaṁ vāyuḥ sarvatra-go mahān
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni mat-sthānītyupadhāraya

translation.simple: Just as the boundless air, though moving everywhere, always rests within the vastness of the sky, know with certainty that all beings gently reside within My divine presence.
translation.deep: This sacred verse tenderly reveals the profound truth of the Divine's all-encompassing embrace. Just as the air, though constantly moving and permeating all, rests eternally within the vastness of the sky, so too, all creation, every living being, finds its gentle repose and existence within the Supreme Self. It speaks of an intimate connection where everything is held within God, yet He remains untouched and distinct, a beautiful mystery of both immanence and transcendence.
translation.essence: The serene truth is that all of creation, in every moment, finds its gentle dwelling and sustenance within the boundless love and presence of the Supreme Lord, just as the air always abides within the vast, open sky.

9-7.sanskrit:
सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम्।

कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम्।।9.7।।
9-7.transliteration:
sarva-bhūtāni kaunteya prakṛitiṁ yānti māmikām
kalpa-kṣhaye punas tāni kalpādau visṛijāmyaham

translation.simple: O Arjuna, at the end of each vast cosmic cycle, all beings gently return to My own material nature. And when a new cycle begins, it is I who lovingly bring them forth once more.
translation.deep: Understand, Arjuna, that at the close of a cosmic epoch, all manifest beings dissolve and merge back into My divine material energy, which is an emanation of My very being. This is a peaceful re-absorption, not an end. Then, as a new cosmic dawn breaks, I effortlessly manifest them again, initiating their renewed journey within the material realm.
translation.essence: The Lord orchestrates the eternal dance of creation and dissolution. All beings return to Him at the end of a cosmic cycle, only to be lovingly brought forth again by His will when the next cycle begins.

9-8.sanskrit:
प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः।

भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात्।।9.8।।
9-8.transliteration:
prakṛitiṁ svām avaṣhṭabhya visṛijāmi punaḥ punaḥ
bhūta-grāmam imaṁ kṛitsnam avaśhaṁ prakṛiter vaśhāt

translation.simple: From My own divine nature, I continually bring forth all living beings. They emerge into existence again and again, guided by the influence of nature's energies, beyond their own will.
translation.deep: Embracing My own spiritual essence, I repeatedly manifest this entire assembly of beings. They come into existence again and again, bound by the inherent laws of material nature, not by their own independent will, revealing My sublime power orchestrating all creation through My divine Prakriti.
