translation.essence: The Lord continually manifests all life through His divine nature, a beautiful cycle where beings emerge, guided by the gentle flow of cosmic forces.

9-9.sanskrit:
न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय।

उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु।।9.9।।
9-9.transliteration:
na cha māṁ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya
udāsīna-vad āsīnam asaktaṁ teṣhu karmasu

translation.simple: O Arjuna, none of these actions truly bind Me. I simply remain, like one observing from afar, without any attachment to the deeds themselves.
translation.deep: Even as the cosmos unfolds through My power, Arjuna, I am never entangled by these activities. My divine presence is like an unmoving witness, untouched by the consequences of creation. This reveals the profound truth of performing duty with a pure heart, free from the desire for results, thus remaining ever liberated.
translation.essence: God's actions are always free from binding, for Divinity remains ever detached, a silent, serene presence amidst all activity.

9-10.sanskrit:
मयाऽध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम्।

हेतुनाऽनेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते।।9.10।।
9-10.transliteration:
mayādhyakṣheṇa prakṛitiḥ sūyate sa-charācharam
hetunānena kaunteya jagad viparivartate

translation.simple: Under My watchful eye, nature brings forth all that moves and all that is still. Because of My presence, O Arjuna, the entire world continues its dance of creation and change.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna tenderly assures us that while material nature brings forth the vast universe and all its beings, it does so solely under His loving supervision. His divine presence is the very reason all creation unfolds and continuously moves. He is the quiet director behind every sunrise, every blossoming flower, and every heartbeat. This deep truth offers immense comfort, reminding us that an all-wise and benevolent consciousness gently guides the entire cosmos.
translation.essence: The entire creation, in all its forms, functions and evolves under the gentle and constant guidance of the Divine.

9-11.sanskrit:
अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम्।

परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम्।।9.11।।
9-11.transliteration:
avajānanti māṁ mūḍhā mānuṣhīṁ tanum āśhritam
paraṁ bhāvam ajānanto mama bhūta-maheśhvaram

translation.simple: When I choose to appear in a human form, some souls, due to their limited vision, fail to recognize My ultimate divine nature. They do not comprehend that I am the Supreme Lord of all beings, the source and sustainer of everything, even when I walk among them in a seemingly ordinary body.
translation.deep: It is a profound challenge for human consciousness to perceive the Absolute when it manifests in a relatable, human body. Souls that haven't awakened to deeper spiritual wisdom might dismiss this human form, unknowingly missing the ultimate reality of My being – the supreme Controller and Source of all life, whose divine essence permeates everything, even a simple human form.
translation.essence: The true wisdom lies in looking beyond outward appearances. Even when the Divine takes a human form, the Supreme Lord of all beings is still present, waiting to be recognized by a pure and discerning heart.

9-12.sanskrit:
मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः।

राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः।।9.12।।
9-12.transliteration:
moghāśhā mogha-karmāṇo mogha-jñānā vichetasaḥ
rākṣhasīm āsurīṁ chaiva prakṛitiṁ mohinīṁ śhritāḥ

translation.simple: When our hopes are set on transient things, our actions are not aligned with higher purpose, and our wisdom remains superficial, the mind becomes confused. Such individuals often adopt a nature that is ungodly and deluding, moving away from spiritual clarity.
translation.deep: This sacred verse invites us to contemplate the very essence of our existence. If our deepest desires are fleeting, our efforts aim at hollow victories, and our wisdom fails to recognize the divine, then our inner self becomes confused. In this state, one tends to embody tendencies that are ungodly and inherently misleading, keeping the soul bound in illusion instead of guiding it towards the ever-present light.
translation.essence: When our aspirations, efforts, and insights are disconnected from the Divine, the heart is led astray, embracing a nature that is deluding and unspiritual.

9-13.sanskrit:
महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः।

भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम्।।9.13।।
9-13.transliteration:
mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha daivīṁ prakṛitim āśhritāḥ
bhajantyananya-manaso jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam

translation.simple: O Arjuna, those noble souls who take refuge in My divine nature, worship Me with unwavering devotion. They understand that I am the eternal source from which all beings emerge.
translation.deep: These profound souls, having embraced the divine aspect of creation, naturally turn their hearts to Me. Their worship is unwavering because they truly know Me as the eternal, imperishable source of all existence. This deep realization allows their minds to remain singularly devoted, finding ultimate solace and purpose in My divine presence.
translation.essence: Great souls, anchored in divine nature, worship the eternal, imperishable source of all beings with single-pointed devotion.

9-14.sanskrit:
सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः।

नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते।।9.14।।
9-14.transliteration:
satataṁ kīrtayanto māṁ yatantaśh cha dṛiḍha-vratāḥ
namasyantaśh cha māṁ bhaktyā nitya-yuktā upāsate

translation.simple: With unwavering devotion, they constantly sing My praises, strive with firm resolve, and humbly bow before Me. Always connected to Me, they worship with pure hearts.
translation.deep: With deep reverence, these devoted souls constantly vocalize My glories and strive with unwavering commitment on their spiritual path. They humbly offer their prostrations, brimming with love and adoration. Such souls remain ever absorbed in Me, and their worship is a continuous, beautiful expression of their eternal connection.
translation.essence: The true devotee's path is marked by ceaseless glorification of the Divine, persistent spiritual effort, and heartfelt reverence. Their worship is an ongoing, loving connection, an unbroken union with the Lord.

9-15.sanskrit:
ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते।

एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम्।।9.15।।
9-15.transliteration:
jñāna-yajñena chāpyanye yajanto mām upāsate
ekatvena pṛithaktvena bahudhā viśhvato-mukham

translation.simple: Some devoted souls offer their wisdom and understanding as a sacrifice, thus worshipping Me. They may see Me as one with all creation, or as distinct and supreme, or in countless forms spread throughout the universe, present everywhere.
translation.deep: Through the sacred offering of spiritual knowledge, many seekers find their way to Me. Some realize Me as the singular, unified Self residing within all beings, while others perceive My distinct and transcendent divine nature. Still others, with a vast and expansive heart, adore Me in myriad manifestations, recognizing My universal form that encompasses all directions and all forms, the One whose divine face is seen everywhere.
translation.essence: Many worship Me by offering the sacrifice of knowledge, recognizing Me either as the one truth in all, as a distinct supreme being, or as the all-pervading universal presence in countless forms.

9-16.sanskrit:
अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम्।

मंत्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम्।।9.16।।
9-16.transliteration:
ahaṁ kratur ahaṁ yajñaḥ svadhāham aham auṣhadham
mantro ’ham aham evājyam aham agnir ahaṁ hutam

translation.simple: Lord Krishna gently shares, 'I am the solemn ritual, the humble sacrifice, and the offering made for departed souls. I am the nurturing food, the sacred mantra, and the pure clarified butter. I am the holy fire, and I am the offering itself.'
translation.deep: In these verses, the Lord graciously unveils His all-encompassing nature. He is not merely present in our spiritual acts; He *is* the very fabric and essence of every component. From the grand Vedic ceremony to the simplest heartfelt offering, from the sustenance that nourishes us to the sacred sounds we utter, and the physical elements like ghee and fire—He permeates all. This profound truth dissolves the illusion of separation between the devotee, the devotion, and the Divine, inviting us to perceive Krishna in every facet of our spiritual journey and daily existence.
translation.essence: Krishna reveals His infinite presence as the very core and substance of all spiritual practices, offerings, and life-giving sustenance, unifying every aspect of devotion within Himself.

9-17.sanskrit:
पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः।

वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च।।9.17।।
9-17.transliteration:
pitāham asya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ
vedyaṁ pavitram oṁkāra ṛik sāma yajur eva cha

translation.simple: Feel the comforting presence of the Divine, for the Lord declares He is our Mother and Father, the very sustainer of all existence. He is the ancient Grandfather who watches over everything. He is the pure knowledge, the sacred Om, and the heart of the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas.
translation.deep: In this profound revelation, the Supreme Lord Krishna unveils His all-encompassing identity. He is the intimate source of both the masculine (father) and feminine (mother) aspects of creation, the eternal sustainer, and the ancient progenitor of all beings. He is the ultimate object of spiritual understanding, the essence of all purity, manifest as the primordial sound 'Om,' and the foundational wisdom embedded within the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas. This verse points to His non-dual nature, being both immanent in the world and transcendent beyond it.
translation.essence: The Lord declares Himself as the ultimate source: the Mother, Father, and Sustainer of the universe. He is the pure knowledge, the sacred Om, and the heart of all Vedic wisdom.

9-18.sanskrit:
गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत्।

प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम्।।9.18।।
9-18.transliteration:
gatir bhartā prabhuḥ sākṣhī nivāsaḥ śharaṇaṁ suhṛit
prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṁ nidhānaṁ bījam avyayam

translation.simple: My Beloved Lord is my path, my sustainer, and my master. He quietly witnesses everything I do. He is my true home, my safe refuge, and my most loving friend. He is the origin of all existence, its dissolution, and its resting place. He is the eternal, imperishable seed of everything.
translation.deep: Reflecting deeply, we find the Divine as the very essence of our journey – the ultimate goal and the path itself. He is the loving sustainer, the powerful Lord, and the silent, ever-present witness to our every thought and deed. He is our soul's true dwelling, the safe haven we seek, and the most sincere friend who wishes us well. From Him, all creation unfolds and into Him it gently returns. He is the firm foundation, the limitless treasure, and the eternal, imperishable seed from which everything arises and is sustained. This reveals His all-encompassing nature, providing comfort and stability in every moment.
translation.essence: The Beloved Lord is everything to us: our guiding path, our unwavering support, our supreme master, and the silent witness of our heart. He is our true dwelling, our safe haven, and our most loving friend. He is the source of all creation and its gentle return, the steadfast foundation, the endless treasure, and the imperishable seed of all existence. Truly, He is all that is, and all that will ever be.

9-19.sanskrit:
तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च।

अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन।।9.19।।
9-19.transliteration:
tapāmyaham ahaṁ varṣhaṁ nigṛihṇāmyutsṛijāmi cha
amṛitaṁ chaiva mṛityuśh cha sad asach chāham arjuna

translation.simple: My divine presence shines as the sun's warmth, and I govern the coming and going of all rain. I am the very essence of life and the gentle touch of passing, the seen and the unseen, O Arjuna.
translation.deep: Realize, O Arjuna, that my divine will orchestrates the very warmth that nourishes the earth and the rain that blesses or withdraws its sustenance. I am the sacred essence that grants immortality and the gentle hand that guides all beings through the cycle of death. Within me, both manifest reality and unmanifest potential beautifully reside.
translation.essence: Krishna declares His divine omnipresence, being the source of the sun's warmth, the rain's flow, life's breath, death's embrace, and all that is, and all that may seem not to be. He is the one underlying truth of everything.

9-20.sanskrit:
त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा

यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते।

ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक

मश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान्।।9.20।।
9-20.transliteration:
trai-vidyā māṁ soma-pāḥ pūta-pāpā
yajñair iṣhṭvā svar-gatiṁ prārthayante
te puṇyam āsādya surendra-lokam
aśhnanti divyān divi deva-bhogān

translation.simple: Some who study the sacred Vedas, cleanse themselves with Soma and holy rites, perform grand sacrifices, and pray to reach the heavenly realms. By their good deeds, they ascend to the world of divine beings and enjoy beautiful, celestial delights.
translation.deep: Having deeply understood the ancient scriptures, and cleansed their hearts through sacred rituals and offerings, some souls offer their devotion, praying earnestly to attain the celestial abodes. By the grace of their pure actions, they ascend to the divine realms, where they lovingly partake in the exquisite pleasures cherished by the gods themselves.
translation.essence: This verse describes how those who perform Vedic rituals and sacrifices with pure hearts aspire to and achieve the temporary joys and divine experiences of the heavenly worlds.

9-21.sanskrit:
ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं

क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति।

एव त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना

गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते।।9.21।।
9-21.transliteration:
te taṁ bhuktvā swarga-lokaṁ viśhālaṁ
kṣhīṇe puṇye martya-lokaṁ viśhanti
evaṁ trayī-dharmam anuprapannā
gatāgataṁ kāma-kāmā labhante

translation.simple: Having enjoyed the vastness of the heavenly realms, these souls return to the mortal world once their accumulated merits are exhausted. In this way, those who follow the path of Vedic rituals driven by desires for enjoyment find themselves in a continuous cycle of birth and rebirth.
translation.deep: This verse offers a gentle yet profound reflection: even the most magnificent enjoyments in heavenly realms are impermanent. When the accumulated merits from pious actions, performed with a desire for such specific outcomes, are exhausted, the soul must descend once more to the earthly plane. It beautifully illustrates that following Vedic rituals primarily for the fulfillment of material desires, while yielding temporary good fortune, ultimately keeps one bound to the continuous cycle of birth and passing. A deeper path, one that seeks transcendence beyond these transient pleasures, is implied.
translation.essence: Even heavenly pleasures have their end. When actions are performed for temporary desires, one remains caught in the gentle ebb and flow of coming and going, a cycle of continuous rebirth.

9-22.sanskrit:
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते।

तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्।।9.22।।
9-22.transliteration:
ananyāśh chintayanto māṁ ye janāḥ paryupāsate
teṣhāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ yoga-kṣhemaṁ vahāmyaham

translation.simple: Those who think of Me with undivided hearts and worship Me with sincere devotion, for these ever-dedicated souls, I personally take care of their spiritual and material welfare. I lovingly provide for all they need and protect what they have.
translation.deep: This profound verse unveils the Lord's unwavering commitment to His devoted. When a soul's thoughts and worship are solely directed towards the Divine, without seeking other shelters, such single-mindedness ('ananyāś cintayantaḥ') creates a sacred bond. For these dear souls, ever absorbed in devotion, the Lord promises to personally bear their 'yoga-kṣemam'. This beautiful promise implies not only the acquisition of what is truly beneficial for them (yoga) but also the loving preservation of their existing spiritual progress and material well-being (kṣema). It is a gentle assurance that when we surrender our all, the Divine lovingly takes full responsibility for our journey and welfare.
translation.essence: When we offer our hearts and thoughts solely to the Divine, with unwavering devotion, the Lord lovingly takes full responsibility for our entire well-being, providing all we need and protecting all we have.

9-23.sanskrit:
येऽप्यन्यदेवता भक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः।

तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम्।।9.23।।
9-23.transliteration:
ye ’pyanya-devatā-bhaktā yajante śhraddhayānvitāḥ
te ’pi mām eva kaunteya yajantyavidhi-pūrvakam

translation.simple: O Arjuna, even those who offer their worship to other divine forms with sincere faith, are in truth worshipping Me. They may not follow the most direct path, but their heartfelt devotion still reaches Me.
translation.deep: This verse gently reveals the all-encompassing nature of the Divine. When a sincere heart, filled with devotion, turns towards any sacred form, that pure offering ultimately finds its way to Me. It signifies that the Supreme Lord is the ultimate destination of all true worship, even if the devotee's perception of the ultimate reality is still unfolding. All sincere spiritual efforts, guided by faith, ultimately draw one closer to the singular Divine essence.
translation.essence: All sincere devotion, offered with faith to any divine form, ultimately finds its way to the one Supreme Being.

9-24.sanskrit:
अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च।

न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते।।9.24।।
9-24.transliteration:
ahaṁ hi sarva-yajñānāṁ bhoktā cha prabhureva cha
na tu mām abhijānanti tattvenātaśh chyavanti te

translation.simple: The Lord lovingly shares that He is the true enjoyer and supreme master of all sacrifices and offerings. When we fail to recognize this divine truth, our spiritual efforts might not yield the most profound and lasting peace.
translation.deep: This verse invites us to understand that every act of devotion, every offering, and every selfless deed ultimately flows towards the Divine. Lord Krishna reveals Himself as the supreme recipient and ultimate orchestrator. When we forget this fundamental truth and limit our understanding, our noble actions, though good, may only bring temporary satisfaction rather than guiding us to the eternal union with Him.
translation.essence: Recognize the Divine as the ultimate enjoyer and master of all your spiritual endeavors. This profound understanding transforms your devotion into a direct path to everlasting peace and true liberation.

9-25.sanskrit:
यान्ति देवव्रता देवान् पितृ़न्यान्ति पितृव्रताः।

भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम्।।9.25।।
9-25.transliteration:
yānti deva-vratā devān pitṝīn yānti pitṛi-vratāḥ
bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti mad-yājino ’pi mām

translation.simple: Those who lovingly worship the celestial beings reach their realms. Those who honor and serve their ancestors join them. Those who offer prayers to spirits go to the spirits. But, dear soul, those who worship Me with devotion, they truly come to Me.
translation.deep: This sacred verse beautifully illustrates a fundamental spiritual law: our focus determines our destiny. When we direct our love and devotion towards particular deities, ancestors, or elemental forces, we naturally align with their spheres and reach their abodes. It gently reminds us that our ultimate longing and the supreme object of our worship ultimately guide us. To fix one's heart on the Divine, on Sri Krishna, is to secure a path directly to His eternal, loving embrace, transcending all other temporary destinations.
translation.essence: What we deeply worship, we ultimately attain. Dedicate your heart to the Supreme Lord, and He will lovingly draw you to Himself.

9-26.sanskrit:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति।

तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः।।9.26।।
9-26.transliteration:
patraṁ puṣhpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayachchhati
tadahaṁ bhaktyupahṛitam aśhnāmi prayatātmanaḥ

translation.simple: If someone offers Me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or even just water, with a heart full of love and devotion, I lovingly accept that humble offering from their pure soul.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse gently assures us that the Divine looks beyond the material value of any offering, seeking only the sincere devotion and purity of heart behind it. A simple leaf or a drop of water, when presented with true love, becomes infinitely precious to the Lord, who lovingly embraces both the offering and the pure spirit of the giver, establishing an intimate connection.
translation.essence: The Divine lovingly accepts any offering, no matter how humble, when it comes from a heart filled with sincere devotion and purity.

9-27.sanskrit:
यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत्।

यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम्।।9.27।।
9-27.transliteration:
yat karoṣhi yad aśhnāsi yaj juhoṣhi dadāsi yat
yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣhva mad-arpaṇam

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, whatever work you do, whatever food you eat, whatever you offer in sacred rites, or whatever gifts you share, even your personal spiritual efforts – perform them all as an offering of love to Me.
translation.deep: This verse invites us to view every moment and every action as an opportunity for spiritual connection. When we dedicate our deeds, our nourishment, our selfless giving, and our spiritual striving to the Divine, we transcend the ordinary. This act of offering purifies our intentions, detaches us from outcomes, and gradually unveils the sacred presence within all experiences, leading to profound inner peace and freedom from karmic ties.
translation.essence: The essence is to spiritualize all aspects of life by consciously offering every action, big or small, to the Supreme Lord. This practice of selfless dedication transforms our existence into a continuous, loving worship, fostering liberation and deep inner harmony.

9-28.sanskrit:
शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः।

संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि।।9.28।।
9-28.transliteration:
śhubhāśhubha-phalair evaṁ mokṣhyase karma-bandhanaiḥ
sannyāsa-yoga-yuktātmā vimukto mām upaiṣhyasi

translation.simple: By offering all your actions to Me, you will be released from the ties of both good and bad results. When your heart is dedicated in this way, you will become truly free and come to My divine presence.
translation.deep: When you lovingly dedicate every action, seeing them not as your own but as offerings to the Divine, you transcend the binding effects of both virtuous and unvirtuous deeds. This path of devoted detachment, where your inner self is aligned with the yoga of renunciation, frees you from all karmic bonds. With a purified heart and a liberated spirit, you will surely attain Me, your ultimate refuge.
translation.essence: Let go of attachment to outcomes; offer all to the Divine. This path of renunciation liberates you from karma and leads you directly to Me.

9-29.sanskrit:
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः।

ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्।।9.29।।
9-29.transliteration:
samo ’haṁ sarva-bhūteṣhu na me dveṣhyo ’sti na priyaḥ
ye bhajanti tu māṁ bhaktyā mayi te teṣhu chāpyaham

translation.simple: Lord Krishna declares, 'I am impartial to all beings, holding no one as disliked or specially dear. Yet, those who lovingly worship Me with devotion, they truly reside within My heart, and I, in turn, lovingly dwell within theirs.'
translation.deep: The Divine reveals an astounding truth: God's presence pervades all existence, showering equal grace upon every soul without preference or prejudice. However, when a heart turns towards the Supreme with genuine devotion and love, a unique and intimate bond is forged. In this sacred connection, the devotee finds their sanctuary in the Lord, and the Lord, in an act of boundless mercy, makes His abode within the devotee's very being. This is the profound mystery of reciprocal divine love.
translation.essence: The Divine is equally present in everyone, neither favoring nor disliking any. Yet, through heartfelt devotion, a beautiful mutual bond is formed: the devotee lives in the Lord, and the Lord lovingly resides in the devotee.

9-30.sanskrit:
अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक्।

साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः।।9.30।।
9-30.transliteration:
api chet su-durāchāro bhajate mām ananya-bhāk
sādhur eva sa mantavyaḥ samyag vyavasito hi saḥ

translation.simple: Even if someone has lived a life of error, should they turn to Me with a heart full of singular devotion, they are to be regarded as truly good. For their resolve is now pure and firm.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse from the Bhagavad Gita offers immense solace, revealing the boundless compassion of the Divine. It gently assures us that no past action, however flawed, can prevent a soul from reaching the Lord, provided they fix their heart solely on Him. When a person, despite their past, takes the firm decision to dedicate themselves to the Supreme with undivided love, that very resolve purifies them instantly. It signifies the transformative power of pure devotion, which transcends all worldly judgments and elevates the soul to true righteousness.
translation.essence: A soul's sincere and undivided devotion to the Divine purifies their past and establishes them in true righteousness.

9-31.sanskrit:
क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति।

कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति।।9.31।।
9-31.transliteration:
kṣhipraṁ bhavati dharmātmā śhaśhvach-chhāntiṁ nigachchhati
kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśhyati

translation.simple: A sincere devotee swiftly becomes righteous and attains unending peace. O Arjuna, declare this truth: My devotee is never lost.
translation.deep: This sacred verse offers a profound assurance of divine grace. It reveals that a heart sincerely turned towards the Lord, even if it has strayed, quickly re-aligns with dharma, becoming virtuous and achieving a lasting, serene peace. Krishna asks Arjuna to declare this powerful truth: a devotee dedicated to Him is never truly lost or abandoned. This is a promise of eternal safety and belonging within the divine embrace.
translation.essence: Krishna's unwavering promise: A devotee swiftly finds purity and everlasting peace, knowing they are never truly lost from His divine presence.

9-32.sanskrit:
मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः।

स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम्।।9.32।।
9-32.transliteration:
māṁ hi pārtha vyapāśhritya ye ’pi syuḥ pāpa-yonayaḥ
striyo vaiśhyās tathā śhūdrās te ’pi yānti parāṁ gatim

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, understand this profound truth: whoever takes complete refuge in Me, even if they are born into circumstances that might be considered challenging or disadvantaged – be they women, merchants, or laborers – they too will certainly attain the supreme spiritual destination.
translation.deep: This sacred verse beautifully illustrates the universal and boundless nature of divine love and grace. It teaches us that the path to the highest spiritual realization is not determined by one's social standing, gender, or the circumstances of birth, but solely by the sincerity of one's devotion and complete surrender to the Lord. All are equally capable of connecting with the Divine and achieving ultimate liberation.
translation.essence: True devotion makes the highest spiritual liberation accessible to everyone, irrespective of birth, gender, or social position.

9-33.sanskrit:
किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा।

अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम्।।9.33।।
9-33.transliteration:
kiṁ punar brāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣhayas tathā
anityam asukhaṁ lokam imaṁ prāpya bhajasva mām

translation.simple: This world is not permanent, nor does it bring lasting happiness. Having come into it, offer your devotion to Me. If others can find Me, how much more easily can pious souls, pure devotees, and wise, saintly kings reach Me.
translation.deep: Reflect upon the nature of existence: this world is ever-changing and cannot provide eternal joy. Knowing this profound truth, surrender your heart and devote yourself to Me. If noble souls—pious Brahmins, sincere devotees, and saintly kings—can easily attain Me, how much more is this path a sacred calling for all, leading to liberation from the cycle of impermanence and sorrow.
translation.essence: Embrace devotion to Me, recognizing this world's impermanence and inability to provide true, lasting happiness. This path is naturally clear and fruitful for the pure-hearted and devoted.

9-34.sanskrit:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु।

मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः।।9.34।।
9-34.transliteration:
man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru
mām evaiṣhyasi yuktvaivam ātmānaṁ mat-parāyaṇaḥ

translation.simple: Always keep your mind on Me, be My loving devotee, offer your worship to Me, and bow down to Me. By connecting your heart in this way, with Me as your ultimate refuge, you will surely come to Me.
translation.deep: Let your entire being be immersed in thoughts of Me. Cultivate a deep and loving devotion, offer all your worship and reverence to Me alone. When you align your heart and soul in this manner, seeing Me as your ultimate shelter and supreme purpose, you will surely reach My divine presence.
translation.essence: Dedicate your mind, heart, and actions to the Divine, making Me your sole refuge. Through this complete surrender, you will attain Me.

10-1.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

भूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः।

यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया।।10.1।।
10-1.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
bhūya eva mahā-bāho śhṛiṇu me paramaṁ vachaḥ
yatte ’haṁ prīyamāṇāya vakṣhyāmi hita-kāmyayā

translation.simple: The Divine Lord spoke: "Beloved Arjuna, O mighty soul, listen again to My most sacred words. I share them with you, for you are truly dear to My heart, and I long only for your greatest welfare."
translation.deep: Here, the Lord lovingly prepares Arjuna, and us, for profound revelations. By calling Arjuna 'mighty-armed' and asking him to 'listen again,' He signifies the readiness required for deeper spiritual understanding. The beautiful assurance that these 'supreme words' are spoken because Arjuna is 'dear' to Him, and purely 'for his benefit,' reveals the tender, compassionate nature of the Divine. It's a sacred invitation to receive wisdom born of boundless love, meant to guide us toward our highest good.
translation.essence: Out of boundless love for His devoted ones, the Divine Lord graciously offers His most profound wisdom, solely for our ultimate good and spiritual upliftment.

10-2.sanskrit:
न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः।

अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः।।10.2।।
10-2.transliteration:
na me viduḥ sura-gaṇāḥ prabhavaṁ na maharṣhayaḥ
aham ādir hi devānāṁ maharṣhīṇāṁ cha sarvaśhaḥ

translation.simple: Even the shining gods and the wise sages do not truly grasp My divine origin. For I am the timeless source from which all gods and all great sages have come.
translation.deep: This sacred verse gently reminds us of the Lord's profound mystery. Even the most powerful celestial beings and the wisest of sages cannot fully understand His divine beginning or limitless glory. For He is the eternal fount, the very first, from whom all gods and all great spiritual masters have beautifully emerged, in every aspect of their being.
translation.essence: The Lord's divine origin and supreme glory remain a beautiful mystery, unfathomable even to the gods and great sages, for He is the ultimate, timeless source of all.

10-3.sanskrit:
यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम्।

असम्मूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते।।10.3।।
10-3.transliteration:
yo māmajam anādiṁ cha vetti loka-maheśhvaram
asammūḍhaḥ sa martyeṣhu sarva-pāpaiḥ pramuchyate

translation.simple: Whoever truly knows Me as the Unborn, without beginning, and the supreme Master of all worlds, becomes clear-minded among mortals and is freed from all past missteps.
translation.deep: To profoundly understand My eternal nature—that I am never born, have no origin, and am the ultimate Sovereign of all realms—is a wisdom that dispels all worldly illusions. This sacred insight liberates a sincere soul from the entanglements of karma and the bewilderment of material existence.
translation.essence: Realizing the Lord's unborn, beginningless, and supreme nature purifies the heart, dissolving delusion and freeing one from all karmic burdens.

10-4.sanskrit:
बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः।

सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च।।10.4।।
10-4.transliteration:
buddhir jñānam asammohaḥ kṣhamā satyaṁ damaḥ śhamaḥ
sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ bhavo ’bhāvo bhayaṁ chābhayameva cha

translation.simple: Lord Krishna lovingly shares that qualities like clear understanding, pure knowledge, freedom from confusion, the gentle art of forgiveness, speaking truth, mastery over our senses, and a peaceful mind all flow from Him. He also reveals that our experiences of happiness and sorrow, coming into existence and passing away, and both fear and fearlessness, truly originate from His divine being.
translation.deep: Here, the Lord unfolds a profound truth: all noble virtues and fundamental states of being are but emanations of His divine power. From the discerning intellect that cuts through confusion, to the quiet wisdom of forgiveness, the steady light of truth, and the calming mastery of our inner and outer worlds – these are His gifts. He also declares that the very cycles of life – the joy and sorrow, birth and cessation, the presence of fear and the gift of fearlessness – all exist within His grand design, urging us to see His presence in all aspects of existence.
translation.essence: This verse gently reminds us that every good quality we cherish – intellect, knowledge, clarity, forgiveness, truthfulness, self-control, and peace – along with all fundamental life experiences such as joy, sorrow, life, death, fear, and fearlessness, all arise from the Supreme Lord. They are manifestations of His divine nature.

10-5.sanskrit:
अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः।

भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः।।10.5।।
10-5.transliteration: ahiṁsā   samatā  tuṣṭis tapo dānaṁ   yaśo    'yaśaḥ  bhavanti    bhāvā   bhūtānāṁ    matta   eva pṛthag-vidhāḥ

translation.simple: All these diverse qualities we see in beings, like non-violence, inner peace, deep contentment, sincere spiritual effort, the joy of giving, and even experiences of honor or its absence – know that each one arises from Me alone.
translation.deep: This profound verse gently reveals that all states of being, every quality, whether seen as virtue or challenge, springs forth from the Divine. From the compassion of non-violence and the serenity of equanimity, to the deep satisfaction of contentment and the discipline of spiritual practice, even the fleeting experiences of honor or its absence – all are but diverse expressions originating from the Supreme Self. This understanding invites a deeper connection, seeing the Lord's hand in every facet of life, encouraging a spirit of acceptance and unwavering devotion.
translation.essence: All qualities and experiences in existence, whether virtuous or challenging, emanate solely from the Divine source.

10-6.sanskrit:
महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा।

मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः।।10.6।।
10-6.transliteration:
maharṣhayaḥ sapta pūrve chatvāro manavas tathā
mad-bhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣhāṁ loka imāḥ prajāḥ

translation.simple: The seven great sages of ancient times, and also the four Manus who guide humanity – all of them came into being from My divine essence, from My very mind. From these great ones, all the beings of this world have originated.
translation.deep: Reflect on the profound truth that the seven revered sages of ancient times and the four Manus, the progenitors of all humanity, came into being directly from My divine essence, conceived within My spiritual mind. From these great souls, all the diverse beings in this world have manifested. This reveals how even the most exalted spiritual leaders and the very fabric of creation originate from Me, showing My all-encompassing nature.
translation.essence: The highest wisdom and all life flow from the Divine. Krishna reveals Himself as the source of the ancient sages and Manus, through whom all beings in this world have come to be, establishing His supreme origin.

10-7.sanskrit:
एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।

सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः।।10.7।।
10-7.transliteration:
etāṁ vibhūtiṁ yogaṁ cha mama yo vetti tattvataḥ
so ’vikampena yogena yujyate nātra sanśhayaḥ

translation.simple: When you truly know My divine greatness and spiritual power, your connection with Me becomes unshaken. There is absolutely no doubt about this profound bond.
translation.deep: To truly know My divine glories and the essence of My spiritual energy means to grasp them not just with the mind, but with the heart. Such deep understanding leads to an unshakable spiritual union with Me. There is no doubt that this steadfast connection brings immense peace and certainty to the soul.
translation.essence: A true understanding of My divine greatness and spiritual power firmly connects the soul to Me, beyond any doubt.

10-8.sanskrit:
अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते।

इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः।।10.8।।
10-8.transliteration:
ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate
iti matvā bhajante māṁ budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord says, 'I am the origin of all that exists, and from Me, everything moves and unfolds. Knowing this profound truth, the wise souls, imbued with deep devotion, offer their worship to Me.'
translation.deep: This sacred verse illuminates the supreme truth: the Divine is the ultimate wellspring from which all creation flows and by which it is sustained. A true understanding of this oneness transforms our perspective, inspiring a profound sense of devotion. Those with awakened wisdom, perceiving the Lord as the all-encompassing reality, wholeheartedly surrender their love and worship, finding supreme peace in this divine connection.
translation.essence: The Lord is the sole origin of all existence. Wise hearts, recognizing this universal source, dedicate themselves to Him with unwavering love and devotion, finding their ultimate refuge.

10-9.sanskrit:
मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम्।

कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च।।10.9।।
10-9.transliteration:
mach-chittā mad-gata-prāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam
kathayantaśh cha māṁ nityaṁ tuṣhyanti cha ramanti cha

translation.simple: My dear ones, those whose thoughts are always on Me, and whose very lives are dedicated to Me, find true happiness. They lovingly speak of Me to one another, constantly sharing My glories, and in this way, they feel deep contentment and profound joy.
translation.deep: When our minds and hearts are fully absorbed in the Divine, and our very breath is offered in devotion, a profound spiritual experience unfolds. Such pure souls find their true purpose in the Lord. They joyfully share insights about Him, mutually inspiring each other through discussions of His divine nature and loving acts. This constant remembrance and shared devotion bring an unparalleled sense of peace, deep satisfaction, and divine joy.
translation.essence: When our minds and lives are centered on the Divine, and we lovingly share this devotion with others by speaking of Him, we experience supreme joy and deep spiritual contentment.

10-10.sanskrit:
तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम्।

ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते।।10.10।।
10-10.transliteration:
teṣhāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam
dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ yena mām upayānti te

translation.simple: To those ever-devoted souls who lovingly serve Me with pure hearts, I grant a special understanding, a wisdom that gently guides them home to Me.
translation.deep: This verse reveals the Lord's profound promise of grace. For those who tirelessly engage in loving service, their hearts overflowing with devotion, the Divine bestows a unique spiritual insight – 'buddhi-yoga.' This isn't merely knowledge, but a deep, intuitive wisdom that illuminates their path, allowing them to truly comprehend their divine connection and find their way home to the Supreme.
translation.essence: Through constant, loving devotion, the Lord bestows the inner wisdom that leads the soul directly to Him.

10-11.transliteration:
teṣhām evānukampārtham aham ajñāna-jaṁ tamaḥ
nāśhayāmyātma-bhāva-stho jñāna-dīpena bhāsvatā

translation.simple: Out of pure compassion for My loving devotees, I reside within their hearts. There, I lovingly remove the darkness that comes from not knowing, lighting up their inner world with the bright lamp of spiritual wisdom.
translation.deep: For those who sincerely devote themselves to Me, I manifest within their very being, driven by boundless compassion. I personally dispel the dense shadows of ignorance that cloud their understanding and obscure their true spiritual self. By My divine grace, a brilliant lamp of self-knowledge is ignited within their hearts, illuminating their consciousness and guiding them towards eternal truth and liberation. It is a profound assurance of My constant, loving presence and guidance.
translation.essence: Out of boundless compassion, the Lord dwells within the hearts of His devotees, personally removing the darkness of ignorance with the brilliant light of divine wisdom.

10-12.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान्।

पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम्।।10.12।।
10-12.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
paraṁ brahma paraṁ dhāma pavitraṁ paramaṁ bhavān
puruṣhaṁ śhāśhvataṁ divyam ādi-devam ajaṁ vibhum

translation.simple: Arjuna spoke, 'Lord, You are the Supreme Spirit, the ultimate refuge for all. You are pure beyond measure, the highest reality. You are the timeless, divine Being, the first of all Gods, unborn, and present everywhere.'
translation.deep: In this verse, Arjuna's heart overflows with deep understanding and devotion for Lord Krishna. He recognizes Krishna not just as a friend, but as 'Paraṁ Brahma,' the Supreme Reality itself, the very essence of existence. Krishna is 'Paraṁ Dhāma,' the ultimate sanctuary, a safe haven where all seeking hearts find peace and ultimate comfort. He is 'Pavitraṁ Paramam,' the purest of the pure, whose presence sanctifies everything. Arjuna beholds Him as the eternal, divine Person, the original God, unborn and all-pervading. This declaration is a loving acknowledgment of the Lord's timeless, boundless, and utterly divine nature, inviting us to see Him as the source of all truth and goodness.
translation.essence: Arjuna, with deep reverence, declares Krishna to be the Supreme, the ultimate sanctuary, the purest essence, the eternal, divine, unborn, and all-pervading Lord.

10-13.sanskrit:
आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा।

असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे।।10.13।।
10-13.transliteration:
āhus tvām ṛiṣhayaḥ sarve devarṣhir nāradas tathā
asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṁ chaiva bravīṣhi me

translation.simple: Arjuna says to Krishna, 'All the great sages, including the divine Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa, declare You to be the Supreme Lord. And You, Yourself, are personally confirming this sacred truth to me.'
translation.deep: Here, Arjuna expresses a profound sense of confirmation and trust. He acknowledges that the most revered spiritual authorities and seers across time—from the celestial sage Narada to the profound wisdom of Asita, Devala, and Vyasa—have all borne witness to Krishna's supreme divinity. This isn't mere hearsay; the Lord's own gentle words are now validating these timeless truths, deepening Arjuna's understanding and devotion to His boundless glory.
translation.essence: The collective wisdom of revered ancient sages, coupled with Krishna's own loving revelation, beautifully affirms His supreme, divine essence to Arjuna's heart.

10-14.sanskrit:
सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव।

न हि ते भगवन् व्यक्ितं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः।।10.14।।
10-14.transliteration:
sarvam etad ṛitaṁ manye yan māṁ vadasi keśhava
na hi te bhagavan vyaktiṁ vidur devā na dānavāḥ

translation.simple: O Keshava, I truly believe every word You speak to me is the absolute truth. Indeed, O Lord, Your true divine form and nature are beyond the understanding of even the gods and the demons.
translation.deep: With profound reverence, Arjuna declares his unwavering faith in every word spoken by Lord Keshava, recognizing it as pure truth. He humbly acknowledges that the Lord's divine essence and manifestations are so vast and subtle that even the celestial gods and powerful demons cannot fully comprehend them. This speaks to the unfathomable nature of the Supreme Lord, accessible fully only through His grace.
translation.essence: This verse beautifully portrays Arjuna's complete faith and surrender to Lord Krishna's words, seeing them as pure truth. It underscores the unfathomable glory of the Divine, whose true nature remains a sacred mystery even to the most powerful beings.

10-15.sanskrit:
स्वयमेवात्मनाऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम।

भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते।।10.15।।
10-15.transliteration:
swayam evātmanātmānaṁ vettha tvaṁ puruṣhottama
bhūta-bhāvana bhūteśha deva-deva jagat-pate

translation.simple: O Supreme Lord, You are the only one who truly knows Your divine Self, by Your own unique power. You are the very source from which all beings arise, the Master of every creature, the God revered by all other gods, and the loving Lord of this vast universe.
translation.deep: Here, Arjuna humbly acknowledges a profound spiritual truth: the ultimate essence of the Divine can only be fully comprehended by the Divine Itself. Lord Krishna, You are beyond all human understanding in Your true form. You are not only the loving Creator who brings all life into being, but also the sovereign ruler of every creature, the supreme Deity to whom even other divine beings offer reverence, and the compassionate orchestrator of the entire cosmos. This realization inspires immense devotion and a calm acceptance of Your infinite glory.
translation.essence: Only Lord Krishna perfectly knows His own boundless divine nature. He is the gentle origin, master, supreme God, and loving Lord of all creation.

10-16.sanskrit:
वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः।

याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि।।10.16।।
10-16.transliteration:
vaktum arhasyaśheṣheṇa divyā hyātma-vibhūtayaḥ
yābhir vibhūtibhir lokān imāṁs tvaṁ vyāpya tiṣhṭhasi

translation.simple: My Lord, I yearn to hear completely about Your divine glories. It is by these beautiful manifestations that You fill all these worlds and lovingly abide within them.
translation.deep: Arjuna, with a heart full of devotion, implores the Lord to reveal the entirety of His divine splendors. He wishes to grasp how the Supreme Being, through these very glories, pervades every realm, residing as the essence within all. It is a deep yearning to understand how the Divine truly exists, permeating and upholding the vast expanse of creation.
translation.essence: This verse reflects Arjuna's heartfelt plea for Lord Krishna to fully describe His divine manifestations, through which He beautifully pervades and lovingly sustains all realms of existence.

10-17.sanskrit:
कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन्।

केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया।।10.17।।
10-17.transliteration:
kathaṁ vidyām ahaṁ yogins tvāṁ sadā parichintayan
keṣhu keṣhu cha bhāveṣhu chintyo ’si bhagavan mayā

translation.simple: O Divine Yogi, how can I constantly remember You and deeply understand You? Please reveal in which beautiful manifestations I should lovingly contemplate Your presence, my Lord.
translation.deep: Here, Arjuna, with a heart full of devotion, expresses his yearning to remain perpetually connected to the Divine. He isn't just seeking intellectual knowledge, but a profound, experiential understanding that allows him to perceive the Lord in every aspect of existence. This verse reflects the devotee's aspiration to integrate spiritual awareness into daily life, asking Krishna to guide him on how to consistently find Him amidst the world's various forms and qualities. It's a prayer for clear vision to recognize the omnipresent Lord.
translation.essence: This verse is a heartfelt prayer from a devotee who longs to always remember the Lord and asks for guidance on how to perceive His divine presence in all of creation.

10-18.sanskrit:
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन।

भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि श्रृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम्।।10.18।।
10-18.transliteration:
vistareṇātmano yogaṁ vibhūtiṁ cha janārdana
bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛiptir hi śhṛiṇvato nāsti me ’mṛitam

translation.simple: O Krishna, please speak more about Your divine power and wonderful manifestations. My heart feels endless joy hearing Your sweet, nectar-like words, and I simply cannot get enough.
translation.deep: Beloved Lord Janardana, I humbly request You to elaborate further on Your mystic union with all existence and the countless ways Your divine glory shines. For the one who hears Your immortal wisdom, O fountain of nectar, there is no end to the deep contentment and spiritual yearning; the soul is perpetually drawn to drink more from this sacred wellspring.
translation.essence: With a heart full of devotion, the listener expresses an insatiable desire to hear more about the Lord's divine powers and manifestations, finding unending spiritual joy in His nectar-like words.

10-19.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः।

प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे।।10.19।।
10-19.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
hanta te kathayiṣhyāmi divyā hyātma-vibhūtayaḥ
prādhānyataḥ kuru-śhreṣhṭha nāstyanto vistarasya me

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord said: 'Listen, Arjuna, I will now share with you My divine glories, which flow from My very Being. I will speak of the most prominent ones, O best of Kurus, for truly, there is no end to the vastness of My divine manifestations.'
translation.deep: Here, the Lord lovingly agrees to reveal His divine opulences, not as external powers, but as manifestations arising from His very Self (atma-vibhuti). He indicates that what He will describe are merely the principal ones, a loving glimpse into His boundless nature. This revelation is a profound gift, inviting us to contemplate the infinite ways the Divine expresses itself throughout creation, reminding us that His presence is eternal and immeasurable.
translation.essence: The Lord, out of compassion, begins to unveil His divine glories, assuring us that His presence is infinite and expresses itself boundlessly in all creation.

10-20.sanskrit:
अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः।

अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च।।10.20।।
10-20.transliteration:
aham ātmā guḍākeśha sarva-bhūtāśhaya-sthitaḥ
aham ādiśh cha madhyaṁ cha bhūtānām anta eva cha

translation.simple: Dearest Arjuna, I am the true essence within every being, dwelling in their hearts. I am the source from which all life springs, the sustaining presence throughout, and the gentle end to which everything returns.
translation.deep: Here, Lord Krishna beautifully reveals His all-encompassing presence. He is the quiet, unchanging Self within every single living being, the very core of their existence. Understand that He is not just a part, but the whole – the initial spark of creation, the steady hand that sustains all life, and the peaceful dissolution when all returns. This knowledge invites us to perceive the Divine in every aspect of life and within ourselves.
translation.essence: The Divine dwells as the innermost Self in all hearts, being the origin, the sustenance, and the end of all that exists.

10-21.sanskrit:
आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान्।

मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी।।10.21।।
10-21.transliteration:
ādityānām ahaṁ viṣhṇur jyotiṣhāṁ ravir anśhumān
marīchir marutām asmi nakṣhatrāṇām ahaṁ śhaśhī

translation.simple: Lord Krishna lovingly reveals Himself: 'Among the great Adityas, I am Vishnu. Of all that shines brightly, know Me as the radiant sun. Among the powerful Maruts, I am Marichi, and among all the stars, I am the gentle moon.' He shows us how His divine presence illuminates the most prominent and beautiful aspects of the world around us.
translation.deep: In this sacred verse, Krishna unveils His omnipresence and supreme essence through specific manifestations. By identifying as Vishnu, the radiant sun, Marichi, and the calming moon, He teaches us to perceive Him as the very source and pinnacle of all power, light, and grace in the cosmos. Each of these specific forms represents a unique aspect of divine excellence, prompting us to recognize that every beauty and grandeur we witness is but a reflection of His boundless glory, inviting a deeper, worshipful contemplation of the universe.
translation.essence: Krishna is the divine core of every great being, the brilliant source of all light, the potent force within the winds, and the serene beauty of the night sky. He is the ultimate origin of all magnificence.

10-22.sanskrit:
वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः।

इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना।।10.22।।
10-22.transliteration:
vedānāṁ sāma-vedo ’smi devānām asmi vāsavaḥ
indriyāṇāṁ manaśh chāsmi bhūtānām asmi chetanā

translation.simple: Lord Krishna lovingly shares: 'Among the sacred Vedas, I am the beautiful Sama Veda, known for its sweet songs. Among the celestial gods, I am Indra, their chief. Of all the senses, I am the mind, which directs them. And in every living being, I am the very essence of consciousness, the spark of life.'
translation.deep: In this verse, Lord Krishna helps us perceive His omnipresence by identifying with the most excellent and fundamental aspects of creation. He is the Sama Veda, representing the profound beauty and devotion found in sacred melody. He is Indra, embodying the divine authority and benevolent order among the celestial beings. He manifests as the mind among the senses, revealing His role as the subtle controller and experiencer of all perceptions. Most profoundly, He declares Himself as consciousness in all beings, signifying that the very awareness and life force animating every creature is a direct emanation of His divine self. This teaching encourages us to find the divine within the finest expressions of life and within our own inner being.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna lovingly reveals His divine presence as the supreme quality, the inner guide, and the very breath of life in the most excellent and fundamental aspects of existence.

10-23.sanskrit:
रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम्।

वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम्।।10.23।।
10-23.transliteration:
rudrāṇāṁ śhaṅkaraśh chāsmi vitteśho yakṣha-rakṣhasām
vasūnāṁ pāvakaśh chāsmi meruḥ śhikhariṇām aham

translation.simple: Among the mighty Rudras, I am Lord Shiva. Among the givers of wealth, I am Kubera. Among the bright Vasus, I am the sacred fire. And among all the high mountains, I am Meru.
translation.deep: Here, the Lord tenderly reveals how His supreme presence graces the most eminent forms throughout creation. In the revered Shankara, the generous Kubera, the purifying fire, and the majestic Meru mountain, He shows that His divine light shines. This wisdom encourages us to perceive His ultimate excellence and beauty in every perfect and prominent aspect of the world, fostering a deeper sense of devotion and wonder.
translation.essence: The Lord beautifully reveals Himself as the pinnacle of power, wealth, purity, and steadfastness across creation, inviting us to see His divine light in all that is supreme and excellent.

10-24.sanskrit:
पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम्।

सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः।।10.24।।
10-24.transliteration:
purodhasāṁ cha mukhyaṁ māṁ viddhi pārtha bṛihaspatim
senānīnām ahaṁ skandaḥ sarasām asmi sāgaraḥ

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, understand that among the wisest priests and spiritual advisors, I am the very essence of Brihaspati. Among all valiant commanders, I am the mighty Skanda. And among all the waters, I am the boundless, deep ocean.
translation.deep: In the realm of spiritual counsel and guidance, envision Me as Brihaspati, the very source of divine wisdom that illuminates the path for all. In the courage and strategy of powerful commanders, behold My strength as Skanda, leading the forces of righteousness. And in the boundless expanse of all waters, sense My presence as the mighty ocean, holding all life within its profound depths, vast and eternal.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna lovingly reveals His supreme presence: as the highest spiritual wisdom embodied in Brihaspati, as the unparalleled might and strategy of Skanda among commanders, and as the infinite depth and expanse of the ocean among all waters. It's a gentle reminder that His divine essence shines through the most excellent aspects of creation, guiding, protecting, and embracing all.

10-25.sanskrit:
महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम्।

यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः।।10.25।।
10-25.transliteration:
maharṣhīṇāṁ bhṛigur ahaṁ girām asmyekam akṣharam
yajñānāṁ japa-yajño ’smi sthāvarāṇāṁ himālayaḥ

translation.simple: Among the great sages, I am Bhrigu. In all words, I am the sacred single syllable 'Om'. Of all forms of worship, I am the quiet, mindful chanting of holy names. And among all that stands firm, I am the grand Himalayas.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly reveals Himself as the essence of creation's most profound and sublime forms. He is Bhrigu, the ancient seer, representing the deepest spiritual wisdom. In all the sounds we utter, He is the sacred syllable 'Om,' the primordial vibration that connects us to the source of all. Of all the ways we offer our devotion, He highlights 'Japa,' the quiet, heartfelt repetition of sacred names, as the purest and most potent sacrifice, turning our inner world into a sanctuary. And as the majestic Himalayas, He embodies unwavering strength, serene stability, and the sublime grandeur of the spiritual path.
translation.essence: This beautiful verse gently assures us that the Divine is intimately present in the highest wisdom, the most sacred sound, the most heartfelt devotion, and the unshakeable grandeur of nature. Krishna is the essence and strength within all that is noble and eternal.

10-26.sanskrit:
अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः।

गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः।।10.26।।
10-26.transliteration:
aśhvatthaḥ sarva-vṛikṣhāṇāṁ devarṣhīṇāṁ cha nāradaḥ
gandharvāṇāṁ chitrarathaḥ siddhānāṁ kapilo muniḥ

translation.simple: Among all trees, I am the venerable Ashvattha. Among the divine sages, I am Narada, ever chanting My glories. Among the celestial musicians, I am Chitraratha, and among the perfected sages, I am the wise Kapila.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly reveals how His divine presence permeates the universe, manifesting as the most exalted in each category. He is the sacred Ashvattha, symbolizing the profound mystery and eternal nature of creation. In the divine sage Narada, He embodies pure devotion and the selfless spreading of spiritual knowledge. Through Chitraratha, He is the enchanting beauty and harmony of celestial music that elevates the soul. And in Sage Kapila, He is the profound wisdom that guides seekers towards liberation. Each manifestation gently points to His all-encompassing greatness, inviting us to see His glory and perfection in every noble expression.
translation.essence: This verse tenderly reminds us that Lord Krishna's divine essence shines through the most beautiful and perfect aspects of creation. From the venerable Ashvattha tree to the devoted Narada, the enchanting Chitraratha, and the profound wisdom of Sage Kapila, He reveals Himself. It encourages us to find His loving presence and supreme glory in every peak of excellence and spiritual purity around us, fostering a sense of constant remembrance and devotion.

10-27.sanskrit:
उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम्।

ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम्।।10.27।।
10-27.transliteration:
uchchaiḥśhravasam aśhvānāṁ viddhi mām amṛitodbhavam
airāvataṁ gajendrāṇāṁ narāṇāṁ cha narādhipam

translation.simple: Among all noble horses, understand that I am Uchchaishravas, the one born from divine nectar. Among the grandest elephants, I am Airavata. And among all humankind, I am the king, the righteous ruler.
translation.deep: Here, Lord Krishna lovingly reveals His presence in the most glorious and excellent forms of creation. When we admire the unparalleled beauty and speed of a divine horse like Uchchaishravas, or the majestic might of Airavata, the king of elephants, or witness the just leadership of a noble king, we are truly beholding a glimpse of the Supreme Lord Himself. He is the very source and essence of all that is splendid, powerful, and righteous in this world, reminding us to see Him in every peak of perfection.
translation.essence: The Lord is the ultimate splendor in every majestic creature and the guiding wisdom in every noble leader, reminding us to perceive His divine presence in all that is excellent and glorious.

10-28.sanskrit:
आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक्।

प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः।।10.28।।
10-28.transliteration:
āyudhānām ahaṁ vajraṁ dhenūnām asmi kāmadhuk
prajanaśh chāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇām asmi vāsukiḥ

translation.simple: I am the mighty thunderbolt among weapons, and among cows, I am the wish-fulfilling Kamadhenu. I am Kandarpa, the spark of creation, and among serpents, I am Vasuki.
translation.deep: The divine presence is seen in the might of the Vajra, symbolizing ultimate, unyielding power. In the generous Kamadhenu, I am the source of all abundance and the fulfillment of every heartfelt wish. I am the sacred impulse of Kandarpa, who initiates the joyful process of creation and the continuation of life itself. And among serpents, I am the revered Vasuki, representing ancient wisdom and the profound depths of existence.
translation.essence: Through these exemplary forms, the Lord reveals His supreme presence in strength, abundance, the joy of creation, and ancient wisdom. All excellence is a reflection of Him.

10-29.sanskrit:
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम्।

पितृ़णामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम्।।10.29।।
10-29.transliteration:
anantaśh chāsmi nāgānāṁ varuṇo yādasām aham
pitṝīṇām aryamā chāsmi yamaḥ sanyamatām aham

translation.simple: Among the great and divine serpents, I am the endless Ananta. Among all beings that live in the waters, I am Varuna. Of the revered ancestors, I am Aryama. And among those who maintain discipline and order, I am Yama.
translation.deep: Here, the Lord reveals how His supreme presence manifests through various cosmic roles. As Ananta, He is the infinite support and foundation of the universe, upon whom all creation rests. As Varuna, He embodies the vastness and essential order of all aquatic life and the cosmic waters. As Aryama, He is the guiding principle among the venerable ancestors, overseeing their sacred duties. And as Yama, He represents the ultimate principle of discipline, righteous judgment, and the natural order that brings balance to all existence. Each form points to the Divine as the underlying truth, structure, and governor of every realm.
translation.essence: This verse gently reminds us that the Divine permeates every aspect of existence, from cosmic support and aquatic life to ancestral guidance and universal justice. It shows how the Lord is the ultimate source of all order and being.

10-30.sanskrit:
प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम्।

मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम्।।10.30।।
10-30.transliteration:
prahlādaśh chāsmi daityānāṁ kālaḥ kalayatām aham
mṛigāṇāṁ cha mṛigendro ’haṁ vainateyaśh cha pakṣhiṇām

translation.simple: Among the mighty ones, I am the pure-hearted devotee Prahlada. Of all that measures and calculates, I am the timeless flow of Kāla. Among the animals, I am the majestic lion, and among the birds, I am the swift and powerful Garuda.
translation.deep: In this sacred verse, the Lord lovingly reveals how His divine presence is manifest in the most outstanding and exemplary forms. He identifies Himself with Prahlada, representing the pinnacle of unwavering devotion even amidst adversity. He is Kāla, the silent and ultimate force of time, which orchestrates all reckonings and changes. Among the creatures of the wild, He is the noble lion, symbolizing courage, strength, and dominion. And among all winged beings, He is the magnificent Garuda, embodying speed, power, and divine protection. This gentle guidance encourages us to perceive the excellence and supreme qualities within creation as reflections of His own divine nature, inviting us to feel His presence in all that is great and good.
translation.essence: The Lord dwells within the highest qualities of creation: the unwavering devotion of Prahlada, the silent power of Time (Kāla), the majestic strength of the lion, and the swift grace of Garuda. This verse beautifully guides us to perceive God's supreme presence in all that is exemplary and powerful, deepening our spiritual connection to Him.

10-31.sanskrit:
पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम्।

झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी।।10.31।।
10-31.transliteration:
pavanaḥ pavatām asmi rāmaḥ śhastra-bhṛitām aham
jhaṣhāṇāṁ makaraśh chāsmi srotasām asmi jāhnavī

translation.simple: Among all things that cleanse and move, I am the gentle wind. Among those who bear arms, I am the righteous Lord Rama. Among all creatures of the water, I am the powerful Makara. And among all flowing rivers, I am the holy Ganga.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly reveals His divine presence within the very best of creation. He is the purifying spirit of the wind, the ideal of virtue and might embodied in Lord Rama, the strongest among aquatic life, like the powerful Makara. And among all rivers, He is the most sacred flow, the holy Ganga. Through these examples, He shows how His supreme essence permeates and shines forth in all excellence, inviting us to perceive His glory everywhere.
translation.essence: This verse beautifully reminds us that the Divine is the supreme essence, manifesting as the very best and most significant in every realm of existence, inviting us to see His glory in all things noble and powerful.

10-32.sanskrit:
सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन।

अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम्।।10.32।।
10-32.transliteration:
sargāṇām ādir antaśh cha madhyaṁ chaivāham arjuna
adhyātma-vidyā vidyānāṁ vādaḥ pravadatām aham

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, know that I am the gentle origin, the nurturing presence, and the peaceful end of all that comes into being. Among all branches of learning, I am the most sacred knowledge of the inner Self. And among all forms of expression, I am the thoughtful discourse that seeks wisdom.
translation.deep: Here, Lord Krishna beautifully reveals His omnipresence as the eternal source, the steady sustenance, and the peaceful culmination of all manifest existence. He kindly informs us that among all wisdom, the sacred knowledge of the true Self (Atman) is His deepest expression, for it liberates the soul. And when people engage in thoughtful discussion, it is His essence that inspires the meaningful quest for truth, leading to clarity and spiritual growth.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna lovingly reminds us that He is the beginning, middle, and end of all existence. He is the purest spiritual knowledge and the very heart of all wise conversations.

10-33.sanskrit:
अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च।

अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः।।10.33।।
10-33.transliteration:
अहमेवाक्षय: कालो धाताहं विश्वतोमुख: || 33||

akṣharāṇām a-kāro ’smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya cha
aham evākṣhayaḥ kālo dhātāhaṁ viśhvato-mukhaḥ

translation.simple: The Lord says, 'Among all letters, I am the primal 'A'. Among balanced compound words, I am the 'Dvanda'. I am also the eternal, unending flow of Time. I am the sustainer of all, present in every direction.'
translation.deep: Here, Lord Krishna beautifully illustrates His omnipresence and fundamental nature. He is the 'A', the very root of sound and beginning of creation. He is the harmonious balance of the 'Dvanda' compound, signifying unity in duality. He is the ever-flowing, changeless Time itself, and the boundless sustainer, whose loving gaze and support embrace all existence, everywhere.
translation.essence: This verse reveals the Divine as the essential origin, the perfect balance, the eternal flow, and the all-pervading sustainer of the universe.

10-34.sanskrit:
मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम्।

कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा।।10.34।।
10-34.transliteration:
mṛityuḥ sarva-haraśh chāham udbhavaśh cha bhaviṣhyatām
kīrtiḥ śhrīr vāk cha nārīṇāṁ smṛitir medhā dhṛitiḥ kṣhamā

translation.simple: I am the gentle end that lovingly takes all things, and I am also the fresh beginning for all that is yet to come. Among women, I am their beautiful qualities: their good name, inner prosperity, gentle speech, clear memory, deep understanding, unwavering resolve, and compassionate spirit of forgiveness.
translation.deep: Ponder deeply on My all-encompassing nature. I am the tranquil dissolution that brings an end to all forms, and I am the vibrant, ceaseless source from which all new beginnings beautifully emerge. Observe My presence in the noble qualities found within women: their serene reputation, their inner prosperity, the gentle power of their speech, the clarity of their memory, the depth of their understanding, their steadfast resolve, and their compassionate spirit of forgiveness. These virtues are reflections of My own divine essence, illuminating the world.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna lovingly declares Himself as the ultimate power that brings about all ends and all new beginnings. He is also the divine spring from which all cherished virtues flow, embodying Himself in the noble qualities of women: their grace, wisdom, steadfastness, and the pure spirit of forgiveness.

10-35.sanskrit:
बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम्।

मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः।।10.35।।
10-35.transliteration:
bṛihat-sāma tathā sāmnāṁ gāyatrī chhandasām aham
māsānāṁ mārga-śhīrṣho ’ham ṛitūnāṁ kusumākaraḥ

translation.simple: Lord Krishna gently reveals His boundless presence, stating that He is the grandest melody among sacred chants, and the revered Gāyatrī among all meters. He declares Himself to be the blessed month of Mārgaśīrṣa and the refreshing beauty of spring among all seasons.
translation.deep: Through these profound examples, the Lord illuminates how His divine essence permeates and defines all that is supreme and auspicious in creation. He is the soul of sacred sound in the Bṛhatsāman, the guiding light of spiritual wisdom in the Gāyatrī mantra. As the cherished month of Mārgaśīrṣa, He brings forth prosperity and reflection, and as the vibrant spring, He symbolizes renewal and joy. This verse encourages us to see beyond the material and recognize the indwelling Divine in every beautiful and perfect aspect of existence.
translation.essence: The Lord lovingly teaches us to perceive His ultimate glory and serene presence in the highest forms of sacredness, beauty, and auspiciousness within the world, inviting us to see Him as the very best in all that is.

10-36.sanskrit:
द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम्।

जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम्।।10.36।।
10-36.transliteration:
dyūtaṁ chhalayatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham
jayo ’smi vyavasāyo ’smi sattvaṁ sattvavatām aham

translation.simple: Among those who engage in games of chance and cleverness, I am the underlying principle of that play. I am the splendor of the brilliant ones. I am victory itself. I am the firm resolve in every endeavor. And I am the pure goodness found in the virtuous.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna reveals His all-encompassing nature, stating that He is the fundamental power and energy behind all actions, even those involving strategy and chance, emphasizing that no aspect of existence is separate from Him. He is the inherent radiance and greatness that shines through magnificent individuals. He embodies the triumph achieved through righteous efforts and the unyielding determination that fuels purposeful action. He is the very essence of goodness and purity that resides within the virtuous, reminding us that every noble quality is a reflection of His divine being.
translation.essence: Krishna declares Himself as the ultimate source of all engagement and strategy, the supreme brilliance, the very spirit of victory, the unwavering power of resolve, and the pure essence of virtue, affirming His omnipresence in every aspect of creation.

10-37.sanskrit:
वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनंजयः।

मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः।।10.37।।
10-37.transliteration:
vṛiṣhṇīnāṁ vāsudevo ’smi pāṇḍavānāṁ dhanañjayaḥ
munīnām apyahaṁ vyāsaḥ kavīnām uśhanā kaviḥ

translation.simple: Lord Krishna lovingly reveals, 'Among the Vrishnis, I am Vasudeva, Myself. Among the Pandavas, I am Arjuna. Among the thoughtful sages, I am Vyasa, and among the great insightful poets, I am Ushana.' He shows us His presence as the finest example within each group.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to understand that the Divine shines through all forms of excellence and virtue in creation. When Krishna identifies with Vasudeva, Arjuna, Vyasa, and Ushana, He is not just naming leaders, but pointing to the very peak of kingship, devotion, wisdom, and poetic insight. It's a profound teaching that wherever we encounter exceptional goodness, courage, knowledge, or spiritual understanding, we are truly witnessing a reflection of the Lord's boundless glory. It inspires us to perceive the divine essence in the most exemplary beings and their qualities around us, fostering a deeper connection with the sacred in everyday life.
translation.essence: Krishna lovingly declares Himself to be the ultimate excellence in every sphere – as the ideal among His kin, among devoted warriors, profound sages, and insightful poets – revealing that all true greatness flows from His divine being.

10-38.sanskrit:
दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम्।

मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम्।।10.38।।
10-38.transliteration:
daṇḍo damayatām asmi nītir asmi jigīṣhatām
maunaṁ chaivāsmi guhyānāṁ jñānaṁ jñānavatām aham

translation.simple: I am the gentle hand of discipline for those who bring order, and the clear path for those who wish to succeed. Among all that is hidden and sacred, I am the serene silence, and I am the pure understanding within the hearts of the wise.
translation.deep: In this verse, Lord Krishna tenderly reveals His divine presence woven into the very fabric of life's principles. He is the underlying power in discipline that guides us towards self-control and harmony. He is the insightful strategy and virtuous path for those who strive for righteous victories. Krishna manifests as the profound and sacred silence that cradles all hidden spiritual truths. Most profoundly, He is the illuminating wisdom that blossoms within the hearts of those who have attained true understanding. This teaching encourages us to perceive the Divine in every aspect of structure, aspiration, and inner knowing.
translation.essence: Krishna lovingly shows Himself as the essence of discipline, the guiding wisdom for success, the sacred silence of all mysteries, and the deep knowledge present in enlightened hearts, illuminating His pervasive presence in all aspects of order, aspiration, and spiritual understanding.

10-39.sanskrit:
यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन।

न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम्।।10.39।।
10-39.transliteration:
yach chāpi sarva-bhūtānāṁ bījaṁ tad aham arjuna
na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṁ charācharam

translation.simple: O Arjuna, know that I am the very seed from which all living beings sprout. There is nothing in this entire creation, whether moving or still, that can exist without Me.
translation.deep: My dear Arjuna, understand that I am the fundamental origin, the divine seed from which all life emerges. There is no being, no object, no part of this entire creation—neither the animate nor the inanimate—that can truly exist separate from My divine presence. Every aspect of existence is sustained by My energy and woven into My very being.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna declares Himself as the ultimate seed of all existence, emphasizing that nothing, moving or unmoving, can manifest or endure without His divine essence.

10-40.sanskrit:
नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप।

एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया।।10.40।।
10-40.transliteration:
nānto ’sti mama divyānāṁ vibhūtīnāṁ parantapa
eṣha tūddeśhataḥ prokto vibhūter vistaro mayā

translation.simple: My divine glories, O Arjuna, truly have no end. What I've just shared with you is merely an indication, a small part of My vast opulence.
translation.deep: The Lord lovingly reveals that His divine splendors are immeasurable and without limit. The glorious manifestations He has just described are but a tiny, illustrative glimpse into His infinite greatness. This encourages a deep sense of humility and wonder, reminding us that the Divine is forever boundless and that our devotion can continually explore new depths of His all-pervading presence.
translation.essence: The Divine's glories are infinite; what is shown is but a loving hint of boundless majesty.

10-41.sanskrit:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा।

तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम्।।10.41।।
10-41.transliteration:
yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṁ śhrīmad ūrjitam eva vā
tat tad evāvagachchha tvaṁ mama tejo ’nśha-sambhavam

translation.simple: Wherever you encounter beauty, strength, or glory in this world, understand that it arises from just a small spark of My own divine brilliance.
translation.deep: Contemplate the profound truth that every expression of beauty, every manifestation of strength, and every sign of glory in existence originates from just a fragment of the Lord's own divine effulgence. This understanding deepens our appreciation for the sacredness of all things and reveals the omnipresent hand of the Divine in the world.
translation.essence: Every spark of greatness, beauty, and power you encounter is a direct emanation from the Lord's boundless glory.

10-42.sanskrit:
अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन।

विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत्।।10.42।।
10-42.transliteration:
atha vā bahunaitena kiṁ jñātena tavārjuna
viṣhṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛitsnam ekānśhena sthito jagat

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, why trouble yourself with knowing every single detail? Simply understand this profound truth: I uphold and sustain this entire vast universe with just a tiny fragment of My infinite, divine Self.
translation.deep: This verse tenderly invites us beyond endless intellectual searching, to a tranquil understanding of the Lord's boundless nature. It assures us that His glory is so immense, He effortlessly supports the entire cosmos – from the smallest atom to the grandest galaxy – with merely a fraction of His divine being. This truth offers profound peace, reminding us of His infinite power, unwavering presence, and all-encompassing love that sustains every aspect of our existence.
