translation.essence: Krishna gently reminds us: His supreme power sustains the entire universe effortlessly, using only a tiny part of His infinite Being. Focus not on countless details, but on His all-pervading, boundless presence.

11-1.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम्।

यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम।।11.1।।
11-1.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
mad-anugrahāya paramaṁ guhyam adhyātma-sanjñitam
yat tvayoktaṁ vachas tena moho ’yaṁ vigato mama

translation.simple: Arjuna said: "O Lord, with such great kindness, You revealed to me the most profound spiritual truth. By Your divine words, the confusion that clouded my heart has now completely faded away."
translation.deep: Arjuna said: "Out of Your immense compassion for me, Lord, You have spoken the supreme and most secret wisdom about the true nature of the Self. Truly, by these sacred words from You, the veil of delusion that enveloped my understanding has been entirely removed, bringing profound clarity to my being."
translation.essence: Arjuna, with deep gratitude, acknowledges that Krishna's supreme spiritual wisdom, born of divine compassion, has completely dispelled his delusion, bringing him peace and understanding.

11-2.sanskrit:
भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया।

त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम्।।11.2।।
11-2.transliteration:
bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṁ śhrutau vistaraśho mayā
tvattaḥ kamala-patrākṣha māhātmyam api chāvyayam

translation.simple: O Lotus-Eyed Lord, I have heard from You, in great detail, about the birth and passing away of all beings. And I have also come to know Your eternal, unchanging glory.
translation.deep: My heart has absorbed Your profound wisdom, O beautiful Lotus-Eyed One. You have lovingly revealed, in extensive detail, how all beings come into existence and eventually dissolve back into You. Through Your words, I now deeply understand Your imperishable greatness – a glory that remains eternal and unchanging, the very foundation of all that is.
translation.essence: O Krishna, Your divine teachings have revealed to me the cycle of creation and dissolution for all beings, and, most wondrously, Your eternal and immutable glory.

11-3.sanskrit:
एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर।

द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम।।11.3।।
11-3.transliteration:
evam etad yathāttha tvam ātmānaṁ parameśhvara
draṣhṭum ichchhāmi te rūpam aiśhwaraṁ puruṣhottama

translation.simple: My dear Lord, what You have spoken about Yourself is indeed the truth. Now, I deeply long to see Your divine, majestic form, O Supreme Person.
translation.deep: O Supreme Lord, everything You have revealed about Your divine nature is indeed true. With a heart full of devotion, I now deeply yearn to behold Your grand, majestic form, O Supreme Person, so I may experience Your complete glory.
translation.essence: This verse reflects Arjuna's complete acceptance of Krishna's divine revelations. From this foundation of faith, a heartfelt desire arises in him to personally witness the Lord's awe-inspiring, universal form, seeking a direct experience of His supreme majesty.

11-4.sanskrit:
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो।

योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयाऽत्मानमव्ययम्।।11.4।।
11-4.transliteration:
manyase yadi tach chhakyaṁ mayā draṣhṭum iti prabho
yogeśhvara tato me tvaṁ darśhayātmānam avyayam

translation.simple: My dear Lord, if You feel I am worthy and able to see it, then, O Master of all spiritual power, please show me Your eternal and never-changing Self.
translation.deep: With profound humility, Arjuna yearns for a glimpse of the Divine. He appeals to Lord Krishna, 'If You, O Master of all spiritual paths, see within me the capacity to truly comprehend, then kindly reveal Your imperishable and eternal Self to me.' This heartfelt prayer is a testament to complete surrender, trusting the Lord's judgment and grace to bestow a vision of His changeless essence, which transcends all temporary forms.
translation.essence: A humble plea from the heart: 'O Lord, if You find me capable, please reveal Your eternal, unchanging Self.' It's a prayer for divine vision, granted solely by the Lord's grace, acknowledging Him as the supreme Master of all spiritual understanding and mystic power.

11-5.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।

नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च।।11.5।।
11-5.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
paśhya me pārtha rūpāṇi śhataśho ’tha sahasraśhaḥ
nānā-vidhāni divyāni nānā-varṇākṛitīni cha

translation.simple: Lord Krishna tenderly spoke to Arjuna, 'My dear Arjuna, look now! Behold My countless forms, thousands upon thousands. See them in their divine beauty, each one unique in color and shape.'
translation.deep: Here, the Blessed Lord opens a window to His limitless presence. He gently asks Arjuna, and through him, all of us, to witness the myriad manifestations of the Divine. Imagine the wonder of seeing countless forms, each vibrant and unique, yet all stemming from the same sacred source. This verse invites us to quietly contemplate the boundless beauty and variety of the Divine, reminding us that every shape, every hue, is but a whisper of His infinite glory.
translation.essence: With gentle love, Lord Krishna beckons Arjuna to witness His countless divine forms, each a unique expression of His boundless beauty and omnipresent nature.

11-6.transliteration:
paśhyādityān vasūn rudrān aśhvinau marutas tathā
bahūny adṛiṣhṭa-pūrvāṇi paśhyāśhcharyāṇi bhārata

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, just behold! See the glorious Adityas, the benevolent Vasus, the mighty Rudras, the divine Ashvins, and the powerful Maruts. And beyond them, gaze upon countless marvels, wonders you have never, ever seen before.
translation.deep: In this sacred moment, the Lord gently reveals to Arjuna that all the revered deities—the radiant Adityas, the sustaining Vasus, the powerful Rudras, the swift Ashvins, and the strong Maruts—are gracefully held within His own boundless form. This vision deepens our understanding, showing that the divine source is not separate but wonderfully encompasses all. It's an invitation to experience the quiet majesty and all-encompassing nature of the Divine, inspiring profound reverence and wonder within our hearts.
translation.essence: Here, the Lord reveals His infinite cosmic form, lovingly showing Arjuna that all divine beings, along with countless new and astonishing wonders, beautifully reside within Him, inviting us to gently behold the boundless and all-encompassing presence of the Divine.

11-7.sanskrit:
इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम्।

मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि।।11.7।।
11-7.transliteration:
ihaika-sthaṁ jagat kṛitsnaṁ paśhyādya sa-charācharam
mama dehe guḍākeśha yach chānyad draṣhṭum ichchhasi

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, look now within My divine form. See the entire universe, with all its moving and unmoving beings, held together as one. And behold whatever else your heart yearns to see.
translation.deep: O Arjuna, within the sanctuary of My divine form, perceive the entirety of creation. All that moves and all that rests, the boundless cosmos, is gracefully united within My very being. Gaze upon this wondrous unity, and know that any truth your heart seeks to behold is manifest right here.
translation.essence: The Divine Lord lovingly reveals that all of creation, in its countless forms and movements, resides eternally and harmoniously within His single, boundless form. Every truth you seek to understand is inherently present within Him.

11-8.sanskrit:
न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा।

दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्।।11.8।।
11-8.transliteration:
na tu māṁ śhakyase draṣhṭum anenaiva sva-chakṣhuṣhā
divyaṁ dadāmi te chakṣhuḥ paśhya me yogam aiśhwaram

translation.simple: Lord Krishna says, "With your ordinary eyes, you cannot behold My complete divine form. Therefore, I lovingly give you a special, divine vision. Now, witness My supreme and majestic power."
translation.deep: Lord Krishna tenderly explains that the true, all-encompassing nature of the Divine is beyond the limited scope of our physical senses. Out of His boundless mercy, He grants a sacred, inner sight – a divine eye – which enables one to transcend earthly perception. Through this grace, one can truly witness His magnificent, universal form and the wondrous, omnipotent power that orchestrates all creation, a profound spiritual revelation.
translation.essence: Our human eyes cannot grasp the Lord's full divine majesty. By His grace, He grants a divine vision, allowing us to perceive His ultimate, wondrous cosmic power.

11-9.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच

एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः।

दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम्।।11.9।।
11-9.transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
evam uktvā tato rājan mahā-yogeśhvaro hariḥ
darśhayām āsa pārthāya paramaṁ rūpam aiśhwaram

translation.simple: Sanjaya beautifully described how, after His words, Lord Krishna, the supreme Master of all spiritual power, gently revealed His most glorious divine form to Arjuna. It was a moment of profound grace.
translation.deep: Sanjaya describes a moment of profound spiritual significance. Having spoken words of wisdom, Lord Krishna, the supreme master of all yogic and divine energies, compassionately unveiled His most magnificent and all-encompassing divine form to Arjuna. This was a direct, personal revelation of the absolute truth, offered as an act of immense grace, allowing Arjuna to witness the Lord's inconceivable glory and power.
translation.essence: This verse captures the essence of divine grace: Lord Krishna, the ultimate source of all power and wisdom, chose to reveal His supreme, awe-inspiring form to Arjuna, bestowing a profound spiritual vision.

translation.simple: Lord Krishna's universal form is wondrous to behold. It has countless faces and eyes, showing endless marvels. Adorned with many divine ornaments, it also holds many celestial weapons, shining brightly.
translation.deep: In this grand vision, the Lord's universal form manifests with an infinite expanse of faces and eyes, symbolizing His all-seeing presence and all-knowing wisdom. Every part of this form is a marvel, radiant with divine adornments, signifying His supreme majesty. The countless celestial weapons held aloft represent His cosmic power, ever ready to uphold dharma and protect the universe, yet presented with a calm, all-encompassing grace.
translation.essence: The Lord's divine form is described here as having endless faces and eyes, showing His boundless presence and perception. It is magnificently adorned with divine jewels and holds many celestial weapons, revealing His supreme splendor and power in the universe.

11-11.transliteration:
divya-mālyāmbara-dharaṁ divya-gandhānulepanam
sarvāśhcharya-mayaṁ devam anantaṁ viśhvato-mukham

translation.simple: He was adorned with divine garlands and beautiful garments, fragrant with heavenly scents. This wondrous divine form was endless, with faces in every direction, showing His omnipresence.
translation.deep: This verse reveals the Lord in His universal form, a vision of boundless divine splendor. He is adorned with celestial garlands and robes, fragrant with heavenly perfumes, symbolizing His transcendent purity and beauty. His presence is described as infinite, with countless faces, signifying His all-encompassing nature and that He is present in every direction, a source of endless wonder and devotion.
translation.essence: The Lord's Universal Form embodies endless divine beauty, wonder, and omnipresence, reminding us of His boundless, all-encompassing nature.

11-12.sanskrit:
दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता।

यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः।।11.12।।
11-12.transliteration:
divi sūrya-sahasrasya bhaved yugapad utthitā
yadi bhāḥ sadṛiśhī sā syād bhāsas tasya mahātmanaḥ

translation.simple: Imagine a thousand suns rising all at once in the sky. Even their magnificent light would only begin to resemble the divine radiance emanating from that Great Soul, the Supreme Lord.
translation.deep: This verse offers a profound glimpse into the Lord's immeasurable glory, showing us that even the most spectacular natural phenomena are but faint reflections of His true splendor. It invites us to ponder the ungraspable magnitude of the Divine, whose light is so intense and all-encompassing that no earthly comparison can fully capture its awe-inspiring essence.
translation.essence: The Lord's divine light is beyond all earthly comprehension, infinitely brighter and more glorious than a thousand suns shining as one. It is pure, boundless, and utterly incomparable splendor.

11-13.sanskrit:
तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा।

अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा।।11.13।।
11-13.transliteration:
tatraika-sthaṁ jagat kṛitsnaṁ pravibhaktam anekadhā
apaśhyad deva-devasya śharīre pāṇḍavas tadā

translation.simple: Then, Arjuna witnessed the entire universe, with all its countless forms and divisions, held together as one within the splendid body of the Lord of all gods.
translation.deep: In that awe-inspiring moment, Arjuna truly understood. He saw the vast and wonderfully diverse cosmos, with all its myriad beings and creations, resting as a single, harmonious whole within the magnificent form of the Supreme Lord. This vision revealed the profound truth: everything originates from and is eternally sustained by the Divine.
translation.essence: Arjuna saw the entire universe, in all its wondrous diversity, perfectly unified and held within the divine body of the Lord, revealing His all-encompassing presence and absolute unity.

11-14.sanskrit:
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः।

प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत।।11.14।।
11-14.transliteration:
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣhṭo hṛiṣhṭa-romā dhanañjayaḥ
praṇamya śhirasā devaṁ kṛitāñjalir abhāṣhata

translation.simple: Then, Arjuna, filled with immense wonder, his hair standing on end from awe, humbly bowed his head to the Lord. With his hands joined in reverence, he began to speak.
translation.deep: Witnessing the breathtaking cosmic form of the Divine, Arjuna was overcome with an exquisite wonder that thrilled his very being, causing his hair to stand on end. In that moment of profound spiritual impact and absolute devotion, he gently bowed his head in complete surrender to the Supreme Lord, and with his palms joined in humble prayer, he prepared to offer his heartfelt words.
translation.essence: This verse beautifully captures Arjuna's immediate and overwhelming response to the divine vision: profound awe, deep reverence, and complete surrender, expressed through his physical reactions and the humble gesture of bowing before he even uttered a word.

11-15.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे

सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान्।

ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थ

मृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान्।।11.15।।
11-15.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
paśhyāmi devāns tava deva dehe
sarvāns tathā bhūta-viśheṣha-saṅghān
brahmāṇam īśhaṁ kamalāsana-stham
ṛiṣhīnśh cha sarvān uragānśh cha divyān

translation.simple: Arjuna humbly said: O Lord, within Your magnificent form, my eyes behold all the celestial beings. I see every diverse creation, gathered there. Lord Brahma, seated upon his lotus seat, is visible, along with all the revered sages and the divine serpents.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully captures Arjuna's profound awe as he beholds the entire cosmos within the Lord's form. It signifies a moment where the individual perception is utterly transformed, expanding to embrace the infinite wonder of creation. Arjuna witnesses the interconnectedness of all existence, from the highest celestial beings to the ancient sages and mystical serpents, all gently held within the Supreme Being. It's a sweet reminder that the divine presence encompasses everything, revealing the Lord as the source and sustainer of all.
translation.essence: This verse reveals Arjuna's astonished vision of the entire cosmos contained within Lord Krishna's divine form. It beautifully conveys the truth that the Supreme Lord is the source and shelter of all beings, from the highest deities to the humblest creations, all existing harmoniously within Him.

11-16.sanskrit:
अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं

पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम्।

नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं

पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप।।11.16।।
11-16.transliteration:
aneka-bāhūdara-vaktra-netraṁ
paśhyāmi tvāṁ sarvato ’nanta-rūpam
nāntaṁ na madhyaṁ na punas tavādiṁ
paśhyāmi viśhveśhvara viśhva-rūpa

translation.simple: O Lord, I gaze upon You everywhere, with countless arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes. Your form is truly endless, O Universal Lord. I cannot perceive Your beginning, middle, or end. You are the Supreme Master of all creation.
translation.deep: O Lord, in this overwhelming vision, I see Your Universal Form everywhere, adorned with countless arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes. Your presence stretches boundlessly in every direction, revealing an infinity that transcends my comprehension. I cannot find Your beginning, Your middle, or Your end, O Supreme Lord of the universe. This sacred sight fills my heart with deep wonder and reverence for Your all-encompassing, eternal nature.
translation.essence: This verse captures the awe-inspiring experience of beholding the Lord's Universal Form as utterly boundless and eternal, without a discernible beginning, middle, or end, embracing the entire cosmos.

11-17.sanskrit:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च

तेजोराशिं सर्वतोदीप्तिमन्तम्।

पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ता

द्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम्।।11.17।।
11-17.transliteration:
kirīṭinaṁ gadinaṁ chakriṇaṁ cha
tejo-rāśhiṁ sarvato dīptimantam
paśhyāmi tvāṁ durnirīkṣhyaṁ samantād
dīptānalārka-dyutim aprameyam

translation.simple: My Lord, I behold Your magnificent form, crowned and holding Your mace and discus. You are a boundless ocean of light, shining brilliantly from all sides. It is hard to fix my gaze upon You, for Your splendor is like countless blazing fires and suns, truly immeasurable.
translation.deep: In this awe-inspiring vision, I perceive You, Lord, adorned with symbols of sovereignty and divine power – the crown, mace, and discus. Your very being is a boundless treasury of light, radiating luminosity in every direction. This form is so intensely brilliant, like the combined force of blazing fires and suns, that it becomes nearly impossible to gaze upon directly. This hints at Your transcendental nature, revealing a glory that surpasses all human comprehension and perception, a light that illuminates all yet remains beyond full grasp.
translation.essence: The verse captures Arjuna's profound awe as he beholds the Lord's cosmic form. He describes it as an immeasurable ocean of light, radiating brilliance from every direction, adorned with divine symbols of power. This overwhelming radiance, like countless suns and fires, signifies the Lord's infinite, transcendent nature, beautiful yet beyond human comprehension.

11-18.sanskrit:
त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं

त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम्।

त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता

सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे।।11.18।।
11-18.transliteration:
tvam akṣharaṁ paramaṁ veditavyaṁ
tvam asya viśhvasya paraṁ nidhānam
tvam avyayaḥ śhāśhvata-dharma-goptā
sanātanas tvaṁ puruṣho mato me

translation.simple: You are the eternal truth, the supreme one to be understood. You are the ultimate support and resting place for this whole universe. You are changeless, the guardian of everlasting righteousness, the ancient, eternal Divine Being – this is my firm conviction.
translation.deep: O Lord, You are the imperishable Reality, the highest truth that all spiritual seekers yearn to comprehend. You are the ultimate foundation and sacred sanctuary for this entire cosmic creation. Undecaying and constant, You are the divine guardian of the eternal cosmic order and righteousness. My unwavering realization is that You are indeed the most ancient, primeval Divine Person.
translation.essence: The Supreme Lord is the imperishable, ultimate truth to be known, the supreme support of the universe, the eternal protector of Dharma, and the primordial, everlasting Divine Being.

11-19.sanskrit:
अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य

मनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम्।

पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम्

स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम्।।11.19।।

translation.simple: My Lord, I see You without a beginning, middle, or end, possessing boundless power. Your arms are countless, and the sun and moon are Your eyes. Your face shines like a blazing fire, and with Your own brilliant light, You illuminate and pervade this entire universe.
translation.deep: O Lord, I witness Your majestic form, eternal and infinite, transcending all limits of time – without beginning, middle, or end. Your divine energy is boundless, Your arms extend endlessly to embrace creation, and the sun and moon serve as Your watchful eyes. Your radiant countenance, like a brilliant fire, radiates a powerful warmth that pervades and illuminates every atom of this vast cosmos. My soul is filled with serene wonder at Your magnificent presence.
translation.essence: This verse reveals the Lord as the ultimate, timeless reality—infinite in power, without origin or end. His cosmic form is all-pervading, with the sun and moon as His eyes, and His inherent brilliance illuminates and sustains the entire universe.

11-20.sanskrit:
द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि

व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः।

दृष्ट्वाऽद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं

लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन्।।11.20।।
11-20.transliteration:
dyāv ā-pṛithivyor idam antaraṁ hi
vyāptaṁ tvayaikena diśhaśh cha sarvāḥ
dṛiṣhṭvādbhutaṁ rūpam ugraṁ tavedaṁ
loka-trayaṁ pravyathitaṁ mahātman

translation.simple: O Great Soul, You alone fill the vast space between heaven and earth, extending into every direction. As I behold Your wondrous and mighty form, all three worlds are deeply moved, feeling a profound reverence and awe.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully conveys the boundless nature of the Divine. The Supreme Lord is not merely present everywhere; He *is* the entire cosmos, the very space between heaven and earth, and every direction. When this majestic and intensely powerful Universal Form is unveiled, it profoundly impacts all beings across the three worlds, stirring within them a mix of wonder, awe, and a deep sense of being overcome by such immense glory.
translation.essence: The Supreme Lord's presence is boundless, encompassing all of creation. His glorious form, though intensely powerful, reveals the ultimate truth of His all-pervading reality, stirring profound awe in all.

11-21.sanskrit:
अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घाः विशन्ति

केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति।

स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः

स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः।।11.21।।
11-21.transliteration:
amī hi tvāṁ sura-saṅghā viśhanti
kechid bhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛiṇanti
svastīty uktvā maharṣhi-siddha-saṅghāḥ
stuvanti tvāṁ stutibhiḥ puṣhkalābhiḥ

translation.simple: In Your magnificent form, O Lord, countless divine beings are seen entering. Some, overcome with a reverent awe, offer You their praises with folded hands. Great sages and perfected souls, uttering words of peace and universal well-being, pour forth abundant hymns of devotion for You.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully illustrates the all-encompassing nature of the Divine. All beings, from celestial gods to wise sages, are drawn into Your boundless presence, each responding in their own way. Some are filled with a profound reverence mixed with awe, while others, with deep wisdom, pray for the welfare of all existence. It shows that whether through fear-tinged respect or through enlightened devotion, all worship ultimately flows towards You, the Supreme Lord.
translation.essence: All creation, from gods to sages, reverently acknowledges Your supreme presence, O Lord, offering praise and seeking universal peace in Your boundless form.

11-22.sanskrit:
रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्या

विश्वेऽश्िवनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च।

गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घा

वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे।।11.22।।
11-22.transliteration:
rudrādityā vasavo ye cha sādhyā
viśhve ’śhvinau marutaśh choṣhmapāśh cha
gandharva-yakṣhāsura-siddha-saṅghā
vīkṣhante tvāṁ vismitāśh chaiva sarve

translation.simple: Even the mighty Rudras, Adityas, and Vasus, along with the Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, Ashvinis, Maruts, and Ushmapas—indeed, all the Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and hosts of perfected beings—they all gaze upon You, Lord, filled with profound wonder.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully illustrates the unparalleled majesty of the Lord's Universal Form. It is not just ordinary beings who are awestruck, but the very architects and inhabitants of various celestial realms—the gods, demigods, and perfected beings—who are themselves powerful and revered. Their collective astonishment underscores the infinite, all-encompassing nature of the Divine, a form so grand it humbles and inspires reverence in even the most exalted entities across creation. It reminds us that before the Lord's supreme glory, all beings stand in humble admiration.
translation.essence: The divine form of the Lord is so universally magnificent that all celestial beings, from the greatest gods to various semi-divine hosts, are utterly captivated and filled with deep awe upon beholding it.

11-23.sanskrit:
रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं

महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम्।

बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं

दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाऽहम्।।11.23।।
11-23.transliteration:
rūpaṁ mahat te bahu-vaktra-netraṁ
mahā-bāho bahu-bāhūru-pādam
bahūdaraṁ bahu-danṣhṭrā-karālaṁ
dṛiṣhṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitās tathāham

translation.simple: Lord, I behold Your immense form, adorned with countless faces and eyes, many arms, thighs, and feet. Your vastness, with numerous bellies and awe-inspiring fangs, fills all beings and me with wonder and a profound tremor.
translation.deep: When the Divine manifests in its full, boundless glory, it transcends human comprehension. This vision is not merely of a multi-limbed deity, but of the very fabric of existence, encompassing all creation and destruction. This awe-inspiring sight, with its myriad expressions and powerful aspects, naturally overwhelms the limited mind. It’s a glimpse into the cosmic dance, where every atom and every universe finds its source and end in the Beloved. This experience, though initially unsettling, ultimately serves to dissolve the limited self, urging complete surrender to the incomprehensible vastness of the Divine.
translation.essence: Beholding the Lord's universal form, vast with countless faces, limbs, and powerful aspects, fills all beings, and Arjuna, with profound awe and sacred tremor, revealing the all-encompassing nature of the Divine.

11-24.sanskrit:
नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं

व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम्।

दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा

धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो।।11.24।।
11-24.transliteration:
nabhaḥ-spṛiśhaṁ dīptam aneka-varṇaṁ
vyāttānanaṁ dīpta-viśhāla-netram
dṛiṣhṭvā hi tvāṁ pravyathitāntar-ātmā
dhṛitiṁ na vindāmi śhamaṁ cha viṣhṇo

translation.simple: O Vishnu, as I gaze upon Your boundless form, touching the very heavens, radiant with countless hues, with vast, open mouth and fiery, wide eyes—my very soul trembles. I can find no calm, no steadiness within myself.
translation.deep: Witnessing Your cosmic manifestation, O Vishnu, so immense it touches the sky, shining with every conceivable color, its gaze piercing and its mouth vast, stirs a profound disquiet deep within my being. In this overwhelming vision, my usual composure and inner peace have completely forsaken me. It is a moment of divine revelation that both humbles and profoundly shakes the human spirit, prompting a raw confrontation with the unimaginable power of the Lord.
translation.essence: When the infinite divine form reveals itself, vast and brilliant, it can initially overwhelm the devotee, shattering worldly peace and stability, and awakening a deeper, transformative surrender.

11-25.sanskrit:
दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि

दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि।

दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म

प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास।।11.25।।
11-25.transliteration:
danṣhṭrā-karālāni cha te mukhāni
dṛiṣhṭvaiva kālānala-sannibhāni
diśho na jāne na labhe cha śharma
prasīda deveśha jagan-nivāsa

translation.simple: O Lord, seeing Your magnificent forms, vast and powerful like the cosmic fire, leaves me disoriented and restless. I seek Your grace, O Lord of all beings, You who are the dwelling place of the entire universe.
translation.deep: Witnessing Your awe-inspiring countenances, immense as the consuming fire of ages, brings a profound disorientation; I lose my sense of direction and inner calm. In this moment of overwhelming revelation, I earnestly implore Your divine grace, O Lord of all deities, O ultimate resting place of the entire cosmos.
translation.essence: In the face of Your grand cosmic presence, which can be both awe-inspiring and overwhelming, my soul seeks Your calming grace and solace. O Lord, You are the heart of all existence, please bless me with Your peace.

11-26.sanskrit:
अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः

सर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः।

भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथाऽसौ

सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः।।11.26।।
11-26.transliteration:
amī cha tvāṁ dhṛitarāśhtrasya putrāḥ
sarve sahaivāvani-pāla-saṅghaiḥ
bhīṣhmo droṇaḥ sūta-putras tathāsau
sahāsmadīyair api yodha-mukhyaiḥ
 vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśhanti
danṣhṭrā-karālāni bhayānakāni
kechid vilagnā daśhanāntareṣhu
sandṛiśhyante chūrṇitair uttamāṅgaiḥ

translation.simple: Arjuna perceives all the sons of Dhritarashtra, accompanied by many kings, moving towards You. Even revered figures like Bhishma and Drona, and the mighty Karna, along with our own chief warriors, are all seen approaching You.
translation.deep: Within this awe-inspiring vision, Arjuna beholds a profound revelation: all beings, from the royal sons of Dhritarashtra to the most celebrated warriors like Bhishma, Drona, and Karna, and indeed, his own valiant commanders, are all irresistibly drawn into Your magnificent Universal Form. This sacred sight gently reminds us of the divine truth that all life's journeys culminate in the Supreme Lord, the timeless refuge and ultimate destination for every soul.
translation.essence: All warriors, from kings to great heroes like Bhishma and Drona, are seen merging into the Divine, illustrating the ultimate return of all souls to the Lord.

11-27.sanskrit:
वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्ति

दंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि।

केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु

संदृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः।।11.27।।
11-27.transliteration: vaktrāṇi te  tvaramāṇā   viśanti daṁṣṭrā-karālāni    bhayānakāni kecid   vilagnā daśanāntareṣu   sandṛśyante cūrṇitair   uttamāṅgaiḥ

translation.simple: O Lord, I behold countless beings swiftly entering Your fearsome mouths, terrible with their mighty fangs. Some are seen caught between Your teeth, their forms appearing utterly consumed, a testament to Your immense power.
translation.deep: In this awe-inspiring vision, O Supreme Lord, I witness the ceaseless flow of all beings into Your formidable, fanged mouths. This portrays the relentless cycle of time and the universal truth that all forms eventually return to their source. Some, appearing caught within Your mighty teeth, symbolize the transient nature of individual existences, gracefully absorbed into the boundless reality of Your divine being, affirming Your absolute control over all creation and dissolution.
translation.essence: This verse powerfully conveys the Lord's all-encompassing sovereignty over the cosmic dance of creation and dissolution, where all beings ultimately merge into the Universal Form, revealing the profound truth of divine will and time.

11-28.sanskrit:
यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाः

समुद्रमेवाभिमुखाः द्रवन्ति।

तथा तवामी नरलोकवीरा

विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति।।11.28।।
11-28.transliteration:
yathā nadīnāṁ bahavo ’mbu-vegāḥ
samudram evābhimukhā dravanti
tathā tavāmī nara-loka-vīrā
viśhanti vaktrāṇy abhivijvalanti

translation.simple: Just as many mighty rivers, with their rushing waters, naturally flow and merge into the vast ocean, so too, these valiant heroes of the human world are entering Your brilliant, all-consuming countenances.
translation.deep: This profound imagery reveals the natural and irresistible pull of the Divine. Like countless rivers surrendering to the ocean's expanse, all of creation, including the most powerful individuals, is ultimately drawn into and absorbed by the Supreme Lord's boundless presence. It teaches us about the grand cycle of existence, where everything originates from and eventually returns to its divine source, demonstrating God's ultimate sovereignty and the inherent destiny of all souls to merge with the Divine.
translation.essence: Like rivers flowing into the ocean, all beings and their life's journey ultimately merge into the Lord's supreme, radiant, and all-encompassing divine form, affirming His absolute power and grace.

11-29.sanskrit:
यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गा

विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः।

तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोका

स्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः।।11.29।।
11-29.transliteration:
yathā pradīptaṁ jvalanaṁ pataṅgā
viśhanti nāśhāya samṛiddha-vegāḥ
tathaiva nāśhāya viśhanti lokās
tavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛiddha-vegāḥ

translation.simple: Just as moths are swiftly drawn into a blazing fire, meeting their end, so too do all beings hasten into Your mighty mouths, O Lord, moving quickly towards their dissolution. It's a gentle reminder that everything ultimately merges back into You.
translation.deep: This profound vision illustrates the universal flow of time and the cosmic cycle of creation and dissolution. All of existence, with a spontaneous urgency, returns to its divine origin. Like fragile moths drawn to an immense flame, all worlds and beings are absorbed into Your vast, all-encompassing form, revealing the relentless unfolding of time and the ultimate truth that You are the alpha and omega of all. This reminds us to look beyond the temporary and find peace in Your eternal presence, understanding that what appears as an end is simply a return to You.
translation.essence: All of creation, like eager moths, rushes inevitably into the divine embrace of the Lord, signifying the eternal cycle of return and dissolution within His supreme form.

11-30.sanskrit:
लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ता

ल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः।

तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रं

भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो।।11.30।।
11-30.transliteration:
lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantāl
lokān samagrān vadanair jvaladbhiḥ
tejobhir āpūrya jagat samagraṁ
bhāsas tavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣhṇo

translation.simple: O Lord, I see Your glorious form with blazing mouths, drawing all beings from every direction into Your very self. Your intense, brilliant light fills the entire universe, shining with an all-consuming radiance.
translation.deep: In this awe-inspiring vision, Arjuna beholds the Lord as the very essence of time, which relentlessly brings all creation to its culmination. The blazing mouths symbolize the sacred cycle of existence, where everything ultimately returns to its source in the Divine. This fierce, all-pervading light reminds us that the Lord's power is absolute, maintaining the cosmic order through both creation and dissolution, a profound mystery of His boundless glory.
translation.essence: This verse gently reminds us of the Lord's all-encompassing power, the one who brings all of existence to its culmination. It's a comforting thought that every phase of life, even dissolution, is part of His divine plan, inviting us to surrender to His eternal embrace.

11-31.sanskrit:
आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो

नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद।

विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यं

न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम्।।11.31।।
11-31.transliteration:
ākhyāhi me ko bhavān ugra-rūpo
namo ’stu te deva-vara prasīda
vijñātum ichchhāmi bhavantam ādyaṁ
na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛittim

translation.simple: O Lord, please reveal to me who You are in this magnificent and awe-inspiring form. I offer my humble salutations to You, the most excellent of all divine beings; please be gracious and kind. My heart yearns to truly know You, the primeval source of all existence, for I simply cannot comprehend the profound workings of Your divine will.
translation.deep: This verse echoes the seeker's profound humility and earnest longing when confronted with the immense, all-encompassing presence of the Divine. Arjuna, in awe and wonder, humbly bows to the Supreme Lord, addressing Him as the 'best among gods,' imploring His grace amidst the overwhelming vision of the Universal Form. His plea to 'know You, the original source' is a timeless yearning of the soul to understand the ultimate truth beyond appearances, coupled with an honest admission that the vast, intricate tapestry of divine action often lies beyond human comprehension, inviting deeper surrender and faith.
translation.essence: A heartfelt prayer for clarity and grace, this verse embodies the soul's awe before the Divine's mysterious grandeur. It is a humble request to understand the Supreme Lord's true nature and purpose, acknowledging that divine ways transcend our understanding, and seeking only His compassion and revelation.

11-32.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो

लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः।

ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे

येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः।।11.32।।
11-32.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
kālo ’smi loka-kṣhaya-kṛit pravṛiddho
lokān samāhartum iha pravṛittaḥ
ṛite ’pi tvāṁ na bhaviṣhyanti sarve
ye ’vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣhu yodhāḥ

translation.simple: The Supreme Lord revealed: 'I am Time itself, the mighty force that brings all worlds to their close. I am here to gather all beings back into Me. Rest assured, Arjuna, even without your participation, none of these warriors arrayed before you will remain, for their journey's end is already ordained.'
translation.deep: The Lord, full of grace, shared: 'I am the very current of Time, the expansive power that draws all creation to its gentle close. I have manifested to bring all these realms back into My being. Be at peace, Arjuna, for even if you were to stand aside, all these brave souls arrayed in the opposing armies would still pass from this world. Their appointed time has arrived, guided by My eternal plan.'
translation.essence: Lord Krishna lovingly reveals Himself as Time, the ultimate and vast force that brings all things to their culmination. He assures Arjuna that the passing of all these warriors is already part of the divine plan, regardless of Arjuna's actions, emphasizing the preordained nature of cosmic events.

11-33.sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व

जित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम्।

मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव

निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन्।।11.33।।
11-33.transliteration:
tasmāt tvam uttiṣhṭha yaśho labhasva
jitvā śhatrūn bhuṅkṣhva rājyaṁ samṛiddham
mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva
nimitta-mātraṁ bhava savya-sāchin

translation.simple: Therefore, dear Arjuna, arise and claim your glory. Overcome your adversaries and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. These foes have already been vanquished by Me. Be merely an instrument in My divine play, O skilled warrior.
translation.deep: Rise, noble soul, for your destiny of honor and a thriving life awaits. Understand with a peaceful heart that the path has already been cleared; these challenges are already overcome by My divine will. Your role is simply to be a pure channel, a loving instrument, through which My plan unfolds. Act with unwavering faith, knowing you are guided.
translation.essence: Trust in the divine plan; rise and act with courage, knowing that the outcome is already ordained. Be a humble instrument of God's will, and let peace guide your actions.

11-34.sanskrit:
द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च

कर्णं तथाऽन्यानपि योधवीरान्।

मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठा

युध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान्।।11.34।।
11-34.transliteration:
droṇaṁ cha bhīṣhmaṁ cha jayadrathaṁ cha
karṇaṁ tathānyān api yodha-vīrān
mayā hatāṁs tvaṁ jahi mā vyathiṣhṭhā
yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān

translation.simple: Know that great warriors like Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, and Karna, along with many others, have already been vanquished by My divine will. Simply act, Arjuna. Do not feel sorrow or fear. Fight with courage, for you are destined to conquer your opponents in this sacred battle.
translation.deep: The Lord reveals a profound truth: the destiny of even the mightiest warriors, such as Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, and Karna, is already determined by His supreme will. They are, in essence, already vanquished by Him, the ultimate orchestrator of all creation. Arjuna is asked to be a pure instrument in this divine unfolding, to act out his duty without attachment to the outcome. This message encourages complete surrender and faith, reminding us that true victory lies in aligning our actions with the divine plan, trusting that the Supreme Lord has already set the course, and our part is to perform our dharma with devotion and a tranquil heart.
translation.essence: The Lord assures that the outcome is already divinely settled. Your duty is to act with faith, free from anxiety, knowing that all events are orchestrated by Him. Fight with courage and a peaceful heart, for victory is assured when you align with His will.

11-35.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच

एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य

कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी।

नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णं

सगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य।।11.35।।
11-35.transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
etach chhrutvā vachanaṁ keśhavasya
kṛitāñjalir vepamānaḥ kirīṭī
namaskṛitvā bhūya evāha kṛiṣhṇaṁ
sa-gadgadaṁ bhīta-bhītaḥ praṇamya

translation.simple: Upon hearing the words of Lord Keshava, Arjuna, with hands folded in reverence, began to tremble. Filled with awe and a sacred fear, he bowed down once more and, with a faltering voice, spoke to Krishna.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully portrays Arjuna's complete surrender and profound awe after experiencing the Lord's universal form. His trembling signifies not mere fear, but a spiritual tremor of realization before the boundless Divine. With hands folded in deep reverence and a voice choked with devotion and humility, he prepares to offer his heartfelt prayers, utterly humbled by the Supreme Truth.
translation.essence: Arjuna, overwhelmed by the divine revelation, expresses his awe and devotion through profound humility. His trembling body and faltering voice mark a moment of complete surrender and spiritual reverence before the Supreme Lord.

11-36.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या

जगत् प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च।

रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति

सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः।।11.36।।
11-36.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
sthāne hṛiṣhīkeśha tava prakīrtyā
jagat prahṛiṣhyaty anurajyate cha
rakṣhānsi bhītāni diśho dravanti
sarve namasyanti cha siddha-saṅghāḥ

translation.simple: Arjuna said: O Lord of our senses, it is truly fitting that the whole world rejoices and becomes filled with love when Your greatness is celebrated. All those who seek to cause harm flee in fear, while all the enlightened souls humbly bow down to You.
translation.deep: Arjuna speaks from his heart: O Hrishikesha, it feels so right, so natural, that Your divine presence and boundless glory fill the world with deep joy and unwavering love. In Your light, all shadows of fear and negativity are scattered, and those who embody harmful intentions flee. At the same time, all the elevated souls, those who have achieved spiritual wisdom, instinctively bow down in humble reverence, recognizing Your supreme truth.
translation.essence: This verse beautifully captures how the Lord's supreme glory naturally evokes joy and devotion throughout the cosmos, scattering fear and evil, while inspiring profound reverence from all perfected beings.

11-37.sanskrit:
कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन्

गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे।

अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास

त्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत्।।11.37।।
11-37.transliteration:
kasmāch cha te na nameran mahātman
garīyase brahmaṇo ’py ādi-kartre
ananta deveśha jagan-nivāsa
tvam akṣharaṁ sad-asat tat paraṁ yat

translation.simple: O Great Soul, why would anyone not bow to You? You are even greater than Lord Brahma, the first creator. O Endless One, Lord of all divine beings, You dwell in all creation. You are the unchanging reality, present in all that exists and all that doesn't, and even beyond.
translation.deep: Arjuna, overwhelmed, asks a rhetorical question: how could anyone not bow to the Lord? This reveals a profound understanding of the Divine as the supreme origin, superior even to the revered Creator Brahma. The names 'Infinite One,' 'Lord of all Devas,' and 'Dweller in all worlds' reflect His limitless power and omnipresence. Finally, declaring Him 'the imperishable, both manifest and unmanifest, and that which transcends even these' beautifully captures the Absolute Truth – the eternal, unchanging reality that encompasses everything, yet remains beyond all categories and definitions.
translation.essence: This verse is an offering of pure devotion, acknowledging the Lord as the supreme, unchangeable source of all creation. He is the Infinite One, greater than all, dwelling within and beyond everything, the eternal truth to whom all beings naturally bow.

11-38.sanskrit:
त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराण

स्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम्।

वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम

त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप।।11.38।।
11-38.transliteration:
tvam ādi-devaḥ puruṣhaḥ purāṇas
tvam asya viśhvasya paraṁ nidhānam
vettāsi vedyaṁ cha paraṁ cha dhāma
tvayā tataṁ viśhvam ananta-rūpa

translation.simple: My Dearest Lord, You are the very first God, the most ancient soul, timeless and eternal. You are the supreme resting place for this entire universe. You know all there is to know, You are that which is to be known, and You are our highest spiritual home. With Your boundless forms, You gently pervade everything.
translation.deep: You are the primal Deity, the timeless Spirit, the ancient wellspring of all existence. In You, O Lord, this entire cosmos finds its ultimate refuge and unwavering foundation. You are the supreme Knower, the ultimate object of all sacred knowledge, and the highest abode to which all beings aspire. Through Your boundless essence, manifesting in infinite forms, You lovingly permeate every particle of this vast creation, holding it all in Your divine embrace.
translation.essence: O Lord, You are the primeval God, the eternal foundation, the ultimate knowledge, and the all-pervading spirit of infinite forms that lovingly embraces the entire universe.

11-39.sanskrit:
वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः

प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च।

नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः

पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते।।11.39।।
11-39.transliteration:
vāyur yamo ’gnir varuṇaḥ śhaśhāṅkaḥ
prajāpatis tvaṁ prapitāmahaśh cha
namo namas te ’stu sahasra-kṛitvaḥ
punaśh cha bhūyo ’pi namo namas te

translation.simple: O Lord, You are the essence of the wind, the fire, the waters, and the gentle moon. You are the creator of all beings, and indeed, the most ancient ancestor. I bow to You again and again, a thousand times over, and then once more, offering my deepest reverence to You.
translation.deep: In this awe-inspiring vision, O Beloved Lord, I perceive You as the very soul of all cosmic powers: the life-breath of the wind, the purifying flame, the nurturing waters, and the serene moon. You are the original creator of all existence, and indeed, the most ancient ancestor from whom everything originates. With a heart brimming with profound gratitude and reverence, I offer You countless salutations, a thousand times over, and then again and again, humbly bowing to Your boundless majesty.
translation.essence: This verse beautifully captures Arjuna's profound realization that Lord Krishna is the very essence of all divine powers and the root of creation. Overcome with loving devotion, he offers an endless cascade of salutations, humbly bowing to the Lord's infinite and all-pervading glory.

11-40.sanskrit:
नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते

नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व।

अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं

सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः।।11.40।।
11-40.transliteration:
namaḥ purastād atha pṛiṣhṭhatas te
namo ’stu te sarvata eva sarva
ananta-vīryāmita-vikramas tvaṁ
sarvaṁ samāpnoṣhi tato ’si sarvaḥ

translation.simple: My humble bows to You, Lord, from every direction – in front, behind, and all around. Your strength is endless, Your valor boundless. You fill all that exists, and truly, You are all that is.
translation.deep: My devotion reaches You, O Lord, from every corner of existence, enveloping You with reverence. From the visible front to the unseen past and future behind, and from every direction that surrounds us, I offer my humble salutations. Your power knows no limits, Your might is beyond measure. Because You permeate every atom, every being, and every space, You truly embody the entirety of creation. This realization deepens my surrender, knowing You are the beginning, middle, and end of all.
translation.essence: I bow to You, O Lord, from all directions, for Your power and might are infinite. You fill everything, and therefore, You are everything. My heart finds peace in this all-encompassing presence.

11-41.sanskrit:
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं

हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति।

अजानता महिमानं तवेदं

मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि।।11.41।।
11-41.transliteration:
sakheti matvā prasabhaṁ yad uktaṁ
he kṛiṣhṇa he yādava he sakheti
ajānatā mahimānaṁ tavedaṁ
mayā pramādāt praṇayena vāpi

translation.simple: O Lord, I used to call You 'Krishna,' 'Yadava,' or 'friend,' speaking to You so casually. I did not truly understand Your immense greatness then. Please forgive this innocent familiarity, whether it was due to my simple mistakes or even out of my deep love for You.
translation.deep: My heart once saw You as a dear companion, Krishna, a friend from the Yadava lineage. Because of this bond, I spoke to You with ease and without much thought, not realizing the profound majesty You carried. I ask for Your forgiveness, O Lord, for treating You with such casualness. This was either from my innocent oversight or the overflowing affection I felt. Now, understanding Your true divine splendor, I realize the sacredness of Your presence, and I pray for Your compassionate understanding of my past ignorance.
translation.essence: Arjuna humbly apologizes to Krishna for treating Him as an ordinary friend and speaking to Him with familiarity, admitting he was unaware of Krishna's supreme divine glory, whether through oversight or pure affection.

11-42.sanskrit:
यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि

विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु।

एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं

तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम्।।11.42।।
11-42.transliteration:
yach chāvahāsārtham asat-kṛito ’si
vihāra-śhayyāsana-bhojaneṣhu
eko ’tha vāpy achyuta tat-samakṣhaṁ
tat kṣhāmaye tvām aham aprameyam

translation.simple: O Lord, I humbly seek Your forgiveness. In moments of shared laughter and ease – whether resting, sitting, or eating together, alone or with others – I may have, in my casualness, shown You disrespect. Please pardon my past actions, O Unfailing One, as I now perceive Your boundless greatness.
translation.deep: My heart feels deep remorse, O Krishna. In our carefree days, while enjoying games, resting, dining, or simply being together, I, in my human limited understanding, may have unintentionally slighted You, treating You merely as a companion. For all such instances, whether private or public, I now prostrate before You. I now understand Your true identity as the immeasurable Divine, the Unchanging Lord. Please, in Your boundless mercy, forgive all my unintentional offenses, born of familiarity rather than malice.
translation.essence: My heart, O Lord, now understands Your immeasurable nature. I humbly seek Your forgiveness for treating You casually during our moments of play, rest, or meals, whether alone or with others. Please forgive this servant's unintentional disrespect.

11-43.sanskrit:
पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य

त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान्।

न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो

लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव।।11.43।।
11-43.transliteration:
pitāsi lokasya charācharasya
tvam asya pūjyaśh cha gurur garīyān
na tvat-samo ’sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto ’nyo
loka-traye ’py apratima-prabhāva

translation.simple: O Lord, You are the loving Father of all creation, both living and non-living. You are the one we revere, our greatest teacher. There is no one like You, nor anyone superior, across all three worlds; Your glory is unmatched.
translation.deep: You, O Supreme Being, are the very source and sustainer, the compassionate Father of everything that moves and everything that rests in this vast universe. Our devotion flows naturally to You, for You are the most worthy of all worship and the ultimate Guru who guides us to truth. My heart knows there is no one who can stand beside You in power or wisdom, let alone transcend You, for Your magnificent presence permeates all three realms with an unparalleled splendor. My soul bows in humble adoration.
translation.essence: You are the benevolent Father of all, the supreme teacher, and the sole object of reverence. No one equals Your power or wisdom; Your glory is incomparable across all worlds.

11-44.sanskrit:
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं

प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम्।

पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः

प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम्।।11.44।।
11-44.transliteration:
tasmāt praṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṁ
prasādaye tvām aham īśham īḍyam
piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ
priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum

translation.simple: Therefore, I bow down, humbly offering my very self, and earnestly seek Your grace, O my adorable Lord. Please be patient with me, O Divine One, just as a loving father forgives his son, a true friend understands his friend, or a beloved one overlooks the faults of their dear one.
translation.deep: With utmost humility, I prostrate my entire being before You, O Supreme Lord, worthy of all praise. I seek Your divine forgiveness and mercy. In this act of complete surrender, I implore You, O Dearest Lord, to treat my imperfections with the boundless compassion of a father towards his child, the unwavering understanding of a loyal friend, and the patient acceptance of a loving beloved.
translation.essence: Humbly I bow, seeking Your divine grace and forgiveness, O Lord. Please treat me with the same tender patience a father shows his son, a friend his friend, or a beloved towards their dear one.

11-45.sanskrit:
अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा

भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे।

तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं

प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास।।11.45।।
11-45.transliteration:
adṛiṣhṭa-pūrvaṁ hṛiṣhito ’smi dṛiṣhṭvā
bhayena cha pravyathitaṁ mano me
tad eva me darśhaya deva rūpaṁ
prasīda deveśha jagan-nivāsa

translation.simple: I am filled with joy to behold Your form, a sight never witnessed before, yet my heart is also troubled by fear. Please, O Lord, show me Your gentle, familiar form again. Be gracious to me, O Master of all gods, O Dweller of the universe.
translation.deep: Witnessing Your magnificent, universal form, a vision unseen by anyone before, my soul rejoices in wonder, but my spirit is also deeply moved by reverence and fear. I humbly pray, O Divine One, to see Your gentle, beloved form once more. Grant me Your grace, O Supreme Lord, the very foundation and home of all existence.
translation.essence: My heart is thrilled by the unprecedented sight of Your cosmic form, yet fear also stirs within my mind. I pray, O Lord, to behold Your serene, original form again. Please bestow Your mercy upon me, O God of all gods, O Shelter of the entire creation.

11-46.sanskrit:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्त

मिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव।

तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन

सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते।।11.46।।
11-46.transliteration:
kirīṭinaṁ gadinaṁ chakra-hastam
ichchhāmi tvāṁ draṣhṭum ahaṁ tathaiva
tenaiva rūpeṇa chatur-bhujena
sahasra-bāho bhava viśhva-mūrte

translation.simple: My heart yearns to see You once more, O Lord, in Your beautiful form, adorned with a crown, holding Your mace and discus. Though You are the Universal Form with a thousand arms, please bless me by appearing as that gentle, four-armed Beloved.
translation.deep: After witnessing the awe-inspiring and overwhelming vastness of Your Universal Form, O Lord, Arjuna's heart gently yearns for the comfort and intimacy of Your familiar, beautiful manifestation. He humbly asks to behold You as the four-armed deity, adorned with divine symbols of sovereignty and protection—the crown, mace, and discus. This longing is a profound expression of a devotee's desire for a personal connection with the Divine, seeking solace and peace in the compassionate, accessible aspect of the Lord, that which inspires deep devotion and love.
translation.essence: A heartfelt plea from Arjuna, requesting the Lord to return to His serene, four-armed form, re-establishing a comforting and personal connection after the overwhelming vision of His cosmic manifestation.

11-47.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं

रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात्।

तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं

यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम्।।11.47।।
11-47.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṁ
rūpaṁ paraṁ darśhitam ātma-yogāt
tejo-mayaṁ viśhvam anantam ādyaṁ
yan me tvad anyena na dṛiṣhṭa-pūrvam

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord said, "Arjuna, out of My loving grace, I have revealed to you this supreme divine form, a vision brought forth by My own mystical power. It shines with immense light, encompasses the entire creation, is without beginning or end, and truly, no one before you has ever witnessed this form of Mine."
translation.deep: In these words, the Lord reveals the immense significance of the cosmic vision granted to Arjuna. He shares that it is by His own 'Atma-yoga,' His mystical and self-sufficient divine power, that this supreme form has been unveiled. This form is not merely grand; it is described as a boundless effulgence, encompassing all of creation, infinite, and the very origin of everything. The Lord's gentle emphasis that no one else has ever witnessed this form before underscores the profound and unique spiritual grace bestowed upon Arjuna, a testament to the Lord's spontaneous pleasure and deep affection for His devoted friend. It reminds us that the highest spiritual revelations are a gift of divine love, not merely a result of human endeavor.
translation.essence: The essence is the Lord's immense and unique grace towards Arjuna. Pleased with His devotee, He manifested His supreme, boundless, and effulgent cosmic form, a vision of His own divine power, previously unrevealed to any other, showcasing the extraordinary love and intimacy shared.

11-48.sanskrit:
न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानै

र्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः।

एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके

द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर।।11.48।।
11-48.transliteration:
na veda-yajñādhyayanair na dānair
na cha kriyābhir na tapobhir ugraiḥ
evaṁ-rūpaḥ śhakya ahaṁ nṛi-loke
draṣhṭuṁ tvad anyena kuru-pravīra

translation.simple: Lord Krishna tells Arjuna that His wondrous, divine form cannot be seen by mere study of scriptures, performing grand sacrifices, giving gifts, or even through strict penances. He reveals that in this human world, no one other than Arjuna could ever witness Him in such a spectacular way.
translation.deep: Here, the Lord reveals that His awe-inspiring universal form, which Arjuna is witnessing, is beyond the reach of conventional spiritual practices. He explains that neither deep study of the Vedas, nor performing great sacrifices, nor giving charity, nor even engaging in severe austerities can enable one to see Him in this glorious manifestation. This verse subtly underscores that such a direct vision is a unique blessing, a divine gift bestowed upon a special soul, like Arjuna, for a deeper purpose.
translation.essence: The core message is that the magnificent, universal form of the Lord cannot be attained by ordinary means, be it scripture study, rituals, charity, or penance. It highlights that such a profound vision is a unique divine bestowal, reserved for a special connection, suggesting that true spiritual revelation comes from grace, not just effort.

11-49.sanskrit:
मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो

दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम्।

व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वं

तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य।।11.49।।
11-49.transliteration:
mā te vyathā mā cha vimūḍha-bhāvo
dṛiṣhṭvā rūpaṁ ghoram īdṛiṅ mamedam
vyapeta-bhīḥ prīta-manāḥ punas tvaṁ
tad eva me rūpam idaṁ prapaśhya

translation.simple: Do not be afraid or bewildered by this awe-inspiring form you have seen. Let go of all fear, let your heart be filled with joy, and behold My gentle, familiar form once again.
translation.deep: My dear Arjuna, let not the sight of My vast and powerful universal manifestation disturb your inner peace or cause any bewilderment. Now, release your mind from all apprehension, let devotion sweeten your heart, and behold My beloved, gentle self once more, finding solace in My eternal and compassionate nature.
translation.essence: Fear not, nor be confused. With a heart full of joy, simply see Me in My gentle, loving form again.

11-50.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच

इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा

स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः।

आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं

भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा।।11.50।।
11-50.transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
ity arjunaṁ vāsudevas tathoktvā
svakaṁ rūpaṁ darśhayām āsa bhūyaḥ
āśhvāsayām āsa cha bhītam enaṁ
bhūtvā punaḥ saumya-vapur mahātmā

translation.simple: Sanjaya recounted: After revealing His magnificent universal form, Lord Krishna, the Great Soul, gently returned to His familiar, human-like appearance. He then tenderly comforted Arjuna, who had been filled with awe and fear.
translation.deep: Sanjaya narrated: Having revealed the overwhelming vastness of His cosmic manifestation, Lord Vasudeva, out of immense compassion for His devotee, lovingly reassumed His gentle, approachable human form. The Supreme Soul, the Mahātmā, then lovingly reassured and comforted Arjuna, who was overwhelmed with a mix of reverence and fear, thus demonstrating His profound care and accessibility to His beloved.
translation.essence: After the awe-inspiring vision, the Lord mercifully returned to His gentle form, offering comfort and peace to His devoted Arjuna. This illustrates the Supreme's tender care and reassurance for His devotees.

11-51.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तवसौम्यं जनार्दन।

इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः।।11.51।।
11-51.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
dṛiṣhṭvedaṁ mānuṣhaṁ rūpaṁ tava saumyaṁ janārdana
idānīm asmi saṁvṛittaḥ sa-chetāḥ prakṛitiṁ gataḥ

translation.simple: Arjuna said: O Janardana, now that I see Your gentle human form again, my mind is tranquil, and I have returned to my natural, peaceful state.
translation.deep: Here, Arjuna expresses a deep sense of relief and return to normalcy. After being overwhelmed by the awe-inspiring and sometimes terrifying Universal Form, his heart finds solace in Krishna's familiar and gentle human manifestation. This verse beautifully illustrates how the devotee's mind, when connected to the Lord's compassionate and approachable form, finds inner calm and restores its natural balance, moving from profound wonder and fear to serene devotion.
translation.essence: True peace for the searching soul is often found not in the awe of boundless power, but in the comforting, gentle presence of the Divine, which brings our consciousness back to its natural state of tranquility.

11-52.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम।

देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः।।11.52।।
11-52.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
su-durdarśham idaṁ rūpaṁ dṛiṣhṭavān asi yan mama
devā apy asya rūpasya nityaṁ darśhana-kāṅkṣhiṇaḥ

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord said: 'This wondrous form of Mine, which you have seen, is exceedingly rare. Even the radiant celestial beings forever yearn to behold this very sight.'
translation.deep: The Lord lovingly conveyed that the magnificent universal form Arjuna was blessed to see is truly beyond compare. It is a vision so profoundly sacred, so filled with divine glory, that even the gods themselves endlessly yearn for its sight. This speaks to the extraordinary grace poured upon Arjuna, granting him an experience of the highest spiritual longing.
translation.essence: This verse tenderly reveals the immense rarity and sacredness of the divine form, a vision so sought after that even the celestial beings long for it, underscoring the deep grace bestowed upon a devoted heart.

11-53.sanskrit:
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया।

शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा।।11.53।।
11-53.transliteration:
nāhaṁ vedair na tapasā na dānena na chejyayā
śhakya evaṁ-vidho draṣhṭuṁ dṛiṣhṭavān asi māṁ yathā

translation.simple: Lord Krishna lovingly explains that His most glorious form, which Arjuna was blessed to witness, isn't something one can achieve merely by studying scriptures, performing austerities, giving charity, or offering sacrifices. It's a special, divine gift to be granted such a vision.
translation.deep: This verse profoundly teaches that while religious studies, penance, charity, and rituals are virtuous spiritual endeavors, they alone do not guarantee the direct and magnificent vision of the Divine. The ability to perceive the Lord in such a transcendent form, as Arjuna experienced, points to a deeper spiritual connection, an inner readiness, and ultimately, a divine bestowal of grace, allowing for an intimate and awe-inspiring encounter.
translation.essence: To truly behold the Lord's sublime form is a profound blessing of divine grace, surpassing what can be earned through mere external practices or intellectual understanding.

11-54.sanskrit:
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन।

ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप।।11.54।।
11-54.transliteration:
bhaktyā tv ananyayā śhakya aham evaṁ-vidho ’rjuna
jñātuṁ draṣhṭuṁ cha tattvena praveṣhṭuṁ cha parantapa

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, only through loving devotion, unwavering and pure, can one truly know Me, see My divine form, and ultimately enter into My supreme being.
translation.deep: The Lord gently assures Arjuna that to truly comprehend His divine essence, to behold His form in its deepest truth, and to become one with Him, requires a very specific key: unwavering, single-minded devotion. This devotion is not just an act, but a state of heart, a profound love that opens the soul's eyes to His reality and guides it into His eternal embrace.
translation.essence: Unwavering, loving devotion is the sacred pathway to truly know the Divine, behold His truth, and find ultimate union with Him.

11-55.sanskrit:
मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः।

निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव।।11.55।।
11-55.transliteration:
mat-karma-kṛin mat-paramo mad-bhaktaḥ saṅga-varjitaḥ
nirvairaḥ sarva-bhūteṣhu yaḥ sa mām eti pāṇḍava

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, the one who performs all their duties for Me, who considers Me their supreme aim, who is lovingly devoted to Me, free from all worldly attachments, and holds no ill-will towards any living being — such a soul surely comes to Me.
translation.deep: This profound verse outlines the integral path of devotion. It's not just about outer actions, but the inner spirit of offering everything to the Divine. When the Lord is your ultimate goal, every endeavor becomes a sacred act. True devotion frees the heart from selfish cravings and attachments, fostering inner peace. And when you see all beings as expressions of the Divine, enmity dissolves into boundless compassion. This complete dedication of heart, mind, and action leads to an unbreakable union with the Supreme.
translation.essence: Dedicate your actions, your purpose, and your heart to the Divine. By letting go of attachments and cultivating kindness towards all, you will ultimately find your way back to the Supreme Self.

12-1.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचएवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते।येचाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः।।12.1।।
12-1.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
evaṁ satata-yuktā ye bhaktās tvāṁ paryupāsate
ye chāpy akṣharam avyaktaṁ teṣhāṁ ke yoga-vittamāḥ

translation.simple: Arjuna asked: Lord, some devotees always worship You with unwavering hearts. Others seek the unchanging, unmanifest Truth. Between these two, who are considered more established in spiritual practice?
translation.deep: Arjuna, with a heart seeking deeper understanding, humbly questioned: 'O Krishna, there are those devoted souls who are always connected to You, worshipping Your personal form with love. And then there are others who strive to realize the eternal, unmanifest reality, beyond all forms. Among these two distinct paths of spiritual endeavor, who do You consider to be more perfected in their yoga, more deeply immersed in true spiritual knowledge?' This question reflects a seeker's desire to know the superior path to ultimate truth.
translation.essence: Arjuna's earnest question is about discerning the path of loving devotion to the personal Divine from the path of meditating on the formless, ultimate reality. He seeks to know which approach leads to a more profound understanding of spiritual union.

12-2.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते।श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः।।12.2।।
12-2.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
mayy āveśhya mano ye māṁ nitya-yuktā upāsate
śhraddhayā parayopetās te me yuktatamā matāḥ

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord said: Those who lovingly fix their minds upon Me, always steadfast in their devotion, worshipping Me with supreme faith—them I consider to be the most perfectly united with Me.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly shares that those who set their hearts and minds firmly upon Him, who remain ever devoted and worship Him with an excellent, unshakeable faith, are held by Him to be the most perfectly connected. This highlights the importance of steady internal devotion and supreme trust in the Divine path, leading to the deepest spiritual union.
translation.essence: Fix your mind on the Divine, worship with steady, supreme faith, and the Lord declares you truly united with Him.

12-3.sanskrit: ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते।सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम्।।12.3।।
12-3.transliteration:
ye tv akṣharam anirdeśhyam avyaktaṁ paryupāsate
sarvatra-gam achintyañcha kūṭa-stham achalandhruvam
 sanniyamyendriya-grāmaṁ sarvatra sama-buddhayaḥ
te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ

translation.simple: Those who with love and dedication worship the Imperishable—that which cannot be described or seen, yet is present everywhere and beyond the grasp of our thoughts. It is the unmoving, ever-constant, and eternal truth.
translation.deep: This sacred path involves deep contemplation on the unmanifest Divine. It is the ultimate Reality, imperishable and beyond all descriptions, residing everywhere yet invisible to the eye. This truth is inconceivable by the mind, ever-stable, unmoving, and eternally firm. It is the steadfast essence that underpins all existence, unchanging through time.
translation.essence: The essence here is devotion to the formless, eternal truth—that which is everywhere, beyond all description and thought, yet is the most steady and unchanging reality. It is a path to connecting with the immutable, divine presence.

12-4.sanskrit: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः।ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः।।12.4।।
12-4.transliteration: sanniyamyendriya-grāmaṁ  sarvatra    sama-buddhayaḥ  te  prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite    ratāḥ

translation.simple: Those who gently guide their senses and see everyone with an equal mind, always dedicated to the well-being of all living beings – they truly come to Me.
translation.deep: When one calms the restless senses and learns to perceive the sacred presence equally in all, without distinction, and when the heart finds joy in tirelessly working for the good of every creature, such a devoted soul, through this path of selfless love and universal compassion, unfailingly reaches My divine abode, becoming one with My being.
translation.essence: Steadying the senses, seeing the Divine in all, and living for the welfare of every creature – this pure devotion leads straight to Me.

12-5.transliteration:
kleśho ’dhikataras teṣhām avyaktāsakta-chetasām
avyaktā hi gatir duḥkhaṁ dehavadbhir avāpyate

translation.simple: For those whose minds are set on the unmanifested, the formless Divine, the journey can be more challenging. It is indeed difficult for souls embodied in a physical form to grasp and attain that imperceptible reality.
translation.deep: When an embodied soul strives to connect with the utterly formless and imperceptible aspect of the Divine, the path often involves significant inner struggle. Our senses and intellect, accustomed to the world of forms and attributes, find it immensely difficult to focus purely on the unmanifest, making this spiritual endeavor profoundly demanding.
translation.essence: The verse gently reminds us that for those living in physical bodies, the direct pursuit of the formless, unmanifested Absolute requires greater spiritual effort. Our human experience, naturally drawn to forms and perceivable qualities, finds it challenging to directly apprehend that which is beyond all manifestation.

12-6.sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः।अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते।।12.6।।
12-6.transliteration:
ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat-paraḥ
ananyenaiva yogena māṁ dhyāyanta upāsate

translation.simple: For those who lovingly dedicate every action to Me, seeing Me as their ultimate shelter, and who worship Me with unwavering devotion, always meditating on My form.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully describes a path of profound surrender, where every action becomes an offering to the Divine. It speaks of those who see Me as their supreme haven and purpose, allowing no other thought to distract their unwavering devotion. Through such continuous meditation and worship, they cultivate an intimate and constant connection, finding deep peace and guidance in My presence.
translation.essence: The heart of this teaching is profound, unwavering devotion: offering every action to the Divine, embracing the Lord as one's ultimate shelter, and meditating with a single-pointed mind to experience continuous divine connection and inner peace.

12-7.transliteration:
teṣhām ahaṁ samuddhartā mṛityu-saṁsāra-sāgarāt
bhavāmi na chirāt pārtha mayy āveśhita-chetasām

translation.simple: O Partha, for those who truly anchor their hearts and minds in Me, I quickly become their rescuer. I lift them without delay from the swirling ocean of birth, death, and all worldly suffering.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse highlights the Lord's profound promise of salvation to His devoted ones. When a soul wholeheartedly dedicates its consciousness to the Divine, rising above fleeting worldly attachments, the Supreme Lord Himself vows to act as the ultimate deliverer. The 'ocean of death and samsara' symbolizes the endless cycle of material existence, often filled with impermanence and sorrow. Yet, for a sincere devotee whose mind is steadfastly absorbed in Him, this formidable ocean becomes a path to liberation, swiftly navigated by the Lord's own loving grace.
translation.essence: Simply fix your heart and mind upon Me, and I, the Lord, will swiftly become your rescuer, lifting you from the vast ocean of worldly cycles into eternal peace and freedom.

12-8.sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय।निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः।।12.8।।
12-8.transliteration:
mayy eva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṁ niveśhaya
nivasiṣhyasi mayy eva ata ūrdhvaṁ na sanśhayaḥ

translation.simple: Place your heart and mind completely in Me. Let your every thought be directed towards Me. When you do this, you will truly dwell in Me, and there's no doubt about it.
translation.deep: This verse offers a gentle yet profound path: by consciously dedicating both our mind, which holds our feelings and desires, and our intellect, which guides our understanding and choices, entirely to the Divine, we are promised an intimate spiritual union. 'Residing in Me' signifies a deep, unwavering connection where our true self finds its eternal home within the sacred essence of the Supreme, beyond all worldly doubts and fleeting experiences.
translation.essence: Offer your thoughts and understanding to Me, and without a doubt, you will find your eternal home, dwelling forever within My divine embrace.

12-9.sanskrit: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम्।अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय।।12.9।।
12-9.transliteration:
atha chittaṁ samādhātuṁ na śhaknoṣhi mayi sthiram
abhyāsa-yogena tato mām ichchhāptuṁ dhanañjaya

translation.simple: If you find it hard to keep your mind steadily fixed on Me, dear Arjuna, then gently try to reach Me through consistent spiritual practice.
translation.deep: Should your mind wander and struggle to rest firmly in My divine presence, do not despair. The Lord, in His boundless compassion, offers a loving alternative: the path of dedicated practice. Through repeated efforts in devotion, meditation, and righteous actions, even if imperfect, you will gradually draw closer to Me, O Arjuna, for every sincere step is acknowledged and cherished.
translation.essence: When fixing the mind directly on the Divine feels difficult, steady, loving practice becomes the gentle means to ultimately connect and attain Him.

12-10.sanskrit: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव।मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि।।12.10।।
12-10.transliteration:
abhyāse ’py asamartho ’si mat-karma-paramo bhava
mad-artham api karmāṇi kurvan siddhim avāpsyasi

translation.simple: If you find it challenging to sustain continuous spiritual practice, then make Me the purpose of all your actions. By simply performing your duties with Me in mind, you will surely achieve spiritual perfection.
translation.deep: Should you find the path of consistent meditative practice or deep spiritual discipline difficult to follow, remember that devotion in action is equally potent. Turn your daily duties and efforts into offerings, performing them all for My sake. This path of consecrated action purifies the heart and inevitably leads to the highest spiritual realization and inner peace.
translation.essence: When direct spiritual practice feels out of reach, offer all your actions to the Divine; through this dedicated service, you will find true perfection.

12-11.sanskrit: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः।सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान्।।12.11।।
12-11.transliteration:
athaitad apy aśhakto ’si kartuṁ mad-yogam āśhritaḥ
sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṁ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān

translation.simple: Should you find it challenging to constantly focus all your efforts upon Me, then with a peaceful and disciplined mind, simply release all attachment to the outcomes of your actions.
translation.deep: If the path of constant meditative absorption in My divine being feels arduous, a loving alternative is offered: cultivate inner discipline and perform all your duties without a personal desire for their results. This surrender of the fruits of action is a powerful step towards purification and inner peace, gradually leading you closer to the ultimate truth, even when direct, unwavering devotion seems a distant goal.
translation.essence: When constant devotion feels challenging, perform your actions with a calm, controlled mind, releasing all attachment to the results.

12-12.transliteration:
śhreyo hi jñānam abhyāsāj jñānād dhyānaṁ viśhiṣhyate
dhyānāt karma-phala-tyāgas tyāgāch chhāntir anantaram
