translation.simple: Indeed, gaining true understanding is more beneficial than mere spiritual practice. Meditation surpasses even this knowledge. But more significant than meditation is letting go of the fruits of your actions. From this act of surrender, a gentle peace immediately follows.
translation.deep: This verse reveals a profound spiritual journey. While consistent practice builds a foundation, deeper knowledge illuminates the path. Meditation then calms the mind, offering focus. Yet, the pinnacle before ultimate peace is the sacred detachment from the outcomes of our deeds. When we act with devotion but release attachment to results, a profound and lasting peace envelops us without delay.
translation.essence: Spiritual progress moves from practice to knowledge, and then to meditation. However, the most direct path to immediate and profound peace is the pure act of surrendering all desire for the fruits of our actions.

12-13.sanskrit: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च।निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी।।12.13।।
12-13.transliteration:
adveṣhṭā sarva-bhūtānāṁ maitraḥ karuṇa eva cha
nirmamo nirahankāraḥ sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ kṣhamī

translation.simple: The beloved devotee bears no ill-will toward any creature. They are a true friend to all, full of gentle compassion. They live free from a sense of 'mine' and 'I', accepting both joy and sorrow with peaceful calm, and are always forgiving.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully describes a soul truly surrendered to the Divine, seeing the same divine essence in every being. Their heart expands in universal friendship and pure compassion. Free from the burdens of 'mine' and 'I', they navigate life's highs and lows with an inner stillness, finding constant peace in the gentle practice of forgiveness.
translation.essence: Cultivate a heart free from enmity, full of friendship and compassion. Let go of 'mine' and 'I', accept life's changes with equanimity, and always be forgiving.

12-14.sanskrit: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः।मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः।।12.14।।
12-14.transliteration:
santuṣhṭaḥ satataṁ yogī yatātmā dṛiḍha-niśhchayaḥ
mayy arpita-mano-buddhir yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ

translation.simple: Always content, with a gentle and controlled heart, and firm in their faith, such a yogi dedicates their mind and wisdom fully to Me. That devoted soul is truly beloved by Me.
translation.deep: A spiritual seeker who finds deep, abiding contentment, whose inner self is perfectly poised, and whose resolve remains unshakable, truly embodies a profound devotion. When such a soul lovingly dedicates every thought and every faculty of their intellect to Me, they ascend to a most cherished place in My heart. This path of unwavering surrender, coupled with inner peace, reveals the deepest joy of divine connection.
translation.essence: The essence lies in cultivating constant inner contentment, maintaining a serene and disciplined self, and holding unshakeable faith. When a devotee offers their mind and intellect fully to the Divine, they become supremely dear to the Lord's heart.

12-15.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः।हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः।।12.15।।
12-15.transliteration:
yasmān nodvijate loko lokān nodvijate cha yaḥ
harṣhāmarṣha-bhayodvegair mukto yaḥ sa cha me priyaḥ

translation.simple: That devotee who causes no distress to others, and who remains undisturbed by the world, is truly dear to Me. Such a soul finds freedom from the fleeting feelings of elation, resentment, fear, and anxiety.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully describes a state of profound inner peace and harmony. A true devotee cultivates a mind so serene that their presence brings no disturbance to anyone, and in turn, the various trials and triumphs of the world do not shake their equipoise. It’s about transcending the dualities of life – not being swayed by extreme happiness or sorrow, anger or fear, but resting in a steady devotion that anchors the soul beyond worldly fluctuations. Such a balanced and compassionate being embodies divine qualities and is deeply loved by the Lord.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna holds dear those serene souls who neither disturb the world nor are disturbed by it, living free from the waves of transient joy, resentment, fear, and anxiety, dwelling in unwavering calm.

12-16.sanskrit: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः।।12.16।।
12-16.transliteration:
anapekṣhaḥ śhuchir dakṣha udāsīno gata-vyathaḥ
sarvārambha-parityāgī yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ

translation.simple: One who lives without personal desires, whose heart is pure, who is skillful in their actions, remains peaceful and untouched by worldly worries, and has given up initiating selfish endeavors—such a loving devotee is truly dear to Me.
translation.deep: This verse describes the profound qualities of a soul truly dedicated to the Divine. It speaks of a devotee who seeks nothing for themselves, having surrendered all personal expectations and finding contentment in Krishna's will. Their mind and heart are pure, unblemished by ego or base desires. They perform their duties with skill and dedication, yet remain detached from the outcomes, viewing all actions as an offering. Untouched by life's dualities, they maintain an inner tranquility, free from all anxiety and sorrow. Such a one has renounced the very impulse to begin actions for selfish ends, acting purely out of love and duty. This selfless, serene, and surrendered soul is profoundly beloved by Krishna.
translation.essence: A pure-hearted, detached, and skillful devotee, free from all worry and selfish ambitions, is truly beloved by the Lord.

12-17.sanskrit: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्ितमान्यः स मे प्रियः।।12.17।।
12-17.transliteration:
yo na hṛiṣhyati na dveṣhṭi na śhochati na kāṅkṣhati
śhubhāśhubha-parityāgī bhaktimān yaḥ sa me priyaḥ

translation.simple: The one who doesn't burst with joy, nor holds onto hatred, nor sinks into sorrow, nor longs for things – who has given up attachment to both pleasant and unpleasant outcomes – that devoted soul is truly dear to Me.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us towards a profound state of inner tranquility. It describes a heart so deeply connected to the Divine that it remains untouched by the fleeting waves of worldly joy and sorrow, attraction and aversion. Such a soul doesn't cling to good fortune nor lament adversity, seeing both as expressions of a divine plan. This beautiful surrender, free from the pull of dualities, reveals a pure and steadfast devotion that is profoundly cherished by the Lord.
translation.essence: Cultivate an even heart, untouched by fleeting joys or sorrows, and release attachment to all outcomes, whether good or bad. This steady devotion is what makes a soul truly beloved by the Divine.

12-18.sanskrit: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः।शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः।।12.18।।
12-18.transliteration:
samaḥ śhatrau cha mitre cha tathā mānāpamānayoḥ
śhītoṣhṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣhu samaḥ saṅga-vivarjitaḥ

translation.simple: A true devotee treats friends and foes with equal kindness. They remain untouched by praise or blame, and stand firm in both comfort and hardship, joy and sorrow. Such a one lives detached from worldly ties.
translation.deep: This verse speaks to a deep spiritual wisdom—the capacity to remain unwavering amidst life's shifting experiences. It describes a soul who perceives the divine essence equally in all, whether they appear as a friend or an adversary. Such a devotee finds inner steadiness, untouched by the fleeting currents of honor and dishonor, cold and heat, or the ups and downs of joy and sorrow. This equanimity springs from a heart detached from worldly expectations, rooted instead in unconditional love for the Divine, allowing for profound inner peace.
translation.essence: The essence of this verse is a heart that remains steady and compassionate through all of life's experiences—seeing everyone with equanimity, accepting both honor and dishonor, and finding peace in joy and sorrow. Such a soul, free from attachment, embodies a beautiful, unwavering devotion.

12-19.sanskrit: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित्।अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्ितमान्मे प्रियो नरः।।12.19।।
12-19.transliteration:
tulya-nindā-stutir maunī santuṣhṭo yena kenachit
aniketaḥ sthira-matir bhaktimān me priyo naraḥ

translation.simple: For Me, dear is the one who sees praise and criticism with an equal heart, whose spirit is quiet, who finds contentment in whatever comes, who feels no strong attachment to a home, and whose mind is steady, overflowing with devotion.
translation.deep: This verse describes a profound state of inner freedom. It speaks of a soul unswayed by the world's fleeting opinions, where external praise or blame cannot disturb the inner peace. Such a devotee finds true joy not in circumstances, but in an unwavering connection to the Divine, accepting life's flow with grace. Their 'home' is not a physical place, but the Lord's presence within, leading to a mind always focused and stable, anchored in loving devotion.
translation.essence: The beloved devotee possesses a serene heart, untouched by external judgments, content with life's offerings, free from worldly attachments, and firmly rooted in unwavering devotion to the Divine.

12-20.sanskrit: ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते।श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः।।12.20।।
12-20.transliteration:
ye tu dharmyāmṛitam idaṁ yathoktaṁ paryupāsate
śhraddadhānā mat-paramā bhaktās te ’tīva me priyāḥ

translation.simple: Those who sincerely follow this sacred nectar of dharma, as I've taught, with deep faith and making Me their highest aspiration, such devotees are immensely precious to Me.
translation.deep: This profound verse whispers a beautiful assurance: those who lovingly embrace this divine wisdom, this 'nectar of righteousness' I have revealed, and follow it with an abiding faith, holding Me as their supreme haven and ultimate purpose – they are cherished beyond measure by Me. It speaks to the deep connection forged when a soul pours its entire being into the path of dharma, trusting fully in the Divine. Such unwavering devotion, rooted in faith and dedicated to the highest truth, establishes an exceptionally sweet bond with the Lord, making that devotee supremely dear to His heart.
translation.essence: Follow the sacred path with faith, hold Me as your highest goal, and know you are supremely beloved by Me.

13-1.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च।

एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव।।13.1।।
13-1.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
prakṛitiṁ puruṣhaṁ chaiva kṣhetraṁ kṣhetra-jñam eva cha
etad veditum ichchhāmi jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ cha keśhava

translation.simple: Arjuna said: O Krishna, I wish to understand what material nature is, and what the individual spirit is. I also long to know about this body, and who it is that truly knows this body. Please enlighten me on what true knowledge is, and what is truly the object of that knowledge.
translation.deep: Arjuna, with a heart open to profound truths, humbly asks Lord Krishna to explain the fundamental elements of existence. He seeks to understand the very fabric of nature (prakriti) and the essence of the individual soul (purusha). His inquiry delves into the body as a 'field' and the conscious entity that perceives it as the 'knower of the field'. This earnest question paves the way for understanding what constitutes true spiritual wisdom (jnana) and the ultimate reality that is worthy of all knowledge (jneya).
translation.essence: Arjuna, with a sincere heart, asks Lord Krishna to reveal the deepest spiritual insights. He yearns to understand the distinction between matter and spirit, the body and the soul residing within it, and what true knowledge means, along with the supreme object of that wisdom. This inquiry marks the beginning of a profound journey towards self-realization.

13-2.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचइदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते।एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः।।13.2।।
13-2.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
idaṁ śharīraṁ kaunteya kṣhetram ity abhidhīyate
etad yo vetti taṁ prāhuḥ kṣhetra-jña iti tad-vidaḥ

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord explains that our body is like a field. And the one who truly knows and understands this field, those with spiritual insight call that one the 'Knower of the Field'.
translation.deep: Here, Lord Krishna beautifully unveils a profound truth. Our physical body, with all its sensations, thoughts, and actions, is likened to a field (Kshetra). It's where life's experiences are sown and harvested. But deeper still, there is a distinct consciousness, a pure awareness, that observes and knows this field. This observer, which is our true self, is not the field itself, but the 'Knower of the Field' (Kshetrajna). Understanding this distinction—that you are not merely your body but the eternal consciousness witnessing it—is the dawn of true wisdom and liberation.
translation.essence: The body is a field of experience; your true self is the divine witness, the knowing consciousness within.

13-3.sanskrit:
क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत।

क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम।।13.3।।
13-3.transliteration:
kṣhetra-jñaṁ chāpi māṁ viddhi sarva-kṣhetreṣhu bhārata
kṣhetra-kṣhetrajñayor jñānaṁ yat taj jñānaṁ mataṁ mama

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, know with certainty that I am the consciousness that resides within every single body, in all beings. Truly understanding the difference between the body and this indwelling spirit is, in My view, the highest wisdom.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna gently guides us to recognize His presence as the very awareness that illuminates every 'field' of existence. He is the conscious spirit within all bodies, O Arjuna. To truly know Him means to understand this distinction: to see the temporary nature of the body and the eternal, conscious Self within. This profound discernment, separating the field from its knower, is what He declares as genuine spiritual insight.
translation.essence: I am the conscious 'Knower' in every being. True wisdom lies in understanding the body from the eternal spirit.

13-4.sanskrit: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत्।स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे श्रृणु।।13.4।।
13-4.transliteration:
tat kṣhetraṁ yach cha yādṛik cha yad-vikāri yataśh cha yat
sa cha yo yat-prabhāvaśh cha tat samāsena me śhṛiṇu

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, listen now as I briefly reveal to you what this field of existence (your body and the material world) truly is, its nature, its transformations, and its origin. I will also speak of the Knower of this field, the divine Self, and His wonderful powers. Hear this from Me in a concise way.
translation.deep: In this sacred verse, Lord Krishna gently invites us to understand the profound architecture of our material existence – the body, its characteristics, its many transformations, and its ultimate origin. More significantly, He promises to illuminate the nature of the true Seer, the divine consciousness (Purusha) who resides within this field. We are urged to hear about the deep impact and glorious power of this Knower, moving us towards a tranquil understanding of our true spiritual identity and its divine connection.
translation.essence: The Lord lovingly promises to reveal the brief yet profound truth of both the material body (the field) and the divine Self (the Knower) residing within it, along with their intricate relationship and divine influence.

13-5.transliteration:
ṛiṣhibhir bahudhā gītaṁ chhandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛithak
brahma-sūtra-padaiśh chaiva hetumadbhir viniśhchitaiḥ

translation.simple: This sacred wisdom, dear to the heart, has been lovingly spoken of by ancient sages. It resonates through various holy chants and is clearly established by the thoughtful words of the Brahma Sutras.
translation.deep: The sacred truth of creation and consciousness has been revealed through many ages. Wise sages, with their profound insights, have sung its praises in various ways. It is beautifully woven into the diverse hymns of the ancient Vedas. Moreover, the deep, reasoned statements of the Brahma Sutras decisively confirm this understanding, guiding us to a clear and certain spiritual path.
translation.essence: The path to understanding the Divine is deeply rooted and universally affirmed, spoken of by sages, sung in sacred verses, and logically established in scriptures, assuring us of its timeless truth.

13-6.sanskrit: महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च।इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः।।13.6।।
13-6.transliteration:
mahā-bhūtāny ahankāro buddhir avyaktam eva cha
indriyāṇi daśhaikaṁ cha pañcha chendriya-gocharāḥ

translation.simple: The Lord explains the fundamental building blocks of our material existence: the vast elements of nature, our sense of 'I' (ego), our discerning intellect, the unmanifest primal nature, the ten gateways of our senses, the mind that coordinates them, and the five kinds of objects our senses encounter. These are the components of the 'field' that He oversees.
translation.deep: This divine wisdom here reveals the intricate fabric of our worldly experience. These elements, from the grossest to the subtle, including our very sense of self and our capacity to think and perceive, are all part of the temporary material creation. They are the 'field' where the soul interacts with the world, a stage set by the Lord for our journey of discovery. Understanding these components helps us discern what is transient and what is eternal, gently guiding us to look beyond them towards the true Knower within, who is untouched by their changes.
translation.essence: This verse gently points out the constituents of our material existence and perception. By understanding these components as the 'field' or the stage of our experience, we are encouraged to look beyond them to the divine, unchanging Self within, the true Knower of this field, always present and always peaceful.

13-7.sanskrit: इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतनाधृतिः।एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम्।।13.7।।
13-7.transliteration:
ichchhā dveṣhaḥ sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ saṅghātaśh chetanā dhṛitiḥ
etat kṣhetraṁ samāsena sa-vikāram udāhṛitam

translation.simple: Our desires and dislikes, our moments of joy and sorrow, the very structure of our body, our awareness, and even our resolve – all these are simply aspects of this 'field' of experience, constantly changing.
translation.deep: Contemplating this verse, we understand that all our feelings – our yearnings, our dislikes, the fleeting joys and sorrows, even the form of our physical body and the consciousness that lights it, and our inner strength – are all facets of this temporary 'field' of existence. They are the constant dance of material nature, distinct from the unchanging Spirit within us.
translation.essence: The heart of this teaching is to gently recognize that all our inner and outer experiences – our longings, our dislikes, our happiness, our sadness, and even our very physical form – are simply the ever-changing 'field.' This understanding invites us to seek the steady, true Self, which remains untouched by these passing states.

13-8.transliteration:
amānitvam adambhitvam ahinsā kṣhāntir ārjavam
āchāryopāsanaṁ śhauchaṁ sthairyam ātma-vinigrahaḥ

translation.simple: To truly understand the self, one cultivates qualities like humility and sincerity. It means living without causing harm to anyone, practicing patience, and being straightforward in thought and deed. Serving a wise spiritual teacher with reverence is important, alongside maintaining inner and outer purity. We strive for steadfastness in our spiritual path and gentle control over our senses and mind.
translation.deep: Delving deeper, these virtues are not mere rules but pathways to the Divine. Humility helps us shed the ego that separates us from the Lord, while sincerity ensures our devotion is true and pure. Non-violence stems from seeing the Divine spark in every being. Patience allows us to gracefully accept life's ebb and flow, knowing all is part of a larger plan. Straightforwardness brings honesty to our spiritual journey. Serving a spiritual teacher is an act of surrendering to wisdom, and purity prepares our inner vessel to receive divine grace. Steadfastness keeps us anchored in our devotion, and self-control helps us direct our vital energy towards higher spiritual goals, fostering a deep inner stillness.
translation.essence: The essence of this verse reveals that true spiritual knowledge is not just intellectual understanding, but a profound transformation of character. Cultivating these divine qualities within our heart and mind is the actual journey towards self-realization and experiencing the serene presence of the Divine.

translation.simple: Gently withdraw your mind from the allure of sense pleasures. Let go of any trace of ego or pride. Reflect calmly upon the realities of birth, old age, sickness, and death, recognizing the inherent sorrow in these stages of life.
translation.deep: This verse encourages a path of gentle wisdom. It invites us to cultivate a loving detachment from the fleeting attractions of the senses, allowing our hearts to turn inward. It calls for the quiet surrender of ego, fostering a spirit of humility and openness. By calmly observing the inherent challenges of birth, old age, illness, and the eventual passing, we gain a deeper understanding of life's impermanence, which inspires us to seek lasting truth and peace within.
translation.essence: Seek inner peace by gently detaching from fleeting desires, embracing humility, and calmly reflecting on life's impermanence, which guides us to everlasting truth.

13-10.transliteration:
asaktir anabhiṣhvaṅgaḥ putra-dāra-gṛihādiṣhu
nityaṁ cha sama-chittatvam iṣhṭāniṣhṭopapattiṣhu

translation.simple: A peaceful heart isn't too attached to family or home. It remains calm and steady, whether life brings joy or sorrow.
translation.deep: This verse guides us to an inner freedom. It's about loving our family and caring for our home without our happiness being fully dependent on them. It teaches us to maintain a balanced mind, accepting both favorable and unfavorable events with a tranquil spirit, knowing that all experiences serve a higher purpose.
translation.essence: Cultivate inner freedom by not clinging to worldly relationships or possessions, and sustain an even-tempered heart through life's varying experiences, good or bad.

13-11.transliteration:
mayi chānanya-yogena bhaktir avyabhichāriṇī
vivikta-deśha-sevitvam aratir jana-sansadi

translation.simple: An unwavering devotion that rests solely on Me, a love that never falters. A preference for peaceful, secluded spots, and a gentle disinterest in the clamor of worldly gatherings.
translation.deep: Here, the path unfolds through an unyielding and singular devotion to the Divine within Me. It speaks of a love that is steadfast, never veering from its sacred focus. It encourages a natural inclination towards quiet, sacred spaces where the soul can truly connect, and a quiet discernment, finding less appeal in the constant chatter and demands of large worldly gatherings, thus preserving inner peace.
translation.essence: The essence lies in cultivating a singular, unwavering devotion to the Divine, cherishing quiet moments for introspection, and gently detaching from the distractions of bustling worldly crowds to nurture inner peace.

13-12.transliteration:
adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvaṁ tattva-jñānārtha-darśhanam
etaj jñānam iti proktam ajñānaṁ yad ato ’nyathā

translation.simple: To always dwell in the wisdom of the Self and to clearly see the true aim of spiritual understanding – this is truly knowledge. Whatever is different from this is deemed ignorance.
translation.deep: True wisdom blossoms not from sporadic inquiry but from a perpetual dedication to the wisdom of the Self (adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvam). It's a journey of continuously delving into the spiritual essence within and around us. Simultaneously, it involves a clear perception of the ultimate purpose and meaning of this profound truth (tattva-jñāna-artha-darśanam) – understanding that it guides us towards divine realization. This unwavering focus on inner spiritual light and its ultimate goal is indeed knowledge; anything that distracts or deviates from this path is considered a veil of ignorance.
translation.essence: Steadfast devotion to inner spiritual knowledge and a clear perception of ultimate truth's purpose is what constitutes true knowledge; all else is simply not knowing.

13-13.sanskrit: ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते।अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते।।13.13।।
13-13.transliteration:
jñeyaṁ yat tat pravakṣhyāmi yaj jñātvāmṛitam aśhnute
anādi mat-paraṁ brahma na sat tan nāsad uchyate

translation.simple: Lord Krishna shares, 'I will tell you of the ultimate truth, knowing which brings eternal peace.' He describes it as the Supreme, beginningless Spirit, which is beyond being called 'existent' or 'non-existent' in our worldly terms.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly promises to reveal the ultimate knowledge, understanding which bestows immortality and freedom from all suffering. This truth is the Supreme Brahman, the timeless, beginningless source of all. Its nature is so transcendental that it cannot be confined by our dualistic ideas of 'existence' or 'non-existence'; it is a reality that transcends all finite description and human comprehension.
translation.essence: The Lord reveals the profound truth of the Supreme Spirit, which is eternal and beyond all worldly classifications of existence or non-existence, bestowing everlasting peace upon those who know it.

13-14.sanskrit: सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्।सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति।।13.14।।
13-14.transliteration:
sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādaṁ tat sarvato ’kṣhi-śhiro-mukham
sarvataḥ śhrutimal loke sarvam āvṛitya tiṣhṭhati

translation.simple: Imagine a loving presence that sees all, hears all, and touches all. That divine power is everywhere, with countless hands to help, countless eyes to witness, and countless ears to listen. It encompasses the entire world, ever-present in every direction.
translation.deep: This sacred verse beautifully portrays the Supreme Being not as a limited form, but as an omnipresent consciousness. It speaks of the Divine having 'hands and feet everywhere,' 'eyes, heads, and faces everywhere,' and 'ears everywhere in the world.' This symbolizes the infinite reach and unlimited capacity of the Divine, acting through all, observing through all, and hearing through all. The Supreme permeates every atom of existence, not confined to one place, but embracing the entirety of creation within its boundless being.
translation.essence: The Divine is universally present, manifesting its power and presence through all beings and all aspects of creation, watching over and pervading everything.

13-15.sanskrit: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम्।असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च।।13.15।।
13-15.transliteration:
sarvendriya-guṇābhāsaṁ sarvendriya-vivarjitam
asaktaṁ sarva-bhṛich chaiva nirguṇaṁ guṇa-bhoktṛi cha

translation.simple: It seems to reflect the light of all our senses, yet it is truly beyond them. It remains unattached to everything, even as it lovingly sustains all that exists. Though untouched by material qualities, it is the ultimate experiencer and master of them all.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully articulates the profound nature of the Divine. It is the very essence that illuminates the functions of all our senses, making all experience possible, yet it remains free from material sense-organs. Eternally unattached to creation, it is simultaneously the loving sustainer of all existence. Beyond the binding influence of the material qualities (gunas), it is nevertheless the ultimate enjoyer and master of all manifestations, ever transcendent yet immanent.
translation.essence: The Supreme Lord is both within and beyond, shining through our senses while having none, sustaining all creation yet remaining unattached, and, though transcending all qualities, is their true master and enjoyer.

13-16.sanskrit: बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च।सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत्।।13.16।।
13-16.transliteration:
bahir antaśh cha bhūtānām acharaṁ charam eva cha
sūkṣhmatvāt tad avijñeyaṁ dūra-sthaṁ chāntike cha tat

translation.simple: The Divine is found both within and outside all beings, in everything that moves and everything that is still. Because of its subtle nature, it can seem hard to grasp, yet it is simultaneously far away and incredibly near to us.
translation.deep: This Supreme Truth pervades all existence, dwelling within the very core of every creature and extending boundlessly beyond. It is the fundamental essence of all that is dynamic and all that is static. Due to its exquisitely subtle nature, it is not readily perceived by our ordinary senses. Yet, in a profound paradox, it appears distant to those who seek it superficially, while being intimately present to those who open their hearts.
translation.essence: The Divine is omnipresent, the life force within and without all creation, present in both motion and stillness. Though its subtle nature makes it elusive to ordinary perception, it is paradoxically both infinitely vast and intimately near.

13-17.sanskrit: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम्।भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च।।13.17।।
13-17.transliteration:
avibhaktaṁ cha bhūteṣhu vibhaktam iva cha sthitam
bhūta-bhartṛi cha taj jñeyaṁ grasiṣhṇu prabhaviṣhṇu cha

translation.simple: The Divine is one, present within all beings, yet it appears in countless forms. It is the loving sustainer of all life, the one who brings everything into existence, and the one who gently draws it all back.
translation.deep: Though the Divine appears distinct in each creature and form, it remains eternally undivided, an omnipresent reality pervading everything. This same supreme truth is known as the loving support and foundation of existence for all beings. It is the source from which all creation emerges, and the gentle force that eventually draws everything back into itself, in a sacred cycle of existence.
translation.essence: The one unified Divine essence, though seen as many, is the creator, sustainer, and ultimate end of all existence.

13-18.sanskrit: ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते।ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम्।।13.18।।
13-18.transliteration:
jyotiṣhām api taj jyotis tamasaḥ param uchyate
jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ jñāna-gamyaṁ hṛidi sarvasya viṣhṭhitam

translation.simple: This divine Reality is the light of all lights, shining beyond any darkness. It is knowledge itself, what is to be known, and the path to knowing. And gently, it resides within the heart of every single being.
translation.deep: Consider this ultimate Truth: it is the effulgence that illumines all other lights, transcending every veil of darkness and ignorance. It embodies pure knowledge, the sacred object of all spiritual pursuit, and the very means by which that understanding is attained. Most wonderfully, this profound essence of the Divine rests within the sanctuary of every heart, awaiting realization.
translation.essence: The supreme Light, beyond all shadows, is the very core of knowledge and its goal. This divine presence lovingly dwells within your own heart.

13-19.sanskrit: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः।मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते।।13.19।।
13-19.transliteration:
iti kṣhetraṁ tathā jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ choktaṁ samāsataḥ
mad-bhakta etad vijñāya mad-bhāvāyopapadyate

translation.simple: Here, the nature of the body, true wisdom, and the ultimate truth to be known have been simply explained. My devotee, understanding all this, comes to truly know Me and attains My divine state.
translation.deep: These verses have concisely unveiled the mystery of the physical realm (the field), the light of spiritual understanding (knowledge), and the Supreme Reality that is to be realized (the knowable). A sincere devotee, who grasps these profound teachings, is uplifted to experience My divine presence and to become one with My sacred nature, finding everlasting peace.
translation.essence: Understanding the body, wisdom, and the Ultimate Truth leads My loving devotee to share in My divine essence and find profound tranquility.

13-20.sanskrit: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि।विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान्।।13.20।।
13-20.transliteration:
prakṛitiṁ puruṣhaṁ chaiva viddhy anādī ubhāv api
vikārānśh cha guṇānśh chaiva viddhi prakṛiti-sambhavān

translation.simple: Understand that both material nature and the spirit within are eternal, without beginning. And all the changes we see, all the qualities we experience, truly come forth from this very nature.
translation.deep: The Divine wisdom teaches us that both the soul, which is our true self, and the material energy, which forms the world around us, are without beginning – they are eternal. All the different forms we perceive, all the feelings and qualities we encounter (like peace, activity, or inertia), are born from this material energy. This helps us lovingly discern our unchanging spiritual core from the temporary dance of matter.
translation.essence: Your eternal spirit and the surrounding nature are both beginningless. All changes and qualities you perceive arise from this material nature.

13-21.sanskrit: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते।पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते।।13.21।।
13-21.transliteration:
kārya-kāraṇa-kartṛitve hetuḥ prakṛitir uchyate
puruṣhaḥ sukha-duḥkhānāṁ bhoktṛitve hetur uchyate

translation.simple: Our material nature, Prakriti, is responsible for all actions, effects, and the feeling of being the doer. But it is the soul, the divine spark within us, that experiences the happiness and sorrow that come from these actions.
translation.deep: The dynamic force of material nature, Prakriti, is the very origin of all action, its causes, and its results. But it is the pure consciousness, Purusha, residing within, that becomes the experiencer of all joys and sorrows that unfold from this interaction.
translation.essence: Nature creates and acts; the divine self within us is the one who feels both happiness and sorrow.

13-22.sanskrit: पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान्।कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु।।13.22।।
13-22.transliteration:
puruṣhaḥ prakṛiti-stho hi bhuṅkte prakṛiti-jān guṇān
kāraṇaṁ guṇa-saṅgo ’sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu

translation.simple: When the soul resides within material nature, it experiences the various qualities of life. It is our attachment to these qualities that leads us to take birth in different conditions, some pleasant and some difficult.
translation.deep: The eternal soul, while dwelling in the lap of nature, experiences the play of the three worldly modes. This deep identification with the shifts of material energy is what binds the self, acting as the cause for its journey through various forms of existence. By tasting the fruits of nature, the soul remains tied to the cycle of birth and death.
translation.essence: Our attachment to the temporary qualities of the world is the bridge that keeps us tethered to the cycle of rebirth; peace is found when we realize we are the observer, not the qualities themselves.

13-23.sanskrit: उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः।परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः।।13.23।।
13-23.transliteration:
upadraṣhṭānumantā cha bhartā bhoktā maheśhvaraḥ
paramātmeti chāpy ukto dehe ’smin puruṣhaḥ paraḥ

translation.simple: Within this very body, a Supreme Spirit resides. This divine presence quietly watches over us, gently approves our path, sustains our being, and experiences life with us. It is truly the Great Lord, our innermost Soul, dwelling here.
translation.deep: Even though dwelling within this physical form, there is a Supreme Being who is entirely transcendent. This sacred presence is the unattached observer of all our thoughts and actions, the one who silently permits the unfolding of our journey, the ultimate sustainer of our very life, and the experiencer of all joys and sorrows. It is revered as the Great Lord and the Supreme Self, immanent yet ever beyond.
translation.essence: The Supreme Spirit within us is the Great Lord Himself – our silent witness, our gentle approver, our loving sustainer, and the ultimate Self, present in this body, yet transcendent.

13-24.sanskrit: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह।सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते।।13.24।।
13-24.transliteration:
ya evaṁ vetti puruṣhaṁ prakṛitiṁ cha guṇaiḥ saha
sarvathā vartamāno ’pi na sa bhūyo ’bhijāyate

translation.simple: When we truly understand the divine Self within us, distinct from material nature and its changing qualities, we find lasting freedom. Even as we live our daily lives, this understanding liberates us from the cycle of birth.
translation.deep: One who deeply understands the eternal Spirit (Purusha) and its distinction from the ever-changing material nature (Prakriti), along with her three qualities (gunas), finds the path to liberation. This profound wisdom, once grasped, frees the soul from rebirth, regardless of their present actions, for their inner vision transcends the world's illusions.
translation.essence: Knowing the true Self as separate from nature's play, one attains eternal peace and breaks free from the cycle of rebirth.

13-25.sanskrit: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना।अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे।।13.25।।
13-25.transliteration:
dhyānenātmani paśhyanti kechid ātmānam ātmanā
anye sānkhyena yogena karma-yogena chāpare

translation.simple: With gentle focus, some seekers behold the Self within their own being through silent meditation. Others discover this sacred truth through the wisdom of understanding, while many more walk the path of selfless service, offering every action to the Divine.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully reminds us that the journey to inner realization is personal and diverse. While some ascend through the profound stillness of meditative absorption, directly experiencing the Atman, others approach this supreme truth through intellectual discernment, seeking to understand the nature of reality. Then there are those who purify their hearts and minds by dedicating all their efforts and outcomes to the Divine, transforming their very actions into a spiritual offering. All these paths, though outwardly different, lead to the same sacred destination: the recognition of the eternal Self.
translation.essence: The Divine Self can be realized in many ways. Some find this sacred truth through the quiet path of meditation within, others through thoughtful understanding, and many more by offering their actions with pure devotion. Each path, sincerely walked, leads to the same divine embrace.

13-26.sanskrit: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते।तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः।।13.26।।
13-26.transliteration:
anye tv evam ajānantaḥ śhrutvānyebhya upāsate
te ’pi chātitaranty eva mṛityuṁ śhruti-parāyaṇāḥ

translation.simple: Even if we don't understand everything ourselves, when we humbly listen to the wise and worship with devotion, we too can surely cross over the cycle of birth and death, just by holding onto those sacred words.
translation.deep: This verse offers profound solace, assuring us that not all spiritual journeys begin with complete personal enlightenment. It highlights the immense value of humble listening and devotional practice, guided by trusted teachers. Even if one's direct understanding is still developing, the sincere act of hearing sacred truths and then offering devotion based on that hearing, coupled with dedication to those teachings, is powerful enough. Such sincere listeners, through divine grace, are certainly uplifted beyond the constraints of mortality and rebirth.
translation.essence: Faithful listening to spiritual wisdom from others, and devoted worship based on it, leads one across the ocean of birth and death.

13-27.transliteration:
yāvat sañjāyate kiñchit sattvaṁ sthāvara-jaṅgamam
kṣhetra-kṣhetrajña-sanyogāt tad viddhi bharatarṣhabha

translation.simple: Oh Arjuna, understand this truth: every single living being, whether it moves or is still, comes into existence from the gentle meeting of the body (the field) and the soul (the knower of that field).
translation.deep: Ponder this deeper, dear one. All forms of life we perceive, from the smallest plant to the grandest creature, are born from a divine interplay. The temporary material form (Kṣetra) unites with the eternal spiritual consciousness (Kṣetrajña). This sacred conjunction is the very source of all manifest existence, beautifully revealing how the spirit animates and breathes life into everything.
translation.essence: The core truth is that all life, in its countless forms, arises from the beautiful union of matter and the eternal spirit.

13-28.sanskrit: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम्।विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति।।13.28।।
13-28.transliteration:
samaṁ sarveṣhu bhūteṣhu tiṣhṭhantaṁ parameśhvaram
vinaśhyatsv avinaśhyantaṁ yaḥ paśhyati sa paśhyati

translation.simple: See the Divine Presence dwelling equally within every living thing, from the smallest ant to the largest tree. Recognize that while all things around us may fade and change, the Supreme Spirit within them remains eternally unchanging. One who truly sees this, truly understands life's deepest truth.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to a profound insight: the Supreme Lord, the very essence of existence, resides impartially within the hearts of all beings. To perceive Him as the unwavering, eternal truth amidst the constant flux of the material world – where bodies are born and perish – is to glimpse reality beyond illusion. This vision liberates one from the attachments to the fleeting, revealing the unshakeable foundation of all life.
translation.essence: To truly see is to perceive the Supreme Lord, constant and eternal, residing equally within all beings, even as their forms pass away.

13-29.sanskrit: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम्।न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम्।।13.29।।
13-29.transliteration:
samaṁ paśhyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśhvaram
na hinasty ātmanātmānaṁ tato yāti parāṁ gatim

translation.simple: When one sees the Divine Spirit, the Lord, dwelling equally in all places and beings, they never harm their true Self through their actions. Such a gentle understanding guides them to the supreme, eternal goal.
translation.deep: To perceive the Lord abiding equally in all beings, in every facet of existence, is to embrace a vision of profound oneness. With this wisdom, one instinctively refrains from any action that might cloud or diminish their own sacred inner spirit. This understanding prevents the self from becoming an obstacle to its own purity, gently leading towards the supreme spiritual state, a journey of everlasting peace and devotion.
translation.essence: Perceiving the Lord's equal presence everywhere cultivates inner harmony, protecting the true Self from harm and gently leading one to the ultimate spiritual destination.

13-30.sanskrit: प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः।यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति।।13.30।।
13-30.transliteration:
prakṛityaiva cha karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśhaḥ
yaḥ paśhyati tathātmānam akartāraṁ sa paśhyati

translation.simple: When we gently observe that all deeds are performed by the workings of material nature, and truly understand that our inner self, the soul, is simply a witness, not the doer, then our vision becomes clear.
translation.deep: This sacred verse invites us to a profound realization: all actions, in every possible way, are truly carried out by the energies of material nature (Prakriti). The eternal Self within us, the pure soul, is ever pristine, untouched by these deeds, acting as a gentle witness. When we truly perceive the soul as the non-doer, distinct from the body and mind, we gain genuine spiritual insight, freeing ourselves from the burden of attachment to results and resting in our peaceful essence.
translation.essence: True wisdom dawns when we understand that all deeds unfold through nature's play, while our soul remains the serene, untouched observer.

13-31.sanskrit: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा।।13.31।।
13-31.transliteration:
yadā bhūta-pṛithag-bhāvam eka-stham anupaśhyati
tata eva cha vistāraṁ brahma sampadyate tadā

translation.simple: When we begin to see all distinct beings as resting within one divine source, and understand that all creation expands from this very same essence, our hearts become united with the Supreme Truth.
translation.deep: When a spiritual seeker profoundly realizes that the myriad distinct forms of all living beings are ultimately held within and emerge from a singular, all-pervading Reality, then their consciousness transcends limitations and merges with the boundless Brahman, experiencing true spiritual liberation.
translation.essence: To perceive the unity in all diversity, and to know that all existence flows from the One Divine, is to truly connect with the Absolute and find ultimate peace.

13-32.transliteration:
anāditvān nirguṇatvāt paramātmāyam avyayaḥ
śharīra-stho ’pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate

translation.simple: O Arjuna, the Supreme Self has no beginning and is free from all material qualities. It is eternal and never diminishes. Even though this Divine Self resides within the body, it does not truly act, nor is it ever tainted by anything. It remains ever pure.
translation.deep: This profound verse reveals the transcendental nature of the Supreme Self, Paramatma. Because it exists beyond time and the influence of material qualities, it is unchangeable and everlasting. Though it appears to reside within every changing body, it remains a silent, pure witness, untouched by the joys, sorrows, actions, or reactions of the physical realm. Just as the vast sky remains untainted by clouds, the Self remains inherently pure and unblemished, reminding us of our own untouched spiritual core and guiding us towards inner peace.
translation.essence: The Supreme Self is eternally pure, without beginning or end, residing within yet utterly untouched by any action or worldly quality. It remains ever peaceful and free.

13-33.sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते।सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते।।13.33।।
13-33.transliteration:
yathā sarva-gataṁ saukṣhmyād ākāśhaṁ nopalipyate
sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate

translation.simple: Just as the vast sky is present everywhere but never stained by anything within it, similarly, our true Self, the soul, resides within the body yet remains ever pure and untouched by its actions or experiences.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse helps us understand the profound nature of our spirit. Even as our body and mind engage with the world, experiencing countless changes and sensations, the eternal soul within remains as pure and subtle as space itself. It witnesses all, yet is never bound or blemished by the fleeting conditions of material existence. This realization brings a deep sense of peace and helps us connect with our inherent, divine essence.
translation.essence: Our soul, subtle and pervasive like the sky, dwells within the body yet remains eternally untainted by its material nature, ever pristine and free.

13-34.sanskrit: यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः।क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत।।13.34।।
13-34.transliteration:
yathā prakāśhayaty ekaḥ kṛitsnaṁ lokam imaṁ raviḥ
kṣhetraṁ kṣhetrī tathā kṛitsnaṁ prakāśhayati bhārata

translation.simple: Just as the single sun brings light to this whole world, so too does the Spirit within us illuminate our entire body and experiences, O Arjuna.
translation.deep: The deeper wisdom here is about the nature of consciousness. Just as the sun's light touches everything without becoming the things it shines upon, the Soul (Kshetrī) illuminates the body (Kshetra) and its experiences. It is the awareness that makes us perceive and feel, yet it remains separate, pure, and unchanging. This insight reminds us that our true essence is this illuminating, eternal spirit, not the temporary physical form.
translation.essence: The soul is the ever-shining light within, illuminating our entire being, just as the sun illuminates the entire world.

13-35.sanskrit: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा।भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम्।।13.35।।
13-35.transliteration:
kṣhetra-kṣhetrajñayor evam antaraṁ jñāna-chakṣhuṣhā
bhūta-prakṛiti-mokṣhaṁ cha ye vidur yānti te param

translation.simple: When we look with the eyes of wisdom, we truly understand the difference between our physical body and the eternal soul within. Those who grasp this truth, and thus find release from the material world's influence, reach the Supreme Abode.
translation.deep: Through the enlightened vision of divine knowledge, a sincere seeker clearly discerns the profound distinction between the physical field of existence and the conscious Spirit that animates it. This profound realization, coupled with the understanding of liberation from the entanglement of material nature, guides such a soul directly to the ultimate Supreme Truth, granting everlasting peace and spiritual fulfillment.
translation.essence: With wisdom's light, one perceives the soul distinct from the body and finds freedom from material nature, thus reaching the Supreme.

14-1.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचपरं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम्।यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः।।14.1।।
14-1.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
paraṁ bhūyaḥ pravakṣhyāmi jñānānāṁ jñānam uttamam
yaj jñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṁ siddhim ito gatāḥ

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord lovingly begins, 'I will now tell you again about the most excellent wisdom. This is the understanding by which all saintly souls have reached the ultimate perfection and freedom.'
translation.deep: The Supreme Lord promises to reveal again a profound truth, the most sacred of all understandings. This is the very wisdom that, when truly known and embraced, has guided countless sincere seekers and sages to a state of supreme liberation, beyond all worldly limitations and sorrow.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna promises to share the ultimate wisdom, the knowledge that leads all sincere souls to supreme liberation and perfection.

14-2.sanskrit: इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः।सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च।।14.2।।
14-2.transliteration:
idaṁ jñānam upāśhritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ
sarge ’pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti cha

translation.simple: Taking refuge in this sacred wisdom, souls attain a nature akin to Mine. They are not born again when creation unfolds, nor do they experience sorrow when the universe dissolves.
translation.deep: When a soul sincerely embraces this profound understanding of reality, they become united with My divine essence. Such illumined beings transcend the cycles of birth and death; they do not enter creation anew, nor are they troubled by the great dissolution of the cosmos, remaining eternally serene in My presence.
translation.essence: Embracing this divine wisdom leads to oneness with My nature, freeing the soul from the cycles of birth and the sorrow of cosmic dissolution.

14-3.sanskrit: मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम्।संभवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत।।14.3।।
14-3.transliteration:
mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbhaṁ dadhāmy aham
sambhavaḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ tato bhavati bhārata

translation.simple: The vast and wondrous material nature is like My divine womb. Within it, I place the seed of life. From this sacred union, O Arjuna, all beings come into existence.
translation.deep: The Supreme Lord explains that the primordial material energy, often called the great Brahman or Prakriti, is His own expansive potency, serving as the cosmic womb. Into this vast realm, He infuses the spiritual seed, which are the individual souls. This divine interaction between the Lord's consciousness and material nature is the ultimate source from which all diverse forms of life in the universe gracefully emerge, O Arjuna.
translation.essence: The Lord is the ultimate origin of all creation. He uses His divine and expansive nature as a cosmic womb, infusing it with the spiritual seed from which every single being arises. All life is a beautiful manifestation of His divine will and presence.

14-4.sanskrit: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः।तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता।।14.4।।
14-4.transliteration:
sarva-yoniṣhu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ sambhavanti yāḥ
tāsāṁ brahma mahad yonir ahaṁ bīja-pradaḥ pitā

translation.simple: Know, O Arjuna, that for every form of life born from any source, material nature is the great mother. And I am the father, the giver of the spiritual seed.
translation.deep: This sacred verse gently unveils the profound mystery of creation. The Lord lovingly explains that every living form, from the smallest to the grandest, emerges from a sacred union. Material nature, vast and all-encompassing, acts as the great mother, offering the very substance for life to manifest. Yet, it is the Supreme Lord Himself who, as the divine father, bestows the spiritual seed, animating all beings with consciousness. Thus, all life flows from His divine glance and loving embrace of nature.
translation.essence: The Lord reveals Himself as the ultimate Father, and material nature as the universal Mother. From their divine union, all creation blossoms into diverse forms of life.

14-5.sanskrit: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः।निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम्।।14.5।।
14-5.transliteration:
sattvaṁ rajas tama iti guṇāḥ prakṛiti-sambhavāḥ
nibadhnanti mahā-bāho dehe dehinam avyayam

translation.simple: My dear friend, Lord Krishna explains that goodness, passion, and ignorance are three qualities born from nature. These qualities gently, yet firmly, bind the eternal soul to this physical body.
translation.deep: O mighty-armed Arjuna, the divine wisdom reveals that Sattva (purity and illumination), Rajas (activity and attachment), and Tamas (inertia and delusion) are fundamental energies of material nature. Although the soul residing within the body is inherently imperishable and eternal, these natural qualities subtly influence and seem to bind it to the experiences of the physical realm.
translation.essence: The soul within is pure and unending. Yet, the qualities of nature—goodness, passion, and ignorance—lovingly connect it to the experience of this earthly body.

14-6.sanskrit: तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम्।सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ।।14.6।।
14-6.transliteration:
tatra sattvaṁ nirmalatvāt prakāśhakam anāmayam
sukha-saṅgena badhnāti jñāna-saṅgena chānagha

translation.simple: O pure-hearted one, among these qualities, Sattva is bright and pure, free from any taint. Yet, it gently ties the soul by drawing it to happiness and by its love for knowledge.
translation.deep: My dear Arjuna, Sattva, being luminous and free from impurities, brings a sense of peace and clarity. It seems perfect, a state of well-being. However, even this pure quality has a way of holding the soul. It binds by fostering attachment to the joy and contentment it brings, and by a deep love for intellectual understanding and spiritual knowledge. While these experiences are noble and elevating, an excessive clinging to them can subtly prevent true liberation, as the soul remains focused on the *experience* rather than the ultimate freedom beyond all experiences.
translation.essence: Even the purest quality of Sattva, which brings light and peace, can gently bind the soul. It does so by cultivating attachment to the joy and understanding it offers, reminding us that true freedom lies beyond all forms of attachment, even noble ones.

14-7.sanskrit: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम्।तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम्।।14.7।।
14-7.transliteration:
rajo rāgātmakaṁ viddhi tṛiṣhṇā-saṅga-samudbhavam
tan nibadhnāti kaunteya karma-saṅgena dehinam

translation.simple: Know, O Arjuna, that the quality of passion arises from strong desires and deep attachments. It holds the embodied soul firmly through its engagement in actions, driven by a yearning for their fruits.
translation.deep: My dear Arjuna, contemplate that the vibrant force of passion, or 'rajo-guna,' is inherently connected to strong desires and heartfelt attachments. This very force, while inspiring activity, subtly binds the spirit within the body, as it becomes deeply engrossed in actions, motivated by a yearning for specific outcomes.
translation.essence: Passion, springing from insatiable desires and attachments, binds the soul as it engages in actions, driven by a yearning for their fruits.

14-8.transliteration:
tamas tv ajñāna-jaṁ viddhi mohanaṁ sarva-dehinām
pramādālasya-nidrābhis tan nibadhnāti bhārata

translation.simple: Understand, dear soul, that this quality of darkness arises from a lack of true wisdom. It quietly deludes all who dwell in a body, binding them with forgetfulness, idleness, and heavy sleep.
translation.deep: This principle of darkness, born from our unawareness of the ultimate truth, spreads a gentle bewilderment over every embodied soul. It holds us, O Arjuna, by fostering neglect of our duties, deep-seated lethargy, and an inclination towards excessive sleep, which keeps the spirit from awakening.
translation.essence: This quality of darkness, springing from a lack of spiritual insight, gently clouds the minds of all beings. It binds us through moments of neglect, feelings of dullness, and the tendency for excessive sleep, holding us back from our true spiritual journey.

14-9.sanskrit: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत।ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत।।14.9।।
14-9.transliteration:
sattvaṁ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata
jñānam āvṛitya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayaty uta

translation.simple: Dear Arjuna, the quality of goodness (Sattva) binds a soul to a feeling of happiness and contentment. The quality of passion (Rajas) ties one to the endless pursuit of activities. And the quality of ignorance (Tamas), by clouding wisdom, attaches a soul to delusion and carelessness.
translation.deep: This sacred verse gently reveals how the three fundamental qualities of nature subtly influence our being. Even pure joy and peace (Sattva) can become a gentle tether, making us comfortable and less inclined to seek beyond. The restless drive of passion (Rajas) keeps us ceaselessly engaged in actions, often for their fruits, creating an intricate web of involvement. But most profoundly, the darkness of ignorance (Tamas) envelops our inner wisdom, leading us to states of heedlessness and misunderstanding, keeping us far from our true, enlightened self.
translation.essence: Sattva binds through the allure of happiness, Rajas through the relentless urge for action, and Tamas through the veil of ignorance and delusion. Each quality, in its unique way, keeps the spirit attached to this material realm.

14-10.sanskrit: रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत।रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा।।14.10।।
14-10.transliteration:
rajas tamaśh chābhibhūya sattvaṁ bhavati bhārata
rajaḥ sattvaṁ tamaśh chaiva tamaḥ sattvaṁ rajas tathā

translation.simple: Beloved seeker, sometimes the quiet light of goodness shines forth, soothing the restlessness of passion and the heaviness of ignorance. At other moments, a strong wave of passion might rise, covering goodness and ignorance. And then, a gentle mist of ignorance could settle, dimming both goodness and passion. This is how these three inner qualities gently shift and interact within us.
translation.deep: O seeker of truth, understand that the three fundamental qualities—serenity (sattva), activity (rajas), and inertia (tamas)—are perpetually at play within all beings. It is revealed that serenity can ascend, gracefully subduing both the dynamic energy of passion and the inert heaviness of ignorance. Conversely, passion can emerge with vigor, overshadowing serenity and ignorance. And similarly, inertia can settle, gently suppressing serenity and passion. This constant, beautiful interplay determines our internal landscape and outward expressions, guiding us to observe and understand the fluid nature of our existence and to strive for higher states of being.
translation.essence: The Lord teaches us that the three qualities – goodness, passion, and ignorance – are always in motion within. One gently rises to influence us most, showing the ever-changing nature of our inner world.

14-11.sanskrit: सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते।ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत।।14.11।।
14-11.transliteration:
sarva-dvāreṣhu dehe ’smin prakāśha upajāyate
jñānaṁ yadā tadā vidyād vivṛiddhaṁ sattvam ity uta

translation.simple: When a gentle radiance of wisdom starts to shine through all the senses of this body, know that the quality of inner goodness and purity has truly blossomed within you.
translation.deep: This verse tenderly explains that when the light of discerning knowledge illuminates our mind and senses, it is a clear sign that the divine quality of *sattva* – purity, peace, and spiritual clarity – has become strong and vibrant within us. It signifies a state where our inner being is aligned with truth, allowing understanding to flow through every perception.
translation.essence: As purity grows within, it illuminates our entire being with the light of true understanding.

14-12.sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा।रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ।।14.12।।
14-12.transliteration:
lobhaḥ pravṛittir ārambhaḥ karmaṇām aśhamaḥ spṛihā
rajasy etāni jāyante vivṛiddhe bharatarṣhabha

translation.simple: O Arjuna, when the quality of passion, known as Rajas, becomes strong within us, one may observe a tendency towards wanting more, a constant engagement in activities, the starting of many new tasks, a feeling of restlessness, and a deep longing for various things. These are the ways Rajas manifests its influence.
translation.deep: This sacred verse tenderly points to the subtle workings of the Gunas. When Rajas, the guna of dynamic energy and action, becomes dominant, the inner self experiences a surge of inclinations: a pull towards accumulating (lobha), an impetus to engage in ceaseless endeavors (pravṛtti), a readiness to initiate numerous projects (ārambhaḥ karmaṇām), an absence of inner stillness (aśamaḥ), and a persistent yearning for objects and experiences (spṛhā). Understanding these manifestations allows us to gently become aware of their presence, fostering a mindful approach to our inner state and guiding us towards a deeper sense of peace and spiritual detachment, rather than being driven by external pursuits.
translation.essence: When the heart is swayed by the active quality of Rajas, desires, restlessness, and a drive for constant engagement increase. Recognizing these inner stirrings helps us cultivate mindful awareness and gently steer towards a more peaceful and spiritually aligned path.

14-13.sanskrit: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च।तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन।।14.13।।
14-13.transliteration:
aprakāśho ’pravṛittiśh cha pramādo moha eva cha
tamasy etāni jāyante vivṛiddhe kuru-nandana

translation.simple: When the quality of Tamas, which is ignorance, becomes dominant, dear Arjuna, one experiences a lack of inner light, a disinterest in action, a tendency towards heedlessness, and a clouding of judgment. It's a gentle reminder to observe these states.
translation.deep: This sacred verse tenderly reveals the signs when Tamas, the energy of inertia and spiritual dimness, becomes prominent in our being. We might notice a loss of inner illumination, a reluctance to engage in meaningful action, a certain forgetfulness or heedlessness, and a deep sense of bewilderment. These are gentle whispers from within, showing us how our inner light can be obscured, clouding our judgment and making us feel lost in illusion. It encourages mindful observation of these states.
translation.essence: This verse lovingly teaches us that when Tamas, the quality of ignorance, grows, we experience a dimming of inner light, a reluctance to act, carelessness, and deep delusion. It's a gentle guidance to recognize these signs and seek the path of clarity and engagement.

14-14.sanskrit: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत्।तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते।।14.14।।
14-14.transliteration:
yadā sattve pravṛiddhe tu pralayaṁ yāti deha-bhṛit
tadottama-vidāṁ lokān amalān pratipadyate

translation.simple: When a soul departs from its body while the quality of goodness (Sattva) is dominant, it ascends to the pure, peaceful realms where the most virtuous and wise souls dwell.
translation.deep: Should a person's earthly journey conclude when the essence of purity and spiritual light, known as Sattva, is most vibrant within them, their soul is then guided to the pristine and unblemished planes of existence. These are the sacred dwelling places reserved for those elevated beings who have truly understood the highest spiritual truths.
translation.essence: To leave this world with a heart overflowing with goodness is to gently enter the serene, pure realms of the enlightened.

14-15.sanskrit: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते।तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते।।14.15।।
14-15.transliteration:
rajasi pralayaṁ gatvā karma-saṅgiṣhu jāyate
tathā pralīnas tamasi mūḍha-yoniṣhu jāyate

translation.simple: When a soul departs while passion and driven activity (rajas) are dominant, it finds birth among those who are deeply engaged in worldly actions and pursuits. And if one leaves the body when ignorance and inertia (tamas) prevail, that soul is born into situations of confusion and spiritual dimness.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to understand the profound influence of our inner state, or Gunas, at the sacred moment of transition. If the energy of rajas—characterized by intense activity, desire, and attachment to the fruits of labor—is dominant when the soul departs, it leads to rebirth in a sphere where constant action and worldly engagement are paramount. Conversely, if tamas—the quality of spiritual inertia, illusion, and heedlessness—holds sway at that moment, the soul is guided to a life path marked by delusion and a dimmed understanding of truth. It lovingly teaches us that the quality of our consciousness, nurtured through our actions and thoughts, truly determines the nature of our journey ahead.
translation.essence: The state of our heart and mind, whether filled with restless activity or clouded by unawareness at the time of departure, lovingly influences the next chapter of our soul's eternal journey. Let us strive for spiritual wakefulness always.

14-16.sanskrit: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम्।रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम्।।14.16।।
14-16.transliteration:
karmaṇaḥ sukṛitasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṁ nirmalaṁ phalam
rajasas tu phalaṁ duḥkham ajñānaṁ tamasaḥ phalam

translation.simple: They say that pure and peaceful joy springs from virtuous and pure actions. But from actions born of restless desire, sorrow inevitably arises. And from actions done in dullness or unawareness, the fruit is simply more confusion.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully explains how the three qualities of nature, the Gunas – Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas – shape the very essence of our actions and their consequences. When we act with purity, clarity, and kindness (Sattva), the result is inner peace, spiritual growth, and a serene mind. However, actions driven by ambition, craving, and restless energy (Rajas) eventually lead to dissatisfaction and suffering, binding us to the cycle of wanting. And when actions are performed out of delusion, laziness, or apathy (Tamas), they cloud our understanding and lead us further into spiritual darkness and bewilderment.
translation.essence: Our actions are like seeds; their fruits perfectly reflect their nature. Choose to act with purity and wisdom, for only then will true peace and spiritual clarity blossom within you.

14-17.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च।प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च।।14.17।।
14-17.transliteration:
sattvāt sañjāyate jñānaṁ rajaso lobha eva cha
pramāda-mohau tamaso bhavato ’jñānam eva cha

translation.simple: From the heart's purity and goodness (Sattva), true understanding and clear knowledge blossom. From restless activity and passion (Rajas), a strong desire for more, even greed, can easily arise within us. And from darkness and inertia (Tamas), comes confusion, heedlessness, and a profound lack of true spiritual awareness.
translation.deep: This divine teaching reminds us how the three qualities of nature influence our inner journey. When Sattva shines within, our spirit awakens to tranquil knowledge, allowing us to discern truth from the fleeting illusions of the world. But when Rajas stirs, a fervent longing for worldly things and experiences takes root, often leading to a cycle of restless pursuits and a sense of incompleteness. And when Tamas descends, it veils our inner sight, leading to spiritual forgetfulness, apathy, and a dimmed perception of life's sacred purpose.
translation.essence: Knowledge and wisdom spring from purity (Sattva), restless desire and wanting from passion (Rajas), and spiritual slumber, confusion, and ignorance from inertia (Tamas). Understanding this helps us choose the path of light.

14-18.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः।जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः।।14.18।।
14-18.transliteration:
ūrdhvaṁ gachchhanti sattva-sthā madhye tiṣhṭhanti rājasāḥ
jaghanya-guṇa-vṛitti-sthā adho gachchhanti tāmasāḥ

translation.simple: Souls guided by purity and goodness (sattva) ascend towards higher spiritual states. Those swayed by passion and earthly desires (rajas) remain within the middle, worldly cycles. But those who succumb to ignorance and darkness (tamas) unfortunately descend to lower realms of experience.
translation.deep: This verse lovingly illuminates how our inner disposition shapes our journey beyond this life. When our hearts resonate with the clarity and serenity of sattva, we naturally gravitate towards spiritual upliftment and closeness to the Divine. A life driven by rajas, full of ambition and attachment to outcomes, keeps us perpetually engaged in the material realm's ebb and flow. However, if we allow our consciousness to be clouded by the inertia and illusion of tamas, our spiritual progress may suffer, leading to states of greater entanglement. It's a profound reminder that our choices, imbued with these qualities, direct our eternal path.
translation.essence: Our predominant inner quality – be it purity, passion, or ignorance – profoundly determines our spiritual trajectory and future state of being. Cultivating sattva leads us towards divine light.

14-19.sanskrit: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति।गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति।।14.19।।
14-19.transliteration:
nānyaṁ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṁ yadā draṣhṭānupaśhyati
guṇebhyaśh cha paraṁ vetti mad-bhāvaṁ so ’dhigachchhati

translation.simple: When a soul perceives that all actions arise from the qualities of nature (Gunas) and understands that there is a Truth far beyond these qualities, then that soul begins to dwell in My divine state.
translation.deep: This verse reveals a profound truth: all the activities we witness, both in the world and within ourselves, are orchestrations of the three qualities of material nature—Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. The wise observer, the 'seer,' understands that the true self is not the doer, but merely a witness to this play of Gunas. When one transcends the identification with these qualities and distinctly perceives the eternal Reality that exists beyond their influence, then one truly begins to enter into My unchanging, divine consciousness. It's a journey of gentle detachment, moving from the illusion of personal agency to the peace of divine realization.
translation.essence: Realizing that nature's qualities perform all actions, and then knowing that which is beyond them, one attains My divine being.

14-20.transliteration:
guṇān etān atītya trīn dehī deha-samudbhavān
janma-mṛityu-jarā-duḥkhair vimukto ’mṛitam aśhnute

translation.simple: When the embodied soul rises above the three qualities of material nature connected to the body, it becomes free from the sorrows of birth, old age, and death, and experiences lasting, peaceful joy.
translation.deep: The human soul, bound by the body, constantly interacts with the three modes of material nature – goodness (sattva), passion (rajas), and ignorance (tamas). These modes arise from and influence our physical existence. When a spiritual seeker learns to transcend the pull and effects of these three qualities, they detach from the material illusions and sufferings inherent in the cycle of birth, decay, and death. This liberation leads to a profound state of spiritual realization, where the soul tastes the divine nectar of true immortality and eternal freedom, beyond all worldly sorrows.
translation.essence: Rising above the material qualities frees the soul from life's cycles of suffering, granting the experience of ultimate spiritual immortality and peace.

14-21.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचकैर्लिंगैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो।किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते।।14.21।।
14-21.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
kair liṅgais trīn guṇān etān atīto bhavati prabho
kim āchāraḥ kathaṁ chaitāns trīn guṇān ativartate

translation.simple: Arjuna humbly asked, 'My dear Lord, how can we recognize a soul who has risen above these three qualities of material nature? What is their way of life? And how can we too transcend these qualities?'
translation.deep: Arjuna's heart yearns to understand the enlightened soul. He asks about the gentle signs that mark one who is beyond the influences of goodness, passion, and ignorance. He also longs to know the path, the sacred journey, by which we can ourselves rise above these worldly currents and find lasting peace within, free from their grasp.
translation.essence: Arjuna's loving inquiry invites us to reflect on the qualities of a truly liberated soul and the devotional path to transcend material nature's sway.

14-22.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव।न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति।।14.22।।
14-22.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
prakāśhaṁ cha pravṛittiṁ cha moham eva cha pāṇḍava
na dveṣhṭi sampravṛittāni na nivṛittāni kāṅkṣhati

translation.simple: Lord Krishna says: O Arjuna, when qualities like clarity, activity, or confusion arise in your mind, a wise soul does not resent them. Nor do they yearn for these states when they naturally fade away.
translation.deep: Here, Lord Krishna beautifully explains the nature of a soul who transcends the modes of material nature. Such a one observes the interplay of clarity, action, and even confusion, understanding them as passing phases. They hold no aversion when these qualities manifest, nor do they feel a longing when they subside. Their inner peace remains steady, for they rest in a deeper awareness beyond the changing states of the mind.
translation.essence: This verse reminds us to observe the coming and going of all our experiences—be it clarity, action, or bewilderment—without attachment or dislike. A truly peaceful heart remains steady, knowing these are just the changing colors of the mind, and rests in unwavering calm.

14-23.sanskrit: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते।गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते।।14.23।।
14-23.transliteration:
udāsīna-vad āsīno guṇair yo na vichālyate
guṇā vartanta ity evaṁ yo ’vatiṣhṭhati neṅgate

translation.simple: Imagine a soul that sits peacefully, watching the world unfold without being pulled into its dramas. They understand that all the comings and goings are just the play of nature's qualities (Gunas). With this gentle awareness, they remain perfectly calm and steady, never wavering from their inner peace.
translation.deep: This verse reveals a profound state of spiritual liberation. It describes a being who has truly understood that the shifting moods of life – the stirring of ambition, the pull of comfort, the urge for action – are all expressions of the Gunas. Such a one observes these energies at play within and around them, yet remains unattached and unmoved, secure in the knowledge that their true self is distinct from these temporary material qualities. They stand as a silent witness, eternally undisturbed by the world's changing tides.
translation.essence: To remain a peaceful, unperturbed observer of life's events, understanding them as the natural workings of the Gunas, and thus staying steadfast in one's serene inner being.

14-24.transliteration:
sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ sva-sthaḥ sama-loṣhṭāśhma-kāñchanaḥ
tulya-priyāpriyo dhīras tulya-nindātma-sanstutiḥ

translation.simple: A tranquil soul embraces both joy and sorrow with an even heart. For them, a humble clod of earth and precious gold are seen with the same serene gaze. Unmoved by what they prefer or dislike, by criticism or commendation, they remain steadfast in their inner peace.
translation.deep: This sacred verse describes a soul perfectly poised and self-contained, one who has transcended the sway of worldly attachments. Such a being observes life's fleeting dualities—the warmth of happiness and the coolness of sorrow—with profound equanimity, understanding their transient nature. Material valuations, whether for a simple pebble or shimmering gold, lose their power to disturb this inner tranquility. With a truly discerning and stable mind, they meet both cherished affections and unwelcome dislikes, both harsh criticism and sweet praise, with an undisturbed spirit, having found their unshakeable abode in the eternal Self.
translation.essence: To experience life's highs and lows, praise and blame, preference and dislike, with an equal and peaceful heart is the mark of a wise soul, ever steady in true spiritual freedom.

14-25.transliteration:
mānāpamānayos tulyas tulyo mitrāri-pakṣhayoḥ
sarvārambha-parityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa uchyate

translation.simple: A soul who remains balanced through praise and blame, and sees friends and adversaries with an equal heart, letting go of attachment to the outcomes of all their endeavors – such a one is truly said to have risen beyond the material qualities of nature.
translation.deep: To be known as one who has transcended the modes of material nature is to cultivate a profound inner balance and unwavering peace. For such a devoted soul, external conditions like honor or dishonor, or relationships labeled as 'friend' or 'enemy,' no longer disturb their serene connection to the Divine. They engage in their duties wholeheartedly, yet gracefully offer up the fruits of all their actions, finding liberation in complete surrender and disinterest in worldly results. This path leads to a dwelling in everlasting tranquility.
translation.essence: Remain balanced through all dualities and act without desire for results; this elevates one beyond material nature to lasting peace.

14-26.sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्ितयोगेन सेवते।स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते।।14.26।।
14-26.transliteration:
māṁ cha yo ’vyabhichāreṇa bhakti-yogena sevate
sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahma-bhūyāya kalpate
