translation.simple: When a soul serves Me with pure, unwavering devotion, they rise above the influence of the material qualities. Such a soul becomes truly ready to realize their divine essence.
translation.deep: This verse lovingly tells us that when a soul offers devotion to Me without wavering, that pure love lifts them beyond the three modes of material nature. This steady, selfless service purifies the heart, allowing one to transcend all worldly bonds and attain the state of Brahman, realizing their eternal, divine self.
translation.essence: Pure, unwavering devotion is the gentle path to transcending material nature and realizing your eternal, divine self.

14-27.sanskrit: ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च।शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च।।14.27।।
14-27.transliteration:
brahmaṇo hi pratiṣhṭhāham amṛitasyāvyayasya cha
śhāśhvatasya cha dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya cha

translation.simple: I am the very foundation for Brahman, for immortality that never fades, and for all that is unchanging. I am the basis of eternal righteousness and the source of pure, unending joy.
translation.deep: Understand, O seeker, that I am the supreme foundation not only of Brahman, the boundless Spirit, but also of the deathless state and all that is immutable. I am the eternal source of everlasting righteousness and the ultimate giver of that profound, unwavering happiness which never ceases. To connect with Me is to touch the very essence of these divine qualities.
translation.essence: I am the ultimate foundation of all divine reality: Brahman, eternal life, unchanging truth, sacred duty, and supreme, unending bliss.

15-1.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम्।छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्।।15.1।।
15-1.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
ūrdhva-mūlam adhaḥ-śhākham aśhvatthaṁ prāhur avyayam
chhandānsi yasya parṇāni yas taṁ veda sa veda-vit

translation.simple: Lord Krishna said: There is a sacred tree, with roots reaching high above and branches spreading below. They speak of this tree as unending. Its leaves are like the Vedic hymns. Whoever truly understands this tree is indeed a knower of the Vedas.
translation.deep: The Blessed Lord revealed a profound truth, describing this worldly existence as an ancient, inverted tree. Its unseen roots originate in the highest divine realms, while its branches extend downwards, forming all experiences and forms of life. Though its cycle of birth and death appears eternal, it is within our power to understand its nature. The sacred Vedic hymns, offering guidance and wisdom, are likened to its rustling leaves. To comprehend this wondrous tree — its divine source, its pervasive presence, and the path to transcend its grasp — is to gain the deepest spiritual insight and true wisdom.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna uses the beautiful imagery of an inverted, unending tree to symbolize our material world, deeply rooted in the divine. Understanding this tree, whose leaves are the sacred Vedas, is the key to true spiritual wisdom and liberation.

15-2.sanskrit: अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा     गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः।अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि     कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके।।15.2।।
15-2.transliteration:
adhaśh chordhvaṁ prasṛitās tasya śhākhā
guṇa-pravṛiddhā viṣhaya-pravālāḥ
adhaśh cha mūlāny anusantatāni
karmānubandhīni manuṣhya-loke

translation.simple: The branches of this worldly tree spread upwards and downwards, nourished by the modes of nature. Its fresh sprouts are the objects of our senses, drawing us in. Its roots reach deep into the human realm, firmly tied by our actions and their results.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully describes the tree of material existence, with its branches extending throughout all realms, both high and low. These branches are kept alive and growing by the three qualities of nature (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas), and their tender leaves are the sense objects that allure our minds. Deep beneath, in the world of human beings, new roots continuously emerge, firmly bound by our past and present actions (karma), perpetuating the cycle of birth and experience.
translation.essence: This teaching reveals how the material world, sustained by our desires and actions, keeps us entangled. It highlights the pervasive influence of nature's qualities and the deep roots our karma forms, guiding us to understand the impermanence of this tree of life.

15-3.sanskrit: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते    नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा।अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल    मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा।।15.3।।
15-3.transliteration:
na rūpam asyeha tathopalabhyate
nānto na chādir na cha sampratiṣhṭhā
aśhvattham enaṁ su-virūḍha-mūlam
asaṅga-śhastreṇa dṛiḍhena chhittvā

translation.simple: In this world, we cannot fully grasp the beginning, end, or true form of this vast existence, much like a deeply rooted tree. Yet, the Lord lovingly guides us: with the powerful weapon of non-attachment, we can gently cut through its strong hold.
translation.deep: The Lord describes this material realm as an ancient, ever-growing tree whose true form, origin, and ultimate foundation remain elusive to our limited perception. Its roots penetrate deeply into the earth of our desires and attachments, binding us to the cycle of birth and death. To transcend this intricate illusion and approach the Divine, we are given a powerful key: the strong weapon of *asaṅga*, or non-attachment. This sacred practice involves cultivating an inner state of detachment from the transient fruits of our actions and the fleeting allure of worldly possessions and relationships. By letting go of our possessive grip, we begin to sever the invisible ties that root us to this temporary existence, thus moving towards the eternal peace offered by the Lord.
translation.essence: This worldly tree, with hidden roots and form, keeps us bound. The Lord's guidance is to cut its hold with the strong, calm sword of non-attachment, leading to liberation.

15-4.sanskrit: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्य    यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः।तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये    यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी।।15.4।।
15-4.transliteration:
tataḥ padaṁ tat parimārgitavyaṁ
yasmin gatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ
tam eva chādyaṁ puruṣhaṁ prapadye
yataḥ pravṛittiḥ prasṛitā purāṇī

translation.simple: With a calm heart, we must seek that divine abode, a sacred place where souls, once arrived, never return to worldly struggles. Let us humbly surrender to that Ancient Source, the First Being, from whom all life and existence gracefully flow, eternally.
translation.deep: This sacred verse invites us to turn our gaze inward, searching for that most elevated and eternal dwelling. It is a place of everlasting peace, where a soul, once anchored, finds release from the ceaseless turning of the world. With profound reverence, we are called to offer our whole being to the Original Divine Person, the primeval source from whom all the ancient streams of creation, with their endless beauty and profound mystery, have flowed forth since time immemorial.
translation.essence: Aspire for the eternal abode where the soul finds perpetual peace. Devotionally surrender to the Divine Origin, the ancient source from whom all creation gracefully unfolds.

15-5.sanskrit: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा    अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः।द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै    र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत्।।15.5।।
15-5.transliteration:
nirmāna-mohā jita-saṅga-doṣhā
adhyātma-nityā vinivṛitta-kāmāḥ
dvandvair vimuktāḥ sukha-duḥkha-sanjñair
gachchhanty amūḍhāḥ padam avyayaṁ tat

translation.simple: Those who are free from pride and illusion, who have overcome the fault of worldly attachments, who are always centered in their spiritual understanding, and whose material desires have calmed. Such souls, liberated from the dualities of joy and sorrow, truly attain that eternal, unchanging abode.
translation.deep: The blessed souls who have shed the burdens of ego-driven pride and delusive thoughts. They have transcended the limitations and pains born from deep worldly attachments. Their consciousness is ever-fixed upon the profound spiritual truth, constantly abiding in the divine Self, their material longings having gracefully receded. Untouched by the alternating currents of pleasure and pain, these undeluded seekers ultimately reach that supreme, imperishable state of being.
translation.essence: Shedding pride, illusion, and attachment, dwelling in the Spirit, free from desires and the sway of joy and sorrow – such wise ones reach the eternal Truth.

15-6.sanskrit: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः।यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम।।15.6।।
15-6.transliteration:
na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śhaśhāṅko na pāvakaḥ
yad gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama

translation.simple: My supreme dwelling place, that divine realm, needs no light from the sun, the moon, or any earthly fire. Once a soul finds its way there, it never again returns to this world of change. It is My eternal home.
translation.deep: This sacred verse gently points to My supreme abode, a realm of pure spiritual light that doesn't rely on the sun, moon, or fire. These earthly lights are fleeting, but My abode shines with an eternal, self-luminous glow. To journey there means transcending the cycles of coming and going, finding true and lasting liberation. It is a state of unbroken peace and divine union, where the soul rests eternally in My presence, never needing to return to the temporary world.
translation.essence: My supreme abode is a self-shining, eternal spiritual realm. Once a soul arrives there, it finds true liberation, experiencing everlasting peace and never returning to the material world. It is the ultimate divine destination.

15-7.sanskrit: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः।मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति।।15.7।।
15-7.transliteration:
mamaivānśho jīva-loke jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ
manaḥ-ṣhaṣhṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛiti-sthāni karṣhati

translation.simple: In this world of living beings, each soul is truly an eternal, precious spark of My own divine self. Though eternal, this soul takes on a living form and experiences the world, drawing the mind and five senses, which are all situated within material nature.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse whispers a profound truth: your very essence, the living being within, is an eternal, cherished portion of the Divine, never truly separate. Although this soul is timeless and unchanging, it finds itself in the material realm, where it engages with the mind and the five senses, which are all creations of nature. Through these instruments, the eternal soul experiences the world, sometimes feeling drawn into its temporary delights and challenges, yet always remaining a fragment of the Supreme.
translation.essence: Your true self is an eternal, divine spark, experiencing life in this world through the mind and senses, which are part of nature.

15-8.transliteration:
śharīraṁ yad avāpnoti yach chāpy utkrāmatīśhvaraḥ
gṛihītvaitāni sanyāti vāyur gandhān ivāśhayāt

translation.simple: Just as a gentle breeze carries the sweet fragrance of flowers from one place to another, so too does the individual soul, when it leaves a body, carry the subtle essence of the mind and senses to its next dwelling.
translation.deep: When the individual soul, the 'master' within each form, takes on a new physical body, it gathers and brings along the subtle faculties of mind and senses. Similarly, when it departs from a body, it carries these inner instruments with it. This journey is beautifully likened to the wind, which, though unseen, faithfully carries aromas from their source, reminding us of the soul's profound and continuous passage, always carrying its experiences and inclinations.
translation.essence: The soul's journey from one body to another is a natural and subtle process, like the wind carrying a fragrance. It always takes with it the essence of the mind and senses, continuing its path guided by the divine order.

15-9.sanskrit: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च।अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते।।15.9।।
15-9.transliteration:
śhrotraṁ chakṣhuḥ sparśhanaṁ cha rasanaṁ ghrāṇam eva cha
adhiṣhṭhāya manaśh chāyaṁ viṣhayān upasevate

translation.simple: Our soul, dwelling within, uses the senses of hearing, sight, touch, taste, and smell, along with the mind, to experience the world around us.
translation.deep: Within this human form, the individual spirit takes hold of the senses – our capacity to hear, see, feel, taste, and smell – and also engages the mind. It is through these delicate instruments that the soul deeply connects with and experiences the vast tapestry of the material world. This verse gently illuminates how our inner being intimately interacts with the outer reality, shaping our perceptions.
translation.essence: The soul's journey in the world is one of mindful perception, experiencing creation's beauty through the gifts of our senses and the guiding presence of the mind.

15-10.sanskrit: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम्।विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः।।15.10।।
15-10.transliteration:
utkrāmantaṁ sthitaṁ vāpi bhuñjānaṁ vā guṇānvitam
vimūḍhā nānupaśhyanti paśhyanti jñāna-chakṣhuṣhaḥ

translation.simple: When the soul departs from the body, or when it resides within, or when it experiences the world's qualities, those who are deluded cannot truly see it. Only those blessed with the eye of spiritual wisdom can perceive its true nature.
translation.deep: The divine essence within, the soul, remains untouched by the changing states of the body—its arrival, its departure, or its engagement with the material world's three qualities. The external senses can never grasp this subtle truth. It is only through the cultivation of pure knowledge and spiritual discernment that one gains the inner vision, the 'jñāna-chakṣuḥ', enabling them to recognize the eternal, unchanging Self, distinct from all temporary experiences and forms. This realization brings profound peace and frees us from the illusions of identification with the fleeting body and mind.
translation.essence: With the eye of wisdom, one perceives the eternal soul, untouched by the body's comings and goings, a truth veiled from those lost in illusion.

15-11.transliteration:
yatanto yoginaśh chainaṁ paśhyanty ātmany avasthitam
yatanto ‘py akṛitātmāno nainaṁ paśhyanty achetasaḥ

translation.simple: True seekers who strive with sincerity behold the divine presence nestled within their own hearts. But even if others make efforts, if their minds are not yet pure, they cannot truly perceive this sacred truth.
translation.deep: Through devoted practice and disciplined effort, spiritual aspirants come to experience the Self, the Supreme Lord, residing within the depths of their own being. Yet, those whose inner nature remains unrefined, whose hearts are clouded, despite their outward endeavors, are unable to discern this most intimate divine presence.
translation.essence: Sincere spiritual endeavor, coupled with inner purity, reveals the Divine within. Without this inner refinement, the truth remains unseen.

15-12.sanskrit: यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम्।यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम्।।15.12।।
15-12.transliteration:
yad āditya-gataṁ tejo jagad bhāsayate ’khilam
yach chandramasi yach chāgnau tat tejo viddhi māmakam

translation.simple: The magnificent light of the sun that brightens the entire world, the soft glow of the moon, and the warming flame of fire – know that all this radiance and energy comes from Me, the Divine.
translation.deep: Reflect upon the universal source of all light and life. The Supreme Lord reveals Himself as the very energy that animates the sun, causing it to illuminate our vast world. He is the gentle effulgence of the moon and the sacred warmth in every fire. This verse invites us to perceive the Divine's omnipresence, seeing Him as the ultimate origin of all vibrant existence and light, guiding our consciousness towards His boundless glory.
translation.essence: All light and energy, be it from the sun, moon, or fire, flows from the Divine. Recognize God as the ultimate source of all illumination and life.

15-13.sanskrit: गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा।पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः।।15.13।।
15-13.transliteration:
gām āviśhya cha bhūtāni dhārayāmy aham ojasā
puṣhṇāmi chauṣhadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ

translation.simple: Lord Krishna lovingly reveals, 'I enter the earth and uphold all living beings with My powerful energy. Becoming the moon, full of life-giving essence, I nourish all plants and herbs.'
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that the Divine presence is not far away but intimately woven into the fabric of our world. The very ground beneath our feet, the life force within every creature, and the nourishment that brings growth to plants—all emanate from the Supreme Lord's boundless energy. He is the quiet, constant force sustaining all, like the moon's gentle light that nurtures life without demanding anything in return. It's a profound assurance of His omnipresent care.
translation.essence: The Lord's divine energy pervades and sustains all life on earth, from the smallest being to every growing plant, showcasing His constant and tender care for creation.

15-14.sanskrit: अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः।प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम्।।15.14।।
15-14.transliteration:
ahaṁ vaiśhvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṁ deham āśhritaḥ
prāṇāpāna-samāyuktaḥ pachāmy annaṁ chatur-vidham

translation.simple: I am the sacred warmth within every living being, dwelling in their bodies as the divine fire of digestion. With the help of the life-giving breaths, I gracefully transform all four kinds of food.
translation.deep: Within the temple of every living body, I, the Divine Self, manifest as Vaishvanara, the sacred digestive fire. It is My energy that lovingly processes all nourishment, working in harmony with the vital breaths of Prana and Apana. This reminds us that every act of sustenance is a divine gift, flowing from My constant presence within you, transforming and sustaining your very being.
translation.essence: The Lord is the inner fire, graciously digesting our food and sustaining all life with His divine presence, moment by moment.

15-15.sanskrit: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो    मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च।वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो    वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम्।।15.15।।
15-15.transliteration:
sarvasya chāhaṁ hṛidi sanniviṣhṭo
mattaḥ smṛitir jñānam apohanaṁ cha
vedaiśh cha sarvair aham eva vedyo
vedānta-kṛid veda-vid eva chāham

translation.simple: The Divine resides in the heart of every being. From Me come memory, understanding, and even the ability to forget. All the sacred Vedas, in their wisdom, seek to know Me alone. I am the very composer of Vedanta and the knower of all the Vedas.
translation.deep: Within the sanctuary of every heart, the Supreme Lord is eternally present. It is from Him that our faculties of memory and discernment arise, and also the divine grace that allows for the removal of ignorance and forgetfulness. All the revered Vedic scriptures, in their vastness, ultimately point towards realizing the Lord as the ultimate truth. He is not merely the subject of the deepest philosophical insights (Vedanta), but also their divine author and the perfect master of all sacred knowledge.
translation.essence: The Lord is the indwelling guide in every heart, the source of all memory and knowledge, and the ultimate truth revealed in every sacred word. He is the master and the essence of all wisdom.

15-16.sanskrit: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च।क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते।।15.16।।
15-16.transliteration:
dvāv imau puruṣhau loke kṣharaśh chākṣhara eva cha
kṣharaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭa-stho ’kṣhara uchyate

translation.simple: In this world, there are two kinds of beings: those that change and eventually perish, which includes all living creatures and their forms, and those that are constant and imperishable, known as the unchanging.
translation.deep: The Lord reveals that within creation, there are two fundamental aspects of existence. 'Kshara' refers to the ever-changing, perishable nature that encompasses all manifest beings—our bodies, minds, and all forms we perceive. 'Akshara' is the unchanging, unmoving essence, often called the 'Kutastha' or the 'steadfast,' which is the eternal foundation witnessing all transformations yet remaining untouched.
translation.essence: This verse lovingly teaches us that while all worldly experiences are temporary, there is an eternal, unchanging essence within and beyond them. This unwavering core is our true, divine nature, ever peaceful and constant, untouched by the flow of time.

15-17.sanskrit: उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः।यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः।।15.17।।
15-17.transliteration:
uttamaḥ puruṣhas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛitaḥ
yo loka-trayam āviśhya bibharty avyaya īśhvaraḥ

translation.simple: Beyond all, there is a most exalted Spirit, distinct and supreme, who is known as the Supreme Self. He is the imperishable Lord, who lovingly enters and sustains all three worlds.
translation.deep: This sacred verse reveals the profound truth of the Divine. Distinct from everything else, there exists the Supreme Spirit, referred to as Paramatma, the Highest Self. This imperishable Lord, with His eternal power, gracefully pervades and sustains all three realms of existence, holding the entire cosmos in His gentle, watchful care. He is the unwavering foundation of all that is.
translation.essence: The imperishable Supreme Lord, Paramatma, lovingly pervades and sustains all of creation with His divine presence.

15-18.sanskrit: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः।अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः।।15.18।।
15-18.transliteration:
yasmāt kṣharam atīto ’ham akṣharād api chottamaḥ
ato ’smi loke vede cha prathitaḥ puruṣhottamaḥ

translation.simple: Lord Krishna says, "I am beyond all that is fleeting and even superior to what is unchanging. Therefore, I am celebrated as the Supreme Person, Purushottama, in this world and in the sacred Vedas."
translation.deep: Lord Krishna tenderly reveals His true nature. He is distinct from and superior to all living beings caught in the cycle of change (the perishable). He is also greater than even the liberated souls and the unmanifest spirit (the imperishable). This unique position, being the highest and most complete truth, is why He is known everywhere and in all sacred texts as Purushottama, the Supreme and most beloved Person.
translation.essence: This verse celebrates the Lord as the ultimate reality, transcending all existence – both changing and unchanging. He is the Supreme Person, Purushottama, ever worthy of our devotion and understanding, the highest truth we can lovingly connect with.

15-19.sanskrit: यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम्।स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत।।15.19।।
15-19.transliteration:
yo mām evam asammūḍho jānāti puruṣhottamam
sa sarva-vid bhajati māṁ sarva-bhāvena bhārata

translation.simple: The one who, without illusion, understands Me as the Supreme Being, truly comprehends all there is to know. Such a wise soul then worships Me with their whole heart and being.
translation.deep: A soul who, released from all delusion, truly recognizes My nature as Purushottama, the Supreme Person, comes to possess all true knowledge. With this profound and clear understanding, they then offer their unwavering devotion to Me, O Bharat, with their entire being, in every aspect of their life.
translation.essence: To know Krishna as the Supreme, beyond all doubt, is true wisdom. This pure understanding inspires complete and loving devotion.

15-20.sanskrit: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ।एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत।।15.20।।
15-20.transliteration:
iti guhyatamaṁ śhāstram idam uktaṁ mayānagha
etad buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛita-kṛityaśh cha bhārata

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, I have now shared with you this most sacred wisdom. When you truly understand its message, you become wise and experience a deep sense of peace, having beautifully fulfilled life's purpose.
translation.deep: To you, O pure-hearted one, I have unveiled this most intimate and profound truth. When this spiritual knowledge takes root in your heart, your intellect blossoms with divine insight. You will then realize your ultimate goal, feeling deeply satisfied and free from all agitation, having achieved all that is truly meaningful in this existence.
translation.essence: This ultimate teaching, revealed by the Divine, brings supreme understanding. Embracing it leads to true wisdom and the profound satisfaction of a life fully accomplished in spirit.

16-1.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः।

दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम्।।16.1।।
16-1.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
abhayaṁ sattva-sanśhuddhir jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitiḥ
dānaṁ damaśh cha yajñaśh cha svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord spoke: Divine qualities begin with fearlessness and a pure heart. Being steady on the path of wisdom, offering charity, practicing self-control, performing sacred acts, studying holy scriptures, undertaking spiritual disciplines, and cultivating simplicity – these are gifts of a divine nature.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly describes the radiant qualities that gently lift the soul. He speaks of a deep inner fearlessness born of unwavering faith, a heart made pure by constant remembrance, and a mind steady on the path of divine wisdom. These are beautifully matched by acts of loving charity, inner mastery, sacred devotion, diligent study of holy words, earnest spiritual practices, and a simple, sincere approach to life. Each quality is a gentle whisper of the divine unfolding within us.
translation.essence: The Lord lovingly reveals the beautiful qualities that adorn a divine spirit: fearlessness, a pure heart, wisdom's steadfastness, generous giving, serene self-control, devoted service, studying sacred truths, gentle discipline, and simple sincerity. These are the tender blossoms on the path to inner peace and divine connection.

16-2.sanskrit: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम्।दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्।।16.2।।
16-2.transliteration:
ahinsā satyam akrodhas tyāgaḥ śhāntir apaiśhunam
dayā bhūteṣhv aloluptvaṁ mārdavaṁ hrīr achāpalam

translation.simple: Cultivate a heart free from harm, always speaking truth. Let go of anger and practice generous giving. Find inner peace and refrain from speaking ill of others. Offer your kindness to all beings, free from greedy desires. Be gentle, modest, and unwavering in your spiritual path.
translation.deep: This sacred verse illuminates the path of inner purity and strength. It guides us to embrace non-violence in every aspect of our being and to remain unwavering in truth. When we surrender anger and practice generous detachment, a deep sense of peace naturally blossoms within. We are encouraged to speak kindly, never spreading ill words, and to extend boundless compassion to all of God's creation. Cultivating a spirit free from craving, adorned with gentleness and humility, and standing firm in our spiritual resolve – these are the precious virtues that draw us closer to the Divine.
translation.essence: This verse beautifully distills the divine qualities that adorn a pure heart: non-harm, truthfulness, freedom from anger, selfless giving, inner peace, kindness to all, absence of greed, gentleness, humility, and unwavering resolve. These are the radiant virtues that lead us to profound spiritual growth and a deeper connection with the Divine.

16-3.sanskrit:
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता।

भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत।।16.3।।
16-3.transliteration:
tejaḥ kṣhamā dhṛitiḥ śhaucham adroho nāti-mānitā
bhavanti sampadaṁ daivīm abhijātasya bhārata

translation.simple: A radiant spirit, a forgiving heart, unwavering determination, pure intentions, freedom from ill-will, and gentle humility – these are the beautiful virtues that bloom in a soul destined for a divine journey, O Arjuna.
translation.deep: This verse describes the profound virtues that mark a soul evolving towards divinity. It speaks of 'Tejaḥ' as an inner glow and spiritual vigor, 'Kṣamā' as the gentle strength to forgive and endure, 'Dhṛtiḥ' as unshakeable resolve in one's spiritual journey, 'Śaucam' as purity in thought, word, and deed, 'Adroho' as the absence of any malice or enmity, and 'Nātimānitā' as the beautiful humility that comes from truly understanding one's place. When these qualities are nurtured, they indicate a divine predisposition, a heart aligned with higher grace.
translation.essence: Inner radiance, forgiveness, steady resolve, purity, kindness, and deep humility are the hallmark virtues of a soul walking the path of divine grace.

16-4.sanskrit: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च।अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम्।।16.4।।
16-4.transliteration:
dambho darpo ’bhimānaśh cha krodhaḥ pāruṣhyam eva cha
ajñānaṁ chābhijātasya pārtha sampadam āsurīm

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, qualities like pretense, excessive pride, ego, anger, harsh words, and a clouded understanding are seen in those who carry a nature that moves away from the divine.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to recognize the subtle signs within ourselves and others that pull us away from our spiritual path. It speaks of the heavy burdens of hypocrisy, the isolating shield of arrogance, the consuming fire of anger, the unkindness of harshness, and the fundamental blindness of ignorance. These are not just actions, but states of being that obscure the light of wisdom and true devotion, belonging to a nature that is not aligned with the divine harmony.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna lovingly points out that hypocrisy, arrogance, a strong ego, anger, harshness, and ignorance are the qualities of those with a nature that is not aligned with the divine. This gentle reminder helps us reflect and choose the path of humility and wisdom.

16-5.sanskrit: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता।मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव।।16.5।।
16-5.transliteration:
daivī sampad vimokṣhāya nibandhāyāsurī matā
mā śhuchaḥ sampadaṁ daivīm abhijāto ’si pāṇḍava

translation.simple: Divine qualities guide us towards freedom, while worldly ones can bind us. But do not worry, dear Arjuna, for you are born with a divine nature.
translation.deep: The virtues that resonate with the divine lead to true liberation, freeing the soul from earthly entanglements. In contrast, qualities rooted in ignorance and attachment only deepen the chains of worldly existence. Yet, take solace, beloved one, for your very essence is imbued with the divine nature, assuring your destined path towards ultimate freedom.
translation.essence: Divine virtues bring freedom; a lower nature brings bondage. But remember, your spirit is inherently divine, destined for liberation.

16-6.sanskrit: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च।दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे श्रृणु।।16.6।।
16-6.transliteration:
dvau bhūta-sargau loke ’smin daiva āsura eva cha
daivo vistaraśhaḥ prokta āsuraṁ pārtha me śhṛiṇu

translation.simple: In this world, dear Arjuna, there are two distinct types of natures or beings: those who walk the divine path and those who follow an ungodly way. The divine qualities have already been explained to you in detail. Now, please listen carefully from Me as I describe the ungodly nature.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna compassionately explains a fundamental aspect of human existence: the presence of two divergent streams of being within the world—the divine and the ungodly. This verse serves as an introduction to understanding the qualities that elevate a soul towards spiritual harmony and those that lead it away. The emphasis on hearing about the ungodly nature after the divine is to equip us with complete knowledge, enabling us to recognize both and consciously choose the path of virtue, aligning ourselves with the divine will.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna reveals two core human natures—divine and ungodly. Having detailed the virtues of the divine, He now prepares to describe the ungodly, guiding us to understand both paths for discerning and choosing our spiritual journey.

16-7.sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः।न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते।।16.7।।
16-7.transliteration:
pravṛittiṁ cha nivṛittiṁ cha janā na vidur āsurāḥ
na śhauchaṁ nāpi chāchāro na satyaṁ teṣhu vidyate

translation.simple: Those who are not guided by spiritual wisdom often miss the true path of what actions to embrace and what to let go of. Purity of heart, right behavior, and truth are not seen in their ways.
translation.deep: This verse gently reveals a truth about those who are distanced from divine understanding. They are unable to discern between actions that truly uplift the spirit and those that bind it. In such a state, the intrinsic spiritual qualities of inner and outer purity (shaucha), virtuous conduct (achara), and the sacred commitment to truth (satyam) remain unmanifested.
translation.essence: Without spiritual guidance, one loses sight of righteous action and pure living, missing the beauty of truth and good conduct.

16-8.transliteration:
asatyam apratiṣhṭhaṁ te jagad āhur anīśhvaram
aparaspara-sambhūtaṁ kim anyat kāma-haitukam

translation.simple: They proclaim this world as without true reality, lacking a firm foundation, and having no divine guiding hand. For them, it arises from mere desire, nothing more.
translation.deep: This verse illuminates a perspective where the entire universe is viewed as lacking ultimate truth and spiritual anchor. Those who hold this belief contend that the world is without divine order or a Supreme Controller, arising only from physical interactions, not a sacred design, and driven solely by base desires, devoid of any higher purpose.
translation.essence: The core of this teaching reveals a view that sees creation as untrue, without a divine basis, and devoid of a Creator, attributing all existence to mere desires rather than a purposeful, spiritual origin.

16-9.transliteration:
etāṁ dṛiṣhṭim avaṣhṭabhya naṣhṭātmāno ’lpa-buddhayaḥ
prabhavanty ugra-karmāṇaḥ kṣhayāya jagato ’hitāḥ

translation.simple: When individuals hold onto a distorted perspective, losing their connection to their true spiritual essence and having limited insight, they tend to perform harsh actions. Such deeds contribute to harm and destruction in the world.
translation.deep: This verse gently reveals the profound consequences of a worldview devoid of spiritual understanding. When one is disconnected from their divine essence and their intellect is shallow, their actions naturally lean towards severity and discord. Such individuals, though sometimes appearing powerful, ultimately become instruments of ruin, not just for the world but also for their own inner peace. It is a tender reminder that cultivating wisdom and a pure heart is essential for harmony, both within and without.
translation.essence: Embracing a deluded perspective, born of lost self-awareness and shallow wisdom, leads to harsh actions that sow discord and ultimately harm the world.

16-10.transliteration:
kāmam āśhritya duṣhpūraṁ dambha-māna-madānvitāḥ
mohād gṛihītvāsad-grāhān pravartante ’śhuchi-vratāḥ

translation.simple: With hearts yearning for endless desires that can never truly be filled, they become clouded by a sense of false pride and show. Deluded, they embrace impure thoughts and ways, leading them down a path far from inner peace.
translation.deep: When the heart is consumed by desires that are impossible to fulfill, a soul can become entangled in self-deception, pride, and arrogance. Lost in delusion, they adopt unrighteous beliefs and practices, moving away from purity and divine connection. This path, though seemingly active, leads to an unquiet spirit, far from the Lord's grace.
translation.essence: When the heart is caught in unending desires and false pride, it embraces impure thoughts and actions, drifting away from inner serenity and divine grace.

16-11.transliteration:
chintām aparimeyāṁ cha pralayāntām upāśhritāḥ
kāmopabhoga-paramā etāvad iti niśhchitāḥ

translation.simple: A heart caught in endless worries, constantly seeking joy only in worldly pleasures, often believes that this present life is the full extent of all there is.
translation.deep: This describes a perspective where anxieties seem boundless, lasting throughout one's entire life in this world. It points to a deep belief that fulfilling desires is the highest aim, without recognizing any spiritual truth beyond the immediate material experience. Such a path, though seemingly fulfilling, keeps one in a cycle of craving and unease, distant from lasting inner peace.
translation.essence: Let us gently remember that lasting peace is not found in endless worries or by making temporary pleasures our ultimate goal. True contentment arises when we look beyond the material, connecting with the eternal spiritual essence that truly defines us.

16-12.transliteration:
āśhā-pāśha-śhatair baddhāḥ kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ
īhante kāma-bhogārtham anyāyenārtha-sañchayān

translation.simple: Hearts caught in a hundred snares of worldly hopes, swayed by desires and anger, they gather wealth unjustly, simply to fulfill their cravings.
translation.deep: This verse reveals a state of being where the heart is tightly bound by an abundance of material hopes. Swayed by intense desires and the fire of anger, individuals in this state strive endlessly to amass fortunes, often through means that are not righteous. Their sole aim is to experience temporary sensory pleasures, unknowingly moving further from lasting peace and true spiritual joy. It's a gentle reminder to observe where our energies are directed.
translation.essence: The core message is a gentle reminder that when our hearts are tangled by excessive hopes, desires, and anger, we may pursue worldly gains unfairly, mistakenly thinking they will bring lasting joy, instead of seeking inner tranquility.

16-13.sanskrit: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम्।इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम्।।16.13।।
16-13.transliteration:
idam adya mayā labdham imaṁ prāpsye manoratham
idam astīdam api me bhaviṣhyati punar dhanam

translation.simple: The verse softly brings to light a heart constantly focused on gathering: 'Today, I have gained this much, and that wish, I shall soon attain. This is now mine, and still more riches will again be added to my store.' It gently invites us to observe this tendency within ourselves.
translation.deep: This profound verse tenderly illustrates a consciousness engrossed in worldly acquisitions and desires. 'Today, I have secured this, and that cherished aspiration, I shall surely achieve. This fortune now belongs to me, and even greater wealth will flow into my possession,' such is the thinking described. It gently guides us to ponder how such a relentless pursuit of external things can keep the spirit bound, subtly pointing towards the deeper, lasting fulfillment that comes from within.
translation.essence: At its core, this verse speaks of the endless human tendency to desire and accumulate, always feeling 'I have this, and I will obtain even more.' It serves as a gentle whisper, reminding us that true and abiding peace blossoms not from material endlessness, but from cultivating a serene heart.

16-14.sanskrit: असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि।ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी।।16.14।।
16-14.transliteration:
asau mayā hataḥ śhatrur haniṣhye chāparān api
īśhvaro ’ham ahaṁ bhogī siddho ’haṁ balavān sukhī

translation.simple: This verse portrays a mind consumed by its own importance. It speaks of thoughts like, 'I have overcome this obstacle, and I will conquer all others too. I am the master, the one who enjoys everything, the accomplished one, strong and truly content.' It highlights a deep sense of 'I' and 'mine' being at the center of all actions and experiences.
translation.deep: This passage gently reveals the nature of an ego-driven mind, lost in the illusion of its own power and control. Such a heart claims all successes and pleasures as its personal achievements, inadvertently forgetting the divine source that orchestrates all. It believes itself to be the sole doer, the ultimate enjoyer, and the independent source of its own happiness and strength, thus moving away from a humble connection with the Divine. It illustrates how deep attachment to the 'I' and 'mine' can obscure true spiritual understanding.
translation.essence: At its heart, this verse tenderly warns us against the pitfalls of an inflated ego, where we take all credit for our accomplishments and overlook the divine grace that underpins all strength and joy. It encourages us to cultivate humility, remembering that true power and lasting peace flow from surrender and recognizing the Supreme's loving hand in every aspect of our lives. It guides us to release the illusion of 'I am the doer' and embrace a path of gentle devotion.

16-15.sanskrit: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया।यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः।।16.15।।
16-15.transliteration:
āḍhyo ’bhijanavān asmi ko ’nyo ’sti sadṛiśho mayā
yakṣhye dāsyāmi modiṣhya ity ajñāna-vimohitāḥ
 aneka-chitta-vibhrāntā moha-jāla-samāvṛitāḥ
prasaktāḥ kāma-bhogeṣhu patanti narake ’śhuchau

translation.simple: I am wealthy, I am of noble birth. Who else can compare to me? I will perform grand offerings, I will give gifts, and I will delight in life. Such are the thoughts of those deluded by a lack of true wisdom.
translation.deep: This verse tenderly reveals how ignorance can cloud our hearts with self-importance. When we cling to our worldly status, wealth, or lineage, believing ourselves superior, we forget the divine source of all good fortune. Such thoughts lead us into actions driven by ego and a pursuit of fleeting joys, diverting us from the lasting peace found in selfless devotion and understanding our true, humble place in the cosmic dance. It's a gentle invitation to look beyond the transient and embrace the eternal.
translation.essence: Let us softly remember that true joy and lasting peace blossom not from worldly pride or possessions, but from a humble heart, ever connected to the loving Divine, free from the illusions of 'I' and 'mine'.

16-16.transliteration: aneka-citta-vibhrāntā    moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ prasaktāḥ   kāma-bhogeṣu    patanti narake  'śucau

translation.simple: When our minds are scattered by many thoughts and caught in delusion's net, clinging deeply to fleeting pleasures, we may find ourselves falling into a state of spiritual impurity and distress.
translation.deep: This sacred verse tenderly reveals how a heart scattered by endless worldly desires and enmeshed in the illusion of fleeting pleasures can lead us away from our true, pure self. It's a gentle call to examine our attachments and to aspire for inner clarity and a spirit unburdened by material cravings, thus avoiding states of distress.
translation.essence: A mind distracted by countless desires and caught in delusion, when attached to sense pleasures, leads one to states of inner impurity and sorrow.

16-17.transliteration:
ātma-sambhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhana-māna-madānvitāḥ
yajante nāma-yajñais te dambhenāvidhi-pūrvakam

translation.simple: Some individuals, full of self-importance, rigid in their ways, and driven by pride in their wealth and status, may perform acts of worship. Yet, these are often just outward displays, done with pretense and not with genuine faith or according to the true spirit of devotion.
translation.deep: This gentle teaching invites us to look within, reminding us that true devotion is not found in outward show or the pursuit of worldly praise. When our hearts are clouded by ego, arrogance, or the intoxication of wealth, our spiritual efforts can become hollow. The Divine is not moved by grand rituals performed without a sincere heart, but by pure intention and humble offerings. It is a call to purify our motives and engage in worship with genuine love and reverence.
translation.essence: Genuine devotion springs from a humble and sincere heart, not from proud displays or actions driven by ego and the desire for worldly recognition.

16-18.sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः।मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः।।16.18।।
16-18.transliteration:
ahankāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhaṁ cha sanśhritāḥ
mām ātma-para-deheṣhu pradviṣhanto ’bhyasūyakāḥ

translation.simple: Hearts that embrace ego, a sense of forceful power, pride, selfish desires, and anger, often come to resent the Divine presence, both within themselves and in others. Such souls are truly envious.
translation.deep: This sacred verse reveals that souls who shelter themselves in the darkness of ego, a misused sense of strength, overbearing pride, insatiable desires, and fierce anger, begin to harbor ill will towards the Divine. They fail to recognize My presence, not only within their own hearts but also within the very essence of all other beings. Such individuals, consumed by envy and malice, unknowingly distance themselves from the universal spirit, disrupting inner peace and harmony with the world.
translation.essence: When ego, pride, selfish desires, and anger take root, they lead the soul to harbor resentment and envy, obscuring the Divine presence within oneself and in others, thus disturbing true peace.

16-19.transliteration:
tān ahaṁ dviṣhataḥ krūrān sansāreṣhu narādhamān
kṣhipāmy ajasram aśhubhān āsurīṣhv eva yoniṣhu

translation.simple: Lord Krishna compassionately explains that souls who repeatedly choose paths of deep hatred and cruelty, living unrighteous lives, are continually guided by the divine hand through cycles of existence into challenging and unspiritual environments. This is a natural consequence, designed to help them eventually learn and grow.
translation.deep: The Supreme Lord, as the ultimate maintainer of the cosmic order, reveals the profound truth of cause and effect for those who embody deep malice and degradation. By their own choices, such individuals are perpetually drawn, through divine arrangement, into births and circumstances that reflect their unwholesome nature. This seemingly stern process is, in truth, an intricate part of His divine plan for their eventual purification and turning towards a more virtuous path.
translation.essence: This verse conveys the fundamental truth that the Lord, in His role as the cosmic orchestrator, ensures that souls deeply entrenched in hatred and cruelty repeatedly experience births and situations that align with these negative tendencies, a divine mechanism for their ultimate spiritual awakening.

16-20.sanskrit: असुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि।मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम्।।16.20।।
16-20.transliteration:
āsurīṁ yonim āpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani
mām aprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yānty adhamāṁ gatim

translation.simple: Those who are lost in delusion and choose ways that lead away from kindness find themselves born again and again in similar states. O son of Kunti, because they do not turn towards Me, they continue to drift further from divine peace.
translation.deep: Such deluded souls, embracing an ungodly nature that clouds their inner wisdom, cycle through births, O son of Kunti. Never truly coming to Me, their journey leads them deeper into shadowed realms, far from spiritual light and the ultimate liberation.
translation.essence: Souls absorbed in delusion and unkindness, failing to seek the Divine, repeatedly experience lives that lead them away from ultimate joy and union with the Lord, sinking into lower spiritual states.

16-21.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः।कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत्।।16.21।।
16-21.transliteration:
tri-vidhaṁ narakasyedaṁ dvāraṁ nāśhanam ātmanaḥ
kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṁ tyajet

translation.simple: The Bhagavad Gita reveals three doors that lead us away from our true, peaceful self: intense desire (lust), burning anger, and endless greed. To find lasting happiness and peace, we are lovingly guided to gently let go of these three.
translation.deep: The Lord kindly teaches us that unbridled desire, consuming anger, and insatiable greed act as formidable gates, leading to spiritual decline and obscuring the divine light within us. These are not just fleeting emotions but profound forces that can mar the purity of our soul. By consciously and with devotion releasing our attachment to these three, we protect our inner sanctuary, paving the way for profound peace and a clear connection to the Divine.
translation.essence: Lust, anger, and greed are the three destructive forces that pull us away from our soul's peace. Let us lovingly release them to safeguard our spiritual journey and inner calm.

16-22.sanskrit: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः।आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम्।।16.22।।
16-22.transliteration:
etair vimuktaḥ kaunteya tamo-dvārais tribhir naraḥ
ācharaty ātmanaḥ śhreyas tato yāti parāṁ gatim

translation.simple: O Arjuna, when a person lets go of these three pathways to darkness—desire, anger, and greed—they naturally choose actions that truly benefit their soul. This sincere effort then leads them to the most wonderful spiritual destination.
translation.deep: My dear Arjuna, a soul who thoughtfully detaches from these three powerful gates leading to spiritual obscurity—uncontrolled desire, burning anger, and grasping greed—begins to naturally align with their highest good. Such a one engages in deeds that elevate the spirit, gently guiding them towards the supreme, blissful state of ultimate liberation and divine realization.
translation.essence: To transcend desire, anger, and greed is to walk the path of true well-being, leading the soul to its supreme, divine home.

16-23.sanskrit: यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः।न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम्।।16.23।।
16-23.transliteration:
yaḥ śhāstra-vidhim utsṛijya vartate kāma-kārataḥ
na sa siddhim avāpnoti na sukhaṁ na parāṁ gatim

translation.simple: When we set aside the gentle guidance of sacred wisdom and act purely from our own desires, we may miss out on true fulfillment, deep contentment, and the most beautiful journey to the Divine.
translation.deep: The Lord gently reminds us that following our own impulses without the anchor of divine wisdom can lead us away from our true purpose. When we disregard the path shown in holy texts, which are meant to purify and elevate us, we close the door to genuine inner peace, spiritual achievement, and the ultimate union with the Divine Self. It's a call to trust in a higher intelligence beyond our fleeting desires.
translation.essence: To truly blossom and find our way to divine joy and our highest calling, we are encouraged to lovingly embrace sacred wisdom rather than being solely led by passing personal desires.

16-24.sanskrit: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ।ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि।।16.24।।
16-24.transliteration:
tasmāch chhāstraṁ pramāṇaṁ te kāryākārya-vyavasthitau
jñātvā śhāstra-vidhānoktaṁ karma kartum ihārhasi

translation.simple: Therefore, let the sacred teachings be your guide when you decide what is right to do and what is not. Understand what these scriptures advise, and then perform your actions in this world.
translation.deep: In your journey through life, dear one, when faced with choices of action, allow the timeless wisdom of the scriptures to illuminate your path. They serve as a pure and unwavering standard, helping you discern between that which uplifts and that which hinders. By understanding the divine guidance held within these sacred verses, you are empowered to act with clarity and purpose, aligning your deeds with the higher spiritual order, bringing peace and harmony to your heart.
translation.essence: Let the ancient wisdom of scripture be your gentle light, guiding every step and inspiring actions that bring divine harmony to your soul.

17-1.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः।तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः।।17.1।।
17-1.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
ye śhāstra-vidhim utsṛijya yajante śhraddhayānvitāḥ
teṣhāṁ niṣhṭhā tu kā kṛiṣhṇa sattvam āho rajas tamaḥ

translation.simple: Arjuna asked, 'My dear Krishna, some people worship with great faith, even if they don't follow all the scriptural rules. What kind of devotion is theirs? Is it goodness, passion, or ignorance?'
translation.deep: Arjuna, with a curious heart, asked Lord Krishna, 'There are those, O Krishna, who offer their worship with sincere faith, yet they may not meticulously adhere to all the prescribed rituals of the scriptures. What is the true nature of their dedication? Does it spring from the mode of goodness, the mode of passion, or the mode of ignorance?' This question delves into the subtle distinctions of devotion when actions deviate from prescribed paths, highlighting the importance of understanding the inner quality of spiritual practice.
translation.essence: Arjuna's question to Krishna seeks to understand the true nature of faith and worship when scriptural guidelines are not strictly followed. He asks whether such devotion, born of sincerity, aligns with goodness, passion, or ignorance, thereby setting the stage for a deeper exploration of the three modes of material nature in spiritual practice.

17-2.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचत्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा।सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां श्रृणु।।17.2।।
17-2.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
tri-vidhā bhavati śhraddhā dehināṁ sā svabhāva-jā
sāttvikī rājasī chaiva tāmasī cheti tāṁ śhṛiṇu

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord said: The faith of embodied beings, which naturally arises from their inner disposition, is threefold. It can be pure and noble, driven by passion, or steeped in darkness. Listen now, as I explain them to you.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna illuminates the profound nature of 'shraddha' or faith. He explains that faith is not a mere external act, but an intrinsic quality of every embodied soul, arising from one's 'svabhava'—their inherent nature, shaped by the Gunas. Thus, our devotion manifests differently: as serene, pure (sattvic) contemplation; as fervent, action-oriented (rajasic) pursuit; or as dim, deluded (tamasic) adherence. Recognizing these three types of faith is crucial for self-awareness and for consciously nurturing a higher, purer form of devotion on our spiritual path.
translation.essence: Our inherent faith, stemming from our nature, manifests in three forms: pure, passionate, or ignorant, shaping our spiritual inclination and path.

17-3.sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत।श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः।।17.3।।
17-3.transliteration:
sattvānurūpā sarvasya śhraddhā bhavati bhārata
śhraddhā-mayo ‘yaṁ puruṣho yo yach-chhraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ

translation.simple: Dear one, each person's faith is a mirror of their deepest inner nature. Whatever we truly believe in our hearts, that is what we become.
translation.deep: The Lord reveals that our faith, O Bharata, is not separate from us; it is born from our inner qualities and spiritual understanding. This conviction, whether it leans towards goodness, passion, or ignorance, profoundly shapes our thoughts, actions, and destiny. We are, in essence, a manifestation of what we hold sacred and true within our hearts, becoming an embodiment of that very faith.
translation.essence: Your faith reflects your deepest nature; what you believe, you become.

17-4.sanskrit: यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः।प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः।।17.4।।
17-4.transliteration:
yajante sāttvikā devān yakṣha-rakṣhānsi rājasāḥ
pretān bhūta-gaṇānśh chānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ

translation.simple: Hearts filled with goodness naturally offer devotion to the celestial beings. Those driven by passion worship powerful nature spirits and formidable beings. And those in ignorance direct their reverence towards ghosts and lower, restless spirits.
translation.deep: This verse tenderly unveils how the inner quality of our being (our Guna) guides the very object of our worship. A heart imbued with goodness (sattva) naturally seeks to connect with benevolent, higher divine beings, aspiring for wisdom and spiritual elevation. When passion (rajas) dominates, one might offer devotion to powerful, earthly spirits, perhaps seeking strength or worldly success. And when shrouded by ignorance (tamas), one might unfortunately turn to lower, restless entities, seeking quick, often dark, outcomes. It beautifully illustrates that the nature of our devotion reflects the very depth and direction of our soul.
translation.essence: The quality of our heart profoundly shapes the objects of our devotion.

17-5.sanskrit: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः।दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः।।17.5।।
17-5.transliteration:
aśhāstra-vihitaṁ ghoraṁ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ
dambhāhankāra-sanyuktāḥ kāma-rāga-balānvitāḥ

translation.simple: Some individuals undertake severe austerities that are not guided by sacred wisdom. They do so, filled with a sense of pride and self-importance, driven by their strong desires and attachments.
translation.deep: This verse gently points to the importance of intention and guidance in spiritual endeavors. When practices are performed without consulting timeless scriptures, and are instead motivated by an inflated ego, a desire for external show, or the compelling force of personal cravings and attachments, their true spiritual benefit is lost. Such actions, though outwardly austere, can become a burden rather than a genuine path to inner freedom.
translation.essence: True spiritual discipline flows from a pure heart, follows divine guidance, and is free from the grip of ego, showmanship, and worldly desires.

17-6.transliteration:
karṣhayantaḥ śharīra-sthaṁ bhūta-grāmam achetasaḥ
māṁ chaivāntaḥ śharīra-sthaṁ tān viddhy āsura-niśhchayān

translation.simple: Without proper understanding, some individuals inflict severe pain upon their own bodies and the elements that compose them. In doing doing so, they also trouble Me, who lives within their innermost self. Know that such actions stem from intentions that are not truly divine.
translation.deep: The Lord teaches us that our physical body is a sacred vessel, a composition of elements, and a dwelling place for the Supreme Self. To senselessly inflict torment upon this body, neglecting its well-being without true understanding or devotion, is to inadvertently trouble the very Lord who resides within. Such harsh and self-destructive acts, born of misguided conviction, indicate a spirit far removed from genuine spiritual realization and loving surrender.
translation.essence: Senselessly harming one's own body is akin to causing distress to the Divine Spirit dwelling within. True spiritual resolve honors the body as a sacred temple of God.

17-7.sanskrit: आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः।यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं श्रृणु।।17.7।।
17-7.transliteration:
āhāras tv api sarvasya tri-vidho bhavati priyaḥ
yajñas tapas tathā dānaṁ teṣhāṁ bhedam imaṁ śhṛiṇu

translation.simple: Lord Krishna tells us that the food we enjoy, and even our sacred acts of devotion, spiritual practice, and giving, all have three distinct qualities. He invites us to listen carefully to understand these differences.
translation.deep: This verse opens our eyes to a profound truth: even our most fundamental preferences and actions reveal the subtle energies (gunas) at play within us. By understanding how our food choices, our forms of worship, our austerities, and our charitable acts are influenced by Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas, we gain insight into our inner state. It's a gentle call to introspection, to observe how these qualities shape our spiritual journey and to aspire for expressions of devotion that are purer and more uplifting.
translation.essence: From our daily meals to our deepest acts of service, everything we do carries a unique quality. By understanding these threefold distinctions, we learn to purify our intentions and actions, moving closer to a state of calm devotion and true spiritual grace.

17-8.transliteration:
āyuḥ-sattva-balārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ
rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛidyā āhārāḥ sāttvika-priyāḥ

translation.simple: Pure-hearted souls cherish foods that foster long life, inner purity, strength, good health, happiness, and a sense of calm contentment. These foods are naturally pleasing, wholesome, nourishing, and comforting to the heart.
translation.deep: For those walking a path of goodness, sustenance is chosen not just for the body, but also for the spirit. The foods that nurture a tranquil mind and a strong, healthy form also expand our lifespan, purify our character, and deepen our joy. They are inherently sweet, wholesome, and substantial, bringing a deep satisfaction to the heart that aligns with a virtuous and peaceful disposition.
translation.essence: Foods dear to a pure spirit promote longevity, clarity, strength, health, happiness, and inner peace, being naturally delicious, nourishing, and comforting to the heart.

translation.simple: Foods that are very pungent, sour, overly salty, intensely hot, sharp, dry, or burning are favored by those whose minds are restless. However, these choices often bring forth feelings of sorrow, grief, and physical discomfort.
translation.deep: The Lord reveals how our food choices influence our inner being. Foods described as excessively pungent, sour, salty, intensely hot, sharp, dry, or inflammatory are dear to individuals governed by the mode of passion (Rajas). While they may offer a fleeting sensory pleasure, these dietary habits ultimately manifest as distress, lamentation, and various ailments, subtly disrupting our physical and mental harmony. This verse gently encourages us to observe how our diet shapes not just our physical health, but also our emotional landscape and spiritual equilibrium.
translation.essence: Foods that are overly intense in taste or character, though sometimes desired by a passionate nature, can bring discomfort to body and mind. True well-being comes from choosing nourishment that fosters peace and health.

17-10.sanskrit: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत्।उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम्।।17.10।।
17-10.transliteration:
yāta-yāmaṁ gata-rasaṁ pūti paryuṣhitaṁ cha yat
uchchhiṣhṭam api chāmedhyaṁ bhojanaṁ tāmasa-priyam

translation.simple: Food that is stale, tasteless, foul-smelling, old, or consists of leftovers and is impure – such food is dear to those whose minds are in the mode of ignorance.
translation.deep: This verse tenderly guides us to reflect on the deep connection between the food we eat and our inner state. When we partake of meals that are stale, lifeless, impure, or merely remnants, we invite the qualities of Tamas – dullness, inertia, and forgetfulness of the Divine – into our being. It is a gentle reminder to nourish our bodies with fresh, vibrant food, thereby fostering a clearer mind and a more receptive heart for spiritual awakening.
translation.essence: To cultivate a clear mind and a pure heart, one should avoid food that is stale, tasteless, or impure, as such nourishment strengthens the veils of ignorance within.

17-11.sanskrit: अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते।यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः।।17.11।।
17-11.transliteration:
aphalākāṅkṣhibhir yajño vidhi-driṣhṭo ya ijyate
yaṣhṭavyam eveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ

translation.simple: When a sacred act is lovingly performed, not wishing for any outcome, but simply because it is the righteous path shown by wisdom, with a calm mind fixed only on doing what's proper – that kind of action arises from a pure and tranquil spirit.
translation.deep: This verse reveals a profound truth about spiritual living: the purest acts are those undertaken without any personal agenda or expectation of reward. When we offer our efforts, our 'yajna,' not for the fruits they might yield, but solely because it aligns with our sacred duty and divine guidance, our hearts become serene. It's a call to elevate our actions, transforming them into selfless service, an offering made with a steadfast mind convinced of its inherent goodness, leading to inner liberation and connection with the divine.
translation.essence: True purity in action means performing sacred duty without desiring results, simply because it is right, with a mind firmly devoted to this truth.

17-12.sanskrit: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत्।इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम्।।17.12।।
17-12.transliteration:
abhisandhāya tu phalaṁ dambhārtham api chaiva yat
ijyate bharata-śhreṣhṭha taṁ yajñaṁ viddhi rājasam

translation.simple: O best among Bharatas, when a sacred act or offering is performed with an eye on its outcome, or simply for the sake of outward show and pride, know that such an offering arises from a restless, passionate nature.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna explains that any spiritual endeavor, when undertaken with a focus on its fruits or merely to be seen by others, originates from the quality of 'rajas.' This passionate mode of nature binds us through desire and attachment to outcomes. True spiritual growth blossoms not from such calculations or outward show, but from an offering of the heart that seeks no reward and expects no applause, dwelling in the quiet joy of giving.
translation.essence: Any sacred act performed with an eye on its fruits or for outward show is rooted in a restless, passionate nature. True devotion seeks no reward and demands no recognition.

17-13.transliteration:
vidhi-hīnam asṛiṣhṭānnaṁ mantra-hīnam adakṣhiṇam
śhraddhā-virahitaṁ yajñaṁ tāmasaṁ parichakṣhate

translation.simple: When a sacred offering or selfless service is performed without following the proper gentle guidance, without sharing the blessed food, without sincere prayers, without humble gifts, and completely without a trusting heart, such an act is known to belong to the mode of ignorance.
translation.deep: This sacred verse tenderly guides us to understand that the true spiritual essence of any offering or service is not just its outward performance, but the inner state of the heart. When a ritual or act of devotion is carried out without adhering to its time-honored principles, without the compassionate sharing of food, without the uplifting power of sacred chants, and without the gesture of humble offerings, it already lacks much. But above all, when it is performed entirely without sincere faith and devotion, such an act is deemed to arise from ignorance, failing to uplift the soul and connect with the divine grace it aims to invoke.
translation.essence: An offering performed without proper care, sharing, prayer, giving, and, most importantly, without sincere faith, is understood as an act born of ignorance, missing its profound spiritual purpose.

17-14.sanskrit: देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम्।ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते।।17.14।।
17-14.transliteration:
deva-dwija-guru-prājña- pūjanaṁ śhaucham ārjavam
brahmacharyam ahinsā cha śhārīraṁ tapa uchyate

translation.simple: Honoring the divine, our teachers, and wise souls; keeping our body and mind pure; being honest and direct in our ways; practicing self-control; and refraining from harm – these are the gentle spiritual practices that form the discipline of the body.
translation.deep: This verse reveals how our physical self can become an instrument for spiritual growth. By reverently honoring the divine, our gurus, and enlightened beings, we cultivate humility and gratitude. Inner and outer purity clears our being. Straightforwardness brings integrity to our actions. Self-restraint, or Brahmacharya, conserves our vital energy for higher purposes. And non-violence, Ahimsa, teaches us universal love and compassion. These are not mere rules, but pathways to transforming our physical existence into a sacred offering.
translation.essence: Our body itself can be a tool for devotion. By showing reverence, maintaining purity, acting with sincerity, practicing self-discipline, and embodying kindness, we perform true bodily austerity, making our physical form a source of spiritual strength and peace.

17-15.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्।स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते।।17.15।।
17-15.transliteration:
anudvega-karaṁ vākyaṁ satyaṁ priya-hitaṁ cha yat
svādhyāyābhyasanaṁ chaiva vāṅ-mayaṁ tapa uchyate

translation.simple: When our words are calm, truthful, kind, and helpful, and we regularly study sacred scriptures, this is known as the austerity of speech. It means using our voice to bring peace and truth, guided by devotion.
translation.deep: Our speech is a sacred gift, and this verse teaches us to use it with utmost care and devotion. Practicing the austerity of speech means consciously choosing words that emanate tranquility, uphold truth, and offer comfort and benefit to others. It's not just about the message, but the gentle, compassionate spirit behind it. Furthermore, regular engagement with holy texts, through recitation or study, purifies our vocal expression, making it a channel for divine energy and wisdom, drawing us closer to the sacred truth within.
translation.essence: The essence of pure speech lies in words that are peaceful, truthful, and kind, nourished by the study of sacred wisdom. It is an offering of harmony.

17-16.transliteration:
manaḥ-prasādaḥ saumyatvaṁ maunam ātma-vinigrahaḥ
bhāva-sanśhuddhir ity etat tapo mānasam uchyate

translation.simple: A serene and calm mind, a gentle and kind nature, thoughtful silence, control over our inner self, and purity in our feelings – these lovely qualities are spoken of as the spiritual discipline of the mind.
translation.deep: This verse lovingly guides us to understand that real spiritual practice extends deeply into our inner being. It teaches that cultivating a serene mind, expressing gentleness in all our interactions, embracing the wisdom of inner silence, diligently mastering our own senses and thoughts, and purifying our deepest intentions—these are the profound 'tapasya' that truly transform our consciousness. Such mental discipline draws us closer to the divine essence within.
translation.essence: A calm mind, gentle spirit, thoughtful silence, self-mastery, and pure intentions form the beautiful spiritual practice of the mind.

17-17.sanskrit: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्ित्रविधं नरैः।अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते।।17.17।।
17-17.transliteration:
śhraddhayā parayā taptaṁ tapas tat tri-vidhaṁ naraiḥ
aphalākāṅkṣhibhir yuktaiḥ sāttvikaṁ parichakṣhate

translation.simple: When spiritual practices are undertaken with deep faith, without any desire for personal reward, and with a focused, tranquil mind, such devotion is known as sattvic, representing purity and goodness.
translation.deep: This profound verse teaches us that engaging in any form of spiritual discipline, be it through action, word, or thought, when it springs from a place of supreme faith and is performed without attachment to its fruits, purifies the heart. It is the sincere offering, free from expectation, that elevates one to the mode of goodness, fostering inner peace and spiritual clarity.
translation.essence: Performing spiritual practices with unwavering faith, free from the desire for personal gain, is the purest form of devotion, bringing inner tranquility and goodness.

17-18.sanskrit: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत्।क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम्।।17.18।।
17-18.transliteration:
satkāra-māna-pūjārthaṁ tapo dambhena chaiva yat
kriyate tad iha proktaṁ rājasaṁ chalam adhruvam

translation.simple: When we engage in spiritual practices, like penance or self-discipline, simply to be seen, praised, or honored by others, it's said that this kind of effort comes from a restless energy. Such endeavors are unsteady and bring no lasting spiritual benefit.
translation.deep: This teaching lovingly guides us to look within, understanding that the sincerity of our heart truly defines our spiritual efforts. When penance or acts of self-control are undertaken primarily to garner applause, reverence, or admiration from others, and are tainted by a subtle sense of ostentation, they are termed 'rajasic' or born of passion. Such endeavors are inherently unstable and ephemeral. Their very nature is one of constant flux, for they seek validation in the changing tides of human opinion rather than in the steadfast devotion of the soul. Lasting peace and genuine spiritual progress emerge from humble, selfless intention, untouched by the craving for external accolades.
translation.essence: Spiritual practices, if done for outward praise or show, are driven by restless energy and yield no lasting peace. Purity of intention is the real offering.

17-19.sanskrit: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः।परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्।।17.19।।
17-19.transliteration:
mūḍha-grāheṇātmano yat pīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ
parasyotsādanārthaṁ vā tat tāmasam udāhṛitam

translation.simple: When spiritual practices, meant for growth, are carried out with stubborn delusion, causing unnecessary pain to one's own body, or with the intention to cause harm to others, such an austerity is considered to be rooted in ignorance.
translation.deep: This verse offers a profound insight into the very spirit of spiritual discipline. True austerity (tapasya) is a journey of purification, undertaken with wisdom and a pure heart. However, if one engages in such practices out of a stubborn, misguided belief, intentionally inflicting pain upon oneself, or worse, uses spiritual acts as a means to undermine or harm another being, then the sacred purpose is lost. Such actions, devoid of compassion and clarity, are declared to be born from the mode of ignorance, reminding us that genuine devotion always seeks upliftment, never detriment.
translation.essence: Austerity performed out of deluded stubbornness, self-inflicted pain, or the desire to harm others, is truly a practice born of ignorance.

17-20.sanskrit: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे।देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्।।17.20।।
17-20.transliteration:
dātavyam iti yad dānaṁ dīyate ‘nupakāriṇe
deśhe kāle cha pātre cha tad dānaṁ sāttvikaṁ smṛitam

translation.simple: When we offer a gift from the heart, simply because it feels right to give, without hoping for anything in return, and we choose a suitable place, time, and recipient, that act of giving is truly pure and divine.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully reveals the very essence of 'sattvic' giving – an offering made with a pure heart, free from the desire for any personal benefit or gratitude. It's an act of profound selflessness, where one gives simply out of a sacred duty, recognizing the divine connection in both the act and the recipient. When such an offering is made thoughtfully, considering the right time, place, and deserving person, it elevates the giver, the receiver, and the act itself to a spiritual plane, fostering inner peace and spiritual growth.
translation.essence: True giving flows from a heart of duty, offered without expectation, and thoughtfully directed to the deserving; such pure charity brings profound peace and spiritual merit.

17-21.sanskrit: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः।दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम्।।17.21।।
17-21.transliteration:
yat tu pratyupakārārthaṁ phalam uddiśhya vā punaḥ
dīyate cha parikliṣhṭaṁ tad dānaṁ rājasaṁ smṛitam

translation.simple: When a gift is given with the hope of receiving something back, or with a desire for future reward, or even with a heavy and reluctant heart, that kind of giving is understood to be influenced by the mode of passion.
translation.deep: Dearest one, true charity blossoms from a pure, selfless heart. If our giving is colored by the expectation of a return favor, a yearning for future benefits, or if it feels like a burden and is offered unwillingly, then such an offering is marked by the mode of passion. It reveals a spirit still caught in worldly calculations rather than resting in the serenity of unconditional generosity.
translation.essence: Giving driven by expectation, desire for reward, or a reluctant spirit is rooted in passion, diminishing its selfless purity.

17-22.transliteration:
adeśha-kāle yad dānam apātrebhyaśh cha dīyate
asat-kṛitam avajñātaṁ tat tāmasam udāhṛitam

translation.simple: If a gift is given without considering the right time or place, or to those who might not truly benefit, and if it's offered without genuine respect or with a feeling of disregard, then such an act of giving is understood to stem from a state of inner darkness or forgetfulness.
translation.deep: This verse invites us to reflect on the deeper spirit behind our acts of giving. It's not just the offering, but the heart and wisdom guiding it. When we give without considering the right context, or to those who may not genuinely receive its blessing, especially if it's done without respect or with a sense of indifference, it doesn't truly uplift. Such an act, arising from a state of tamas — a kind of spiritual inertia or forgetfulness — may not bring purity to the giver or true benefit to the recipient. It gently reminds us that conscious, respectful giving is key to spiritual growth.
translation.essence: The essence reminds us that acts of charity are most pure when offered with deep respect, wisdom, and a discerning heart. Giving without mindful consideration, or with a sense of disregard, stems from a deeper spiritual unawareness, rather than radiating true light and compassion.

17-23.sanskrit: तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः।ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा।।17.23।।
17-23.transliteration:
oṁ tat sad iti nirdeśho brahmaṇas tri-vidhaḥ smṛitaḥ
brāhmaṇās tena vedāśh cha yajñāśh cha vihitāḥ purā

translation.simple: The sacred words 'Tat' and 'Sat' are remembered as profound expressions of the Absolute Truth, hinting at its ultimate three-fold nature. From this divine origin, the spiritual seekers, the holy scriptures, and all pure acts of devotion were established in ancient times.
translation.deep: This verse reveals how 'Tat' and 'Sat' serve as profound and foundational designations of Brahman, the Ultimate Reality, whose essence is remembered as threefold. 'Tat' points to the transcendent, the 'That' beyond human comprehension, while 'Sat' signifies eternal existence, absolute truth, and intrinsic goodness. It is by the spiritual authority vested in these expressions that the ancient spiritual seekers, the timeless Vedas, and all sacred rituals and selfless offerings were ordained, anchoring all righteous actions in the divine source.
translation.essence: The divine words 'Tat' and 'Sat' reveal the Absolute Truth, the very foundation from which all spiritual wisdom, sacred knowledge, and pure devotional acts eternally flow, guiding our journey towards the Divine.

17-24.transliteration:
tasmād oṁ ity udāhṛitya yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ
pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṁ brahma-vādinām

translation.simple: Therefore, those who walk the path of ultimate truth always begin their acts of devotion, generosity, and self-discipline by gently uttering 'Om'. They do this to follow the sacred path laid out in the scriptures.
translation.deep: For this very reason, seekers who are immersed in the understanding of Brahman consistently dedicate their prescribed actions—be they ceremonial offerings, acts of giving, or practices of austerity—by first invoking the sacred syllable 'Om'.
