This holy sound, resonating with the very essence of the Supreme, sanctifies their efforts, ensuring that every deed is imbued with spiritual purity and divine intention, as guided by the ancient wisdom.
translation.essence: Chanting 'Om' before engaging in spiritual duties like sacrifice, charity, and austerity purifies these actions, connecting the seeker directly to the Divine.

17-25.sanskrit: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः।दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षि।।17.25।।
17-25.transliteration:
tad ity anabhisandhāya phalaṁ yajña-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ
dāna-kriyāśh cha vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣha-kāṅkṣhibhiḥ

translation.simple: When we perform sacred duties, acts of self-discipline, and charity, desiring only spiritual freedom and not any worldly reward, we connect with a higher purpose. These actions become pure offerings on our path to liberation.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to understand that truly spiritual acts are those performed with an inner understanding that they are for 'That' – the ultimate Reality, the Divine. Whether it's a ritual, a penance, or an act of giving, when done by seekers of liberation without any personal desire for the outcome, they transcend ordinary actions. They become sacred practices that purify the heart, detach us from the cycle of karma, and draw us closer to the supreme freedom of Moksha.
translation.essence: Perform all actions—sacrifice, penance, and giving—for the sake of liberation, understanding they are offerings to the Divine, free from attachment to their fruits.

17-26.sanskrit: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते।प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते।।17.26।।
17-26.transliteration:
sad-bhāve sādhu-bhāve cha sad ity etat prayujyate
praśhaste karmaṇi tathā sach-chhabdaḥ pārtha yujyate

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, the sacred word 'Sat' is used to describe what is real, true, and good. It is also used to refer to actions that are noble and commendable.
translation.deep: O Partha, the profound word 'Sat' signifies not only the fundamental existence and reality of everything, but also its inherent goodness and purity. When we refer to 'Sat', we are acknowledging that which is eternal, righteous, and beneficial. This blessed word is also employed to describe actions that are pure, commendable, and aligned with divine purpose, performed with a sincere and virtuous heart.
translation.essence: The word 'Sat' embodies truth, goodness, and the performance of noble deeds, guiding us towards a life aligned with divine reality.

17-27.sanskrit: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते।कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते।।17.27।।
17-27.transliteration:
yajñe tapasi dāne cha sthitiḥ sad iti chochyate
karma chaiva tad-arthīyaṁ sad ity evābhidhīyate

translation.simple: When we commit ourselves firmly to acts of devotion, self-purification, and selfless giving, that steadfastness is called 'Sat', which signifies goodness and divine reality. And any deed undertaken with the heart's intention for this 'Sat' is also truly 'Sat'.
translation.deep: Our unwavering commitment to spiritual offerings, disciplined self-control, and acts of benevolence is itself declared as 'Sat', the ultimate, eternal reality. Furthermore, any action performed with the conscious intention of aligning with this 'Sat' is also intrinsically 'Sat'.
translation.essence: Steadfastness in devotion, self-discipline, and giving, when performed with sincerity and aligned with the Supreme Truth, is known as 'Sat'. And any action entirely dedicated to this 'Sat' is also considered 'Sat'.

17-28.sanskrit: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत्।असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह।।17.28।।
17-28.transliteration:
aśhraddhayā hutaṁ dattaṁ tapas taptaṁ kṛitaṁ cha yat
asad ity uchyate pārtha na cha tat pretya no iha

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, any offering, charity, or spiritual endeavor performed without a sincere heart and true faith is considered 'asat' – it doesn't truly count. It brings no lasting benefit, neither in this world nor after passing on.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that the outer action alone isn't enough; the inner disposition of faith (śraddhā) is paramount. Without this bedrock of devotion and conviction, even seemingly pious acts—be it ritual offerings, generous giving, or rigorous penance—lack their spiritual essence. They fail to connect us with the divine and therefore bear no true, lasting fruit, either for our present well-being or our journey beyond this life. It underscores that the heart's intention elevates the deed.
translation.essence: The sincere heart, filled with faith, is what truly sanctifies our actions. Without this devotion, all our efforts—offerings, gifts, or penance—remain spiritually barren, yielding no true peace or lasting good, here or beyond.

18-1.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम्।

त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन।।18.1।।
18-1.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
sannyāsasya mahā-bāho tattvam ichchhāmi veditum
tyāgasya cha hṛiṣhīkeśha pṛithak keśhi-niṣhūdana

translation.simple: Arjuna spoke, 'O mighty-armed One, I yearn to truly understand the nature of 'sannyasa' – full renunciation. And O Lord of the senses, I also wish to know clearly the essence of 'tyaga' – the act of letting go.'
translation.deep: Arjuna, with a deep spiritual longing, turns to Lord Krishna, the Master of his senses, to unravel the profound meaning of 'sannyasa' – a life of complete renunciation – and 'tyaga' – the act of letting go, particularly of attachment to outcomes. He seeks to understand the true essence of each, distinctly, knowing that this wisdom is crucial for navigating his duties and truly finding peace on the spiritual path.
translation.essence: Arjuna, with a seeker's heart, asks Lord Krishna to reveal the true nature of renunciation (sannyasa) and selfless abandonment (tyaga), preparing the ground for profound teachings on ultimate spiritual liberation.

18-2.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः।

सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः।।18.2।।
18-2.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
kāmyānāṁ karmaṇāṁ nyāsaṁ sannyāsaṁ kavayo viduḥ
sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṁ prāhus tyāgaṁ vichakṣhaṇāḥ

translation.simple: The Blessed Lord explains that some wise souls understand true renunciation (sannyasa) as letting go of actions performed solely for personal desires. However, those with deeper insight declare that true sacrifice (tyaga) is the surrender of all attachment to the outcomes of any action.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna distinguishes between two paths of detachment. Sannyasa, as understood by some insightful beings, means abstaining from actions driven by selfish desires for their fruits. Yet, the truly discerning sages define Tyaga as the profound act of relinquishing attachment to the results of all actions, whether performed out of duty or natural inclination. This wisdom guides us towards a state where our efforts are offered without expectation, freeing the heart from the cycle of hope and disappointment.
translation.essence: The Lord teaches us the difference between merely giving up actions driven by desire and the deeper spiritual practice of surrendering the results of all actions. The latter, tyaga, is the path of true liberation and peace, cultivating a heart free from attachment to outcomes.

18-3.sanskrit:
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः।

यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे।।18.3।।
18-3.transliteration:
tyājyaṁ doṣha-vad ity eke karma prāhur manīṣhiṇaḥ
yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma na tyājyam iti chāpare

translation.simple: Some wise souls believe that all actions, by their very nature, carry imperfections and are best given up. Yet, other thoughtful souls say that actions like sacred offerings, selfless giving, and spiritual discipline should never be abandoned.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully illustrates the differing perspectives among spiritual seekers regarding action. Some enlightened beings, seeking ultimate liberation, advocate for a complete withdrawal from all worldly deeds, viewing them as inherently imperfect and binding. Yet, other profound masters emphasize the purifying and elevating power of virtuous actions—like performing sacred duties, engaging in selfless charity, and undertaking spiritual austerities. They teach that these specific acts are not to be renounced, but rather to be performed with a spirit of devotion, as they guide us closer to the Divine.
translation.essence: At its core, this verse reveals a profound spiritual question: Is freedom found in abandoning all action, or in thoughtfully performing actions that uplift and purify? It highlights that sacred duties like sacrifice, charity, and spiritual effort are seen by many as essential tools for growth, not burdens to be cast aside.

18-4.sanskrit: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम।त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः।।18.4।।
18-4.transliteration:
niśhchayaṁ śhṛiṇu me tatra tyāge bharata-sattama
tyāgo hi puruṣha-vyāghra tri-vidhaḥ samprakīrtitaḥ

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, please listen now to My clear teaching about renunciation. Indeed, this act of letting go is described as having three distinct forms.
translation.deep: Here, Krishna lovingly calls Arjuna to listen closely, promising a clear revelation about renunciation. He gently tells us that this profound act of letting go is not just one thing, but manifests in three distinct ways, guiding us towards deeper spiritual understanding.
translation.essence: The Lord lovingly invites us to understand the true, threefold nature of renunciation, a crucial path to inner peace and spiritual freedom.

18-5.sanskrit: यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत्।यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम्।।18.5।।
18-5.transliteration:
yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma na tyājyaṁ kāryam eva tat
yajño dānaṁ tapaśh chaiva pāvanāni manīṣhiṇām

translation.simple: Never abandon acts of selfless service, giving, and spiritual discipline; these are essential duties. For the wise, these practices of devotion, charity, and self-control are true purifiers of the soul.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna emphasizes that the sacred duties of selfless action (Yajna), generous giving (Dana), and inner discipline (Tapas) are not merely optional but are vital responsibilities. When performed with a thoughtful heart and sincere intention, these very acts gently cleanse the mind and purify the spirit of the discerning, leading them towards greater clarity and inner peace.
translation.essence: Selfless service, giving, and spiritual discipline are purifying duties for the wise, leading to inner clarity.

18-6.sanskrit: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च।कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्िचतं मतमुत्तमम्।।18.6।।
18-6.transliteration:
etāny api tu karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā phalāni cha
kartavyānīti me pārtha niśhchitaṁ matam uttamam

translation.simple: Beloved Arjuna, even pure acts like worship, giving, and self-discipline should be undertaken, but always letting go of any attachment to them or their results. This, My dear one, is My certain and most excellent teaching.
translation.deep: In this verse, Lord Krishna gently guides us toward true spiritual freedom. He teaches that even sacred duties like prayer, charity, and penance should be performed, but with a pure heart, free from attachment to their outcomes. This isn't about abandoning good deeds, but about transforming our attitude towards them. When we act without selfish desire for results, our actions become offerings, purifying the mind and drawing us closer to the divine. This is the profound wisdom that brings lasting peace and liberation.
translation.essence: Perform all your sacred duties with devotion, dear one, but always release attachment to their outcome and the act itself. This is Krishna's ultimate wisdom for true peace.

18-7.sanskrit: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते।मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः।।18.7।।
18-7.transliteration:
niyatasya tu sannyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate
mohāt tasya parityāgas tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ

translation.simple: Beloved soul, it is truly not proper to abandon the duties meant for you by divine arrangement. To give them up out of mere confusion or forgetfulness of their sacred purpose is said to be an act born of spiritual darkness.
translation.deep: This sacred verse gently guides us, reminding us that the duties inherently given to us by our nature and circumstances are not to be simply abandoned. True spiritual freedom does not come from escaping these responsibilities. When we give them up out of a confused state of mind or illusion, believing it to be true renunciation, it is declared to be an act rooted in the quality of 'tamas' – a state of inertia and darkness that obscures divine wisdom. Instead, we are encouraged to approach our duties with clarity, offering them to the Divine, rather than fleeing from them in bewilderment.
translation.essence: It is not fitting to abandon one's essential duties. To do so out of delusion is considered an act rooted in spiritual inertia. Fulfill your dharma with a serene and surrendered heart, not by fleeing from it.

18-8.sanskrit: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत्।स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत्।।18.8।।
18-8.transliteration:
duḥkham ity eva yat karma kāya-kleśha-bhayāt tyajet
sa kṛitvā rājasaṁ tyāgaṁ naiva tyāga-phalaṁ labhet

translation.simple: If one abandons a task simply because it feels difficult or causes a little bodily discomfort, thinking it's too much trouble, that kind of giving up is rooted in worldly passion. It won't bring the peaceful spiritual reward of true detachment.
translation.deep: When a person forsakes their prescribed duties purely because they perceive them as burdensome or fears physical hardship, their act is classified as 'Rajasic' renunciation. This mode of action, driven by personal comfort and aversion to struggle, does not yield the profound spiritual benefit or ultimate liberation that sincere, selfless detachment offers to the soul.
translation.essence: True spiritual detachment isn't about avoiding hardship. To abandon duties out of fear of discomfort is a worldly reaction, not a path to inner peace. Embrace your responsibilities with a calm and dedicated heart; for genuine spiritual reward blossoms from selfless action, not from seeking personal ease.

18-9.sanskrit: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन।सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः।।18.9।।
18-9.transliteration:
kāryam ity eva yat karma niyataṁ kriyate ‘rjuna
saṅgaṁ tyaktvā phalaṁ chaiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, when you carry out your prescribed duties, simply understanding them to be your responsibility, and you do this without being attached to the work itself or its results, that kind of selfless offering is considered pure renunciation.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us towards a profound inner freedom. It teaches that true renunciation isn't about forsaking our duties, but rather about refining our consciousness. When we act solely out of a sense of rightness, unburdened by hopes for reward or fear of failure, we align ourselves with a higher purpose. This 'sattvic' abandonment of attachment and outcomes purifies the heart, transforming our work into an act of devotion and bringing deep tranquility.
translation.essence: Perform your sacred duties, O Arjuna, simply because they are right. Let go of attachment to both the action and its outcomes. This is the path of pure renunciation, leading to inner peace.

18-10.sanskrit: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते।त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः।।18.10।।
18-10.transliteration:
na dveṣhṭy akuśhalaṁ karma kuśhale nānuṣhajjate
tyāgī sattva-samāviṣhṭo medhāvī chhinna-sanśhayaḥ

translation.simple: A soul truly dedicated to renunciation, filled with purity, neither dislikes a challenging task nor becomes attached to a pleasant outcome. Such a wise one is completely free from all confusion.
translation.deep: One who understands the essence of renunciation, dwelling in the inner clarity of Sattva, finds true equanimity. They do not recoil from duties that may seem unappealing, nor do they become ensnared by the allure of successful endeavors. This steady state, born of profound wisdom, dissolves all uncertainties, revealing a mind that is clear and unwavering.
translation.essence: The pure-hearted renunciate, wise and steadfast, transcends both dislike and attachment, living in doubt-free clarity and inner peace.

18-11.sanskrit: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः।यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते।।18.11।।
18-11.transliteration:
na hi deha-bhṛitā śhakyaṁ tyaktuṁ karmāṇy aśheṣhataḥ
yas tu karma-phala-tyāgī sa tyāgīty abhidhīyate

translation.simple: It is truly impossible for any embodied being to completely stop all actions. We are always engaged in some deed or another. But a real renunciant is one who lets go of the desire for the results of their actions.
translation.deep: For those dwelling in a physical body, dear one, it is indeed impossible to cease all actions entirely. Our very nature in this material realm compels us to engage. However, the true spirit of renunciation doesn't lie in abandoning our duties, but in lovingly releasing our attachment to their outcomes. One who acts with diligence, offering the fruits of their labor without craving personal reward or fearing loss, is truly celebrated as a renunciant, a soul liberated from the grip of binding desires.
translation.essence: Action is an inherent part of life's journey. True inner freedom and renunciation blossom when you release attachment to the fruits of your efforts, offering them with a calm and surrendered heart.

18-12.sanskrit: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम्।भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित्।।18.12।।
18-12.transliteration:
aniṣhṭam iṣhṭaṁ miśhraṁ cha tri-vidhaṁ karmaṇaḥ phalam
bhavaty atyāgināṁ pretya na tu sannyāsināṁ kvachit

translation.simple: My dear one, for souls who cling to the desire for rewards from their actions, the future brings forth a variety of results – sometimes pleasant, sometimes unpleasant, and sometimes a mix. But for the pure heart that has truly let go of all attachment to these fruits, such outcomes simply never arise.
translation.deep: The Lord teaches that for those who perform actions with an eager expectation of their outcomes, the karmic reactions manifest in the future in a threefold way: as happiness, as sorrow, or as a combination of both. This cycle of receiving varied fruits continues for the attached soul. Yet, for the blessed renunciant who has truly surrendered all personal desire for these fruits, offering every action as a loving service to the Divine, these binding results simply do not manifest. Such a soul lives in profound freedom and unshakeable peace, untouched by the dualities of worldly outcomes.
translation.essence: A gentle reminder that desiring the fruits of our actions binds us to future experiences – good, bad, or mixed. But when we offer our efforts with loving devotion, without longing for a specific outcome, we are freed from all such karmic bonds, finding profound peace in the Lord.

18-13.sanskrit: पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे।सांख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम्।।18.13।।
18-13.transliteration:
pañchaitāni mahā-bāho kāraṇāni nibodha me
sānkhye kṛitānte proktāni siddhaye sarva-karmaṇām

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, please listen carefully. I will now tell you about five important factors. These are taught in ancient wisdom and are the very foundation for all the actions we perform and how they come to be.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna invites Arjuna to look deeper into the nature of action itself. He explains that ancient wisdom, particularly the Sāṅkhya tradition, reveals that every single deed, no matter how small or great, is influenced by five fundamental causes. Understanding these factors helps us to transcend the illusion of being the sole doer, allowing us to perform our duties with greater wisdom and peace, recognizing the interplay of divine principles in all outcomes.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna reveals five fundamental elements that shape all actions, a timeless wisdom helping us understand and calmly engage with life's endeavors.

18-14.sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम्।विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम्।।18.14।।
18-14.transliteration:
adhiṣhṭhānaṁ tathā kartā karaṇaṁ cha pṛithag-vidham
vividhāśh cha pṛithak cheṣhṭā daivaṁ chaivātra pañchamam

translation.simple: Every action we perform involves five key aspects. There's the body, which is the base, then the individual who feels like the doer. We also use various instruments like our mind and senses. Different kinds of efforts are put forth. And finally, there's a fifth, divine factor, an unseen hand of destiny or providence.
translation.deep: When we examine any deed, Lord Krishna reveals its five components. First is the 'adhiṣṭhānam,' our physical body, the foundation upon which all activity rests. Then comes the 'kartā,' the perceived doer, the 'I' that identifies with the action. Next are the 'karaṇas,' the distinct instruments—our senses, mind, and intellect—through which we interact with the world. Fourth are the 'ceṣṭās,' the diverse exertions and movements we make. And profoundly, the fifth element is 'daivaṁ,' the divine influence or cosmic will, which guides and permits all outcomes. This reminds us that even with our best efforts, a higher power orchestrates the ultimate unfolding of events, fostering humility and trust.
translation.essence: Ultimately, every endeavor, great or small, unfolds not solely by our personal will, but through the harmonious interplay of our body, mind, instruments, effort, and crucially, the gentle grace of the Divine. This understanding brings peace, knowing a greater design is at work.

18-15.sanskrit: शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः।न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः।।18.15।।
18-15.transliteration:
śharīra-vāṅ-manobhir yat karma prārabhate naraḥ
nyāyyaṁ vā viparītaṁ vā pañchaite tasya hetavaḥ

translation.simple: Whatever a person does—with their body, through their words, or in their thoughts—be it righteous or otherwise, these five factors are always the reasons behind it.
translation.deep: The Bhagavad Gita tenderly explains that every single action we initiate, be it with our physical body, through our spoken words, or within the quiet sanctuary of our mind—whether it aligns with righteousness or deviates from it—is always influenced by five fundamental causes. This teaching offers profound insight, inviting us to reflect on the deeper springs of our deeds and choices.
translation.essence: Every action, stemming from body, speech, or mind, whether just or unjust, is ultimately born from five specific underlying causes.

18-16.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः।पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः।।18.16।।
18-16.transliteration:
tatraivaṁ sati kartāram ātmānaṁ kevalaṁ tu yaḥ
paśhyaty akṛita-buddhitvān na sa paśhyati durmatiḥ

translation.simple: When a mind, not yet clear in its spiritual understanding, believes 'I alone am the one who does everything,' such a person truly misses the deeper truth. This limited view prevents them from seeing how many elements contribute to every action.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to reflect on our perception of action. If, due to an undeveloped intellect, we hold the belief that we are the sole originators and performers of all deeds, we are missing a profound spiritual reality. True understanding reveals that every action is a complex interplay of various factors—the body, the instruments of perception, the efforts made, and a guiding divine influence. To remain absorbed in the ego's claim of singular doership is to overlook this divine orchestration, preventing the soul from experiencing true humility and interconnectedness.
translation.essence: Humility blooms when we understand that our individual 'self' is not the sole doer. Real insight comes from recognizing the many elements, including the divine, that truly bring actions to fruition.

18-17.sanskrit: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते।हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते।।18.17।।
18-17.transliteration:
yasya nāhankṛito bhāvo buddhir yasya na lipyate
hatvā ‘pi sa imāl lokān na hanti na nibadhyate

translation.simple: A peaceful soul, who doesn't claim 'I am the doer' and whose heart remains pure and unattached to outcomes, is truly free. Even when engaged in the world's most intense actions, such a soul neither truly acts nor is bound by them.
translation.deep: This verse reveals a profound truth about spiritual freedom. When the heart has no trace of 'I am the doer,' and the intellect remains pure, untouched by the world's allurements or outcomes, one transcends all karmic ties. Even when performing actions that seem immense or challenging, such a soul is not truly acting in an ego-driven way, and thus remains untouched by any binding consequences. This is the path of inner liberation, where true peace resides regardless of external circumstances.
translation.essence: Serve with a heart free from 'I' and 'mine,' and an intellect untainted by outcome. In this surrender, actions no longer bind, and the soul finds eternal peace.

18-18.sanskrit: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना।करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः।।18.18।।
18-18.transliteration:
jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ parijñātā tri-vidhā karma-chodanā
karaṇaṁ karma karteti tri-vidhaḥ karma-saṅgrahaḥ

translation.simple: Before any action begins, there is the knowledge of what to do, the goal we wish to achieve, and us, the ones who know and plan. These three factors inspire us to act. Once the action is underway, there is the doer, the instrument used, and the action itself. These three form the very basis of all activity.
translation.deep: This sacred verse illuminates the subtle origins of all human endeavor. It teaches that the impulse to act, the very spark of motivation, is always three-fold: it stems from the knowledge we possess, the object of that knowledge we desire to achieve, and our very self as the knower. These three elements initiate every deed. Furthermore, when an action is brought into manifestation, its full expression is also three-fold: it involves the doer, the instrument through which the action is performed, and the action itself. Contemplating these six aspects helps us to understand the profound interconnectedness of thought and deed, inviting us to act with greater mindfulness and devotion.
translation.essence: Every action unfolds in two divine triplets: it begins with the knower, knowledge, and the known inspiring the deed; and it concludes with the doer, the instrument, and the action manifesting it.

18-19.sanskrit: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः।प्रोच्यते गुणसंख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि।।18.19।।
18-19.transliteration:
jñānaṁ karma cha kartā cha tridhaiva guṇa-bhedataḥ
prochyate guṇa-saṅkhyāne yathāvach chhṛiṇu tāny api

translation.simple: Lord Krishna explains that our way of knowing, our actions, and even our sense of being the one who acts, all come in three distinct forms. These forms are shaped by the subtle qualities of nature, known as the Gunas. He gently encourages us to listen and understand these differences accurately.
translation.deep: This profound verse reveals how the very fabric of our being – our intellect, our endeavors, and our identity as the doer – is influenced by the three Gunas: Sattva (goodness), Rajas (passion), and Tamas (ignorance). By recognizing these inherent distinctions, we are invited to cultivate a deeper awareness of ourselves and the world around us. This understanding is a guiding light, helping us to discern which qualities are at play within us, allowing us to align our thoughts and actions with greater peace, clarity, and spiritual growth.
translation.essence: Our knowledge, actions, and sense of self are all uniquely colored by the Gunas. Understanding this distinction brings greater insight and helps us move towards inner harmony.

18-20.sanskrit: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते।अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम्।।18.20।।
18-20.transliteration:
sarva-bhūteṣhu yenaikaṁ bhāvam avyayam īkṣhate
avibhaktaṁ vibhakteṣhu taj jñānaṁ viddhi sāttvikam

translation.simple: When we gaze upon all creation and perceive the singular, everlasting spirit dwelling within each, undisturbed by their outward forms, know this vision to be true and pure.
translation.deep: This profound knowledge reveals that beyond the diverse appearances of bodies and forms, there is a fundamental unity – an eternal, unbroken spiritual essence that animates all. It's the realization that the divine spark is equally present in every being, connecting us all in a timeless embrace. This insightful vision, which sees oneness amidst multiplicity, is characterized by clarity, peace, and spiritual illumination, truly reflecting the sattvic quality.
translation.essence: To see the same eternal spirit in every heart, despite all distinctions, is the essence of pure wisdom.

18-21.sanskrit: पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान्।वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम्।।18.21।।
18-21.transliteration:
pṛithaktvena tu yaj jñānaṁ nānā-bhāvān pṛithag-vidhān
vetti sarveṣhu bhūteṣhu taj jñānaṁ viddhi rājasam

translation.simple: When our understanding sees only separate forms and distinct qualities in every being, recognizing them as fundamentally different from each other, know that such knowledge is born of a restless, active mind. It's when we focus on the many rather than the one.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to reflect on the nature of our perception. If our awareness is fixed on the myriad distinctions and unique attributes of each individual and every part of creation, seeing them as utterly separate entities, then this kind of knowledge is said to be Rajasic. While it helps us categorize and function in the world, it keeps us engaged in the realm of duality, preventing us from experiencing the unifying presence that binds all beings together. It reflects a mind that is vibrant and active, yet perhaps not fully settled in the truth of interconnectedness.
translation.essence: To perceive only distinctions and differences among all beings, without sensing the common thread of spirit, is knowledge colored by the dynamic, often turbulent, nature of the material world. True insight seeks unity beyond varied forms.

18-22.transliteration:
yat tu kṛitsna-vad ekasmin kārye saktam ahaitukam
atattvārtha-vad alpaṁ cha tat tāmasam udāhṛitam

translation.simple: Knowledge that is obsessed with a single, small thing as if it were the whole truth, without any reason or real depth, is said to be in the mode of darkness.
translation.deep: When our vision becomes so narrow that we cling to a trivial fragment of life as if it were the ultimate reality, we lose our connection to the Divine whole. This type of understanding is irrational and lacks a foundation in truth. It traps the soul in a small, distorted perspective, preventing us from seeing the vastness of God's creation.
translation.essence: True wisdom is expansive and logical; clinging blindly to a narrow, groundless viewpoint is a sign of spiritual ignorance.

18-23.transliteration:
niyataṁ saṅga-rahitam arāga-dveṣhataḥ kṛitam
aphala-prepsunā karma yat tat sāttvikam uchyate

translation.simple: When an action is performed as a pure duty, without any attachment to it, free from strong likes or dislikes, and without hoping for a specific outcome, such an action is truly called 'sattvic' – pure and righteous.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse encourages a profound way of living. It speaks of performing our actions not just as tasks, but as offerings, done out of a sense of pure duty. When we act without attachment to the activity itself, free from the strong pull of desire or the push of aversion, and without anxiously anticipating the results, our work transforms. Such selfless action purifies our heart, aligns us with a higher purpose, and brings an inner calm that truly reflects the sattvic mode of being.
translation.essence: To act purely is to fulfill one's duty with detachment, free from personal cravings or dislikes, and without desire for the outcome.

18-24.sanskrit: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः।क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम्।।18.24।।
18-24.transliteration:
yat tu kāmepsunā karma sāhankāreṇa vā punaḥ
kriyate bahulāyāsaṁ tad rājasam udāhṛitam

translation.simple: When we act with a strong desire for the results, or with a sense of 'I am the one doing this,' and we put in a lot of straining effort, such actions are understood to be moved by a restless, passionate energy.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to recognize actions born from a yearning for personal reward or an egoistic feeling of 'I am the sole doer.' When such actions are performed with great, often anxious, exertion, they are considered to be rajasic. It's a call to observe how our desires and self-importance can infuse our deeds, potentially disturbing our inner tranquility rather than fostering surrender.
translation.essence: Actions stemming from personal desire, ego, and intense struggle are of the mode of passion, often clouding our path to peace.

18-25.sanskrit: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम्।मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते।।18.25।।
18-25.transliteration:
anubandhaṁ kṣhayaṁ hinsām anapekṣhya cha pauruṣham
mohād ārabhyate karma yat tat tāmasam uchyate

translation.simple: My dear one, when an action is begun from a place of confusion, without considering the troubles it might bring, the losses it might cause, or the harm it might create, then such an action is known as one arising from ignorance.
translation.deep: Beloved soul, when the intellect is obscured by deep delusion, and an action is commenced without a moment's reflection on its potential for future suffering, the ruin it could bring, or the injury it might inflict, and without considering one's true capacity or righteous duty, then such an endeavor is declared to be rooted in Tamas. This signifies a state where spiritual wisdom is dimmed, leading to choices that deepen the bonds of illusion rather than liberating the spirit.
translation.essence: An action initiated through delusion, without reflecting on its potential for harm, loss, or negative consequences, is understood to be Tamasic.

18-26.transliteration:
mukta-saṅgo ‘nahaṁ-vādī dhṛity-utsāha-samanvitaḥ
siddhy-asiddhyor nirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika uchyate

translation.simple: A gentle soul, free from worldly ties and humble, who works with steady zeal. When efforts bear fruit or don't, they remain untouched, holding a peaceful heart. This is a doer touched by goodness.
translation.deep: A truly spiritual being, free from the entanglements of desire, never claims personal glory for their deeds. With unwavering resolve and inner joy, they carry out their duties. Whether the outcome is favorable or not, their heart remains undisturbed, knowing that all is part of a greater divine flow. Such a one, the Gita says, acts in pure goodness.
translation.essence: A doer acts in pure goodness when free from attachment, humble, persistently joyful, and untouched by the swings of success or failure.

18-27.sanskrit: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः।हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः।।18.27।।
18-27.transliteration:
rāgī karma-phala-prepsur lubdho hinsātmako ‘śhuchiḥ
harṣha-śhokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ

translation.simple: A person who works only for rewards, is driven by strong desires and greed, and is easily swayed by joy or sorrow, is said to be acting in the mode of passion.
translation.deep: When our actions are fueled by a craving for results, we become restless and lose our inner purity. This 'Rajasic' way of living makes us slaves to our emotions—feeling elated in success and devastated in failure. Such a path is often marked by greed and a lack of consideration for others, as the ego is solely focused on personal gain.
translation.essence: True peace is impossible when our motivation is rooted in greed and an obsession with outcomes.

18-28.sanskrit: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः।विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते।।18.28।।
18-28.transliteration:
ayuktaḥ prākṛitaḥ stabdhaḥ śhaṭho naiṣhkṛitiko ‘lasaḥ
viṣhādī dīrgha-sūtrī cha kartā tāmasa uchyate

translation.simple: A person who is undisciplined, stubborn, dishonest, and lazy—someone who is often gloomy and habitually delays their work—is described as a worker in the mode of darkness.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna explains the characteristics of a 'Tamasa' doer, whose actions are clouded by ignorance. Such an individual lacks refinement and spiritual connection, often remaining stuck in stubborn pride or deceit. Instead of acting with clarity, they are weighed down by a heavy heart and the habit of procrastination, preventing any real growth or peace.
translation.essence: To walk the path of light, we must recognize and let go of the heaviness of laziness, dishonesty, and constant delay. True devotion thrives in a heart that is active, sincere, and free from the shadows of gloom.

18-29.sanskrit: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं श्रृणु।प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय।।18.29।।
18-29.transliteration:
buddher bhedaṁ dhṛiteśh chaiva guṇatas tri-vidhaṁ śhṛiṇu
prochyamānam aśheṣheṇa pṛithaktvena dhanañjaya

translation.simple: Listen carefully, dear Arjuna. I will now explain to you, fully and distinctly, the three kinds of intellect and the three kinds of inner resolve, each determined by their natural qualities.
translation.deep: In this verse, Lord Krishna gently invites us to deeply consider the subtle workings of our inner self. He promises to reveal how our understanding and our determination are influenced and colored by the three qualities of nature (Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas). This wisdom helps us discern the origins of our thoughts and actions, guiding us toward greater clarity and spiritual growth.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna prepares to fully explain the three distinct types of intellect and resolve, classified according to the three qualities of nature.

18-30.sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये।बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी।।18.30।।
18-30.transliteration:
pravṛittiṁ cha nivṛittiṁ cha kāryākārye bhayābhaye
bandhaṁ mokṣhaṁ cha yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī

translation.simple: O Arjuna, the understanding that clearly discerns what truly moves us forward and what gently calls us to withdraw; what is right to do and what is best to avoid; what causes fear and what grants fearlessness; what binds us and what sets us truly free – such an intellect, dear Partha, is serene and pure, rooted in goodness.
translation.deep: This verse beautifully describes a profound inner wisdom, Arjuna, an understanding that radiates from a tranquil and pure heart. It's the subtle ability to see through life's complexities, discerning which paths truly serve our spiritual growth and which merely create entanglement. This clear intellect helps us lovingly distinguish actions that lead to lasting peace from those that foster anxiety, and ultimately, it illuminates the sacred way to inner freedom from all temporary bonds. Such spiritual discernment, born of goodness, is a gentle guide on our journey.
translation.essence: A pure and tranquil intellect, dear Arjuna, clearly sees what leads to true freedom and what to entanglement, guiding us with wisdom.

18-31.sanskrit: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च।अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी।।18.31।।
18-31.transliteration:
yayā dharmam adharmaṁ cha kāryaṁ chākāryam eva cha
ayathāvat prajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī

translation.simple: O Arjuna, an intellect that struggles to see the clear path between right and wrong, or to truly know what action to take and what to avoid, is an understanding touched by the restless quality of passion.
translation.deep: A deeper contemplation reveals that an intellect swayed by Rajas (passion) often misinterprets the subtle nuances of Dharma and Adharma. It may act based on selfish desires, fear, or a yearning for worldly rewards, rather than from a place of pure understanding. This leads to confusion about one's true responsibilities and a distorted view of what truly serves the divine purpose. Such an intellect, though active, lacks the serene clarity needed for spiritual progress, often leading to actions that bind rather than liberate.
translation.essence: The heart of this teaching reminds us that when our understanding is clouded by passion, discerning the right path becomes challenging. May we pray for an intellect free from agitation, so we may clearly see divine will in every action.

18-32.sanskrit: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसाऽऽवृता।सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी।।18.32।।
18-32.transliteration:
adharmaṁ dharmam iti yā manyate tamasāvṛitā
sarvārthān viparītānśh cha buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī

translation.simple: O Arjuna, an intellect that is veiled by the darkness of ignorance often mistakes what is unrighteous for what is right. It perceives all things in a distorted and contrary way. Such an understanding, dear Partha, is known to be of the mode of Tamas.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to recognize a state of mind where spiritual discernment is lost. When the intellect is enveloped by Tamas, or deep ignorance, it perceives darkness as light and untruth as truth. This isn't just a simple mistake; it's a profound twisting of reality, where noble intentions become misguided and the true purpose of life's experiences is completely misunderstood. Such an intellect, unable to see clearly, leads one astray from inner harmony and the path of divine wisdom.
translation.essence: At its heart, this verse reminds us that true wisdom begins with recognizing when our understanding is clouded. Let us pray for the light of divine knowledge to dispel the darkness of ignorance, so we may clearly discern the path of righteousness and embrace a vision aligned with truth and inner peace.

18-33.sanskrit: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः।योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी।।18.33।।
18-33.transliteration:
dhṛityā yayā dhārayate manaḥ-prāṇendriya-kriyāḥ
yogenāvyabhichāriṇyā dhṛitiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī

translation.simple: O Arjuna, the inner strength that steadily holds your mind, life-breath, and senses, keeping them focused and unwavering through spiritual practice, that steadfastness comes from goodness.
translation.deep: True fortitude, dear Arjuna, is a profound inner resolve. It's the spiritual power that gently but firmly guides your thoughts, breath, and senses, preventing them from scattering. When this unwavering devotion is your anchor, keeping everything aligned with your higher purpose, know that this steadfastness shines with the pure light of sattva, the mode of goodness.
translation.essence: Sattvic steadfastness is the calm, unwavering inner strength that harmonizes mind, breath, and senses, keeping them devotedly fixed on the spiritual path.

18-34.sanskrit: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन।प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी।।18.34।।
18-34.transliteration:
yayā tu dharma-kāmārthān dhṛityā dhārayate ‘rjuna
prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣhī dhṛitiḥ sā pārtha rājasī

translation.simple: O Arjuna, when your inner strength helps you pursue your duties, wishes, and material goals, but it comes with a strong attachment to what you might gain and a desire for the fruits of your actions, that kind of steady resolve, O Partha, is born of the quality of passion.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to understand a particular kind of inner firmness. While it may empower us to fulfill our responsibilities, pursue our aspirations, and manage our material world, its essence lies in the deep attachment to the outcomes. When our determination is fueled by an eager longing for the fruits of our efforts and a preoccupation with what we will gain, it's considered Rajasic. This passionate resolve, though powerful, keeps the mind tethered to the cycle of expectation and often leads to a subtle restlessness, pulling us away from the serene surrender that brings lasting peace.
translation.essence: The core message here reminds us that even good intentions, if accompanied by deep attachment to desired outcomes, lead to a passionate, rather than peaceful, resolve. True inner strength blossoms when we act with dedication but release our grasp on the fruits.

18-35.sanskrit: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च।न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी।।18.35।।
18-35.transliteration:
yayā svapnaṁ bhayaṁ śhokaṁ viṣhādaṁ madam eva cha
na vimuñchati durmedhā dhṛitiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī

translation.simple: O Arjuna, when a person's resolve holds them bound to excessive sleep, fear, sorrow, deep sadness, and pride, never letting go, such a stubbornness, stemming from a clouded understanding, is considered to be of the nature of darkness and inertia.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that not all forms of steadfastness are beneficial. The 'Tamasic' resolve described here is one that anchors a soul to states of imbalance and suffering. It's a stubbornness that refuses to release the grip of lethargy (often implying spiritual dullness), overwhelming anxieties, profound grief, soul-crushing despondency, and puffed-up arrogance. Instead of leading to liberation, this misguided determination solidifies one's connection to these lower energies, preventing spiritual awakening and true contentment. It highlights how vital it is to examine the true nature and fruit of our own resolve.
translation.essence: True spiritual strength comes from a resolve that liberates, not one that binds. When our inner determination keeps us captive to shadows like fear, sorrow, and pride, it reflects a wisdom yet to blossom. Let us aspire for a pure, clear resolve that guides us towards inner peace and freedom, moving away from attachments that hold us in darkness.

18-36.sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ।अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति।।18.36।।
18-36.transliteration:
sukhaṁ tv idānīṁ tri-vidhaṁ śhṛiṇu me bharatarṣhabha
abhyāsād ramate yatra duḥkhāntaṁ cha nigachchhati
 yat tad agre viṣham iva pariṇāme ‘mṛitopamam
tat sukhaṁ sāttvikaṁ proktam ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam

translation.simple: Now, O Arjuna, listen as I describe the three kinds of happiness. There is a joy that one comes to delight in through steady practice, and which ultimately brings all sorrow to an end.
translation.deep: Here, the Supreme Lord introduces the nature of happiness, hinting at a profound state that unfolds with consistent spiritual discipline. This divine joy, cultivated through dedicated effort and devotion, gradually purifies the heart and mind. It is a blissful experience that doesn't merely lessen suffering but utterly transcends it, leading the soul to an everlasting inner peace where sorrow can no longer touch.
translation.essence: Lord Krishna teaches that genuine happiness, discovered through steady spiritual practice, is the path to truly ending all suffering.

18-37.transliteration: yat  tad agre    viṣam   iva pariṇāme    'mṛtopamam  tat sukhaṁ  sāttvikaṁ   proktam ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam

translation.simple: The kind of happiness that feels difficult or bitter at the very beginning but turns into nectar-like sweetness in the end is known as the purest joy. This peace comes from a mind that is clear and at rest within itself.
translation.deep: True joy is often found through initial discipline and sacrifice. While the path may seem challenging at first, much like a bitter medicine, it eventually leads to the eternal nectar of self-realization. This superior state of being arises from the clarity of one's own soul and an intellect that has found its home in the Divine.
translation.essence: Pure happiness is born from inner discipline; it begins as a challenge but ends as an eternal blessing.

18-38.transliteration:
viṣhayendriya-sanyogād yat tad agre ’mṛitopamam
pariṇāme viṣham iva tat sukhaṁ rājasaṁ smṛitam

translation.simple: Sometimes, the joy we find through our senses in worldly things feels wonderfully sweet at first. But the Gita reminds us that such happiness, which later brings a feeling like bitterness, is born of passion. It's a passing pleasure that doesn't truly satisfy.
translation.deep: The sacred teachings reveal that happiness derived from the union of our senses with external objects may initially feel like divine nectar. Yet, if such joy leads us away from inner peace and towards endless craving, its ultimate outcome can be quite unsettling, even sorrowful—much like a subtle poison. This is the nature of 'rajasic' happiness, born of passion and driven by outward pursuits. It gently guides us to reflect on where we seek our lasting contentment.
translation.essence: Joy sought in external delights, though sweet initially, often turns to future disquiet. True peace lies deeper than such fleeting pleasures.

18-39.sanskrit: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः।निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्।।18.39।।
18-39.transliteration:
yad agre chānubandhe cha sukhaṁ mohanam ātmanaḥ
nidrālasya-pramādotthaṁ tat tāmasam udāhṛitam

translation.simple: The kind of comfort that feels good at first but then clouds our clarity and understanding, born from deep sleep, idleness, or a lack of careful attention – that is said to be happiness in the mode of darkness.
translation.deep: This verse tenderly illuminates the nature of 'tamasic' happiness. It's the deceptive comfort that initially promises ease but ultimately blurs our spiritual vision and deepens our attachment to the material. Such states emerge from an excess of sleep, a surrender to idleness, or a mind lost in heedlessness. They do not elevate the soul but rather keep it bound, preventing true inner awakening and genuine, lasting peace.
translation.essence: Beware of comfort that, while pleasing at first, ultimately clouds our inner sight; for joy born of sleepiness, idleness, or inattention only veils true wisdom and belongs to the mode of ignorance.

18-40.sanskrit: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः।सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्ित्रभिर्गुणैः।।18.40।।
18-40.transliteration:
na tad asti pṛithivyāṁ vā divi deveṣhu vā punaḥ
sattvaṁ prakṛiti-jair muktaṁ yad ebhiḥ syāt tribhir guṇaiḥ

translation.simple: No being, whether on this earth or in the celestial realms among the gods, is ever truly free from the three qualities born of material nature. Every soul in this creation is gently guided and influenced by these gunas.
translation.deep: Reflect on the profound truth that within the material realm, no entity—from a human on earth to the deities in the heavens—can completely escape the deep influence of sattva, rajas, and tamas. This verse lovingly reveals how these qualities, arising from nature itself, intricately shape all experiences and actions. It offers a gentle encouragement to observe their play and aspire towards a state of being that transcends their binding embrace.
translation.essence: On earth, in the heavens, or even among the gods, all beings are touched by the three qualities of material nature. This verse softly reminds us that understanding the pervasive presence of sattva, rajas, and tamas is a loving invitation to transcend their influence.

18-41.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परंतप।कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः।।18.41।।
18-41.transliteration:
brāhmaṇa-kṣhatriya-viśhāṁ śhūdrāṇāṁ cha parantapa
karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāva-prabhavair guṇaiḥ

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, the sacred duties of those who teach and guide, those who protect and govern, those who trade and cultivate, and those who serve with their hands, are all gracefully distinguished according to their own inborn nature and inner qualities.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna reveals a profound truth: the work we are meant to do in this world springs forth from our very essence, our 'svabhava,' which is shaped by the divine interplay of the Gunas. This understanding encourages us to recognize that each soul is uniquely inclined towards certain actions, and by embracing these natural tendencies, we find our true purpose and contribute to the beautiful harmony of creation, not by external force, but by inner calling.
translation.essence: Our inherent nature and qualities lovingly guide us to our unique work, fulfilling our divine purpose in the grand design.

18-42.sanskrit: शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च।ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम्।।18.42।।
18-42.transliteration:
śhamo damas tapaḥ śhauchaṁ kṣhāntir ārjavam eva cha
jñānaṁ vijñānam āstikyaṁ brahma-karma svabhāva-jam

translation.simple: A truly spiritual soul naturally develops a calm mind, mastery over their senses, and a gentle discipline. They are pure in heart and action, always forgiving, and straightforward in their dealings. Possessing sacred knowledge, real wisdom, and firm faith, these are the beautiful qualities that naturally arise from their inner nature.
translation.deep: For those whose very essence resonates with the Divine, certain noble qualities manifest spontaneously. This includes the tranquility of mind (śama) and steady control over the senses (dama). They engage in spiritual efforts (tapas) and maintain both inner and outer purity (śaucam). Boundless patience and forgiveness (kṣānti), along with unwavering integrity and honesty (ārjavam), grace their character. A profound grasp of spiritual knowledge (jñānam), its practical realization (vijñānam), and an unshakeable faith in the spiritual path (āstikyam) are the inherent actions, the very dharma, of such a soul, blooming from their intrinsic spiritual nature.
translation.essence: Inner peace, self-control, purity, forgiveness, honesty, wisdom, and unwavering faith are the natural virtues of a soul aligned with the Divine.

18-43.sanskrit: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम्।दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम्।।18.43।।
18-43.transliteration:
śhauryaṁ tejo dhṛitir dākṣhyaṁ yuddhe chāpy apalāyanam
dānam īśhvara-bhāvaśh cha kṣhātraṁ karma svabhāva-jam

translation.simple: A brave spirit, inner radiance, steady resolve, skillful action, never retreating from a challenge, giving generously, and a natural feeling of leadership – these are the duties that gently flow from the very nature of a protector.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us that true valor isn't just physical strength, but an inner luminosity (Tejas). It speaks of unwavering resolve (Dhriti), the wisdom of skillful action (Dakshyam), and the profound courage to stand firm in the face of adversity, never abandoning one's sacred duty. The heart of a protector naturally extends to selfless giving (Daanam) and a noble sense of stewardship, a connection to the Divine quality of governance (Ishwarabhava). These virtues are not acquired but awaken from within, a beautiful expression of the soul's unique calling.
translation.essence: Courage, steadfastness, skill, generosity, and a guiding spirit are the inherent virtues that blossom naturally from a protector's true essence.

18-44.sanskrit: कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम्।परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम्।।18.44।।
18-44.transliteration:
kṛiṣhi-gau-rakṣhya-vāṇijyaṁ vaiśhya-karma svabhāva-jam
paricharyātmakaṁ karma śhūdrasyāpi svabhāva-jam

translation.simple: Some find their calling in farming, protecting animals, and engaging in commerce, as this flows from their innate nature. Others, by their very being, are drawn to tasks of dedicated service.
translation.deep: The Gita reveals how our inherent nature, or 'svabhāva,' gently guides us toward particular forms of action. For some, this inclination manifests as the vital work of cultivating the earth, caring for cows, and facilitating trade, thereby sustaining the community. For others, a spirit of humble service is their natural path. When we align our work with our true self, each task becomes a sacred offering, bringing peace and purpose to our hearts.
translation.essence: Each soul finds its unique purpose in work, whether through providing for society or offering devoted service, aligning with its true nature to make every effort a sacred offering.

18-45.sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः।स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु।।18.45।।
18-45.transliteration:
sve sve karmaṇy abhirataḥ sansiddhiṁ labhate naraḥ
sva-karma-nirataḥ siddhiṁ yathā vindati tach chhṛiṇu

translation.simple: When we lovingly engage in the duties meant for us, we gradually find inner peace and fulfillment. It is through steadfast dedication to one's own path that true success blossoms.
translation.deep: This verse gently guides us to understand that our unique path, our 'svadharma,' is a sacred trust. By performing our allocated duties with sincerity and devotion, without attachment to results, our hearts are purified. This dedicated action transforms into a spiritual practice, slowly unveiling the divine perfection that resides within and leading us closer to ultimate liberation.
translation.essence: True spiritual fulfillment arises from humbly and devotedly fulfilling the responsibilities given to us, transforming every action into an act of worship.

18-46.sanskrit: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः।।18.46।।
18-46.transliteration:
yataḥ pravṛittir bhūtānāṁ yena sarvam idaṁ tatam
sva-karmaṇā tam abhyarchya siddhiṁ vindati mānavaḥ

translation.simple: All beings find their start in Him, and His presence gently pervades everything we experience. When we perform our own duties with a heart full of devotion, offering them to Him, we discover true fulfillment and inner peace.
translation.deep: The Supreme Lord is the very wellspring from which all life's activities emanate, and His divine essence is interwoven throughout the entire fabric of creation. By consecrating one's inherent duties and actions as a loving worship to this all-encompassing Divine, the sincere seeker gradually attains spiritual perfection and profound realization.
translation.essence: Dedicate your actions to the Lord, who is the origin of all and pervades everything; through this devotional service, you will reach ultimate fulfillment.

18-47.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्।।18.47।।
18-47.transliteration:
śhreyān swa-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣhṭhitāt
svabhāva-niyataṁ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣham

translation.simple: It is better to follow the path meant for you, even if you do it imperfectly, rather than flawlessly performing someone else's duty. When you sincerely act according to your true nature, you remain free from fault.
translation.deep: This verse gently reminds us to embrace our unique journey. 'Svadharma' refers to the duties and actions that align with our deepest, inherent nature. Even if our efforts seem imperfect, performing work suited to our true self brings more spiritual benefit than flawlessly executing a role not meant for us. By honoring our inner calling, we stay true to ourselves and are protected from negative karma.
translation.essence: Find peace by embracing and performing your unique, divinely-guided duties. To act from your true nature is to be free from fault and aligned with divine will.

18-48.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्।सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः।।18.48।।
18-48.transliteration:
saha-jaṁ karma kaunteya sa-doṣham api na tyajet
sarvārambhā hi doṣheṇa dhūmenāgnir ivāvṛitāḥ

translation.simple: My dear Arjuna, do not give up the work that flows from your own nature, even if it appears to have some imperfections. Just as fire is always veiled by smoke, all our undertakings are touched by some flaw.
translation.deep: This profound wisdom guides us to accept the path meant for us. The Lord reminds us that no endeavor in this material world is entirely free from imperfections. To forsake our inherent duty because of perceived faults would be to miss the essence of our existence. Just as smoke naturally accompanies fire, a certain degree of imperfection is part of all human actions. Our spiritual growth lies in performing our natural duties with sincerity and devotion, seeing beyond the flaws and understanding that the divine plan unfolds through our sincere efforts, even if they are not outwardly perfect.
translation.essence: Perform your natural duties with love, even if they seem imperfect. Remember, all actions carry a trace of imperfection, just as fire is always accompanied by smoke. Embrace this truth and act with a serene heart.

18-49.sanskrit: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः।नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति।।18.49।।
18-49.transliteration:
asakta-buddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigata-spṛihaḥ
naiṣhkarmya-siddhiṁ paramāṁ sannyāsenādhigachchhati

translation.simple: With a mind unattached to anything, a self gently controlled, and a heart free from desires, one naturally finds the ultimate freedom. This highest perfection comes through the spirit of true renunciation.
translation.deep: The journey to profound spiritual liberation unfolds for the one whose intellect remains untouched by the fleeting allure of worldly attachments, embracing a tranquil detachment in all spheres. Such a soul, having gently mastered their inner being and released all forms of material longing, naturally progresses towards the supreme state of Naiṣkarmya-siddhi. This isn't inaction, but the divine art of performing all duties with unwavering focus on the divine, devoid of personal desire for the fruits, thus achieving ultimate freedom from the cycle of karma through the profound wisdom of Sannyasa—true renunciation.
translation.essence: Detach your mind, conquer your desires, and master your self. Through such serene renunciation, you will attain ultimate liberation and peace.

18-50.sanskrit: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे।समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा।।18.50।।
18-50.transliteration:
siddhiṁ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me
samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣhṭhā jñānasya yā parā

translation.simple: O Arjuna, please understand from Me, in simple terms, how a soul that has found spiritual perfection truly comes to know the Divine. This is the highest understanding.
translation.deep: Lord Krishna lovingly invites us to understand, in essence, how a soul that has purified its being and achieved spiritual perfection truly comes to realize the boundless Divine. This teaching reveals the profound culmination of all wisdom, leading to a deep, direct experience of the ultimate truth.
translation.essence: Krishna beautifully shares the secret of how a perfected soul comes to know the Divine, which is the very peak of all spiritual wisdom.

18-51.sanskrit: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च।शब्दादीन् विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च।।18.51।।
18-51.transliteration:
buddhyā viśhuddhayā yukto dhṛityātmānaṁ niyamya cha
śhabdādīn viṣhayāns tyaktvā rāga-dveṣhau vyudasya cha

translation.simple: With a purified mind and firm resolve, one gently takes control of their inner self. They lovingly let go of the pull of worldly sensations like sounds and sights, and release the feelings of strong liking or disliking.
translation.deep: When the intellect becomes clear and bright, free from confusion, and the spirit is steadied by unwavering determination, a seeker begins to master their own being. This involves gracefully stepping back from the captivating allure of sensory experiences, recognizing their transient nature, and gently untangling oneself from the binds of deep affection and strong dislike, which often cloud our true perception and peace.
translation.essence: Cultivate a pure mind and steady will. Release the grip of the senses, and rise above attraction and aversion, finding true inner peace.

18-52.sanskrit: विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः।ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः।।18.52।।
18-52.transliteration:
vivikta-sevī laghv-āśhī yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ
dhyāna-yoga-paro nityaṁ vairāgyaṁ samupāśhritaḥ

translation.simple: A sincere seeker finds peace in quiet places, eats with moderation, and gently controls their words, body, and thoughts. They are always focused on meditation and find true solace in detachment from the world.
translation.deep: The path of inner peace is cultivated by choosing serene surroundings, nourishing the body simply, and gently guiding one's speech, actions, and thoughts. Constantly absorbed in the sacred practice of meditation, such a soul deeply embraces non-attachment, finding true freedom from worldly pulls and a steadfast connection to the divine.
translation.essence: Embrace quietude, mindful living, and self-mastery. Dedicate yourself to meditation and detachment for profound spiritual progress and inner peace.

18-53.sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम्।विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते।।18.53।।
18-53.transliteration:
ahankāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhaṁ parigraham
vimuchya nirmamaḥ śhānto brahma-bhūyāya kalpate

translation.simple: When we gently release our ego, our pride, our desires, our anger, and our deep need to possess things, a profound calm settles within. We become free from the feeling of 'mine,' and our hearts become ready to experience the ultimate divine truth.
translation.deep: To truly align with the Supreme, one must learn to relinquish the heavy burdens of ego and its attachments—arrogance, self-importance, unbridled desires, and consuming anger. By letting go of the relentless drive to accumulate and claim, a state of non-possessiveness blossoms. This liberation from 'mine' cultivates an unwavering inner peace, making one fit to realize the eternal nature of the Divine.
translation.essence: Releasing ego, pride, desire, anger, and possessiveness brings deep inner peace, making one truly ready to realize the Divine.

18-54.sanskrit: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम्।।18.54।।
18-54.transliteration:
brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śhochati na kāṅkṣhati
samaḥ sarveṣhu bhūteṣhu mad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām

translation.simple: When one connects with their true spiritual self, their heart becomes filled with joy and peace. They neither mourn for what is lost nor long for what is not there. Seeing all beings with an equal and loving eye, they come to experience My supreme devotion.
translation.deep: Having realized their identity with the Divine Spirit, the soul achieves a profound and joyful serenity. Such a person transcends the sorrows of the world and is free from all restless desires. By perceiving the divine essence equally in all creation, a supreme and unparalleled love for the Supreme Lord blossoms naturally within their heart.
translation.essence: Through spiritual awakening, a serene heart emerges, free from grief and craving. This state of equality towards all beings naturally leads to the highest, most pure devotion to the Divine.

18-55.sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः।ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम्।।18.55।।
18-55.transliteration:
bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaśh chāsmi tattvataḥ
tato māṁ tattvato jñātvā viśhate tad-anantaram

translation.simple: Through loving devotion, one truly understands My nature and My boundless greatness. Once this profound truth is known, that soul then comes to merge with Me.
translation.deep: It is by the path of sincere and unwavering devotion that a soul comes to truly perceive My essence, comprehending My limitless majesty and fundamental being. When this deep, heartfelt understanding blossoms, born of pure love, then that devoted soul naturally finds its way into ultimate union with My divine presence.
translation.essence: Pure devotion reveals My truth and My glory, and this true knowing leads to ultimate union with Me.

18-56.sanskrit: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः।मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम्।।18.56।।
18-56.transliteration:
sarva-karmāṇy api sadā kurvāṇo mad-vyapāśhrayaḥ
mat-prasādād avāpnoti śhāśhvataṁ padam avyayam

translation.simple: Even as you carry out all your daily duties, if your heart rests in Me, through My grace, you will surely attain that eternal, unchanging spiritual dwelling.
translation.deep: This beautiful verse assures us that our engagement in worldly duties does not hinder our spiritual journey. When we sincerely perform all our actions, yet remain ever-sheltered in the Divine, our efforts become sacred. Through the Lord's boundless grace, we are gently guided to that ultimate, unchanging, and eternal spiritual abode, a place of supreme peace beyond all transient experiences.
translation.essence: Performing all actions with devotion and shelter in the Divine leads, by His grace, to the eternal, unchanging spiritual state.

18-57.sanskrit: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः।बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव।।18.57।।
18-57.transliteration:
chetasā sarva-karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat-paraḥ
buddhi-yogam upāśhritya mach-chittaḥ satataṁ bhava

translation.simple: With a serene heart, offer all your actions to Me, making Me your ultimate purpose. Through spiritual wisdom, always keep your mind lovingly fixed upon Me.
translation.deep: This beautiful guidance invites us to a deeper way of living. It's about gently offering every action and its fruit to the Divine, recognizing that the true source of all is the Supreme. When we make the Divine our highest aspiration and rely on pure spiritual wisdom, our mind naturally becomes attuned. This constant remembrance transforms our daily life into a continuous act of loving devotion, bringing profound inner stillness and purpose.
translation.essence: Offer all your actions and your entire mind to the Divine, making the Supreme your constant focus and cherished goal.

18-58.sanskrit: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि।अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि।।18.58।।
18-58.transliteration:
mach-chittaḥ sarva-durgāṇi mat-prasādāt tariṣhyasi
atha chet tvam ahankārān na śhroṣhyasi vinaṅkṣhyasi

translation.simple: When your mind rests in Me, My grace will gently carry you over every difficulty. But if, driven by pride, you choose not to listen, you will surely stray from the path.
translation.deep: If your inner being is absorbed in Me, then through My divine favor, you will transcend all the intricate challenges of existence. Yet, should you allow your ego to overpower reason and disregard My loving instructions, you will inevitably wander into distress.
translation.essence: Fix your mind on Me, and My grace will conquer all your hardships. Resist My guidance due to ego, and you will surely stumble.

18-59.sanskrit: यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे।मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति।।18.59।।
18-59.transliteration:
yad ahankāram āśhritya na yotsya iti manyase
mithyaiṣha vyavasāyas te prakṛitis tvāṁ niyokṣhyati

translation.simple: My dear one, if you mistakenly believe, out of ego, 'I will not participate,' know that such a resolve is fleeting. Your very being, your inherent nature, will lovingly impel you towards your destined path.
translation.deep: This wisdom reveals a profound truth: the 'I' that asserts its will to withdraw, born of ego, is ultimately an illusion. Our inherent nature, our 'prakriti,' is a divine force, gently yet firmly orchestrating our actions according to a cosmic design. It teaches us surrender, acknowledging that a greater flow guides our journey, even when our personal will resists.
translation.essence: Ego's refusal is temporary; your true nature will lovingly lead you to your path.

18-60.sanskrit: स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा।कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत्।।18.60।।
18-60.transliteration:
swbhāva-jena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā
kartuṁ nechchhasi yan mohāt kariṣhyasy avaśho ’pi tat

translation.simple: O Arjuna, you are bound by your own nature and the work born of your qualities. Even if you choose not to act now because of confusion, your own inner drive will eventually compel you to do it, even against your will.
translation.deep: Each of us is shaped by our inherent nature, known as Svabhāva, which is formed by our past actions and tendencies. When we face difficult moments, delusion may make us want to turn away from our path. However, the momentum of our true nature is so powerful that it eventually steers us back toward our purpose, moving us even when the mind hesitates.
translation.essence: You cannot run away from who you are. Your inner nature is the blueprint of your journey; trust in its flow rather than fighting against your calling.

18-61.sanskrit: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति।भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया।।18.61।।
18-61.transliteration:
īśhvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ hṛid-deśhe ‘rjuna tiṣhṭhati
bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā

translation.simple: The Supreme Lord dwells in the heart of all living beings, O Arjuna. By His divine energy, He guides the journey of every soul, as if they were seated upon a vast machine of life.
translation.deep: In the sacred space of the heart, the Divine resides as the inner witness. Through the power of His Maya, He orchestrates the movement of all beings, who experience life as though they are mounted on a mechanical vehicle. While we feel we are the sole doers, it is the indwelling Presence that provides the vital force for our journey.
translation.essence: The Divine is not far away in the heavens; He is the silent companion within your heart, lovingly steering your life's path through every turn.

18-62.sanskrit: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत।तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम्।।18.62।।
18-62.transliteration:
tam eva śharaṇaṁ gachchha sarva-bhāvena bhārata
tat-prasādāt parāṁ śhāntiṁ sthānaṁ prāpsyasi śhāśhvatam

translation.simple: Seek refuge in the Divine with your entire heart. By His grace, you will find supreme peace and reach the eternal home where you truly belong.
translation.deep: Surrender every part of your being—your thoughts, feelings, and actions—to the Lord who dwells within. When you offer yourself fully, His divine grace will lead you to a state of everlasting stillness and a spiritual resting place that is beyond all time.
translation.essence: Complete devotion and surrender are the keys to receiving divine grace, which bestows eternal peace and ultimate liberation.

18-63.sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया।विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु।।18.63।।
18-63.transliteration:
iti te jñānam ākhyātaṁ guhyād guhyataraṁ mayā
vimṛiśhyaitad aśheṣheṇa yathechchhasi tathā kuru

translation.simple: I have shared with you the most sacred of all secrets. Now, reflect on this wisdom deeply and completely, and then act as your heart chooses.
translation.deep: The Divine has revealed the most profound truth, more hidden than any mystery. Having been blessed with this knowledge, you are invited to contemplate it in its entirety. True spiritual growth comes when we use our God-given free will to act with a clear and conscious mind.
translation.essence: Divine wisdom is a guiding light that empowers us to make our own choices with clarity and grace.

18-64.sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः।इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्।।18.64।।
18-64.transliteration:
sarva-guhyatamaṁ bhūyaḥ śhṛiṇu me paramaṁ vachaḥ
iṣhṭo ‘si me dṛiḍham iti tato vakṣhyāmi te hitam

translation.simple: Listen once more to My most secret and supreme word. Because you are so very dear to Me, I am speaking this for your own well-being.
translation.deep: The Divine reveals the deepest mysteries not to the curious, but to the beloved. This verse captures the moment where instruction turns into an intimate promise, showing that spiritual truth is a gift of love intended for our highest good.
translation.essence: True wisdom is a whisper of love from the Divine to a soul they cherish.

18-65.sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु।मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे।।18.65।।
18-65.transliteration:
man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru
mām evaiṣhyasi satyaṁ te pratijāne priyo ‘si me

translation.simple: Always keep Me in your thoughts and offer Me your love. In everything you do, honor Me and bow before Me. I promise that you will surely come to Me, for you are truly dear to My heart.
translation.deep: Let your consciousness be fully absorbed in the Divine. Become a soul of pure devotion, turning every action into a sacred offering and every gesture into an act of humble reverence. Through this complete union of heart and mind, you shall transcend all and reach Me. This is My solemn vow to you, spoken because of the deep affection I have for you.
translation.essence: The most direct path to the Divine is through constant remembrance, heartfelt devotion, and total surrender, anchored in the eternal bond of love between the Creator and the seeker.

18-66.sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः।।18.66।।
18-66.transliteration:
sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śharaṇaṁ vraja
ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣhayiṣhyāmi mā śhuchaḥ

translation.simple: Let go of all your worries and various obligations, and simply take shelter in Me alone. I will free you from all your mistakes and burdens. Do not worry; do not grieve.
translation.deep: This is the ultimate promise of the Divine. It calls for the total surrender of the ego and the many roles we play in the world. When we stop relying on our own limited strength and place our complete trust in the Supreme, the Divine takes full responsibility for our spiritual journey, dissolving the weight of our past actions and guiding us to liberation.
translation.essence: Complete surrender to the Divine is the highest path, bringing absolute freedom from fear and the end of all sorrow.

18-67.sanskrit: इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन।न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति।।18.67।।
18-67.transliteration:
idaṁ te nātapaskyāya nābhaktāya kadāchana
na chāśhuśhruṣhave vāchyaṁ na cha māṁ yo ‘bhyasūtayi

translation.simple: This sacred wisdom is a gift meant for those who are sincere and devoted. It should not be shared with those who lack self-discipline, those who have no love for the Divine, those who do not wish to listen, or those who harbor ill-will toward Me.
translation.deep: Sri Krishna emphasizes that spiritual truth requires a prepared heart. Just as a seed needs fertile soil to grow, this profound knowledge only takes root in a person who has cultivated discipline and devotion. To offer these teachings to someone who is envious or unwilling to listen is to ignore the sanctity of the message. True understanding flows naturally when the seeker is humble and ready.
translation.essence: The beauty of divine wisdom is best understood by a heart filled with devotion and a mind calmed by discipline.

18-68.sanskrit: य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति।भक्ितं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः।।18.68।।
18-68.transliteration:
ya idaṁ paramaṁ guhyaṁ mad-bhakteṣhv abhidhāsyati
bhaktiṁ mayi parāṁ kṛitvā mām evaiṣhyaty asanśhayaḥ

translation.simple: Whoever shares this sacred and secret wisdom with those who love Me, doing so with pure devotion, will undoubtedly come to Me.
